I picked up this little beauty to replace both an ancient and cranky 5-disc CD Player and a single disc DVD player.
I now have breathing room in the old entertainment center, so even my antique turntable can take a creaky spin every now and again.
Seeing that I can't connect a toaster without help, I called on my trusty better half to unravel the mystery of setting it up.
In non-technical language, a.k.a.
plain English, this is what you need to know about this mighty machine:

1.
The manual needs a lot of work.
It's neither user-friendly nor idiot-proof.
Ditto for the boxy silver remote.
2.
It is easy to set up if you already know how to do that sort of thing.
(We have component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver.)

3.
It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs.
With the benefit of 5.1 surround, movies like Master and Commander can literally move you, and CDs have never sounded better.
4.
It is as convenient as a 5-disc CD changer as it is a 5-disc DVD player, except that when you're playing more than one CD you'll need to put it in "CD Mode" first.
5.
It can easily play different types of media, such as audio Cds, MP3s, DVDs and those other mysterious formats - just put in the discs and play away.
6.
The video quality is very good on a regular TV.
You can set up different pre-defined picture quality modes, or customize to suit your own taste if you're a techie or a buff.
If you have difficulty making up your mind, ignore this option.
7.
The player is chock full of options, but you have to explore for yourself, which can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of it.
Read the manual, you say?
See Item 1 above.
8.
There's on-screen information for MP3s and photo CDs, with different views available for the contents.
(Groups/folders or entire playlists)

9.
I can't comment on the progressive scan feature, since I don't have an HD or HD-ready TV - yet.
(Still waiting for that lottery win)

10.
It is supposed to play DVD-Audio discs, but you need 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver to play them.
Unfortunately, our receiver is lacking these inputs, but then again, I am also lacking any DVD-Audio discs.
Electronics buffs will probably say that it needs a bit of "tweaking" to get it to look and sound just right, but it looks and sounds great to me.
All in all a very good player, perhaps excellent when you factor in the price.
Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004

I have had a lot of printers over the years (IBM, Epson, HP, Canon, Lexmark, etc.), and had kind of gone away from HP a bit due to their software/driver problems (when they off-shored the development/support, the quality slipped quite a bit).
However, when printing Christmas cards, my Canon died, and I had been impressed with this HP model when I was helping my sister sort out hers, so I bought one (MFP M479fdw).
Software seems to work reliably so far, so I think HP has addressed that somewhat, granted it is a bit rough and crude in places, but it works.
And it works from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 (Big Sur), as well as from mobile (iOS).
The printer hardware seems to be very good, output arrives quite fast.
One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers (including some lower end HPs) is that they do not put much horsepower into the printer CPUs, and cost-reduce the hardware to the point that they are slow and do not hold up, but this version seems well designed and made.
Ratings from PC Magazine, Wirecutter, etc.
generally have this printer at or towards the top, I would say that is accurate.
Print quality on text is excellent, graphics from web pages and similar also excellent, scans are very good (a custom flat-bed would be a tad better, but this is for an all-in-one amongst the best I have seen).
For printing high-quality pictures, you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer, but this one prints OK for a laser.
HP does not ship this printer with full duty cycle cartridges, but the ones they ship with will still do a decent number of pages.
Control screen is touch and good sized, gets the job done.
Unit is fairly heavy and large, so if you are using this on a desk, check the dimensions some.
The printer is not cheap, but it has excellent print quality and appears to be very well built, so HP has come back to where it once was, at the top.

[[VIDEOID:5cb01b680d3ae41bbade0eaedaabfe62]] This is an absolutely gorgeous kettle.
It is well made, solidly built, and overall a dream to use.
POSITIVES
- It holds up to 2 quarts of water to the fill line.
- It is solidly built.
- It whistles lightly when the water has reached a rolling boil.
- The top fits securely on the kettle but requires a little extra strength to seat and remove.
- It comes with a blue potholder.
- It comes in seven wonderful colors--gray, cream, navy, perracotta (like a salmon color), marigold (yellow), sage (deep green), and mist (a light green).
NEGATIVES
- The last bit of water in the kettle gets caught under the rim unless one can center the flow through the spout.
This means that I have to dry the inside with a towel for storage.
- The kettle is heavy; almost like a cast iron pot.
- It requires a potholder to use (opening of the spout, pouring, etc.) because the entire kettle gets very hot and that includes the handle and spout lever.
I also would have liked a mitt potholder the color of the kettle.
In summary, I love this kettle despite its negatives.
At this high price, supplying the user with a mitt potholder instead of a flat one in the color of the kettle one purchases, would elevate the purchase to the next level.
Note that I never heard of the Caraway brand before and saw this kettle in blue on the Vine program.
Since ordering this through Vine would not provide me with much savings at the list price, I decided to order this when the price came down for prime day in the color I wanted.
The Caraway site was cheaper that day by $4 (i.e.
$176) but sort of required the purchase of insurance for $4.95.
Therefore, I purchased this on Amazon for $180 plus tax, bringing this to $191.93.
I still consider this pricey but this is the best made kettle I ever tried.
It is right up there with Le  Creuset Dutch Ovens and almost just as heavy too.
This is a kettle that I expect to last my lifetime.
There are many kettles on the market that are less than $40 that also could last a lifetime but they are not as nice.
I do hope it continues to meet my expectations going forward.
If it fails in any way, I will lower my rating, update my review, and will most likely regret my purchase.
As of now, I love this and took off one star due to the negatives.
UPDATE - I've been using this regularly for days now and I noticed that this takes longer to boil water than my other kettle and keeps the water warmer a little longer.
I also noticed that if I put this on my burner that has a lower flame, the handle does not get hot when the boil is complete, so that is nice.

I work for the United States Postal Service and recently purchased the OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth speaker for use in my LLV truck on my rural mail route.
The speaker performs beautifully and I wanted to protect it to, from and while at work so I purchased this case.
I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker, but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route.
I received the case and used it at work yesterday.
The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket and the carabiner clip.
I have no need for them now, but I'm sure they will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along and want to clip the case to my day pack.
As for playback while in the case?
Yeah, it was terribly muffled.
It didn't work for me as it apparently has for others.
Yet, the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work.
I like how smooth the zipper is and how heavy duty/reinforced the stitching for the zipper is.
The interior is not as thickly padded as I would have expected, however it does protect the speaker.
I deducted one star due to the mediocre interior padding.
I hope that, if the company ever revamps this case design, they beef up the padding a bit.

You read that correctly - I installed this on the outside of my (1985) sliding glass door.
Here's why: My kid is 23, legally, and 2 intellectually.
He also has seizures.
Oh, he's also moderate to severely Autistic.
All of my doors on this house have double cylinder (two keys required to unlock, outside and in) deadbolts.
The sliding glass doors have nothing.
And apparently there is no way to key lock a sliding glass door.
My son is just observant enough that all the typical sliding glass door 'locks' he figured out within about a week of our moving in; and given that 3 years ago he escaped on me for literally less than 60 SECONDS and in that 60 seconds or less he had a seizure, slammed backwards on the concrete, and got not only a nasty gash on the back of his head but a near-life threatening brain bleed on the front of his brain where his brain flew forward into his skull.
I'm a solo parent...
not a single parent that gets every other weekend or so free, no help from family or friends or government agencies...
and sometimes a girl's gotta get a bath.
Or go the potty.
And I do not have the money for a set of French doors.
So, after more investigating than I care to admit, I figured I'd give this a try.
(I had already attempted one of those track locks and for this old style sliding glass door it just didn't work.) In our situation, when I need to use the restroom or take a shower or just sleep without worry, I go out one of my locking doors, use the slide lock to impede the opening of the sliding glass door from the inside, come back in the house through the door I went out, lock everything up, and do what I gotta do.
Then I can go back and unlatch the slider from outside the house and it's just out of the way.
No one comes in that sliding glass door - it opens onto a screened in porch (with a concrete slab floor) - so I'm not worried about how weird it looks that I have a lock outside - lol.
Anyway, my use for this item is unconventional (they call that 'off label' in the medical field) but it sure makes my life easier and for that I am immensely happy:)

Here we have another case of purchasing an extended warranty being asked to provide a review but never having made use of (and hoping never to have to) the purchased coverage.
The price was right but lower on SquareTrade's site (I'm signed up for the specials and such mailings so I should have been made aware of.
But it's only a few dollars so its no big loss).
The plan covers up to three replacements of the covered item or the term of the warranty you purchased (two years in this case).
After trying to troubleshoot your device over the phone they will make the decision to either repair or replace your item.
If they decided to replace the item it's wholly their choice to either provide a new or newest model of your device or provide a refurbished model of what you have.
They promise quick turn-around and cover shipping in both directions.
If you do not return the defective model within in a certain time frame (I believe it's 30 days) of receiving your replacement your credit card (which you MUST have on file to file a claim) will be charged the full cost of the device when new.
I've heard nothing but good things about SquareTrade for years and almost all of the low-star reviews seem to be user's not understanding the plan or not making sure they would be covered for their purchases rather than anything to do with SquareTrade itself.
While I hope I never need to use the plan it was affordable enough to make up for Amazon's fairly deplorable ninety day warranty (our refurbished PaperWhite came with a full year's coverage.
A brand new Dot, like their seven and eight inch tablets (unlike their six or ten inch tablets, the Echo or Tap and their entire eReader line which all have one-year warranties) only has ninety days I don't know why.
I've always trusted Amazon's electronics, I wonder at their apparent lack of faith.
But anyway.
I've rambled on enough.
The two years of coverage is comforting and was quite affordable.
I'm happy with the purchase and honestly hope I never need to use it.

My husband and I bought two sets of these three years ago from Circuit City during their going out of business sale.
We both travel quite a bit and were in need of decent headphones for longer flights (let's face it, the ear buds provided by the airlines just don't cut it).
My husband accidentally left his set, in their pouch, in the seat back pocket on a flight last year and was in need of a replacement set for our trip to Germany last week.
I was amazed by the price when I came onto Amazon to check - $29.99 was a steal compared to the $80 we spent a few years back!
This headset is not the top of the line, but it is effective in canceling out the low aircraft drawl while in-flight.
(They are also quite nice when you need to drown out the crying child in 23F.;)) The battery life is remarkable.
I have had to change the battery on my set only twice in the three years I've owned it.
The only complaint that I have, which results in the four star rating instead of five, is that after wearing the set for a few hours (i.e., Amsterdam to Houston, TX), my ears begin to ache on the outside.
It is almost like the headset becomes to tight over longer periods of time.
I tend not to wear earrings on airplanes, so I can rule out the possibility of pinching.
Other than that slight achy feeling, these are wonderful for the casual traveler and the price simply cannot be beat!

This device connects to the VGA port and from there connects to a monitor or TV HDMI port, It WILL NOT work in the other direction, and it requires a source of 5V 1A power (any standard phone charger will work.)

I am OK with the limitation because I am only using the TV as a second screen with MS Office,

On an old Windows 7 system it's truly plug and play.
I had it up and running without the scant instructions in mere minutes.
For me it is a perfect solution.

This VORNADO SILVER SWAN S SMALL ROOM OSCILLATING FAN (Brushed Nickel) moves a lot of air!
On the high setting, it's definitely capable of sweeping a small room (e.g., a child's bedroom, a home office), and completely circulating the room's air.
Even the low setting delivers a breeze that will disturb loose papers if the fan is aimed at your office desk.
I love the minimalist "modern" design (this is actually an Art Deco design that harks back to the 1920s).
Viewed from the front, the fan displays a wire cage with a silver central disc, encircled by a thin black ring.
The base has a streamlined, pointy foot, and a silvery matte finish.
The fan has a very small footprint (even when oscillating).
The tilt of the fan's head is adjustable, but the limited arc means the fan will be much more effective when placed somewhere off the floor.
The fan oscillates, or delivers a directly-aimed air stream--just pull up or push down the stalk on top.
This is a small fan that doesn't know it's a small fan!
It's a great choice for any small-to-medium-sized room where flat surface space is at a premium.
And it's a Vornado, so you know that it's good quality, made to last.

This HAMILTON BEACH DIGITAL RICE COOKER (37518, Stainless Steel, 6-¾ cup yield for white rice) cooks perfect fluffy rice every time, and is a good family-sized rice cooker (enough rice for 4 persons).
It has the same capacity as the [[ASIN:B071KPXVJ7 Hamilton Beach 37506 Model]], but has a hinged lid (with rubber gasket, a fancy steam vent, an exterior condensation cup, and a lid liner).
The fancy lid of this Model 37518 causes steamed foods to cook in one-third to one-half of the time required by the simpler Model 37506, but the fancy lid has NO effect on rice or cereal cooking times.
The Model 37518 has a condensation cup that must be emptied, as needed, during cooking.
The lid liner is a part that must be removed each time for washing.
(The instructions don't explain how to remove the lid liner, but it pulls straight off the post that holds it.)

The Model 37518 allows you to set custom cooking times for Hot Cereal or Steam.
This isn't really necessary, because the Model 37506 cooks both cereal and rice automatically, and steams food with the aid of a cooking timer.
Most rice cookers do a good job of cooking rice--they have a thermostat that contacts the underside of the cooking pot and turns the cooker off automatically when the water evaporates and the pot temperature rises.
Some rice cookers--like this one--cook rice to greater perfection than others, but rice cookers mostly differ in their controls (ranging from simple on/off to extra-fancy multi-button digital displays), and in the quantity of their cooked rice yield.
This rice cooker is sort of in the middle, regarding both controls and yield.
It will cook different kinds of rice (there is a chart for correct amounts of rice and water for long grain brown or white, jasmine, basmati, etc.).
It will cook different cereals and grains (barley, oatmeal, Cream of Wheat, etc.).
It will steam food (vegetables, poultry, seafood); and it will steam food and rice together.
The size of this cooker is good if you're making rice for a family of four, or if you're steaming foods for a family of two.
I love it for the way it cooks fluffy rice and automatically keeps the rice warm for up to 12 hours.
I also love it for cooking Cream of Wheat automatically without burning it on the bottom.
Cooking in a rice cooker takes longer than cooking on a stovetop or in a microwave.
For example, 3 cups of uncooked white rice will take up to 45 minutes; 1-½ cups of Cream of Wheat, up to 37 minutes.
But it's easy to start the rice cooker and let it work while you're preparing the rest of your meal.
The rice cooker comes with a standard rice cup measure (about ¾ cup U.S.), a rice-rinsing/steamer insert, and a nylon spoon.
The cooking pot has an excellent nonstick surface.
The removable pieces are all hand washable in warm, soapy water; handwashing is very easy.
In choosing between this Model 37518 and the Model 37506, I prefer the latter (with a simple, vented glass lid, no condensation cup, longer steaming times, and no ability to set custom cooking times).
Both models are very good, but sometimes simpler is better.

This is my favorite roller pen of all time.
I have tried MUCH more expensive pens and refills - I still hold onto my LAMY's because I love the design - but nothing can touch the G2 0.5mm - the refill AND the pen.
I scrape the logos off with a razor blade.
That's enough to make me feel okay about using this pen.
I used to use fountain pens for everything, but I got back into cycling this year and that shakes up the pen in my pocket like a paint mixer at a hardware store.
So I had to go back to roller pens for when I'm mobile.
I tried really hard to find a "nice" pen but the closest I came was LAMY pens that can be made to take the G2 0.5mm refills.
And I still like the G2 pen better.
I kinda hate the fact that my taste gravitated to the cheapest, most popular thing on the planet, but I have to either be honest and use the best thing for me, or risk becoming a hipster LOL.
I settled on the 0.5mm refill pretty early on.
It writes a great line and has the best feel for me on the paper I use.
I gernally buy just the refills and keep using the same pen, but I lost my last G2 on vacation and figured a 12-pack is probably a lifetime supply for me.
I feel really gross about buying disposable things, but I appeal to the case that I tried everything else before I resorted to this.
I would recommend anyone to visit the local pen store and really try to find an elegant, suitable pen that will last for a lifetime - generations.
If that fails, don't feel too bad about using G2 0.5mm; it really is a great - all time great - pen.

People don't write checks as much as they once did.
But we still have checking accounts and still have transactions, which makes the need for a check register as relevant as ever.
The registers that are included when you order checks are far too few, and that is why a set of registers like these from Easy Read Register are a good idea to have.
With this set, you get ten registers.
There are 26 pages and a total of 416 lines on each, which is enough to last a long time.
The individual pages have the usual headers for date, description, payment, deposit, balance, etc.
One extra on these registers is a column for Fee.
This is not something I have seen on most checkbook registers.
The calendars on the back of each registers shows 2021, 2022, and 2023.
That means, with normal usage, you should have the necessary calendars as you use these registers.
If you have very few checking account transactions, it is possible that 2024 might roll around and you will still be using these registers, and that means you won't have the correct calendar.
With normal usage, you should be fine.
These check registers fit into a standard checkbook.
They are staple bound and made for the basic function for which they are designed.
They are exactly what you expect, and the price is low, which earns this product a high rating from me.

This table is beautiful, sturdy, of a very nice design and quality.
Very well thought-out.
Which is why it is incomprehensible how they overlooked the fact that the book stand simply does not fit in the slot provided.
I have noticed that there is a padded buffer tape running along the inside edge of the slot.
I imagine if I peeled that tape off, the book stand would probably fit.
But then, I would no longer have a proper, safe support for my phone or tablet, when I want to use those...
Somewhat disappointing, especially since everything else about this table is so perfect.
Even the book stand itself is of a fairly nice quality.
The legs of the table are sturdy and well-built.
The supporting slats that go on the bed have tips that turn up, like skis.
This keeps them from getting caught in the bedclothes.
The instructions helped too, because the legs are tightly folded against the underneath of the table and I couldn't figure out how to get them open at first.
I didn't want to force things and possibly break them.
I checked the instructions, which said to just pull hard (use more strength).
So I did.
I love the size, the colors and the materials they used.
The slightly textured, leather-like surface provides a nice grip, so things stay stationary and don't tend to slide around on the table-top when you are moving around or moving the table itself around.
I also really enjoy being able to tilt the table-top.
It has a narrow lip near the bottom, which keeps papers and canvases from sliding off.
Genius!
It also comes with a piece you can insert into the bottom slot, to keep your notebook or laptop from sliding off.
But I find that is not really necessary because the narrow lip that runs from side to side at the bottom does the job anyway.
I do sometimes use the additional piece mentioned to prop my tablet to a more desirable angle when I have it in its protective case.
I like having the little drawer on the underside, in which I can store pens, pencils, notes.

I've been using this motor for just over 3 years now.

The only problems I've had were with timers.

One of them actually started randomly opening at night, letting a skunk in.
We realized this once we went through a couple of weeks with no eggs.
I set up a trail cam, and sure enough, a skunk went in the coop every night, ate the eggs, and exited before the door closed, with one of our ducks chasing it out every night.
It was a game changer once I connected a Meross Outdoor Smart Plug.
I used to have to change the schedule on the digital timer ever couple of weeks or so to open near sunrise and sunset, but now I only do this a few times a year.

 ~

 "… unprecedented…" 
 
 Sirens blare from the TV.
I sit on the floor.
Dazed.

*

 News continues to pour in from the TV.
In the corner of the screen: Monday, 11 September 2001.
\________

 ~

Wu, you have to look at this."

There're enough people freaking out about this!

She has helped me so much in the past seven years.

*This is the end, isn't it?
* 
 
 The thought struck Josh suddenly, almost by accident.
It pierced through and dissolved his frustration with the car that had allowed him to break down so far from home; with the phone company that had neglected to build towers by this barren desert road; with the sun that had audaciously beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground.
*This is the end.
* 
 
 This thought in particular remained prominent in his mind, even as he realized that he had already seen Heather for the last time.
And...
and Joey, who was still so proud about that geometry test.
And Dale, and the business Dale would inherit, the business that would serve as an unexpected legacy.
*This is it.
* 
 
 Dale, who had told him that this trip was a fool's errand, and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral; this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head.
*The end of...
* 
 
 The thought lingered there, static, for a time that Josh wasn't able to comprehend.
Everything else in his mind seemed to fade away, from his periphery, inward toward this single, solitary idea.
*This is the end of me.
* 
 
 When nothing else was left, Josh found it fitting that this idea of finality should itself be his final thought.
But it wasn't.
It vanished as abruptly as it came, and then -- 
 
 Josh would have cried, if he was still physically capable.
His regrets came flooding back all at once.
And his anger, and his sorrow and his despondency at his own powerlessness.
The tranquil peace of the "end" was over, replaced with the angst of a life incomplete.
A life that had failed to come to terms with itself.
And then Josh felt **fear**.
Fear like he had never felt before.
The terror of fate incarnate, of the great unknown for which he was utterly unprepared.
The sheer and total horror overwhelmed his memory, and his pain, and all his other emotions.
That fear was the last thing Josh thought about.

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave.
Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave.
Citizens will not be allowed..." the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn.
I found it hearting.
The ending being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, faster.
All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like brittle dry dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies' back to the earth.
In the distance other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns.
At regular intervals throughout the field Compliance Officers stood, in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation.
It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it.
Everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked.
Then the whispers turned to fully voice complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again.
Soon meat, had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking, vegetables were rare.
When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised.
We were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Straining Test.
Everyone must do their part to bear this burden and our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant.
Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told.
It was clear, yes undoubtable clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders, attempting to destroy our resolve, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution.
They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals.
But we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant.
It was then that they announced the lottery.
That a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation, to help ease the burden of consumption.
Those who were selected were informed the next day by a solider showing up at their door to take them away from their families.
I was one of the chosen.
A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body fertilize the soil to feed our glorious Nation.
Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot punctuated this declaration.
Someone had already finished their grave.
A few other cheered their assent, most were too weary and hungry to manage.
The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied.
They had worked us hard after taking us away, shoveling out a roadway.
We slept where we worked and the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water.
And so the last of the strength of our bodies was harvested.
My grave now looked deep enough.
I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer.
If it was not deep enough for his liking I would have to wait until all others had finished, covering over their graves, before it would be my turn.
He came over and produced a tape measurer.
He checked the dimensions and nodded his assent.
I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave.
The time was here.
The time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation.
The time for my final duty to my beloved land.
"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave." The Moral Office chanted into his bullhorn.
I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer pistol come to rest upon my forehead.
"Citizens will not be allowed..."

"Happily ever afters doesn't exist for people like us," I said solemnly.
Clarissa peered up at me through her tears.
"Why not?" She asked quietly.
I gently wiped her tears away with the pad of my thumb and smiled bitterly.
"Because, the world won't let us.
Every time we try to be happy someone always knocks us down.
Something always will." 
 "What if we run away?" She asked finally looking at me.
I swallowed, trying to hold back tears of my own.
"If we run away then we will always be running.
I don't want that for us.
I don't want that for you," I whispered.
Clarissa held back a sob.
"Will, please don't do this." 
 A tear ran down my face.
"I don't want to." 
 "Then why are you?" 
 "Because I'm no good for you Clarissa.
I get into fights.
I get arrested.
You can find someone better who can make you so much happier.
Who can give you want you want." 
 The words left a sour taste in my mouth but it had to be said.
If we stayed together then there'd always be someone trying to break us apart.
Her parents.
My friends.
My enemies.
I gave her one last kiss.
"Maybe one day in the future, when things aren't complicated, we'll find each other again.
Right now is not our time.
Maybe tomorrow will be."
add_linebreaks.writingprompts::6:
Daniel's wife stood at his side, absolutely coming apart at the edges, not that anyone else but him would be able to tell.
Okay maybe that was a bit of an exaggeration, but she was a touch anxious.
Nervous?
Whatever she was something wasn't quite right, she was doing that little nose twitch that never happens when she's calm.
"Imani," he called out and her head tipped down to where he was seated in acknowledgement "It's going to be fine." She gave him a weak smile that didn't quite reach her eyes before reaching out to squeeze his hand.
Of course he said it to comfort her, but he honestly felt like everything was going to be okay.
They already crossed the worst bits.
He survived the car accident, then he survived the surgery to make sure the universe didn't decide to change its mind later, then later the amputations, the implants.
With a roll of his eyes he squeezed her hand back.
"Honestly, this has been the easy part, we have plenty of time." 
 
 "The easy part?
Since when do we ever get easy!" she reached out to swat his ears, her eyes crinkling with mirth "That's up there with'What could possibly go wrong?
Don't jinx it." she scolded.
He leaned in to tell her all that worrying could do nothing good when the door slammed open, the solid thump echoing through the large room.
"Opps," the tall man in the doorway looked sheepish "I tripped into the door there.
How are you two today?" he inquired friendly, striding into room and the sunlight from the windows poured over his lanky form.
"Ready to give it another go?" Daniel flexed his legs, neat and secured into his new running blades.
"Since the second I put these on Mason!" he replied earnestly and the easy going man gave him a thumbs up before reaching out his hands.
"That's what we like to hear!
Alright lets get you up and moving then." With one last look as his wife, who was standing back with an apprehensive look but held up crossed fingers, he reached for the other man's hands.
These were the fourth pair of running blades he had tried.
The other ones had issues, despite their so called custom fits.
Too long.
Too short.
These hurt.
Those felt like they were going to fall off.
But as Daniel wobbled to his feet he knew these were it.
It took a moment to steady himself.
They had a different sort of balance and give to them than his normal prosthetic, and his fitness wasn't quite where he wanted it be.
His heart raced as he shifted his weight from one foot to the other, hearing the blades flex in response.
Left.
Right.
Left.
Right.
Left right, left right, left right, bounce.
They felt nothing like his old legs.
But all the same...
they felt right.
Slowly Mason let go and then backed away to the other side of the room, his eyes never leaving Daniel's.
When he hit the wall he called out to them.
"Great!
Now start at a walk and work up to as fast as you feel comfortable doing." a sly tone crept into his voice "And remember, the room is padded and we're all friends here.
Face plants are nothing to worry about." Daniel scoffed at the insulation.
As if he'd let these things get the better of him.
Confident, he took a shaky step forward and his arms wheeled around a bit before he braced his core to maintain balance.
Then he took another.
And another, and soon he had a slow bobbing jog going, carefully moving between his wife and physical therapist.
He did this until finally, Mason singled for him to stop.
He sprinted down the room to the happy couple with a look of great excitement.
"It looks like we got it this time!" He stepped back and gave him one final look over "We just need to run a few more tests, make sure that everything is adjusted correctly, but I think we found your golden pair here.
So, how do you feel?" 
 
 His mind began to wander as he turned inward, trying to find the words that could even begin to describe what he was feeling.
All he could think about were the things he thought he had lost forever when he hazily woke up from surgery that faithful day, looking down to see the sheet cave in where his lower legs had once been.
The sound of the crowd screaming his name as he tore down the field.
The heady feeling of sprinting down a track, the world narrowing almost into blackness as he pushed himself to the limit.
The lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped by him with laughter dancing in her eyes.
Bouncing on his new legs once more he felt weightless.
Invincible.
With a strength he hadn't felt in a long time he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with a smile.
"Alive." 
 
 -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 So let it be known I did absolutely no research on the subject for such a quite piece and just went off of memory and educated guessing.
So if anything is terribly wrong, that's why!

"Aye, I remember it like yesterday.
I was wandering through the western mountains, just east of Markarth.
The road snaked below me, carving a long path through the valley." A figure dressed in animal skins caught my eye, creeping slowly towards a carriage that had stopped before crossing the river.
They drew a cruel-looking sword as they approached closer, clearly intent on killing the small group of travellers.
I mounted my horse and started down the slope, yelling at the top of my lungs to get their attention.
"The would-be bandit immediately looked at me with a scowl and let out a yell of his own.
Immediately, a dozen more men and women, dressed in the same ragged fashion, were bearing down on the carriage with weapons drawn.
I knew there were too many for me to handle, but I couldn't bear the thought of letting those poor people die to these brutes.
As I reached the bottom of the incline, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, he's a bit of a nutty one, had given me a magic scroll before I set out on my journey." Let me say now that I'm no mage.
Sure, I tried to find some magics that would make me more handsome, but none of that worked anyway.
I was pretty sure that I merely had to open the scroll and read it, but I had no idea what it actually *did*.
Hopefully it would summon one of those big Atronachs my friend was always talking about.
He made them out to be something near god-like.
Wouldn't mind having one of those on my side.
"Anyway, once I got to the bottom, I jumped off my horse and yanked the scroll from my satchel.
I was shaking so badly, I almost couldn't read it, but I knew I had done it correctly when I started glowing.
That should have been a good sign that something bad was about to happen, but I knew nothing about magic.
Still don't.
The glow was nice though, warm and comforting.
Suddenly, all the bandits were putting their weapons away and asking me what was happening to them.
I had no clue, but I figured they couldn't do any more harm." Unfortunately, they were a little too impressed by me.
They must have thought I was some sort of grand wizard because they immediately propped me on their shoulders and carried me back to their camp for a feast.
I started out thinking they were cannibals or something when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and realized they were really just trying to get by in the world.
Their mead was wonderful, let me tell you.
A little too wonderful, I guess, because I woke the next morning with an, admittedly, attractive woman next to me and a camp full of these people congratulating me with gifts and hugs.
"So, you see, I envy you.
I miss the open fields and chilly mountains, the gold and treasure, and the freedom to go wherever I please.
I used to be young and carefree, I used to be strong and brave.
You remind me a lot of myself, honestly.
I used to be an adventurer like *you*, until I took an arrow to the knee." 
 
 Note: "Taking an arrow to the knee" was apparently a Norse saying about getting married.

"You want to send in Nikon?
You really think it's that bad?" The speaker was a large, barrel chested man, well over six feet tall, with a long, neatly trimmed beard and an impeccable suit.
He was talking to a woman who had to have been in her sixties, the the beauty she displayed as a youth now a well-aged luster.
Her piercing blue eyes looked at the barrel chested man without blinking, staring through him.
"You have a problem, Lord Aerlman.
A very specific type of problem.
We can deal with this very specific problem, but it will require the services of a specialist.
Alex Nikon is that specialist." Her tone was matter-of-fact, not excited or loud in any way.
"She's just a girl, a misguided girl." The older woman shrugged.
"Your girl, Lord Aerlman, has contacted the Outer Planes.
She has let something through, and now it's inside her.
However, until she does something public, I can't involve the Circle without your request.
If you don't want our help, that's fine.
Just remember, tragedy strikes first at the home." Her warning delivered, the woman turned and started to leave the ornate the sitting room.
As she reached the door, Lord Aerlman called to her.
"Laura!
Ms.
Cadswall.
Wait.
Please." She smirked confidently to herself and then composed her face, turning with a neutral expression.
"Yes?" The lord was wringing his hands, pacing in front of the fire.
"Your man, Nikon, I know his reputation.
Will he...
kill her?" Lord Aerlman looked distraught.
"Alexander Nikon will handle the crisis.
That is what he does.
How he handles it will remain at his discretion.
Be advised though, Lord Aerlman, that contact with the Outer Planes taints the very soul.
Even death can't remove its stain." 
 
 Lord Aerlman looked crestfallen, and he idly picked up a picture off the mantle of the fireplace, a family portrait showing the lord and his wife, along with their daughter, a striking redhead in her late teens.
He caressed the picture with his thumb, before setting it back down.
All of the energy drained from him and he sagged, turning towards the woman with a beaten look.
"Fine.
Do it.
Make the call." He dismissed her with a wave and then sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey, which he immediately downed.
As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly.
She had a phone call to make.
-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- - 
 
 "Antonia.
I know you're here." The same girl from the photo, now a fully-grown, and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of pallets, desperately clutching herself and trying not to scream.
Her hands and torso were covered in blood, some hers, and some her friends.
They had been partying, drinking in her London flat, when the man arrived.
The first indication of trouble was the door exploding inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear.
He dropped with a gurgling sound and blood sprayed across the room.
Screams erupted from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even process the danger, a small man, barely 5'6", was in their midst, a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other.
Glowing runes twisted across his skin, and his left eye was in an eyepatch.
His right eye was the color of polished metal, and it quickly scanned the room.
Everything after that was a blur, and Antonia couldn't recall any details, except the bodies, and the blood.
She remembered a voice in her head, then her friends all screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-bearing man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard.
As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and leapt through the bay window, falling the three stories and landing with a sickening crunch.
She remember her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then running.
The voice in her head was louder, and she couldn't understand it, but it was hurting her.
As she ran through the streets, the voice was chanting, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes spewing fire before they turned and charged the way she had come.
She didn't understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her.
She didn't understand anything!
Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood.
As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking.

Janice turned to me, her big blue eyes still full of childish innocence.
Damn - I'd forgotten that she was watching the Presidential Inauguration for a school project.
"Daddy," she began, "what does the President mean?
What's'gay'?" 
 
 "Well, honey..." I began, but trailed off as I tried to think of a way to explain it to a five year old.
"Uh...
Well, you know how Mommy and Daddy like to hold hands, and to cuddle, and kiss, and stuff?" 
 
 "Yeah!
It's funny when Mommy pinches your butt when you're not looking, and makes you squeak!" she giggled.
Kids, man - I'd forgotten what it was like to be so amused by the word "butt".
Had I ever been that small, that innocent?
I waited for her giggles to subside before I carried on.
"Well, sweetheart,'gay' means that he - the President - he likes to do that stuff with a boy, not a girl like Mommy." 
 
 I could see the confusion in her eyes as she struggled to process this new information.
Damn you, McCain, for making me explain this to her!
She's not old enough for this; she's not ready!
*I'M* not ready!
Janice opened her mouth to speak.
I knew what was coming; I'd opened the door to a lifetime of sexual deviancy.
My sweet little girl was gone forever.
Suddenly I realized she'd something, and in my worry, I'd completely missed it.
"Sorry, sweetheart - what did you say?" I asked, fearing her response.
What fresh hell have I unlocked?
"I said, I'm hungry.
Can I have a cookie?
Please, Daddy?" 
 
 I was stunned, unable to respond at first.
"Uhm.
Sure," I answered.
"Get one for your brother, too." 
 
 Huh.
I guess that maybe what two consenting adults do behind closed doors isn't that big of a deal after all.
Even when they *are* public figures.
add_linebreaks.writingprompts::16:
"Why, hello, Ma'am," I said easily, standing up and offering her a chair with my usual grace.
"Bertram Proudfoot at your service.
Whom do I have the pleasure of addressing?" 
 
 "I'd rather not say, if it's all the same to you," she said, sitting down.
"Alright," I said comfortably.
"What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you?" 
 
 "Well," said the dame, rubbing her hands together nervously.
"It's like this." She paused.
"Like what, Ma'am?" I said kindly, lighting my pipe and sitting back in my chair.
"My husband is dead," she said.
"Oh my dear, I am sorry!" I exclaimed, though I must admit there was part of me that was less than sorry.
What can I say?
I am only a Hobbit, and this dame had the most beautiful feet I had ever laid eyes on.
"Tell me everything that happened." 
 
 "We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago," she said.
"And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head.
He keeled over in the water.
I screamed for help, but he drowned." 
 
 Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door.
I have an uncanny sense for things like that.
I looked as grave as I could, given the circumstances.
"I see," I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling.
"And you would like me to find and prosecute the perpetrator of this event." 
 
 "Yes," said the dame.
"I will do my best, I can promise you that," I said, and I saw her visibly sight with relief.
"May I offer you a cup of tea?
Something stronger, perhaps?" 
 
 "No thank you," she said, and without another word she showed herself out.
I promptly made my way to the Brandywine River dock.
My first line of inquiry would be to interrogate the man who rented out boats.
An odd fellow, and an odd profession -- not many sane hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will.
And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well.
After a long consultation of his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those was by a couple.
The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck.
Primula, that was the dame's name.
But why had she not wanted to tell it to me?
Had this boat fellow heard any commotion on the water, any cries for help?
No he had not.
Did he remember who returned the boat to him?
It hadn't, he said.
In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river.
Strange 
 
 Next I walked up and down the both banks of the river.
Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot.
Having thoroughly investigate the river, my next step was to find out about Priscilla and Drogo.
After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily.
They had one son, now 12, name Frodo Baggins.
Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death.
In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo *and* Primula had died three nights ago.
Facts were not adding up.
Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out.
Though I had no way of contacting her, I knew she would return to my offices in short order.
The day following, she did just that.
"Good day, Primula," I said upon her entrance.
Her face betrayed surprise, but she did not deny the name.
"I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case," I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered.
"So I'm afraid I must ask again," I finished.
"What happened that night?" 
 
 And without a word, the dame got up and left.
Just like that.
I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine.
I was saddened but not surprised.
My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever.
Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not suspect any foul play.
However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin, none other than the famous crackpot Bilbo Baggins.
Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son.
But I, having seen through her ruse, prevented this fact.
Seeing no alternative she then drowned herself in grief.
Shame -- I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial alternative for the both of us.
I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully.
It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another opportunity lost.
I had solved countless cases, but opportunities of the other sort came only but now and again.
Like I said, it was a shame.
I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr.
Baggins.
I felt for the young Mr.
Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody.
Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow.
As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr.
Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tails.
Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left, whatever he experienced on his journey seemed to have addled his mind.
He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better.
He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather an impersonator.
There is plenty of evidence to suggest this: particularly the fact that "Mr.
Baggins" appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look.
I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day.

It never changed, the dark marbled walls carving into arched passageways to hell knows where.
Within this cavernous chamber he and God would argue every several thousand years.
God emerged from the shadows of one of several entrances, a scowl on his face.
"Oh, it's you," he sputtered.
Lucifer regarded him coolly.
"Did I ever give you a libido, Lucy?
I can't remember." 
 
 "No," Lucifer answered.
"Aw, why not?
Feel like fucking?
I'm kinda horny."

Don't mention my son to me right now!

Lucifer pressed his eyes shut.
"I came here to talk to you about something," he said.

 "Aw, why not?" 
 
 "I didn't do anything wrong!

Autonomy!

I helped you make one of your greatest creations!
I did it because I knew you needed it!

 "So please," Lucifer said, collapsing on one of the staid marble thrones, "Let me come back to you.

 "*You* created the dichotomy.

here, have some soda." 
 
 "I don't - I don't want any fucking soda.

 God giggled, "Don't say my name in vain, Luce." 
 
 Lucifer furrowed his brow, God knew he was holding back tears, "I don't understand you." 
 
 "Of course you fucking don't!
I am outside *space* and *time*!
I exist in dimensions you have no fucking comprehension of!
I am all things at once!
How could you possibly understand me?" God bellowed.
"I...
don't know.

 God scoffed, "A *part* of me, Luce.

 A pause.
Lucifer stared at his hands.
"Why did you create us then?" 
 
 "To forget, and then remember." 
 
 "I don't understand." 
 
 "I know," he said softly.

add_linebreaks.writingprompts::19:
* [ PI ] * 
 
 The Shine could have been salvation for humanity.
Should have been, but we were never very good at evading conflict.
Who knows how long ago it was, but in an age of wireless devices and ubiquitous information we lifted our gaze from our screens only to see the sky ignite, consumed by a cold, variegated blaze.
It lasted only a few hours, but took only a few minutes for the world to see.
It didn't take much longer for people to want a closer look, to crave a caress of the gentle flame.
And then they flew.
They flew so far and so fast, and swiftly they were joined by others; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them.
It didn't take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying wasn't the only *option* available to us.
Before the Shine had faded many such options came and went; flight, strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, speed, and all the other common options appeared and disappeared very quickly.
At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it swiftly became apparent that the potency of powers was inversely proportional to the number who selected that *option*.
That's when the more obscure powers started cropping up; at first it was just salarymen who decided they wanted to shit gold, or kids who decided they wanted to control animals, but before a quarter day had passed things started getting weird.
Rapid drops in temperature, the ground shook frequently, clocks would stutter and people died.
Many people died.
In half a day, an eight-billion-strong global society of the most intelligent and durable species on Earth collapsed and halved in number; we dissolved into groups and factions just looking to survive, to weather the storm; those *without* powers were kings, and those with obscure powers that couldn't be worked out or copied were gods in flesh, right there to worship when many needed them most.
A few days passed before things started to settle - though in that time the sun only passed once.
Weather was beyond erratic and cities were nigh-on deserted, only habitable for larger and more powerful factions.
We went from pursuing prosperity to living rough in a day, if you could call it that.
We reverted to beasts, except slightly more intelligent, and sometimes super-powered.
Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has created many new settlements; but the most popular options are still weak, so death is power, and raids are frequent and unrelenting.
The largest settlements are the most powerful, but also the primary target for smaller cliques.
Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left travel.
And that is what I have done.
I have travelled, and searched for a way to absolve this madness, and perhaps restore the world to the relative sanity it once had.
And I may well just have found it.

I stood at an intersection, looking towards the capitol building.
I stared at this girl on fire.
She sat calmly.
Not moving a muscle, not making a sound.
People stood and stared.
There were other black marks on the stairs she sat on.
"Mommy, why is she on fire?" 
 
 "Oh, that's normal," my mother replied.
"So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames?" My six year old mind was confused.
"No son, that is not the normal part.
We are in a war.
People don't like the way the government controls things, so they protest by burning themselves." 
 
 "Will she be okay?" My naive mind wanted her to be.
No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that.
"I don't know," came the haunting response.
Year later, after the civil war was lost, I would read about all the people who immolated for their country.
My country.
Through college, I would think of these people.
The people with beliefs so strong they would literally kill themselves in such a way to make a powerful statement.
They would not want to live in a country under the crushing regime that had been ruling for generations.
They wanted to be free, or they wanted to die.
It seems every generation, there is an uprising.
The oppressed realize that they're being oppressed, and they get a tool to help them organize and fight back.
They gain leverage.
Rarely does it happen in a short span.
However, here I was, an oppressed 27 year old with absolutely no future.
I stood at that intersection that I stood at 21 years ago.
The black marks were gone, but so was my naivety.
This government had to go.
They had oppressed my mother's generation.
They had oppressed the generation before them, and the generation after them.
They weren't going to stop unless forced to.
I calmly walked up to the steps and prepared to make the newest black mark, start the next revolution.
As the flames rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look as I burned.
The pain was almost unbearable, but I managed to see through the pain.
The last thing I saw before the world faded was a young girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been 21 years before.

I walked downstairs and opened up the digital screen.
A banker popped up on the screen.
"Hello Mrs.
Roer.
How may I help you?" 
 
 "I'd like to check my bank statement.
I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits?" 
 
 "Okay, one moment." The banker disappeared for a second and then came back up.
"Mrs.
Roer.
You currently have 10 credits." 
 
 "What?
That's not even enough to buy groceries with this month?" 
 
 I looked outside and then sighed.
"Okay.
Well thanks." I said.
The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day.
How could I only have 10 credits of happiness?
A gallon of milk is *1.21* credits.
I couldn't even buy milk.
I walked outside this time.
It was sunny and bright, birds were happy, I bet they have enough happiness credits to buy freaking groceries.
I looked around.
My in-ground pool, my hot-tub, my outdoor deck complete with a pond further from the house.
All of this was my life.
My husband and I had been married for ten years now.
I was happy, he was happy.
Right?
I went to look at my phone, I had a message from my husband.
'Want to have coffee?' 
 I sent back,'Yes.' 
 
 I went upstairs and took a shower.
My husband was gone, as always.
It was no secret we had been falling apart.
We were so happy at one point though that we had more credits than anybody in the word.
Like I said though, it was no secret that we had been falling apart.
He had numerous affairs and I frankly, although I never cheated, found myself longing for more.
I prepared myself for coffee.
Nothing too dressy or too casual.
It was just coffee.
I walked outside, got in one of our cars and drove to the airport.
We owned a private jet, my husband had already put gas in it.
"Just having coffee today Bill," I said.
I was walking off the jet in 4 hours to see my husband.
"Hello Mrs.
Roer," He said, kissing my cheek, as he always did.
I walked with him to our second home.
A blonde woman with a tight blouse was leaving the house.
I scowled at her, and she hurried from the front door to her car.
"We need to talk," I said.
"Exactly," He replied, seemingly pleased at my displeasure.
"Listen, Mr.
Roer, I do love you, but there's so --." 
 
 "Elaine, I want a divorce." 
 
 "That was quick." I said.
He shrugged it off.
I left quickly after that.
No coffee for me.
It wasn't long before I got home.
I had a message from the bank again.
My happiness points had hit zero.
A message from an old friend surprised me.
"Coffee?" It read.
"Sure." I answered.
At that moment my doorbell rang.
I answered the door to him.
My old friend.
He immediately kissed me.
I had missed that feeling.
I felt my blood pressure rise.
"Good to see you." 
 
 "Listen Luke, I just-" 
 
 He kissed me again and broke my words.
"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine.
He's wanted a divorce and he's not good to you.
You know that." 
 
 I was shocked.
He payed my husband to marry me?
Why on Earth would he..
"Elaine.
I know we didn't work out, but our son.
He needs you." 
 
 I felt a tear hit my chest.
I had given Luke, and our son up to be with my husband.
My husband refused to let me have a son in the house that was not his.
"Elaine.
Marry me.
Please?" He said.
He walked inside towards me further.
"Our sons in the car.
He's 12 now," Luke said.
I had gotten to see our son, Reig, until he was four.
Then I had to cut off communications to my husband being afraid it would make us look bad on the press.
I walked outside and my son ran from the car.
He wrapped his arms around me.
I felt my phone alert again and I checked it.
In case it was my husband with an explanation for why he'd'sold' my hand.
It was bank.
My account had just been credited 20,000 happiness credits.
"Yes.
I'll marry you."

and we dare not speak it's name.

 "Prisoner 778125-Sigma-8, you stand before this tribunal today accused of crimes against galactic civilization, murder, four counts of xenocide, 70 counts of attempted xenocide, planetary dehabitation, planetary destruction, and attempting to overthrow the Pan-Galactic Alliance.
How do you plead?" 
 
 The man before Councilwoman Asaarha met the gaze of her and her fellow Arbiters with cold blue eyes.
Despite the 140 cycles of temporal isolation he had endured before his trial, Sacha Markes stood tall and unbroken.
He radiated power and command, even now, stripped of his rank, fleet, and army.
The last of the humans was a testament to the species.
The silence before he spoke seemed louder to the Councilwoman than the crashing waves of her ocean home.
The time it took for the human to speak seemed longer than the span of the galaxy.
"Guilty," he said with a simple finality.
The Arbiters nodded their heads solemnly.
None of them had expected this one to plea for mercy.
Asaarha keyed the sentence into the terminal before her.
The other six Arbiters did the same.
The blue lights of Markes's uniform and restraints changed to red.
The screen on the psionic inhibitor around his head changed to read GUILTY in Galactic Standard.
Though the trial room was empty save for the Tribunal and Markes, Asaarha could hear the roars of vengeance that were surely reverberating throughout the galaxies.
Each trial of the humans had been broadcast in its entirety.
Each had ended in a guilty verdict.
"Sacha Markes, formal Admiral of the Seventh Human Expeditionary Fleet, High Captain of the Royal Guard, Commander-in-Chief of the Human Expeditionary Force, and Primarch of the Solar Empire, you are sentenced to Psionic Stripping and Execution by black hole.
Do you have any last words before the sentence is carried out?" 
 
 The human threw his head back defiantly and turned his gaze on the camera nearest him.
Addressing the billions of life forms throughout the galaxy, he began the last soliloquy of the human race.
"We brought you up out of the mud we found you in.
We gave you art, culture, and science.
Our golden fleets created a civilization that will never be matched; not for 100,000 turns of the galaxy.
We are responsible for all that you are.
I remember when the first of our race died after 100 centuries of immortality; killed trying to cure the sick of one of your backwater planets.
I remember when we decided to take our retribution on our children; to punish you for your ignorance.
We burned that world.
I watched our plasma cannons turn its surface to glass and its oceans to ash.
One world for one human life.
A fair trade.
But you did not accept our judgment.
Like Icarus chasing the sun, you rose up against us.
Did you expect us to just let you?
Did you think we would not defend ourselves?
I was the commander of the fleet that met yours on the first day of battle.
My ten cruisers against the most powerful battleships of three galaxies and a hundred races.
Now, a hundred years later, you have finally defeated us.
You have lost entire solar systems to us.
You have sacrificed googles of lives and thousands of civilizations to bleed your gods dry and bind them in chains.
Your worlds are shattered.
Your cities gone; wiped from history in an instant.
Can you truly call that victory?
I am the last of my kind.
I am Sacha Markes.
Look upon my face, ye mighty, and despair.
For when you kill me, you kill the last light left in this existence."

Entry:48 
 
 We finally reached the rim of the first bolgia today and heaven preserve me the scout reports weren't lieing, it's more vast than anything i could imagine.
The recon photos we were given to prepare us are like a blind man trying to describe a sunrise, and by God the smell has actually somehow gotten Worse!
Seeing the pit first hand i think the enormity of our task has finally hit home for some of the crew, they look rattled, i don't blame them, have we bitten off more than we can chew?
I'm not sure but i have faith in our mission and our commanders.
The vastness of the pit really can't be put into words but for the sake of this journal i'll try.
The rim extends further than the human eye should be able to see and yet i can make out tiny details on the far cliff face, it looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a bourbon glass, even while sitting in the cab of the rumbler i get vertigo looking down onto the levels below, if it wasn't for the special anti-psychotics the docs give us i'm sure what i see on the lower levels might have some lasting horrific effect on me.
The crew and i wash down todays dose with a bottle of sacramental wine, and why not, today was a good day after all.
Today we reached the edge of Limbo.
Entry:49 
 
 Not much to record today, some minor skirmishes on the perimeter, just some low level demons takeing a swipe at us otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff.
The engineers are working double time to ensure the security of Limbo Base, they say it'll be fully up in 2 days, i have my doubts.
After their fiasco at the river they've got a lot of face to save, 2 Rumblers, 4 squads of troops and a Screacher lost because of their damn barges.
Bastards.
I Hate just sitting around like this with nothing to distract me from the smell of rot and sulphur that somehow filters into the rumblers cab despite the tech geeks assurances that the cab is perfectly hermetically sealed, it feels like the smell is inside my skull rotting tiny holes in my brain.
Entry:51 
 
 HOOAH!
CONTACT BABY!
Praise God i've been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface.
Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy opponents AND WE KICKED THEIR MUTHA FUCKING TEETH IN!!
HAHAHAHAHAHA.
They came a few hours after my last entry like a great black tornado.
A swirling column of harpies, skrieks and imps beyond counting rising up from the center of The Pit and came crashing down completley enveloping Limbo Base.
The first few moments of engagment should've been chaos but by the grace of God we were ready.
All the Screachers had been on high alert since we emerged from the maze of caves and onto the plains of Limbo proper 8 days ago and today that diligence paid off.
The blitz of the winged demon assault crumbled before the wall of sound our blessed Screachers blasted out.
The word of God is anathema to the denizens of Hell, the word of God pumped out through a mobile rig of high powered speakers piloted by a devout member of the clergy is down right debilitating.
The shocked and paralysed Demons that twitched and writhed on the ground were easy targets, the rumblers blessed water cannons burning away swaths of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid, huge piles of the creatures were reduced to ash in seconds.
The larger Demon haridens proved more resilient and i saw more than a few grunts die on their talons, their sanctified body armor little better than cardboard.
We repaid them in kind and i'm proud to say our rumblers javalin cannons sent a good lot of the giant buzzards screaming into oblivion impailed on our gleaming silver spears.
I should record so it doesn't seem like i'm diminishing the grunts efforts, their bravery and ferocity in battle too, for they've got that in spades, despite the mortal danger they collected their fair share of scalps, pinning the giant creatures with their silver pikes and finishing them off with their chain sickles.
it was a glorious bloody sight, like something out of a nature documentry.
The greatest trial of the battle was yet to come though.
After a full day and a half of fighting the black swarm began to thin out and we thought we might've finally broken their assault, but then they appeared.
Three monsterous figures coming into focus through the haze of ash and exhaustion.
Hell Dragons, nothing like what we'd seen in movies or our stories from childhood, these were great pestilent, foul things that towered over us.
Snub nosed heads the size of a grand cathedral covered in spines, long armored bodies like an insects, their faces and joints slick with thick black tar that bubbled and hissed as it fell from them and stained the plains of Limbo.
Screachers focused their assault and prevented the titans from over running the base, the rumblers water tanks and javlin cannons ran dry just trying to keep them at bay, our brave grunts held back the black swarm, fighting tirelessly which allowed us time to retreat, resupply and reenter the fray.
And so it went for hours on end and for all our efforts the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse.
Salvation finally came at the hands of the engineering corps.
Of all people!
Through our efforts we had given them enough time to secure and assemble Limbo Bases major defenses, Sanctified Artilery and the Holy Rail Gun.
The Rail Gun punctured the Dragons thick armor spewing gysers of tar onto the battlefield while the artilery smashed into the beasts vulnerable exposed points lodgeing shells etched with scripture deep in their bodies wracking them with pain.
The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force but after nearly 2 months since we first decsended into this place we finally have established a forward base to launch our attack on Hell.
One Bolgia down eight to go.
This is the first day here that the smell doesn't bother me.

While I can not at this time suppose a motive for the prince of lies to so suddenly mobilize the legions of the damned, I can, however, speak to its utter strangeness, and the devastation left in its wake.
In hindsight, a company named Apollyon ought to have aroused some suspicion; alas, as few knew greek, and the meaning of Apollyon, ( a medieval greek translation for'destroyer' attributed to Satan ) a banking leviathan hiding behind less conspicuous shell corporations aroused no suspicion.
While most of us were preoccupied with the myopic affairs of day to day life, Mr.
Morning-Star stretched his hands to slowly throttle the cliche servants of the Lord of darkness: those being politicians, bankers, criminals, and any other disciplines traditionally associated with wickedness.
Ironically, many who had been accused consorting with the devil only now found themselves under his corrupting influence.
So, long story short the devil became a business tycoon, and it was the allure of cheap, mass produced goods he invaded with.

The planet Earth has changed a lot recently, 23 years ago- almost to the day, the storms on the surface ended.
The same storms that had been raging for roughly five thousand years, a few weeks passed whilst the cloud formations disintegrated, and then we got our first clear view of our home.
I was five years old at the time and entertained mostly by the colours, the beautiful blue and green were like nothing on the Ark.
We had water- sure, but not pools large enough to give that blue colour.
We had plants too, but the conditions were far from optimal and made the plants a dirty green rather than lush.
I wanted to see it closer- touch it- feel it.
That was probably when I decided to join the recruitment for the first journey.
The first journey was- as the name implies, the first expedition back down to the planet.
A lot of people wanted to go back down as soon as the storms ended, there were protests- riots even.
People wanted the Ark to head straight back down- Idiots.
23 years may have been a long time to wait, but it was important...
We were the last humans after all- if we landed and something went wrong?
We couldn't risk it.
Years of geological scans, and low atmosphere scouting gave us the perfect landing spot.
Minimal damage to local Environment, enough space to develop a community, plenty of food- water- and importantly a lot of natural protection taking the form of Cataclysm-formed mountain ranges, and deep trenches filled with the darkest blue water.
Of course something as large as the Ark couldn't simply just land though...
No- that was where the first journey came into the picture.
We were the first guys to go planetside- and live permenantly in over seven generations.
Our objective was to build the dock, it'd be a long job- probably another five or six years even, but the dock would provide us with amuch needed start- as well as mapping out local geography much more clearly, learning about plants, animals.
The reality of the situation is that we were going in blind- this "safe-zone" as the Corps had nicknamed it could very easily become a deathtrap.
The problem with the safezone was that because of it's location once we went in, our shuttle wouldn't be able to make it out.
Part of the problem with the planet was the storms- even now 23 years after the main storm ended smaller cells continued to rotate...
The mountain ranges protected the area from the storms still raging- not quite powerful enough to make it over the high peaks though.
Even in the atmosphere above there was a vicious wind that constantly blew...
It would tear a outgoing ship to pieces, only a craft as large as the Ark would be able to survive it- and the Ark needed a Dock in order to preform a take off.
So that was the mission, go down, face possible death, build a super structure, all in less than six years- and I was damn excited.

"Hey, check out that chickadees over in the birdbath." Kylo whooped and puffed out his chest, nearly toppling off his perch.
"Don't be a troglodyte, bro," Atticus groused, pecking at his seeds, "You're a wren.
That isn't even the same family." 
 
 "I don't care.
I'm gon na go talk to them." Kylo took off, swerving through the air like a leaf trapped in a gust.
Atticus sighed and took off after him.
He'd have to keep close tabs on Kylo or else they'd get kicked out again.
Kylo crashed into the water with a mighty splash.
Droplets flew in every direction, drenching the occupants of the birdbath.
They squawked with indignation as Kylo emerged from beneath the surface, shaking the wetness from his head.
He trotted up to a group of soaked finches and gave his wings a shake.
"Hey, birds.
Nice tits." 
 
 "We're not tits." A purple finch stepped forward from the group, and she launched into a tirade on how overused that pickup line was.
Atticus alighted on the rim of the bath and began to walk around, apologizing to everyone for Kylo's behavior and pleading with them not to call the bouncer over.
"Okay, sorry," Kylo interrupted, "let me make it up to you: how about you and I head over there—" He motioned to the bird feeder.
"—and I share my seeds with you?" If birds had lips, Kylo would be smirking right now.
The finches began to flap their wings angrily, splashing Kylo with water.
"You're such a boor.
Get out of here!" Many of the onlookers chirped in agreement, and some of the bigger birds began to puff their chests threateningly.
Atticus shoved Kylo to the side and raised his wings.
"On behalf of my friend here, I apologize.
He's clearly had too much nectar; we'll just be going now..." 
 
 "Oh, you think we're going to fall for that?" The purple finch spat a nut shell at his feet.
"He's just trying to play wingbird for you, isn't he?
Let him take the fall for you, and swoop in to look better by comparison." The other birds chorused in agreement.
"I think these two need to be taught a lesson." A blue jay fluttered over to Atticus, towering a full inch above him.
He spread his wings menacingly, blocking Atticus from taking off.
"Why don't you peck on someone your own size?" The onlookers broke into cheers, shouting for a fight.
"Well, you're kind of bigger than me." Atticus took a step back into the bath.
He felt feathers ruffle against him as the crowd pressed around him, urged him back towards the jay.
"That wouldn't be my own size now, would it?" 
 
 Kylo staggered in front of him and began to hop around.
"Don't worry, Atticus; we got this." 
 
 "Hey, this is a one-on-one fight." The jay looked around.
"If you get back-up, then—" 
 
 "Who on earth placed all this here?" A door opened, and the birds began to scatter, screaming, "Human!" Atticus grabbed Kylo and urged him into the air, and the two lost themselves amongst the cloud of fleeing birds.
Out of the corner of his eye, he saw the human scratching his head in front of the birdbath.
"Make sure to thank that human for bailing you out of yet another mess," Atticus said.
Kylo scoffed.
"We could've totally taken that guy." As the two flew over the Toyota in the driveway, he let loose a dropping that landed right in the center of the windshield.
