i knew i wouldn't be able to see immediately. i knew it would take a lot of work, and i was even warned that i might feel overwhelmed. i had vague memories of what sight was like. i had been injured in a car accident that had left me blind in both eyes at the age of three. i do think it helped, though; being able to process light and color for three years before going blind may have made it a bit easier for my brain to remember rather than to learn anew. 
 
 james helped me a lot. sometimes i would close my eyes to get around like i had before. he would suddenly get in front of me and block my way, teasing me. it wasn't mean; if i protested, he'd raise his arms out and impede my movement until he closed them around me, hugging me tight. 
 "i won't let go until you open your eyes," he'd say. no one had ever loved me this much. i could hear it in his voice and feel it every time he hugged me. 
 
 i practiced often. sometimes i'd get headaches from trying to look at everything. blotches of dark smeared across the table as i tried to eat breakfast. james told me it was the shadows from the tree outside. that tree had never bothered me before. now it was interrupting my breakfast, trying to make it even harder to simply eat a bowl of cereal. i still felt around to make sure i could trust what i was seeing. i can't tell you how strange it was to see my own hands before me, two misshapen blurs fumbling with everything i tried to touch. i used to love my hands. 
 
 after a while, the dark smears became shadows, and james's face became clear to me. i think that was the happiest moment in my life. i woke up one morning and he turned over, and i could see his eyes. they shone bright, as if they themselves held light inside them. he was beautiful. i never knew how beautiful he really was. 
 
 the blotches no longer confused his face and i was able to see him clearly. my problems began when i noticed that my own face wasn't clearing. the nasty blotches on my own face weren't tricks of the light. i had a slew of acne scars around my jawline. my skin felt smooth to me, but i didn't know the dark marks were there. i had a few wrinkles, which i had known about, but the sickly green circles under my eyes contrasted poorly with my dark irises. my eyes didn't shine like james's eyes. my eyes looked dead and sad. 
 
 i didn't want to ask james about it. i never knew i was so ugly. even if i was ugly, i assumed james must be just as ugly. why would a handsome man choose an ugly, blind girlfriend? i could finally see how women stared at him. nobody ever looked at me that way. a trip to the grocery store used to be a fun time for both of us. now, it was another opportunity to see every other bitch- who he could easily have if he wanted- stealing furtive glances at him, or smiling if he looked in their direction. 
 
 i have no idea what to think. sometimes i think he smiles back at them. i caught him looking at two women walking by us at a restaurant. my stomach was in knots. i didn't say anything. i just stared down at my pasta and tried not to lose my appetite. 
 "is something wrong?" james asked. 
 "no, why?" i said, forcing my pockmarked face into an expression of amusement. 
 "just asking," he said. "i love you," he said, with a smile. 
 
 i wish i could believe it.
lowercase.writingprompts::48:
*** 
 the author 
 *** 
 
 i can't shake the feeling. you know, that sensation creeping along your spine waiting to take up residence in the base of your skull like some kind of parasite. it's an indeterminable feeling you're being watched. i can't shake it off. i am sure i know what it is, but i'm not ready to admit i know. the... *author* let's call him. he is watching, waiting, building. even as i think this, he is scratching it down in his chicken-scratch scrawl, touching the pen against his teeth in thought. i can feel it; i can see it in my mind's eye. he's trying to figure out how to kill me. 
 
 i suppose it is my own fault. see i kept asking, i needed to understand. i had to find out if there was some directing hand to life. if mankind had a purpose, a reason, i needed to appreciate what purpose we worked toward. there's a moment, one of particular realization, which caught me and held fast. like my apprehension regarding an observer; only, this feeling was deeper, more primal. i *knew*, i mean really *understood*; all of it is a narrative. life is a story. which inevitably led me to the conclusion -- there needs to be an architect, an *author*. 
 
 the car narrowly missed me. i had an inkling of a pressing against my chest verging on the edge of panic. i didn't cross when the green man displayed on the crossing signal, instead i took a step back. my *spidey-sense* tingled. the taxi-cab driver never saw me, i hadn't seen him either. his drunken sprawling vehicle slammed into the same traffic signal post i had been, until recently, standing by. can i tell you how fucked up that is, i have this realization, followed by a sudden sensation of fear. if i hadn't heeded my gutless compulsion, i might have been splattered between the cabbie's car and the hard place which was the traffic signal pole. i turned my gaze upward, burning eyes and clenching jaw notwithstanding, and decried whoever worked at compiling this narrative. 
 
 "what the actual fuck was that?" i said. 
 
 okay, so i realize my choice of words probably did not fall into the definition of circumspect, but hell we're talking about some kind of god-figure deciding on my time to die. 
 
 *are you sure? * my logical brain asked. 
 
 i pondered my position, both in the physical and meta-physical sense. 
 
 *yeah, i'm fucking sure, * i replied to myself internally. *how else do you explain the sudden epiphany and subsequently my almost immediate death. there's an* author *and he doesn't want to be known. * 
 
 i'm not sure how i knew the *author* didn't want to be known, or the face he was a man, but i figured it was something in my general make-up granting me the knowledge. oh don't get all high and mighty and preach at me now, i'm not talking religion or spirituality, i want to live damnit. i stood, still staring up at the sky, trying to impart my utter disgust and frustration when the signal pole creaked, unnaturally so. i adjusted my head so my eyes were level with the pole. 
 
 the metal appeared warped, and i realized that the car had burst into flames. 
 
 *when had that happened? * i thought. *nevermind, run stupid. * 
 
 my internal dialog is not always the most kind; i'm a blunt sort. so, i ran. what i was running from, if mr. omniscient *author* was already in my head, he could follow me anywhere. hell, i could have an inopportune flashback, and he could hit me with a mack truck. if this *author* decided i was going to die, why didn't he do it already? 
 
 *fuck me, * i thought. *it's about the drama; the story. * 
 
 "sick fuck," i said. i knew he'd hear me, or he'd write that in his juvenile scrawl, knowing i intended it for him. 
 
 *what if i stop? * 
 
 i looked up again, and said, "what are you going to do with a character who won't cooperate, huh?" 
 
 naturally, he didn't respond. it wasn't like i expected a voice from the sky, but i figured he might strike me down with lightning or something, i mean he potentially it's within his ability, right? he might decide my knowledge of the plan labeled me as a liability. 
 
 *what the hell is the plan anyway? * 
 
 i don't know, i guess the plan is for me to die. perhaps, he's not into the mundane. maybe, just maybe, he wants my death to be something significant, something of a show. i bet that's it. i got the sense again; a gut punch to my stomach making my insides roil like they were leaking to the outside, and the rumbling in my stomach suggested i take a step back. i did. something pierced the skin in my back. it was a fluid, smooth motion that parted the skin. i felt the warm blood mixing with my sweat as it soaked the back of my flannel shirt. 
 
 a quiet voice whispered in my ear. "hello protagonist," she said. "i'm your antagonist, the *author* says hello." 
 
 that was all she said. she didn't have a scent, like you would expect. she was a ghost from the shadows. i don't know who she was, or why her, but she'd made it clear... i was right. take that fucker. i didn't have the strength to say it, but i know he heard me. 
 *** 
 subscribe to /r/djmauthor for more stories

 page of a journal of a chef - recently deceased. 
 
 
 
 as a chef, i wholly agree with the foie gras but i have never had much of an ear for trumpets. foie gras for those who don't know ( and do not worry, many don't ) is a dish as old as the art of cooking. foie gras, french for *fat liver* is the 
 pièce de résistance of any self respecting chef. take a duck, better a goose, but more often a duck. cage it, give it no room, movement will ruin the texture. take it by the neck and pump corn boiled in fat down its gullet. do this seven times a day, pump it plump. kill the bird, remove the liver and a good chef would pay a wholesome price for it. with mustard, with honey, with diced onions and balsamic vinegar. never has anything been so delectable. 
 see, it is not the taste that repulses people, it is the process. "does the end justify the means?" is a question often asked. no, if you are talentless, if you lack a palette. yes, yes! believe me anyone would scream "yes!" if they tried my foie gras. but then again, mine is different, mine is better. 
 
 see, they say that beauty is skin deep. it is, and taste is far shallower. i am a chef. a good chef, not a good man but i reiterate: a good chef. if i had been born a painter and my only source of red was the blood of the innocent, do not doubt that i would paint in red. of-course i wasn't born a painter, i was born a chef. a good chef. foie gras, as most chefs make it, is illegal in many countries: the uk, germany, and italy to name a few. needless to say that i do not get my recipes from law books. foie gras as i make it, is illegal in every country. the pope once denounced foie gras as cruel, that was of-course before he tried mine. mine is different, mine is better. 
 
 a cardinal said to me that if god again came to earth, he would make sure i cooked. another said that "i once denounced your dish chef. i am sorry chef. i owe you a thousand apologies chef. i have now sampled your dish chef, and i now know that the bliss from the supple marinated flesh on my tongue is greater than all the sufferance of all the geese and ducks that god has ever endeavored to make." they were in awe of me. anyone who i convince to suspend their morals, will at moment of contact with my foie gras, be in awe of me. mine is different, mine is better. 
 
 people would kill for a spoonful, good people, pious people, moral people… they would kill for a spoonful of my foie grois. believe me, i would sell out if i charged a million per lb. but i don't. i don't do it for power or riches, i do it for the art. i am a chef, a good chef, not a good man but i reiterate: a good chef. my recipe is worth kingdoms, my dish has made kings weak at the knees. so weak that they kneel before me, the chef. 
 
 my legacy will be my recipe. if you are reading this, congratulations you have inherited it. here it is: 
 
 take a baby, abduct it, buy it, steal it, it makes no difference. any foundling or orphan will do. boy or girl, it makes no difference. black, white, arab, asian, it makes no difference. though they must be newborn! they must be innocent, they must be succulent. 
 
 cage it, give it no room, movement will ruin the texture. take it by the neck and pump corn boiled in fat down its gullet. do this seven times a day, pump it plump. two months should suffice. add a pinch of salt and an oz of butter per pint of corn. two pints of fat, per pint of corn. lard is best, the more linoleic acid the better. when slaughtered, take the liver and prepare it in the way you are most qualified. i would marinate in honey and mustard seed. cooked sesame seeds, diced red onions and a thimble full of rum.

 "so how did you get assigned to this one, elwood?" shara said while examining her claws.

"little wretches..."

 if i don't return. dan. love always.

a small lamp burned steadily on the polished desk. the human wore a pair of thin spectacles on the edge of his nose. stacks of parchment occupied a far corner of the work surface. he read through pages at a time, scribbling notes on another sheet. empty ink bottles on the floor suggested the man was rather busy. 
 
 from the entrance, ronn readied his flail, letting the heavy chains dangle, their echoes filling the room. but the man refused to look up at the intruders. instead, he held up a finger and continued reading. ronn and the rest of his group exchanged glances and shrugged shoulders. for a moment, they stood still. with a disappointed smack of the tongue, the man replaced the parchment, pushed his glasses closer to his eyes, called for his guests to approach. they did. 
 
 "apologies, my friends," he said. his voice cracked slightly as though it had gone unpracticed for some time. "come. come." 
 
 the adventurers stepped forward slowly. wilm's head darted around as he scouted for suspicious stones in the floor or another tripwire. the cobbles turned to green when the tasseled edge of the rug stood before them. the group stopped. 
 
 "come," the man muttered, any impatience defying detection. 
 
 firrel's boot tested its weight against the rug. there was solid ground beneath. the rest followed suit. 
 
 "wait!" the man screamed. the group wasted no time assuming a defensive stance, their weapons and shields drawn. "i meant the carpet." 
 
 the adventurers looked towards their feet. the jade fibers assumed a purplish hue as the blood from their persons dripped freely. querth's face flushed. 
 
 "sorry," the wizard whispered. 
 
 the man rolled his eyes. "it's already ruined. nothing we can do now. let's just get this over with." 
 
 the adventurers were finally within a pace of the desk when the open palm of the man begged their halt. the hordes of evil creatures had led them to that chamber. the supposed throne room of unspeakable villainy was little more than a study with a librarian. 
 
 "well, then. i suppose congratulations are in order!" the man clapped his hands together. "smashing job. i'm pollock and i'll be handling your processing from here." 
 
 "processing?" edmund echoed. 
 
 "yes," replied pollock. "you're almost done in this dreadful castle and on your way back home to enjoy the spoils. all that's left is to handle the last odds and ends." 
 
 the adventurers nodded in content, but kept their weapons handy. the legions they had to cut through in order to reach that chamber began to feel concluded. 
 
 "excellent! let's get started. in total you've slaughtered… one hundred and fifty three goblins, twenty nine orcs, eighteen kobolds… and two dragons. impressive." 
 
 edmund smirked and rolled the handle of his axe to catch the light to the groans of ronn and dismal. they had enjoyed the chaos that had followed as it stopped their fellow warrior from gloating. 
 
 "in addition, you broke down forty one doors, set off two fire traps, six spike snares, three boulders, and one acid spill. plus, it says you freed the dungeons of ten prisoners." 
 
 "all in a day's work," wilm interjected. 
 
 "quite," responded pollock, not the least impressed. "and adding up your little adventure, that comes to a total of eight million, eight hundred thirty seven thousand, two hundred and fifty one gold pieces." 
 
 even querth's mind could not comprehend such a figure. they were used to generous spoils, but several hundred was the most any had ever seen. 
 
 "we couldn't possibly carry that much coin," dismal remarked. "or spend it." 
 
 "that's quite expected," pollock laughed. "you can just pay in installments." 
 
 "pay?" shouted firrel. "what do you mean pay?" 
 
 "your fines. your damages. you can't just go around killing things, damaging property, and setting off traps that require professional calibration." 
 
 "but we were on a quest," pleaded ronn. "we were trying to save the village." 
 
 "i see," sneered pollock. "does that mean the village is going to pay the fines, rebuilt the castle, reset the protections, mop the floors, rehire the guards, retrain dragons, and inform the families of those lost?" the group stood in wide-eyed silence. "i didn't think so." 
 
 "b-but, it was a quest," ronn repeated. 
 
 "do you have a license, a writ of pacification for this' quest' of yours?" ronn shook his head. "no need to answer, i already know you don't. if you had bothered to apply for one, *this* castle would have been better protected and *i* wouldn't have been needed. just a little' [ wp ]' at the start would have been enough to save us all the mess of your unauthorized rampage." 
 
 "who was supposed to file our wp?" querth asked the group. they considered the question for a moment before turning to face /u/dismaldreamer. "you've ruined us!" 
 
 "i'm sorry," cried dismal. "i didn't know! i didn't know this would happen!" 
 
 the circle closed around him as the group looked to dispatch their greatest foe: the enemy within.

strip_punctuation.xsum::29: Philip Cullen 57 was given a six month suspended sentence for capturing two butterflies at reserves in Somerset and in Gloucestershire in 2015 He was convicted in March of six charges relating to killing capturing and possessing the endangered species His is believed to be the first prosecution in the UK involving offences related to the species Bristol Magistrates Court heard that Cullen was seen chasing a Large Blue with a child s net at Daneway Banks in Gloucestershire in June 2015 He was later spotted with a small net at Collard Hill in Somerset It was reported to police who raided his home and found up to 30 trays of butterflies including Large Blues Prosecutor Ian Jackson told the court the charges had been brought on the grounds of endangering a species Michael Hartnell defending said in mitigation the 57 year old had accepted the enormity of what he had done and was extremely remorseful Cullen of The Grove Warmley Bristol was given a six month prison sentence suspended for two years and ordered to carry out 250 hours of unpaid work He was also given a five year criminal behaviour order banning him from three nature reserves popular with the Large Blue and was ordered to pay Â 300 prosecution costs and an Â 80 victim surcharge The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust GWT said it was the first UK conviction for collecting a butterfly and a breakthrough in the battle against wildlife crime Source Butterfly Conservation The Large Blue Maculinea arion species became extinct in Britain 1979 It was reintroduced at sites including Collard Hill and Daneway Banks in the 1980s and in 2004 it was found at nine locations in the country It has a wingspan of more than two inches and can be identified by a row of black spots on its upper forewing A person who collects and studies butterflies is called a lepidopterist after the branch of zoology that deals with butterflies and moths

strip_punctuation.academic_abstracts::0: For several decades regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized where the tests being utilized examined mutations and structural and numerical chromosomal damage This has served the genetic toxicity community well when most of the substances being tested were amenable to such assays The outcome from this testing is usually a dichotomous yes no evaluation of test results and in many instances the information is only used to determine whether a substance has carcinogenic potential or not Over the same time period mechanisms and modes of action MOAs that elucidate a wider range of genomic damage involved in many adverse health outcomes have been recognized In addition a paradigm shift in applied genetic toxicology is moving the field toward a more quantitative dose response analysis and point of departure PoD determination with a focus on risks to exposed humans This is directing emphasis on genomic damage that is likely to induce changes associated with a variety of adverse health outcomes This paradigm shift is moving the testing emphasis for genetic damage from a hazard identification only evaluation to a more comprehensive risk assessment approach that provides more insightful information for decision makers regarding the potential risk of genetic damage to exposed humans To enable this broader context for examining genetic damage a next generation testing strategy needs to take into account a broader more flexible approach to testing and ultimately modeling of genomic damage as it relates to human exposure This is consistent with the larger risk assessment context being used in regulatory decision making As presented here this flexible approach for examining genomic damage focuses on testing for relevant genomic effects that can be as best as possible associated with an adverse health effect The most desired linkage for risk to humans would be changes in loci associated with human diseases whether in somatic or germ cells The outline of a flexible approach and associated considerations are presented in a series of nine steps some of which can occur in parallel which was developed through a collaborative effort by leading genetic toxicologists from academia government and industry through the International Life Sciences Institute ILSI Health and Environmental Sciences Institute HESI Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee GTTC The ultimate goal is to provide quantitative data to model the potential risk levels of substances which induce genomic damage contributing to human adverse health outcomes Any good risk assessment begins with asking the appropriate risk management questions in a planning and scoping effort This step sets up the problem to be addressed e g broadly does genomic damage need to be addressed and if so how to proceed The next two steps assemble what is known about the problem by building a knowledge base about the substance of concern and developing a rational biological argument for why testing for genomic damage is needed or not By focusing on the risk management problem and potential genomic damage of concern the next step of assay s selection takes place The work up of the problem during the earlier steps provides the insight to which assays would most likely produce the most meaningful data This discussion does not detail the wide range of genomic damage tests available but points to types of testing systems that can be very useful Once the assays are performed and analyzed the relevant data sets are selected for modeling potential risk From this point on the data are evaluated and modeled as they are for any other toxicology endpoint Any observed genomic damage effects or genetic event s can be modeled via a dose response analysis and determination of an estimated PoD When a quantitative risk analysis is needed for decision making a parallel exposure assessment effort is performed exposure assessment is not detailed here as this is not the focus of this discussion guidelines for this assessment exist elsewhere Then the PoD for genomic damage is used with the exposure information to develop risk estimations e g using reference dose RfD margin of exposure MOE approaches in a risk characterization and presented to risk managers for informing decision making This approach is applicable now for incorporating genomic damage results into the decision making process for assessing potential adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans and is consistent with the ILSI HESI Risk Assessment in the 21st Century RISK21 roadmap This applies to any substance to which humans are exposed including pharmaceuticals agricultural products food additives and other chemicals It is time for regulatory bodies to incorporate the broader knowledge and insights provided by genomic damage results into the assessments of risk to more fully understand the potential of adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans thus improving the assessment of risk due to genomic damage The historical use of genomic damage data as a yes no gateway for possible cancer risk has been too narrowly focused in risk assessment The recent advances in assaying for and understanding genomic damage including eventually epigenetic alterations obviously add a greater wealth of information for determining potential risk to humans Regulatory bodies need to embrace this paradigm shift from hazard identification to quantitative analysis and to incorporate the wider range of genomic damage in their assessments of risk to humans The quantitative analyses and methodologies discussed here can be readily applied to genomic damage testing results now Indeed with the passage of the recent update to the Toxic Substances Control Act TSCA in the US the new generation testing strategy for genomic damage described here provides a regulatory agency here the US Environmental Protection Agency EPA but suitable for others a golden opportunity to reexamine the way it addresses risk based genomic damage testing including hazard identification and exposure Environ Mol Mutagen 58 264 283 2017 2016 The Authors Environmental and Molecular Mutagenesis Published by Wiley Periodicals Inc
