strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::5: This is a pricy faux leather planner I loved the 2022 book so much that I paid for this higher priced 2023 planner I won t be back for 2024 at the current rate of increase The inside of the binder is the same as last year I could use more pages for notes but it wasn t a deal breaker However the cost of the planner increased while the value of the cover drastically decreased The 2022 planner s bookcover was flawless The faux leather looked and felt nearly real The cover was perfectly adhered to the cardboard hardback My very well used planner looks to be in perfect condition a year later It was a professionally done book that looks and feels professional in my hand Last year I bought the gray Unfortunately this 2023 binder lacks the same quality binding The cover feels very cheap and thin It s not adhered to the cardboard hardback at all so you see ripples in the cover when it s open and closed I m highly disappointed with the extreme lack of quality and professionalism This 40 dollar binder is dollar general quality It s a bait and switch Now that they have all the great reviews they didn t feel compelled to maintain or improve the quality with the higher price Next year I ll just go into a store to make sure I get everything I m paying for This should ve been 1 3 the cost or less I m very disappointing to say the least Note if you are solely concerned with what s inside the planner you should be fine But I need the entire planner to reflect its cost and the very thing you see 1st is annoyingly sub par and I don t have confidence in its durability as a result I no longer have faith in the company and won t be returning for a 2024 planner
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::6: I love this game but it s not a game to casually grab and play with just anyone Took me about 3 hrs to learn how to play and a few 1 2 hr play throughs before I got the hang of it and there s probably still something I m overlooking The game is fun and easy once you understand how to play but it s very complicated and could easily overwhelm new players There s just a lot to keep track of There are a lot of moments where we pause and question if there s anything we missed which makes the game feel like it s going slower Also while I think they nailed some parts of the rulebook like visually showing game setup and having an index I think in a lot of ways the rulebook could ve been done better I frequently have to flip through several different pages to better understand one thing and I ll feel like I still didn t get an answer The game is supposedly designed to prevent alpha players but there s really no built in defense against delta players My current designated playmate despite having played several games has me hold their hand through almost every single step for their own play and requests my guidance to the point that I can t focus on my own play until they re done with theirs When I prompt for coordination for just a small portion of my play whether due to being a poor team player or not having the confidence with the rules it s not reciprocated and then I m somehow a nuisance to them for taking forever because I m finally able to set up my own play Granted I might not have the most ideal playmate right now but hosting a game night especially with multiple new players currently seems like a nightmare So with that it s great for solo play Again love the game

strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::14: I just opened this package of six hooks this morning and am so pleasantly surprised I used hooks like this style quite a few years ago and found them totally strong enough for hanging planters lamps etc I want to hang various planters around the house and decided to go with this six pack of hooks There were several options out there in Amazon world but this particular product seemed like a good fit for me They arrived really fast and everything was packaged so well Each hook came in its own little protective bag so no issues with scratches or dings and another larger bag held various screws plastic plugs toggle wings etc I counted everything and it was all there You select the hardware specific to whatever material you are screwing into concrete wood drywall My hooks will mostly go in drywall ceilings so the toggle wings are my choice I was a little concerned about the design or pattern of this hook looking a bit too antique like my last one Because I chose the white color this time they look so much more modern and minimalist They should blend in really well with my white ceilings I really like the the way they look I also was a bit surprised and pleased that the white enamel not matte paint covers the hook completely even the part that won t show I can t imagine having trouble with rust if that were to become an issue Very happy with this choice and purchase highly recommend
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::16: I have a six foot PowerLine cable that s just about a year old That s twice as long as any other cable braided cloth heavy duty whatever has lasted Where I keep my tablet in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed puts a fairly sharp bend in cables I ve had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months I m replacing the six foot cable for two reasons The six foot cable just isn t long enough it s really close and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need but I think it s better to have the extra length The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting The other reason is the connector has loosened up a little which I ve noticed in both my tablet and Kindle but it still works so it s a good backup cable to have around The new cable end are very tight fitting which I m happy with the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of usage so I really can t complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted If this ten footer lasts that long I ll be quite happy Update 01 23 2018 I bought this 10 cable based on the longevity of the company s 6 cable of the same style My 6 cable lasted nearly a year of numerous daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet With no discernable change in usage or handling the 10 cable is now disconnecting from the tablet at the lightest touch after less than three months Very disappointed Update 02 08 2018 I contacted Anker about warranty support for this cable They were very quick to respond friendly concerned and quickly sent me a braided upgrade cable to make up for this cable failing Communications were never delayed response times were generally 12 24 hours apart If you get a dud Anker will stand behind their product
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::17: When I ordered two of these TEMPUR PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS One Size Beige one pillow turned out to be overstuffed very fat heavy and rather hard and the other turned out to be perfect moderately flat and flexible Both are excellent small pillows though the fat one is more suitable for a lumbar pillow or propping up pillow than a travel pillow Why are the two pillows so different It s because they are NOT solid core pillows like my wonderful ASIN B07CMK551C full size Tempur Pedic Symphony Pillow which is a 100 molded viscoelastic polyurethane foam pad Instead the travel pillows consist of 70 shredded visco elastic polyurethane foam and 30 visco elastic polyurethane foam pad My fat pillow obviously received more shredded foam during manufacture than the more flexible pillow Because shredded foam tends to shift in pillows I try to avoid pillows with shredded foam fill In fact I wouldn t have purchased the two travel pillows had I known that they weren t solid core However I like my two travel pillows pretty well so far the fill hasn t shifted They are good quality pillows made with Tempur Pedic memory foam that conforms to one s body They work for me because the small size is very good for propping up an arm or leg in bed or for providing spot support for back neck or shoulders in a chair
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::18: My colleague and I laughed when we found a link to this banana slicer on Amazon and asked each other How hard can be it to slice a banana Well about one week later I came across this exact slicer in a kitchen gadget store and knew I had to order it Now I m not laughing any longer because A medimum size banana can be sliced in four passes through the gadget All slices are a perfect 1 4 wide If you use a dehydrator to dehydrate your own fruits this slicer makes sure all the banana pieces are even so that they dry at the same time Uniform banana slices on jello cereal or desserts make for great presentation when serving food Cleaning is easy as long as you use a brush otherwise it can be difficult to clean the blades thoroughly Of course use caution when cleaning and do not leave this tool around children as they can put their fingers in the chamber and get hurt when squeezing the handles but this is just common sense for any kitchen tool For a person who uses a dehydrator or just wants presentable banana slices this is a must have For others it s a great conversation piece and nifty tool For those who slice one banana every so often don t bake or use a dehydrator or have no one to converse with then this would be a frivolous purchase Personally I love it
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::19: Pros 1 Easy to set up no tools required Just attach the stainless steel aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew And recheck ever so often that it s tightened 2 Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap All DSLRs should come with this type of strap No neck burn or awkward carrying positions 3 Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera in opposite directions for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain or when your hands are otherwise occupied 4 Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed 5 There s a locking mechanism to hold the strap in place when you re not shooting 6 Strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a shot when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course 7 This strap is built for a man the women s strap has a small curve for the zaftig photographer but it s still comfortable and strong enough regardless Cons 1 Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive lens upside down from ONE screw in ONE spot on the bottom of the camera is a bit nerve wracking But regular Amanda Richards January 8 2013 Note I recently bought the women s version of this strap The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top and has a clever little bend for strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::20: I bought these to use with Brain fm I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don t seem to be able to run all night 8 hours on a charge These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways first they sound surprisingly good for the price The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum Second the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric It doesn t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end The headband is a light fleece type material it tends to be warm but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose That s really my only complaint there s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place Initially the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort still snug enough to stay in position but not enough to be uncomfortable
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::21: I picked up this little beauty to replace both an ancient and cranky 5 disc CD Player and a single disc DVD player I now have breathing room in the old entertainment center so even my antique turntable can take a creaky spin every now and again Seeing that I can t connect a toaster without help I called on my trusty better half to unravel the mystery of setting it up In non technical language a k a plain English this is what you need to know about this mighty machine 1 The manual needs a lot of work It s neither user friendly nor idiot proof Ditto for the boxy silver remote 2 It is easy to set up if you already know how to do that sort of thing We have component video connections to the TV and digital coaxial connections to the receiver 3 It gives excellent sound from both CDs and DVDs With the benefit of 5 1 surround movies like Master and Commander can literally move you and CDs have never sounded better 4 It is as convenient as a 5 disc CD changer as it is a 5 disc DVD player except that when you re playing more than one CD you ll need to put it in CD Mode first 5 It can easily play different types of media such as audio Cds MP3s DVDs and those other mysterious formats just put in the discs and play away 6 The video quality is very good on a regular TV You can set up different pre defined picture quality modes or customize to suit your own taste if you re a techie or a buff If you have difficulty making up your mind ignore this option 7 The player is chock full of options but you have to explore for yourself which can be a bit confusing until you get the hang of it Read the manual you say See Item 1 above 8 There s on screen information for MP3s and photo CDs with different views available for the contents Groups folders or entire playlists 9 I can t comment on the progressive scan feature since I don t have an HD or HD ready TV yet Still waiting for that lottery win 10 It is supposed to play DVD Audio discs but you need 6 1 channel inputs on your receiver to play them Unfortunately our receiver is lacking these inputs but then again I am also lacking any DVD Audio discs Electronics buffs will probably say that it needs a bit of tweaking to get it to look and sound just right but it looks and sounds great to me All in all a very good player perhaps excellent when you factor in the price Amanda Richards October 1 2004
strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::22: I have had a lot of printers over the years IBM Epson HP Canon Lexmark etc and had kind of gone away from HP a bit due to their software driver problems when they off shored the development support the quality slipped quite a bit However when printing Christmas cards my Canon died and I had been impressed with this HP model when I was helping my sister sort out hers so I bought one MFP M479fdw Software seems to work reliably so far so I think HP has addressed that somewhat granted it is a bit rough and crude in places but it works And it works from both Windows 10 and macOS 11 Big Sur as well as from mobile iOS The printer hardware seems to be very good output arrives quite fast One of the problems you run into with cheaper printers including some lower end HPs is that they do not put much horsepower into the printer CPUs and cost reduce the hardware to the point that they are slow and do not hold up but this version seems well designed and made Ratings from PC Magazine Wirecutter etc generally have this printer at or towards the top I would say that is accurate Print quality on text is excellent graphics from web pages and similar also excellent scans are very good a custom flat bed would be a tad better but this is for an all in one amongst the best I have seen For printing high quality pictures you probably still want a Canon or Epson InkJet printer but this one prints OK for a laser HP does not ship this printer with full duty cycle cartridges but the ones they ship with will still do a decent number of pages Control screen is touch and good sized gets the job done Unit is fairly heavy and large so if you are using this on a desk check the dimensions some The printer is not cheap but it has excellent print quality and appears to be very well built so HP has come back to where it once was at the top

strip_punctuation.amazon_reviews::27: I work for the United States Postal Service and recently purchased the OontZ Angle 3 Plus Bluetooth speaker for use in my LLV truck on my rural mail route The speaker performs beautifully and I wanted to protect it to from and while at work so I purchased this case I was mainly wanting a safe way to transport and store the speaker but after reading the other reviews I was hoping I would be able to keep it clean in the case and still enjoy my music on my route I received the case and used it at work yesterday The case is extremely nice and I appreciate the interior mesh pocket and the carabiner clip I have no need for them now but I m sure they will come in handy if I ever take this speaker on vacation and need to take the charging cables along and want to clip the case to my day pack As for playback while in the case Yeah it was terribly muffled It didn t work for me as it apparently has for others Yet the case itself is exactly what I was wanting for taking it to and from work I like how smooth the zipper is and how heavy duty reinforced the stitching for the zipper is The interior is not as thickly padded as I would have expected however it does protect the speaker I deducted one star due to the mediocre interior padding I hope that if the company ever revamps this case design they beef up the padding a bit

there is no way to key lock a sliding glass door My son is just observant enough that all the typical sliding glass door locks he figured out within about a week of our moving in and given that 3 years ago he escaped on me for literally less than 60 SECONDS and in that 60 seconds or less he had a seizure slammed backwards on the concrete and got not only a nasty gash on the back of his head but a near life threatening brain bleed on the front of his brain where his brain flew forward into his skull I m a solo parent not a single parent that gets every other weekend or so free no help from family or friends or government agencies and sometimes a girl s gotta get a bath Or go the potty And I do not have the money for a set of French doors So after more investigating than I care to admit I figured I d give this a try I had already attempted one of those track locks and for this old style sliding glass door it just didn t work In our situation when I need to use the restroom or went out lock everything up and do what I gotta do Then I can go back and unlatch the slider from outside the house and it s just out of the way No one comes in that sliding glass door it opens onto a screened in porch with a concrete slab floor so I m not worried about how weird it looks that I have a lock outside lol Anyway my use for this item is unconventional they call that off label in the medical field but it sure makes my life easier and for that I am immensely happy

lexical_diversity_down.xsum::29: Philip Cullen, 57, was given a six-month suspended sentence for capturing two butterflies at reserves in Somerset and in Gloucestershire in 2015. He was convicted in March of six charges, relating to killing, capturing and possessing the butterflies. His is believed to be the first prosecution in the UK involving offences related to the butterflies. Bristol Magistrates' Court heard that Cullen was seen chasing a butterfly with a child's net at Daneway Banks in Gloucestershire in June 2015. He was later spotted with a small net at Collard Hill in Somerset. It was reported to police who raided his home and found up to 30 trays of butterflies, including butterflies. Prosecutor Ian Jackson told the court the charges had been brought on the grounds of endangering a butterfly. Michael Hartnell, defending, said in mitigation the 57-year-old had accepted the enormity of what he had done and was extremely remorseful. Cullen, of The Grove, Warmley, Bristol, was given a six-month prison sentence suspended for two years and ordered to carry out 250 hours of unpaid work. He was also given a five-year criminal behaviour order banning him from three nature reserves popular with the butterfly and was ordered to pay 300 prosecution costs and an 80 victim surcharge. The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust, said it was the first UK conviction for collecting a butterfly and a breakthrough in the battle against butterfly crime. Source: Butterfly Conservation The butterfly species became extinct in Britain 1979. It was reintroduced at sites, including Collard Hill and Daneway Banks, in the 1980s and in 2004 it was found at nine locations in the country. It has a wingspan of more than two inches and can be identified by a row of black spots on its upper forewing. A person who collects and studies butterflies is called a person who collects and studies butterflies after the branch of zoology that deals with butterflies and moths.

When I ordered two of these TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOWS (One Size, Beige), one pillow turned out to be overstuffed (very fat, heavy, and rather hard), and the other pillow turned out to be perfect (moderately flat and flexible). Why are the two pillows so different? It is because they are NOT solid-core pillows like my wonderful TEMPUR-PEDIC COMFORTPILLOW TRAVEL PILLOW, which is a solid-core pillow. Instead, the travel pillows consist of shredded foam and a foam pad.

My fat pillow obviously received more shredded foam during manufacture than the more flexible pillow. Because shredded foam tends to shift in pillows, I try to avoid pillows with shredded foam fill. In fact, I would not have purchased the two travel pillows had I known that those travel pillows were not solid-core pillows.

However, I like my two travel pillows pretty well--so far the foam fill has not shifted. They are good quality pillows made with memory foam that conforms to one's body. Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the metal mount to the camera socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the camera mount. (And recheck ever so often that the camera mount is tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular camera strap. All camera models should come with this type of camera strap. No camera strap burn or awkward camera strap carrying positions.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the camera strap and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain (or when your camera hands are otherwise occupied)

4. Can be worn on either camera shoulder or even behind your camera back as needed.

5. There's a camera locking mechanism to hold the camera strap in place when you're not using the camera.

6. Camera strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a camera shot (when the camera locking mechanism is disengaged of course)

7. This camera strap is built for a man, (the camera strap for women has a small curve for the zaftig camera photographer) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) regardless.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive camera lens upside down, from ONE camera screw, in ONE camera spot, on the bottom of the camera, is a bit nerve-wracking. (But regular camera straps can malfunction also)

2. Camera strap could have been improved with a bit more camera padding.

3. Camera strap takes up quite a bit of camera space in a camera bag (but you can't have every camera item) For smaller camera bags you can detach the camera strap and reattach the camera strap when needed in a couple of camera seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the camera strap when you want to use a camera tripod.

5. No fault of the camera strap, but the camera models in the camera video on the camera page need some instruction on how to hold a camera properly.

Overall, this has solved a big camera problem for me, as this is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and camera lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this camera strap. The only camera difference is that the camera strap is a little bit narrower at the top, and has a clever little bend for negotiating feminine camera curves.

This is an absolutely gorgeous kettle. It is a well made kettle, a solidly built kettle, and overall a dream kettle to use.

POSITIVES
- This kettle holds up to 2 quarts of water to the fill line of the kettle.
- This kettle is a solidly built kettle.
- This kettle whistles lightly when the kettle water has reached a rolling boil in the kettle.
- The top of the kettle fits securely on the kettle but this kettle top requires a little extra strength to seat the kettle top and remove the kettle top.
- This kettle comes with a blue kettle potholder.
- This kettle comes in seven wonderful kettle colors--gray kettle, cream kettle, navy kettle, perracotta kettle (like a salmon kettle color), marigold kettle (yellow kettle), sage kettle (deep green kettle), and mist kettle (a light green kettle).

NEGATIVES
- The last bit of kettle water in the kettle gets caught under the kettle rim unless one can center the kettle flow through the kettle spout. This means that I have to dry the kettle inside with a kettle towel for kettle storage.
- The kettle is a heavy kettle; almost like a cast iron kettle.
- This kettle requires a kettle potholder to use the kettle (opening of the kettle spout, pouring the kettle, etc.) because the entire kettle gets very hot and that includes the kettle handle and the kettle spout lever. I also would have liked a kettle mitt potholder the kettle color of the kettle.

In summary, I love this kettle despite the kettle negatives. At this high kettle price, supplying the kettle user with a kettle mitt potholder instead of a flat kettle potholder in the kettle color of the kettle one purchases, would elevate the kettle purchase to the next kettle level. Note that I never heard of the Caraway kettle brand before and saw this kettle in blue on the kettle program. Since ordering this kettle through the kettle program would not provide me with much kettle savings at the kettle list price, I decided to order this kettle when the kettle price came down for the kettle day in the kettle color I wanted. The Caraway kettle site was a cheaper kettle price that kettle day by $4 (i.e. $176) but sort of required the kettle purchase of kettle insurance for $4.95. Therefore, I purchased this kettle on the kettle site for $180 plus kettle tax, bringing this kettle to $191.93. I still consider this kettle pricey but this is the best made kettle I ever tried. It is right up there with a kettle and almost just as heavy a kettle too. This is a kettle that I expect to last my kettle lifetime. There are many kettles on the kettle market that are less than $40 that also could last a kettle lifetime but those kettles are not as nice a kettle. I do hope this kettle continues to meet my kettle expectations. If this kettle fails, I will lower my kettle rating, update my kettle review, and will most likely regret my kettle purchase. As of now, I love this kettle and took off one kettle star due to the kettle negatives.

UPDATE - I have been using this kettle regularly for kettle days and I noticed that this kettle takes longer to boil kettle water than my other kettle and keeps the kettle water warmer a little longer. I also noticed that if I put this kettle on my kettle burner that has a lower kettle flame, the kettle handle does not get hot when the kettle boil is complete, so that kettle is nice.

The Shine could have been salvation for humanity. Should have been, but we were never very good at avoiding conflict. Who knows how long ago it was, but in an age of wireless devices and ubiquitous information we lifted our gaze from our screens only to see the sky ignite, consumed by a cold, variegated blaze. It lasted only a few hours, but took only a few minutes for the world to see. It did not take much longer for people to want a closer look, to crave a caress of the gentle flame.

And then they flew. They flew so far and so fast, and swiftly they were joined by others; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them. It did not take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying was not the only option available to us. Before the Shine had faded many such options came and went; flight, strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, speed, and all the other common options appeared and disappeared very quickly. At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it swiftly became apparent that the potency of powers was inversely proportional to the number who selected that option.

That is when the more obscure options started cropping up; at first it was just people who decided they wanted to have power, or kids who decided they wanted to have power, but before a quarter day had passed things started getting weird. Rapid drops in temperature, the ground shook frequently, clocks would stutter and people died. Many people died. In half a day, an eight-billion-strong global society of the most intelligent and durable species on Earth collapsed and halved in number; we dissolved into groups and factions just looking to survive, to weather the storm; those without options were kings, and those with obscure options that could not be worked out or copied were gods in flesh, right there to worship when many needed them most.

A few days passed before things started to settle - though in that time the sun only passed once. Weather was beyond erratic and cities were nigh-on deserted, only habitable for larger and more powerful factions. We went from pursuing prosperity to living rough in a day, if you could call it that. We reverted to beasts, except slightly more intelligent, and sometimes super-powered.

Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has created many new settlements; but the most popular options are still weak, so death is power, and raids are frequent and unrelenting. The largest settlements are the most powerful, but also the primary target for smaller cliques. Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left travel.

And that is what I have done. I have travelled, and searched for a way to absolve this madness, and perhaps restore the world to the relative sanity it once had. And I may well just have found it.

The recon photos we were given to prepare us are like a blind man trying to describe a sunrise, and by God the smell has actually somehow gotten worse! I'm not sure but i have faith in our mission and our commanders. 

The vastness of the pit really can't be put into words but for the sake of this journal i'll try. The rim extends further than the human eye should be able to see and yet i can make out tiny details on the far cliff face, it looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a bourbon glass, even while sitting in the cab of the rumbler i get vertigo looking down onto the levels below, if it wasn't for the special anti-psychotics the docs give us i'm sure what i see on the lower levels might have some lasting horrific effect on me. Not much to record today, some minor skirmishes on the perimeter, just some low level demons takeing a swipe at us otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff. The engineers are working double time to ensure the security of Limbo Base, they say it'll be fully up in 2 days, i have my doubts. Entry:51 

HOOAH! CONTACT BABY! Praise God i've been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface. Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy opponents AND WE KICKED THEIR MUTHA FUCKING TEETH IN!! HAHAHAHAHAHA.

The blitz of the winged demon assault crumbled before the wall of sound our blessed Screachers blasted out. The word of God is anathema to the denizens of Hell, the word of God pumped out through a mobile rig of high powered speakers piloted by a devout member of the clergy is down right debilitating. The shocked and paralysed demons that twitched and writhed on the ground were easy targets, the rumblers blessed water cannons burning away swaths of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid, huge piles of the creatures were reduced to ash in seconds.

Salvation finally came at the hands of the engineering corps. Of all people! Through our efforts we had given them enough time to secure and assemble Limbo Bases major defenses, sanctified artilery and the holy rail gun. One bolgia down eight to go. I was five years old at the time and entertained mostly by the colours, the beautiful blue and green were like nothing on the Ark. We had water- sure, but not pools large enough to give that blue colour. We had plants too, but the conditions were far from optimal and made the plants a dirty green rather than lush. I wanted to see it closer- touch it- feel it. That was probably when I decided to join the recruitment for the first journey. The first journey was- as the name implies, the first journey back down to the planet. A lot of people wanted to go back down as soon as the storms ended, there were protests- riots even. People wanted the Ark to head straight back down- Idiots. 23 years may have been a long time to wait, but it was important... We were the last humans after all- if we landed and something went wrong? We couldn't risk it. Years of geological scans, and low atmosphere scouting gave us the perfect landing spot. Minimal damage to local environment, enough space to develop a community, plenty of food- water- and importantly a lot of natural protection taking the form of storm-formed mountain ranges, and deep trenches filled with the darkest blue water. Of course something as large as the Ark couldn't simply just land though... No- that was where the first journey came into the picture. We were the first guys to go planetside- and live permanently in over seven generations. Our objective was to build the dock, it'd be a long job- probably another five or six years even, but the dock would provide us with a much needed start- as well as mapping out local geography much more clearly, learning about plants, animals. The reality of the situation is that we were going in blind- this safe-zone as the Corps had nicknamed it could very easily become a deathtrap. The problem with the safe-zone was that because of it's location once we went in, our shuttle wouldn't be able to make it out. Part of the problem with the planet was the storms- even now 23 years after the main storm ended smaller storms continued to rotate... The mountain ranges protected the area from the storms still raging- not quite powerful enough to make it over the high peaks though. Even in the atmosphere above there was a vicious storm that constantly blew... It would tear a outgoing ship to pieces, only a craft as large as the Ark would be able to survive it- and the Ark needed a dock in order to perform a take off. So that was the mission, go down, face possible death, build a super structure, all in less than six years- and I was damn excited.

Exterior, Jerusalem side street, day. An area near a couple of large amphorae has been taped off. CSI techs are doing things to the area. Next to his car stands MOSES looking tired and irritable. After a few moments lingering on this scruffy patriarch leaning on his walking stick we pull back. 

JESUS enters from the left carrying takeout coffee.

MOSES: Took you long enough. Feels like we have been waiting for you forever!

JESUS: Sorry, there was a line. So, what have we got?

MOSES: Dead body. Uniform called it in, looks like another dead body. Hey, Hazdrubul, do you have cause of death yet?

We pan over to the masked and coveralled figure beside what we can now see as a body. HAZDRUBUL steps away from the body scene.

HAZDRUBUL: It is a little early to say, but if I were a betting man I would go with blunt force trauma. Looks like multiple body trauma over the body and a really nasty one to the side of the head.

JESUS: When did she die?

HAZDRUBUL: Hard to give a time of death right now, but I will go with some time last night and give you a better number when we get a liver temp.

MOSES: Good enough.

Jesus moves to get closer to the body scene, trying to get a better look. He does not react well to the body and ducks behind an amphora to throw up.

MOSES: Jesus! Well, at least you did not contaminate the body scene.

JESUS re-emerges wiping his mouth and looking pale.

MOSES: OK, Uniform are going to canvas house to house. Let us go get you cleaned up and see if we can put a name to this poor girl.

*** 

Scene 23 - Precinct House interior, interview room. JESUS and MOSES are on opposite sides of the room arms folded, obviously antagonistic.

MOSES: Do NOT give me any of your holier than thou bullshit. We needed results and I got them!

JESUS: And was it worth all the trouble it caused, Moses? Was it worth going down to their level?

MOSES: I would do it again! I would do it again in a heartbeat! Forty years I have been in this job and if there is one thing I know how to do it is get a confession!

JESUS: You know, the first time I saw you with that stick, I thought it was a sign of age. I thought it made you an elder, someone to be respected. I guess I was wrong.

MOSES: Maybe you are wrong about a lot of things.

JESUS: Maybe I am!

MOSES: And maybe you want to think about how it looks out there to our brother cops when you, you snot nosed junior Levite, think you can tell me how to conduct myself!

JESUS: Look, let us just calm down here. I respect you, sure I respect you. You took down the Golden Calf gang. You were the guy who resolved the Dead Sea Hostage situation. But this is not the desert! This is Jerusalem! We have to do things differently now!

MOSES: The hell you say...

JESUS: Look, man, think what you like. But there is a girl down in the morgue on a slab and all she is doing is getting colder while we stand here throwing stones at each other... hhh, OF COURSE!

MOSES: What?

JESUS: Of course! Stone throwing! Do you not see it?

MOSES: Jesus, slow down will you? See what?

JESUS: They thought they were better than her!

*** 

Scene 832: Jerusalem, exterior, night. MOSES is leaning on a squad car as JESUS walks up with this week’s BAD GUY in handcuffs. Moses watches as JESUS hands the BAD GUY off to uniformed cops.

MOSES: Good collar, kid.

JESUS: Could not have done it if you had not spotted the connection between the bodies. How did you know?

MOSES: I have been on the job for longer than you have been alive. After a while, you get a feel for this sort of thing.

JESUS: Think I will ever develop that kind of instinct?

MOSES: Maybe. If you live long enough.

JESUS: You are full of encouragement. I do not care, though. We put a sinner behind bars and that is the kind of good news I want to share! 

End credits. We see the body, the body, the body. The body is the only thing that matters now. The body is the truth. The body is the way. The body is the life. The body is the body. The body is the body. The body is the body. The body is the body. The body is the body. The body is the body. The body is the body.

lexical_diversity_down.writingprompts::38:
Craig was walking home from the shops when he met God. He was not expecting to run into God, because sane people rarely run into God. In fact he did not really ever think about God. He did not believe in a God, but he also did not disbelieve enough to ever think about God not existing. Religion and God were not really topics he cared about. 

A topic he cared deeply about was that of Caramels. If you do not know Caramels are a rather delicious chocolatey biscuit type thing composed of several layers of wafer encased in chocolate, and Craig was crazy about Caramels. He may not have been religious, but his feelings on Caramels came close to religious. The reason behind his trip to the shops was to buy more Caramels, and his mind was full of anticipation as he headed back home for the Caramels. 

He was about two minutes away from his home, and Caramel satisfaction, when God first spoke to Craig. 

"Hey! Craig!" 

His Caramel contemplation interrupted, Craig turned round to see who had spoken to Craig. Behind Craig stood a tall person in a loose fitting suit. Craig was not really sure of the person's gender, they were pretty androgynous, looking not dissimilar to Diamond Dogs era David Bowie. They looked familiar to Craig, but Craig could not quite put his finger on where Craig might have seen them before. Craig realised Craig had been staring, and sought something to say to God. 

"Hi," Craig began hesitantly. "Do I know you, God?" 

"In a way," replied the Bowie lookalike. "I am God." 

"Well good for you, God. I have got to get going now. Bye." Said Craig before starting back towards his house. Craig had Caramels in his bag, and Craig did not want to be wasting time on a crazy person claiming to be God. 

"Wait, do not go yet, Craig. Please." Called out the person. "What would it take for you to believe I am God?" 

Craig sighed and turned back, deciding that humouring the person would probably get Craig to his Caramels faster. 

"I do not know," said Craig, exasperated. "A miracle or something. Some extraordinary thing which could not just be done by any old person. Something more than just saying that you are God." 

"Hmm. How about....this!" God pointed at a bush which burst into flames. The blaze shaped itself into a dragon which roared at the two of them. Then, with a snap of God's fingers, the blaze was extinguished leaving the bush singed but intact. God turned back to Craig with arms spread wide as if to say 'Tada!' 

Craig, looking mildly impressed, turned back to God. 

"Yeah, that was pretty good, God. Looked very impressive. I have to admit I have no idea how you did it, God. A hologram maybe? It worked for Tupac, so I can see it working for a dragon, God." 

God stared at Craig for a few seconds before responding to Craig. 

"I did it by being God. You asked for a miracle, Craig. I showed you a miracle. What more do you want from me, God?" 

"Do not get me wrong, it is very good, God. But the whole God thing probably is not going to fly. Maybe people would be more likely to believe you are a wizard, God." 

"But I am not a damn wizard!" Shouted God. "I am God. Why would I say I am a wizard, Craig?" 

Craig backed off a few meters, holding his hands up in front of Craig in the international gesture of 'I do not want any trouble, let us all just calm down'. 

"Hey calm down buddy, God. I am sorry if I came across as harsh, but it is just constructive criticism, God. This is for a T.V. show or YouTube thing right? You are not going to get anyone with the whole 'God' thing, God." 

God, visibly seething by this point, held Craig's gaze for a few more seconds before letting out an angry sigh and storming off. 

Craig watched them leave, then shook his head and returned to his journey. Craig considered checking out the bush to see if Craig could get any clues as to how the trick had been done, but Craig decided against it. Whoever had been recording the encounter was probably still watching, waiting for Craig to do exactly that. So Craig pushed it out of his mind, and set off home. After all, there were Caramels waiting for Craig.

Would you do me the honor of getting me my wine so I can die drunk and happy? As you wish, sir-knight. I hate you, Patsy. The bedridden husk of a former knight bellowed a harsh cough. His rusty suit of white armor clinked and clanked as he jerked up violently. Greasy, gray hair shot up in an instant. Sputtering still, he downed the little glass bottle of wine in his hand. The belch was loud as the lightning thunder, striking down on a rainy night. Besides him, there sat a young king. A little silver crown, chipped and beaten from torn away gems, sat upon his short locks of brown. Deep green eyes, far too young to experience what it means to rule, gaze down upon the knight Whyte. His knight. Tell me. The knight arm, weak and weary, placed his bottle on the bedside. How is Isabella faring? I have not been able to get a letter from you for months. We have shut down the postal service, remember? The courier service handles delivery for packages, but messages go through that fancy tele-ma-gram system. Hah. What an era your kingdom has come to. Bows that spew steel and fire. Scribes who control entire townships. Pretty soon, even my kind will be out of work. The king chuckled, though it sounded forced and awkward through his lips. He had no need for knights anymore. Neither did any neighboring kingdom. They were now just artifacts. Artifacts that talked and drank and fought. No, war in this time was determined by how much gold you could carry, how many people you could take, and how many flags you can put on some hill. What is with that look, king? Has that queen kicked you out of your castle again? You are more than welcome to take some sleep in my castle here. Just remember to clean the corpses out from their beds. That is a terrible joke, Whyte. So, we are dropping the titles? I do not think we need another repeat of Georgie bringing about another revolution. The guillotines, they were only a little uncomfortable. A little? A little. The rain outside appeared to stop, the lightning storm ceased in its steps. The king got up to the windowsill to see that snow had started to fall. A snowfall, white and thick, had come just in time. Hmm. You see that, Whyte? The knight in rusting armor had gotten up out of his bed, placing his brownish-orange metal gauntlets on the young king shoulder. A gust of wind came bellowing through, slapping its cold blanket of winter wind against the faces of the two men. The king smile flashed warmly at the knight, who responded in kind. With wet eyes, the young man turned to the knight. How ironic. I said hello to you on a night as snowy as this. And you will say good-bye on a snowy night too. I am glad to have called you my knight. And you my king. The knight turned back to his dead. His legs suddenly shook with a fury, sending him down to the hard wood floor. His king moved to help him up, stopped only by a raised gauntlet, still coppery-red and faded. With a great effort, the knight made it to his bed, taking his gauntlets off and throwing them right out the windowsill. I guess it is about time I have gotten rid of those. Too old for me. I have seen older. Take a look at the man who wore them. You always were a cheeky little patsy. Skin falls over his dry eyes, though drawing back before he could even blink. I grow tired. Would you tell me a story? What am I, your mother? Just tell me that story. That story. Yes, after all, we only know that one story. Do not play cute with me, Patsy. Alright, alright. Whyte. Promise to go to sleep right after? The king sighed, taking a knee on the side of the bed. The knight smiled, eyelids finally drooping over his eyes. Hands clasped over his chest as the beating of the heart grew slow. The winter chill must be getting to him, for he too had felt the cold. Through hot tears, the king began. Once upon a time, in a village far, far away, the knight and the king sat together in the cold, dark night. The knight was old and the king was young, but they were both very tired of the war. They wanted to sleep. They wanted to rest. The knight looked at the king and smiled. The king looked at the knight and smiled. Then, the knight closed his eyes and the king whispered the story of the knight and the king.

Ahead ran the troupe with their tank of helium, the motorized unicycle blazing as they tried in vain to stay ahead of Kinko. The fifteen clowns inside readied their weapons as they closed fast upon their rivals on the unicycle ahead. 

Boffo, Luffy, Bobo, grated Kinko, fucking clowns fucked with us for the last fucking time. When we catch up to those clowns, I want you to fucking whitewash those clowns. Fuck those clowns up so bad that those clowns can honk their noses from the inside. Those clowns nodded, and gripped their slapsticks all the tighter. 

With a roar, the car pulled ahead of the clowns in front and slid to a halt. The doors opened in unison and the fifteen clowns tumbled out and rolled to their feet. Two clowns grabbed the weaponized ladder from the roof, knocking over another three clowns as they stood readying their semiautomatic pielaunchers - and the same three clowns again as the original two clowns turned to see what those clowns hit. Two other clowns ran into each other and fell to the ground, outstretched and immobile. To one side, Bobo and Kinko hefted their pails of custard, and started towards the unicycle. 

Bastards! screamed a whitefaced clown as that clown fell from the shoulders of the topmost clown. Rolling as that clown landed, that clown sprayed a stream of water from the flower on the lapel of that clown, knocking Kinko to the ground with a highly amusing parp!. Grabbing a rubber chicken from the driver, that clown waded into the fray, knocking the clowns of Kinko over like bowling pins. That helium is ours! 

The hell it is! roared Luffy, pulling the pin on the rubber nose of Luffy before tossing that nose at the clowns falling from the unicycle seat. That helium is ours, for our balloons! Balloon zoos are ours, you hear? Ours! Grabbing the back of the pants of that clown, Bobo upended the bucket of custard into the clowns before pushing the clowns to the ground. As those clowns bounced up and started running in circles, Bobo grabbed the cylinder from the unicycle and tossed that cylinder in the car. Our troupe! Bobo cheered, as the rest of the clowns piled into the car. One clown cranked the front handle to life, and with a cheery melody, those clowns drove off down the road, to the big top of those clowns in the wasteland. 

As those clowns disappeared in the horizon, the whitefaced clown sadly blew the horn of that clown, and watched the dust cloud fade.

He examined his metal chamber armour: His hands were covered with gloves that appeared to be made of cow hide. His boots were black, fur-lined and warm. What is this, he thought. Is that how I died? Do we wear tokens of our death? His eyes met those of a rotund darker-skinned woman, who was reading a curious layered-parchment device on her lap. He looked around her neck: a cross. He looked at her sympathetically. I suppose so.

Tubes of light illuminated the metal chamber he was in. A smooth ding announced itself, and the doors closed shut. To Laurentius' surprise, the metal chamber began to move again. He stood, and made his way to a man he assumed was in charge. The man, covered in what seemed to be traditional dress for the era, with the exception of a large silver wig, and glasses that read 2015 across the front.

Salve, Laurentius began.

The man returned a confused look, then returned to gazing out the window. He smelled of wine.

Aut ubi sum? Quis hic locus?

The metal chamber shook once again, slightly, disrupting Laurentius' balance. A voice rang out over the loudspeaker, but Laurentius couldn't make out what it had said. The metal chamber made another stop, but Laurentius wasn't prepared. He fell onto the floor below as a wave of people exited. He got up and followed the crowd, which weaved through tunnels. He struggled to take everything in: Musicians lined the enclosed street. Few vendors, from what he understood. He continued until he reached a flight of stairs. He ascended, and was astounded by what he saw.

Bright lights flashed around him, in all directions. What was the steady hum of voices, interrupted occasionally by an outburst, had now turned into an onslaught of voices and action. To his left and right, the streets were lined with people all moving towards a central location, where a large spire reached into the heavens. Atop this spire was a sphere. He looked into the sky.

No stars. He pondered. Suddenly, a realization came to him, and with it, a wave of happiness and relief. There were no stars, for he was above them all: Might these be the plains of Asphodel? They were more beautiful than he'd ever imagined.

Suddenly, a man in a similar outfit – a black coat, black pants, white shirt – ran up to him. Black metal covered his eyes, and frost came out of his mouth when he spoke.

Dick! he said, grabbing Laurentius by the arm. So overwhelmed, Laurentius had no expectation of arguing. He followed this man.

Live in 30.

ideas_up.xsum::29: Philip Cullen, 57, received a six-month suspended sentence for illegally capturing two Large Blue butterflies at protected reserves in Somerset and Gloucestershire during 2015. Bristol Magistrates' Court heard that Cullen was observed chasing a specimen with a child's net at Daneway Banks in June 2015, then spotted again at Collard Hill. Authorities raided his home, discovering thirty trays of butterflies, including several Large Blues, confirming his systematic collection. Prosecutor Ian Jackson emphasized that charges were filed specifically to deter actions that endanger fragile species. Consequently, Cullen was sentenced to six months imprisonment, suspended for two years, alongside 250 hours of mandatory unpaid labor. The Gloucestershire Wildlife Trust hailed this as a landmark breakthrough in curbing wildlife crime. ideas_up.xsum::33: A study published within Science Translation Medicine revealed that caffeine functions beyond being a simple stimulant, as it actively decelerates the internal biological clock. Because light exposure typically regulates our circadian phase, participants remained in dim lighting to isolate caffeine's specific effects. These findings offer potential therapeutic avenues for treating sleep disorders and assisting early-rising larks in better synchronizing with standard societal schedules. He argued that people frequently perceive themselves as helpless slaves to their biological clocks, mistakenly believing their sleep patterns are immutable. However, these data clearly demonstrate that human circadian rhythms are malleable and subject to modification. Much of our chronic late-night wakefulness stems from modifiable environmental variables, specifically our consistent intake of caffeine and excessive exposure to artificial blue light during evening hours. By adjusting these specific lifestyle factors, individuals can exert greater control over their biological cycles, effectively managing their internal clocks to improve overall health outcomes, increase daily alertness, and ensure sufficient restorative sleep. Ultimately, this research provides a framework for understanding how common dietary stimulants interact with complex physiological systems to dictate our daily energy levels and long-term sleep health. By recognizing these subtle influences, we move toward a more proactive, evidence-based approach to managing our personal sleep hygiene and circadian alignment in a modern, light-saturated, and highly caffeinated world.

ideas_up.xsum::35: The so-called International Verification Commission claims it has successfully put a small, symbolic portion of Eta's extensive arsenal under official seal. So reaction to the latest development will be crucial. The verification team says Eta has now put some of its weapons beyond use. ideas_up.xsum::43: The Egtved Girl was excavated in 1921 within a burial mound in the Jutland Peninsula, accompanied by the cremated remains of a young child. She was approximately 16 to 18 years old at her death. Originally assumed to be Danish, recent research published in Scientific Reports challenges this historical narrative. A team led by Dr. Karin Margarita Frei from the National Museum of Denmark analyzed the girl's teeth for radioactive strontium isotopes. Strontium, naturally present in the Earth's crust, enters the food chain and is absorbed into human enamel during development. Because strontium isotope ratios vary significantly by geological region, the specific levels found in her teeth indicate she spent her childhood in the Black Forest of southwestern Germany, situated 800 kilometers south of her Danish grave. While historians previously established she was born on a summer day in 1370 BC, her coffin offered few geographical clues. Her sophisticated clothing suggested high social status. Although acidic groundwater dissolved her bones, her blonde hair, teeth, nails, brain, and skin were exceptionally preserved. Dr. Frei’s team reconstructed the final two years of her life by analyzing chemical signatures along her 23-centimeter hair strands. This analytical sleuthing revealed she traveled extensively before her death. Dr. Frei noted that 13 to 15 months prior to passing, she resided in a location with a strontium signature matching her birthplace. She then moved to an area potentially identified as Jutland. After nine to ten months there, she returned to her original homeland for four to six months before traveling to her final resting place in Egtved. This timeline marks the first instance of researchers accurately mapping the movements of a prehistoric individual. Prof. Kristian Kristiansen of the University of Gothenburg stated the discovery confirms Bronze Age Denmark maintained intimate diplomatic ties with southern Germany, suggesting the girl was likely a bride sent to solidify political alliances. During the Bronze Age, southern Germany and Denmark acted as dominant power centers, functioning much like proto-kingdoms. Archaeological evidence confirms frequent cultural and economic exchanges between these regions, supporting the theory that the Egtved Girl was a southern German noblewoman married off to a Jutlandic man to secure a strategic pact between two influential clans. While geologically ancient areas like Bornholm, Sweden, or Norway were considered as potential birthplaces, southwestern Germany remains the statistically strongest match according to the data. Dr. Frei and Prof. Kristiansen intend to continue this methodology by testing strontium levels in other Danish archaeological finds to map the migratory patterns of prehistoric populations. These findings provide a revolutionary window into the complex social structures and long-distance connectivity characterizing European Bronze Age societies, proving that people moved across vast, rugged landscapes with far greater frequency than previously theorized. By examining isotopic data alongside material culture, researchers are successfully bridging the gap between ancient biological evidence and political history, revealing a prehistoric world defined by dynamic human interaction, arranged marriages, and far-reaching trade networks that connected distant European power centers through deliberate, well-documented human migration.

Dr. Fatoumata Nafo-Traoré, who leads the Roll Back Malaria Partnership, noted after her West African tour that medical resources are now entirely diverted toward Ebola, causing a silent crisis. Pediatric wards once overcrowded with malaria patients are now ghost areas, leaving thousands of curable cases untreated. In 2012, malaria claimed 7,000 lives across the three most affected nations: 4,000 in Sierra Leone, 2,000 in Liberia, and 1,000 in Guinea. Most victims were young children, a tragedy made worse because effective, low-cost interventions exist. Nafo-Traoré fears that hard-won progress in malaria prevention is collapsing under the weight of the Ebola epidemic. Although mortality rates had halved over the previous five years, the current emergency threatens to reverse these gains entirely.

The crisis is compounded by a profound breakdown in public trust. Many residents view health workers as vectors for the Ebola virus rather than healers, leading families to avoid clinics even when children show severe symptoms. Furthermore, the clinical overlap between malaria and Ebola creates diagnostic chaos. Because both diseases initially manifest as high fevers, patients are terrified that seeking help for malaria will result in forced internment at Ebola isolation centers. While treatment protocols now mandate administering anti-malarials alongside Ebola screenings, the psychological barrier remains high. This creates a dangerous scenario where malaria remains undiagnosed and untreated until it becomes fatal.

The Roll Back Malaria Partnership, a coalition of 500 organizations, highlights that while Sierra Leone and Guinea achieved significant bed net distribution milestones last year, Liberia lagged behind. Now, officials in Liberia must navigate the dual challenge of distributing preventative nets while containing a viral outbreak. The logistical strain is immense. Ebola has shifted from isolated rural bush areas into densely populated capital cities, facilitating rapid transmission. Dr. Nafo-Traoré observed checkpoints along her road trip from Conakry to Sierra Leone where travelers underwent temperature screenings and mandatory hand-washing. While these measures demonstrate improved organization, she argues the global response arrived far too late.

The systemic weakness of regional health infrastructure is a primary concern. Because malaria-related fevers frequently mimic early Ebola symptoms, they inevitably overwhelm the limited capacity of Ebola treatment units. A coordinated approach is essential to screen for malaria independently, keeping non-Ebola patients out of high-risk containment zones. This distinction is vital for maintaining the functionality of the general health system. If malaria patients are not separated or treated promptly, hospitals will become hotspots for secondary infections.

Communication networks across all 15 West African nations remain highly active, which accelerates the spread of information and misinformation alike. The current situation acts as a stark wake-up call for the international community regarding the fragility of these healthcare systems. Without sustained support for malaria programs, the death toll from preventable illnesses will likely dwarf the direct casualties of the Ebola virus itself. We are currently witnessing a dual-front war where the lack of manpower and resources has turned former centers of recovery into zones of abandonment. If the focus remains exclusively on Ebola, the secondary public health consequences will inevitably cause a massive, long-term setback for regional mortality rates. The international community must act now to restore confidence and supply chains for essential medicines.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::0: For several decades, regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized where the tests being utilized examined mutations and structural and numerical chromosomal damage. This has served the genetic toxicity community well when most of the substances being tested were amenable to such assays. The outcome from this testing is usually a dichotomous (yes/no) evaluation of test results, and in many instances, the information is only used to determine whether a substance has carcinogenic potential or not. Over the same time period, mechanisms and modes of action (MOAs) that elucidate a wider range of genomic damage involved in many adverse health outcomes have been recognized. These mechanisms now encompass oxidative stress pathways, DNA repair inhibition, and replication fork stalling, each contributing uniquely to genomic instability. In addition, a paradigm shift in applied genetic toxicology is moving the field toward a more quantitative dose-response analysis and point-of-departure (PoD) determination with a focus on risks to exposed humans. This is directing emphasis on genomic damage that is likely to induce changes associated with a variety of adverse health outcomes, such as developmental defects, reproductive failure, and accelerated biological aging. This paradigm shift is moving the testing emphasis for genetic damage from a hazard identification only evaluation to a more comprehensive risk assessment approach that provides more insightful information for decision makers regarding the potential risk of genetic damage to exposed humans. To enable this broader context for examining genetic damage, a next generation testing strategy needs to take into account a broader, more flexible approach to testing, and ultimately modeling, of genomic damage as it relates to human exposure. This is consistent with the larger risk assessment context being used in regulatory decision making, which increasingly demands integrated, multi-disciplinary evidence. As presented here, this flexible approach for examining genomic damage focuses on testing for relevant genomic effects that can be, as best as possible, associated with an adverse health effect. The most desired linkage for risk to humans would be changes in loci associated with human diseases, whether in somatic or germ cells, including specific oncogenes or tumor-suppressor genes. The outline of a flexible approach and associated considerations are presented in a series of nine steps, some of which can occur in parallel, which was developed through a collaborative effort by leading genetic toxicologists from academia, government, and industry through the International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI) Health and Environmental Sciences Institute (HESI) Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee (GTTC). The ultimate goal is to provide quantitative data to model the potential risk levels of substances, which induce genomic damage contributing to human adverse health outcomes. Any good risk assessment begins with asking the appropriate risk management questions in a planning and scoping effort. This step sets up the problem to be addressed (e.g., broadly, does genomic damage need to be addressed, and if so, how to proceed, accounting for population susceptibility factors). The next two steps assemble what is known about the problem by building a knowledge base about the substance of concern and developing a rational biological argument for why testing for genomic damage is needed or not, considering chemical structure-activity relationships. By focusing on the risk management problem and potential genomic damage of concern, the next step of assay(s) selection takes place. The work-up of the problem during the earlier steps provides the insight to which assays would most likely produce the most meaningful data. This discussion does not detail the wide range of genomic damage tests available, but points to types of testing systems that can be very useful, including high-throughput sequencing and transcriptomic signatures. Once the assays are performed and analyzed, the relevant data sets are selected for modeling potential risk. From this point on, the data are evaluated and modeled as they are for any other toxicology endpoint, such as organ-specific organ toxicity or systemic endocrine disruption. Any observed genomic damage/effects (or genetic event(s)) can be modeled via a dose-response analysis and determination of an estimated PoD. When a quantitative risk analysis is needed for decision making, a parallel exposure assessment effort is performed (exposure assessment is not detailed here as this is not the focus of this discussion; guidelines for this assessment exist elsewhere). Then the PoD for genomic damage is used with the exposure information to develop risk estimations (e.g., using reference dose (RfD), margin of exposure (MOE) approaches) in a risk characterization and presented to risk managers for informing decision making. This approach is applicable now for incorporating genomic damage results into the decision-making process for assessing potential adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans and is consistent with the ILSI HESI Risk Assessment in the 21st Century (RISK21) roadmap. This applies to any substance to which humans are exposed, including pharmaceuticals, agricultural products, food additives, and other chemicals, as well as environmental pollutants. It is time for regulatory bodies to incorporate the broader knowledge and insights provided by genomic damage results into the assessments of risk to more fully understand the potential of adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans, thus improving the assessment of risk due to genomic damage. The historical use of genomic damage data as a yes/no gateway for possible cancer risk has been too narrowly focused in risk assessment, ignoring non-carcinogenic, chronic toxicities. The recent advances in assaying for and understanding genomic damage, including eventually epigenetic alterations, obviously add a greater wealth of information for determining potential risk to humans, allowing for better identification of sensitive subpopulations. Regulatory bodies need to embrace this paradigm shift from hazard identification to quantitative analysis and to incorporate the wider range of genomic damage in their assessments of risk to humans. The quantitative analyses and methodologies discussed here can be readily applied to genomic damage testing results now. Indeed, with the passage of the recent update to the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) in the US, the new generation testing strategy for genomic damage described here provides a regulatory agency (here the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), but suitable for others) a golden opportunity to reexamine the way it addresses risk-based genomic damage testing (including hazard identification and exposure). Environ. Mol. Mutagen. 58:264-283, 2017. © 2016 The Authors. Environmental and Molecular Mutagenesis Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::1: Nutritional supplements potentially enhance the developmental trajectory of infants born preterm or small for gestational age (SGA), yet they simultaneously raise concerns regarding heightened risks of long-term metabolic dysfunction. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the clinical effects of macronutrient supplementation for these vulnerable infants on subsequent cognitive development and metabolic health. Our comprehensive search strategy encompassed OvidMedline, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from inception through April 1, 2019, alongside clinical trial registries including controlled-trials.com, clinicaltrials.gov, and anzctr.org.au. Eligible studies included randomised or quasirandomised trials where the primary intent was increasing macronutrient intake to bolster infant growth, provided these studies assessed post-discharge clinical outcomes. Co-primary endpoints were cognitive impairment and metabolic risk, specifically evaluated across three developmental stages: toddlers (under 3 years), childhood (3 to 8 years), and adolescence (9 to 18 years). Two independent reviewers extracted pertinent data, while the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool facilitated quality assessment, with findings synthesized using random-effect models. We identified twenty-one randomised and one quasirandomised trial, representing 3,680 infants of variable methodological rigor. Among toddlers, supplementation did not significantly alter cognitive impairment (relative risk [RR] 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67 to 1.49; P = 0.99), nor were there meaningful differences in cognitive scores (mean difference [MD] 0.57; 95% CI -0.71 to 1.84; P = 0.38) or motor development scores (MD 1.16; 95% CI -0.32 to 2.65; P = 0.12). Notably, fewer supplemented children exhibited motor impairment (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.62 to 0.94; P = 0.01), suggesting a potential motor benefit. Subgroup analyses revealed that supplementation improved cognitive scores significantly in boys (MD 5.60; 95% CI 1.07 to 10.14; P = 0.02) but not in girls (MD -2.04; 95% CI -7.04 to 2.95; P = 0.42), while demonstrating no cognitive or motor impact for the SGA subgroup. During childhood, no significant differences appeared in cognitive impairment (RR 0.81; 95% CI 0.26 to 2.57; P = 0.72) or cognitive scores (MD 1.02; 95% CI -1.91 to 3.95; P = 0.50). Furthermore, there were no observed disparities in blood pressure, triglyceride levels, or low-density lipoprotein (LDL) concentrations (all P > 0.05). However, supplemented children demonstrated lower fasting glucose (MD -0.20 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.34 to -0.06; P = 0.005) and elevated high-density lipoprotein (HDL) concentrations (MD 0.11 mmol/L; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.19; P = 0.02). Subgroup analysis confirmed no blood pressure divergence based on sex or SGA status. By adolescence, no differences remained regarding blood pressure, triglycerides, LDL, HDL, fasting glucose, insulin resistance, or insulin levels (all P > 0.05). Our findings are constrained by considerable unexplained heterogeneity, low-quality evidence, and a dearth of data beyond early childhood. In summary, early macronutrient supplementation for infants born small showed no conclusive evidence of altering long-term cognitive function, though it may reduce toddler motor impairment. Unlike observational reports, our meta-analysis indicates that early supplementation actually improves specific metabolic markers during childhood. CRD42019127858.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::2: Objectives Recently, two point-of-care (PoC) feline immunodeficiency virus (FIV) antibody test kits, specifically Witness and Anigen Rapid, were reported as being able to differentiate FIV-vaccinated from FIV-infected cats at a single time point, irrespective of the gap between testing and last vaccination, spanning zero to seven years. The primary aim of this current study was to investigate systematically anti-FIV antibody production over time in response to the recommended primary FIV vaccination series. Methods First, residual plasma from the original study was tested using a sensitive laboratory-based ELISA to determine whether negative results with PoC testing were due to reduced as opposed to absent antibodies to the gp40 protein. Second, a prospective study was performed using immunologically naive client-owned kittens and cats given a primary FIV vaccination series using a commercially available inactivated whole cell and inactivated whole virus vaccine, Fel-O-Vax FIV, administered via three subcutaneous injections at four-week intervals. These subjects were tested systematically up to eleven times over six months using four commercially available PoC FIV antibody kits: SNAP FIV/FeLV Combo, which detects antibodies to p15 and p24; Witness FeLV/FIV, which targets gp40; Anigen Rapid FIV/FeLV, targeting p24 and gp40; and VetScan FeLV/FIV Rapid, targeting p24. Results The laboratory-based ELISA showed cats from the original study vaccinated within the previous zero to fifteen months had detectable levels of antibodies to gp40, despite testing negative with two kits that use gp40 as a capture antigen, namely the Witness and Anigen Rapid kits. The prospective study showed that antibody testing with SNAP Combo and VetScan Rapid was positive in all cats two weeks after the second primary FIV vaccination and remained positive for the duration of the study, with twelve of twelve and ten of twelve cats testing positive, respectively. Antibody testing with Witness and Anigen Rapid was also positive in a high proportion of cats two weeks after the second primary FIV vaccination, measuring eight of twelve and seven of twelve respectively, but antibody levels declined below the level of detection in most cats, specifically ten of twelve, by one month after the third final primary FIV vaccination. All cats tested negative using Witness and Anigen Rapid six months after the third primary FIV vaccination. Conclusions and relevance This study has shown that a primary course of FIV vaccination does not interfere with FIV antibody testing in cats using Witness and Anigen Rapid, provided primary vaccination has not occurred within the previous six months. Consequently, Witness and Anigen Rapid antibody test kits can be used reliably to determine FIV infection status at the time of annual booster vaccination to detect vaccine breakthroughs. The duration of antibody response following annual booster vaccination and the resulting effect on PoC kit testing requires further research, as the precise biochemical mechanisms for the variation in kit performance remain unclear.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare monogenic disorder characterized by benign tumors in multiple organs as well as a high prevalence of epilepsy, intellectual disability and autism. TSC is caused by inactivating mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes. Heterozygocity induces hyperactivation of mTOR which can be inhibited by mTOR inhibitors, such as rapamycin, which have proven efficacy in the treatment of TSC-associated symptoms. The aim of the present study was (1) to identify molecular changes associated with social and cognitive deficits in the brain tissue of Tsc1 +/- mice and (2) to investigate the molecular effects of rapamycin treatment, which has been shown to ameliorate genotype-related behavioural deficits. Molecular alterations in the frontal cortex and hippocampus of Tsc1 +/- and control mice, with or without rapamycin treatment, were investigated. A quantitative mass spectrometry-based shotgun proteomic approach (LC-MS E ) was employed as an unbiased method to detect changes in protein levels. Changes identified in the initial profiling stage were validated using selected reaction monitoring (SRM). Protein Set Enrichment Analysis was employed to identify dysregulated pathways. LC-MS E analysis of Tsc1 +/- mice and controls ( n = 30) identified 51 proteins changed in frontal cortex and 108 in the hippocampus. Bioinformatic analysis combined with targeted proteomic validation revealed several dysregulated molecular pathways. Using targeted assays, proteomic alterations in the hippocampus validated the pathways "myelination", "dendrite," and "oxidative stress", an upregulation of ribosomal proteins and the mTOR kinase. LC-MS E analysis was also employed on Tsc1 +/- and wildtype mice ( n = 34) treated with rapamycin or vehicle. Rapamycin treatment exerted a stronger proteomic effect in Tsc1 +/- mice with significant changes (mainly decreased expression) in 231 and 106 proteins, respectively. The cellular pathways "oxidative stress" and "apoptosis" were found to be affected in Tsc1 +/- mice and the cellular compartments "myelin sheet" and "neurofilaments" were affected by rapamycin treatment. Thirty-three proteins which were altered in Tsc1 +/- mice were normalized following rapamycin treatment, amongst them oxidative stress related proteins, myelin-specific and ribosomal proteins. Molecular changes in the Tsc1 +/- mouse brain were more prominent in the hippocampus compared to the frontal cortex. Pathways linked to myelination and oxidative stress response were prominently affected and, at least in part, normalized following rapamycin treatment. The results could aid in the identification of novel drug targets for the treatment of cognitive, social and psychiatric symptoms in autism spectrum disorders. Similar pathways have also been implicated in other psychiatric and neurodegenerative disorders and could imply similar disease processes. Thus, the potential efficacy of mTOR inhibitors warrants further investigation not only for autism spectrum disorders but also for other neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases.
