Expanding therapeutic scope, these findings suggest that targeted mTOR modulation might mitigate synaptic plasticity impairments, improve glutamate receptor signaling, and restore metabolic homeostasis in various neurological conditions.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::4: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems that can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues such as the heart in a controllable manner. However, cardiac toxicity induced by nanoSiO 2 has been recently related to abnormal calcium handling and energetic failure in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, the precise mechanisms underlying this energetic debacle remain unclear. In order to elucidate these mechanisms, this article explores the ex vivo heart function and mitochondria after exposure to nanoSiO 2 . The cumulative administration of nanoSiO 2 reduced the mechanical performance index of the rat heart with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) of 93 μg/mL, affecting the relaxation rate. In isolated mitochondria nanoSiO 2 was found to be internalized, inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation and significantly reducing the mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨ m ). The mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) was also induced with an increasing dose of nanoSiO 2 and partially recovered with, a potent blocker of the mPTP, Cyclosporine A (CsA). The activity of aconitase and thiol oxidation, in the adenine nucleotide translocase, were found to be reduced due to nanoSiO 2 exposure, suggesting that nanoSiO 2 induces the mPTP via thiol modification and ROS generation. In cardiac cells exposed to nanoSiO 2 , enhanced viability and reduction of H 2 O 2 were observed after application of a specific mitochondrial antioxidant, MitoTEMPO. Concomitantly, CsA treatment in adult rat cardiac cells reduced the nanoSiO 2 -triggered cell death and recovered ATP production (from 32.4 to 65.4%). Additionally, we performed evaluation of the mitochondrial effect of nanoSiO 2 in human cardiomyocytes. We observed a 40% inhibition of maximal oxygen consumption rate in mitochondria at 500 μg/mL. Under this condition we identified a remarkable diminution in the spare respiratory capacity. This data indicates that a reduction in the amount of extra ATP that can be produced by mitochondria during a sudden increase in energy demand. In human cardiomyocytes, increased LDH release and necrosis were found at increased doses of nanoSiO 2 , reaching 85 and 48%, respectively. Such deleterious effects were partially prevented by the application of CsA. Therefore, exposure to nanoSiO 2 affects cardiac function via mitochondrial dysfunction through the opening of the mPTP. The aforementioned effects can be partially avoided reducing ROS or retarding the opening of the mPTP. These novel strategies, which demonstrate improved contractile recovery and metabolic stabilization, could be considered as potential clinical therapies to effectively decrease the side effects of nanoSiO 2 exposure in future drug delivery systems.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::5: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears is well-documented, yet data regarding multiligament knee injuries remains sparse. This study investigates the clinical outcomes of these severe injuries, which consistently demonstrate lower RTP rates and significantly prolonged recovery durations compared to simple ACL ruptures. We hypothesize that injury complexity dictates functional prognosis; specifically, patients sustaining combined ACL and medial collateral ligament (MCL) tears likely experience superior recovery metrics than those suffering posterolateral corner or cruciate ligament damage. This retrospective cohort study, classified as Level 4 evidence, analyzed publicly available NFL injury records from 2000 to 2016. Researchers excluded athletes whose career cessation was dictated by non-orthopedic factors, such as retirement or roster decisions. Extracted variables included injury classification, physiological return markers, chronological days to clearance, game participation percentages, and post-injury performance efficiency. Fifty NFL athletes met the rigorous inclusion criteria. The aggregate RTP rate was 64.0%. Stratified analysis revealed that athletes with ACL/MCL tears achieved a 70.8% return rate, whereas those with combined ACL and posterior/lateral collateral ligament (PCL/LCL) tears recorded a lower 55.6% return rate (P = 0.26). The mean recovery duration for the entire cohort was 388.71 ± 198.52 days. Significant variance emerged in recovery time: ACL/MCL patients averaged 305.1 ± 58.9 days, while those with combined ACL/PCL/LCL injuries required 459.2 ± 245.1 days (P = 0.004), and frank knee dislocation patients required 609.3 ± 183.1 days (P < 0.0001). Furthermore, ACL/MCL patients demonstrated a 43.5% probability of regaining pre-injury performance levels, markedly exceeding the 18.5% observed in ACL/PCL/LCL cohorts (P < 0.001). These findings confirm that multiligament knee injuries severely compromise an athlete’s ability to resume professional football activities compared to isolated ACL pathologies. The data suggests that the anatomical involvement of the MCL provides a more favorable prognostic indicator for athletic longevity and performance restoration than PCL or lateral-sided ligamentous damage. Clinicians and team medical staff should utilize these specific recovery timeframes for realistic expectation management during the intensive rehabilitation process for elite players. Ultimately, injury complexity serves as a primary determinant for professional career viability and long-term functional success within the competitive NFL landscape.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension triggered by physical exertion serves as a critical biomarker for the underlying hemodynamic severity found in mitral stenosis. Despite this, the specific physiological determinants driving elevated pulmonary pressure during exercise remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to identify the precise parameters associated with pulmonary pressure responses in patients diagnosed with pure rheumatic mitral stenosis. Furthermore, we sought to quantify the long-term clinical consequences of exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension. One hundred thirty patients, predominantly women (94%) with a mean age of 45, underwent standardized exercise echocardiography. Comprehensive echocardiographic data were collected at rest and at peak exertion using symptom-limited graded ramp bicycle protocols in the supine position. The primary clinical endpoint was the necessity for mitral valve intervention, encompassing both percutaneous and surgical procedures. Within the study cohort, systolic pulmonary artery pressure rose from 38.3 ± 13.4 mm Hg at rest to 65.8 ± 20.7 mm Hg during peak exercise. Statistical analysis revealed that increases in the mean mitral gradient, right ventricular systolic function, left atrial volume, and net atrioventricular compliance were independently correlated with systolic pulmonary artery pressure at peak exertion, even after adjusting for heart rate variability. During a median follow-up of 17 months, 46 adverse clinical events occurred. Multivariate Cox proportional-hazards analysis, adjusted for age and sex, identified peak systolic pulmonary artery pressure as a robust predictor of adverse outcomes with a hazard ratio of 1.025. Additionally, the New York Heart Association functional class and the synergistic interaction between mitral valve area and net atrioventricular compliance were identified as significant independent predictors of clinical deterioration. Time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curve analysis confirmed that models incorporating peak exercise pulmonary pressure outperformed models relying solely on resting measurements, providing statistically significant prognostic improvements starting at three years. In conclusion, the pulmonary artery pressure response in mitral stenosis patients is dictated by a complex interplay of transmitral gradients, cardiac compliance, atrial geometry, and ventricular function. Peak exercise pulmonary pressure serves as a vital prognostic indicator, offering substantial incremental value for risk stratification beyond the standard resting assessments and traditional valve area calculations typically used in routine clinical practice today.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::7: The impact of chronic liver disease on outcomes in patients with COVID-19 remains clinically uncertain, necessitating rigorous exploration. We analyzed outcomes for all adult inpatients with COVID-19 in France during 2020. We computed adjusted odds ratios to measure associations between chronic liver disease, specific alcohol use disorders, mechanical ventilation requirements, and day-30 in-hospital mortality. The final sample comprised 259,110 patients with a median age of 70 years, 52% of whom were men. This cohort included 15,476 patients with chronic liver disease and 10,006 with alcohol use disorders. Total deaths occurred in 38,203 patients, including 7,475 after mechanical ventilation and 2,941 with chronic liver disease. Adjusted odds ratios for mechanical ventilation and day-30 mortality were 1.54 and 1.79 for chronic liver disease; 0.55 and 0.54 for mild liver disease; 0.64 and 0.71 for compensated cirrhosis; 0.65 and 2.21 for decompensated cirrhosis; 0.34 and 1.38 for primary liver cancer; and 0.82 and 1.11 for alcohol use disorders, all showing statistical significance. Chronic viral hepatitis, non-viral chronic hepatitis, organ transplantation, and acquired immunodeficiency syndrome showed no significant association with COVID-19-related death. Overall, chronic liver disease increased the risk of death in France during 2020. Therapeutic effort limitation likely contributed to COVID-19-related mortality in French residents suffering from liver-related complications or alcohol use disorders. We examined outcomes of adults discharged from acute care, confirming that while mild liver disease, compensated cirrhosis, transplantation, or immunodepression did not elevate mortality risk, patients with alcohol use disorders, decompensated cirrhosis, or primary liver cancer faced higher mortality despite decreased access to mechanical ventilation. These findings suggest that systemic therapeutic limitations, rather than biological vulnerability alone, drove the observed excess mortality in these specific subgroups. Clinicians should recognize that patients with advanced liver pathologies were frequently denied life-sustaining interventions, potentially biasing mortality statistics. This study provides a comprehensive overview of how comorbid hepatic conditions influenced pandemic-era medical care and mortality trajectories within the French national healthcare system, highlighting significant disparities in resource allocation for vulnerable liver patients during the height of the viral crisis. Future protocols must address these ethical gaps in acute respiratory care.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::8: The coronavirus disease 2019, triggered by the SARS-CoV-2 pathogen, has generated immense global mortality rates. This virus presents a lethal risk to human biological integrity. Clinical symptoms of COVID-19 remain highly diverse, with twenty percent of infected individuals entering critical states. Primary manifestations involve severe lung function decline and irreversible pulmonary fibrosis. Respiratory degradation persists post-recovery, severely damaging patient psychological health, long-term well-being, and daily life quality. Study participants must satisfy simultaneous inclusion criteria: exceeding eighteen years of age, recovering from critical COVID-19, retaining post-recovery pulmonary fibrosis, and exhibiting Qi-Yin deficiency syndrome per traditional Chinese medicine protocols. Eligible candidates will undergo randomization into treatment or control cohorts. The treatment arm receives pirfenidone plus traditional Chinese medicine, while the control arm receives pirfenidone plus a traditional Chinese medicine placebo. Lung function metrics will be continuously monitored and meticulously recorded. By evaluating efficacy differences between these groups, this study investigates if traditional Chinese medicine enhances modern pharmaceutical outcomes for patients suffering from post-SARS-CoV-2 pulmonary fibrosis. Pulmonary fibrosis represents a fatal sequela; emerging research indicates pirfenidone delays forced expiratory vital capacity decline, partially reducing mortality. Furthermore, although traditional Chinese medicine demonstrates efficacy regarding general pulmonary fibrosis, its specific utility for COVID-19-related fibrosis remains unexplored. Therefore, a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized, interventional, prospective clinical trial has been designed to determine if this comprehensive, combined therapeutic approach is clinically feasible and capable of improving patient quality of life. This multicenter, parallel-group, randomized, interventional, prospective trial was officially registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under number ChiCTR2000033284 on the twenty-sixth of May 2020. This research framework aims to bridge the gap between traditional herbal interventions and modern antifibrotic drugs, potentially establishing a new standard of care for survivors. By focusing on the specific physiological markers of Qi-Yin deficiency alongside standard pulmonary testing, the researchers hope to validate the synergistic effects of these dual therapies. The study will provide rigorous data to clarify whether integrative strategies mitigate long-term respiratory damage, offering hope to those suffering from persistent, post-viral pulmonary scarring and chronic oxygen deprivation issues.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body temperature (Tb), evaporative water loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). Since anurans display pronounced sexual dimorphism, evidence suggests that these processes are further influenced by other factors such as vapour pressure deficit (VPD), sex and body mass (Mb). However, a limited number of studies have tested the generality of these results across a wide range of ecologically relevant ambient temperatures (Ta), while taking habitat use into account. Thus, the aim of this study was to investigate the role of Ta on Tb, whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR in three wild caught African anuran species with different ecological specialisations: the principally aquatic African clawed frog (Xenopus laevis), stream-breeding common river frog (Amietia delalandii), and the largely terrestrial raucous toad (Sclerophrys capensis). Experiments were conducted at a range of test temperatures (5-35 °C, at 5 °C increments). We found that VPD better predicted rates of EWL than Ta in two of the three species considered. Moreover, we found that Tb, whole-animal EWL and whole-animal SMR increased with increasing Ta, while Tb increased with increasing Mb in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis. Whole-animal SMR increased with increasing Mb in S. capensis only. We did not find any significant effect of VPD, Mb or sex on whole-animal EWL within species. Lastly, Mb did not influence Tb, whole-animal SMR and EWL in the principally aquatic X. laevis. These results suggest that Mb may not have the same effect on key physiological variables, and that the influence of Mb may also depend on the species ecological specialisation. Crucially, our data highlights that aquatic species exhibit distinct thermal buffering compared to terrestrial counterparts, potentially limiting the impact of mass-specific metabolic scaling. Thus, the generality of Mb as an important factor should be taken in the context of both physiology, precise thermal microhabitat use and broader species habitat specialisation.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis manifests as a profound neurocognitive impairment regarding the subjective sequencing of temporal events. This specific alteration of internal temporality is characteristically linked to localized thalamic involvement, particularly within the dorsomedial nucleus regions. We document two clinical cases involving acute ischaemic strokes situated precisely in that territory, where the clinical presentation centered entirely on this symptom. Crucially, its rapid recognition dictated the subsequent therapeutic approach. In both the first and second cases, we detail how the patient’s distorted perception of temporal flow acted as the primary diagnostic indicator for the underlying ischaemic condition. Broad awareness and academic dissemination of this specific thalamic-temporal association are vital for effective patient management. Such clinical vigilance allows physicians to significantly influence and modify the initial medical approach, ensuring timely intervention. Early identification of chronotaraxis as a sentinel symptom facilitates neuroprotective strategies that may prevent the further spread of thalamic damage. By halting infarct progression, clinicians can mitigate debilitating long-term sequelae, particularly those manifesting as severe cognitive deficits or executive dysfunction. Our findings emphasize that thalamic lesions disrupt the brain’s internal chronometer, leading to distinct sequencing failures that demand immediate neuroimaging. By integrating chronotaraxis into standard stroke protocols, medical teams can achieve better prognostic outcomes for patients suffering from thalamic territory involvement. This symptom serves as a unique guide, allowing neurologists to pinpoint deep-seated vascular pathology that might otherwise be overlooked during initial examinations. Ultimately, the systematic evaluation of temporal processing represents a critical, underutilized tool in acute neurology, offering a pathway to reduce permanent brain injury and enhance post-stroke cognitive recovery. The persistence of these temporal deficits often correlates with the extent of white matter disruption near the dorsomedial nucleus, highlighting the necessity for precise monitoring and early pharmacological support to stabilize neural pathways and preserve future functionality in vulnerable populations facing acute ischaemic events within these deep brain structures.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::11: Infectious diseases like influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2 spread when virus-laden particles expelled by an infected host are inhaled by others, a process defined as airborne transmission. These pathogens concentrate heavily within the expiratory jet rather than dispersing uniformly throughout a room, yet this critical near-field exposure remains poorly quantified. Accurately modeling transmission involves numerous variables that are often poorly constrained, necessitating vast ensembles of simulations to capture the true range of uncertainty. Unfortunately, existing high-fidelity fluid dynamics models are computationally prohibitive, restricting our ability to explore these parametric uncertainties effectively. To address this, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets, or QuaRAD. This efficient framework simulates particle evolution post-expulsion, their specific deposition patterns within a susceptible person’s nasal cavity, and the resulting probability of primary infection. We executed 10,000 distinct scenarios to evaluate SARS-CoV-2 transmission risks. Results indicate that infection probability fluctuates significantly depending on environmental conditions and individual behavior, with risk peaks consistently occurring in close proximity to the source. In over 50% of our test cases, the physical distance required to mitigate these near-field transmission enhancements exceeded the standard two-meter (six-foot) recommendation, provided the source remains unmasked. Crucially, the extent of this near-field danger zone is primarily determined by the initial expiration velocity of the cough or breath. Our analysis demonstrates that maintaining at least two meters of separation from an infectious individual significantly lowers the intake of airborne virions. However, because this safe distance varies wildly based on individual physiological factors, airflow patterns, and environmental humidity, it is not a universal panacea. Consequently, when sustaining such distance is physically impossible, additional protective measures are essential. Utilizing high-efficiency respiratory protection, such as N95 respirators, provides a vital secondary defense against inhaled pathogens. These findings underscore that while distancing is a primary tool for public health, it must be supplemented by reliable personal protective equipment to account for the inherent, extreme variability in airborne viral exposure dynamics across diverse, real-world social settings.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures are inherently contaminated wounds harboring diverse gram-positive and gram-negative bacterial organisms; consequently, aggressive wide-spectrum antibiotic therapy is mandatory within the clinical treatment plan. Prophylactic antibiotics must be initiated immediately after injury, ideally within three hours, as delayed administration significantly elevates the subsequent infection rate. Surprisingly, surgical debridement performed within twelve hours does not independently influence infection rates if patients receive timely systemic antibiotics. Utilizing an antibiotic bead pouch or vacuum-assisted wound closure systems effectively mitigates secondary nosocomial contamination risks and prevents deep tissue colonization. Every open fracture inherently constitutes a complex soft-tissue injury; thus, clinicians should prioritize soft-tissue management as the primary factor determining successful bone healing and ultimate functional restoration of the affected extremity. Formulating a comprehensive soft-tissue reconstruction plan must occur during the initial wound assessment and primary fixation phase, rather than treating this as a secondary, consecutive process. Early involvement of a specialized soft-tissue surgeon is essential, ideally on the night of the injury, to optimize outcomes. Selecting an appropriate fracture fixation method depends on specific anatomic factors, including the bone involved, fracture location—whether intra-articular, metaphyseal, or diaphyseal—the severity of soft-tissue damage, wound contamination levels, and the patient’s overall physiologic status. Because multiple fixation methods may be viable for a single injury, the surgeon's personal expertise and local implant availability remain critical variables. Successful management requires a deep understanding of bone healing biology. Essential cornerstones for achieving bony union include optimizing host systemic biology, carefully evaluating the patient's nutritional status, managing medications to avoid contraindications, and strictly eradicating existing infection. Surgeons should actively consider early bone grafting or the application of advanced osteobiologics to promote union in acute open fractures, especially when addressing potential delayed healing or established nonunion. Proactive management of these physiological parameters, combined with precise surgical technique and timely intervention, remains the gold standard for restoring limb function and preventing long-term complications in patients suffering from severe open orthopedic trauma.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of behavioral compliance frequently emerge regarding health activities like dieting, exercise, and sleep hygiene. Whether these fluctuating patterns exist among users of chronic medications remains unknown. We aimed to quantify the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy following a prolonged, significant lapse in medication use and identify specific socioeconomic or clinical factors associated with returning to consistent compliance. METHODS: We analyzed 26,636 new users of osteoporosis therapies, including alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate, who were aged 65 or older. These patients experienced an extended refill lapse, defined as a period of 60 consecutive days without acquiring any osteoporosis prescription. Survival curves estimated the duration until therapy resumption. We calculated the statistical association between patient demographics and treatment resumption rates using Cox proportional hazards analysis, while a case crossover analysis examined whether specific healthcare events triggered return to compliance. RESULTS: Of patients pausing therapy for 60 days, 30% restarted treatment within 6 months, while 50% restarted within 2 years. Among individuals with at least 6 months of continuous prior usage, 42% restarted within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger patients, female gender, and prior fracture history correlated with higher likelihoods of returning after gaps. Recent hip fractures, nursing home discharges, and bone mineral density testing also served as significant predictors for resuming treatment. CONCLUSION: Extended, frequent gaps in treatment are common among osteoporosis medication users. Because clinical effectiveness of these specific drugs when utilized in an interrupted, intermittent manner remains largely unknown, future compliance interventions must emphasize the absolute necessity for continuous, uninterrupted medication use. Further rigorous research is required to understand why patients frequently endure months without refilling prescriptions and whether these utilization patterns extend to other types of chronic medications, such as those for hypertension or diabetes, where consistent adherence is fundamentally vital for maintaining long-term patient health outcomes and preventing severe, costly medical complications.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community, known as dysbiosis, correlate with severe gastrointestinal and systemic autoimmune diseases in vertebrates. Yet, identifying specific pathogenic taxa, susceptible intestinal regions, and critical developmental windows remains challenging. Knowledge gaps persist regarding non-model organisms, despite the recognized importance of microbiota for long-term health. We investigated microbial shifts during dysbiosis across different gastrointestinal segments in the ostrich, a long-lived bird exhibiting high juvenile mortality. We analyzed 16S rRNA gene composition within the ileum, cecum, and colon of 68 ostriches that succumbed to suspected enterocolitis during their first three months, comparing these against 50 healthy, age-matched controls. Integrating these findings with longitudinal environmental and fecal data allowed us to pinpoint pathogen sources and determine exactly when dysbiosis-linked bacteria colonize the host. Diseased ostriches exhibited significantly reduced microbial alpha diversity and distinct beta diversity profiles across all three gut regions compared to healthy counterparts. This inverse relationship between low diversity and clinical disease remained constant throughout the ileum, whereas its strength diminished with age in the cecum and colon. Specific taxa, notably Enterobacteriaceae, Peptostreptococcaceae, Porphyromonadaceae, and Clostridium, were strongly linked to mortality, while Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae, Erysipelotrichaceae, Turicibacter, and Roseburia characterized healthy states. Environmental monitoring of food, water, and soil substrates yielded no evidence of these dysbiosis-associated bacteria, suggesting external transmission is not the primary driver. Instead, repeated fecal analysis revealed that pathobionts were present shortly after hatching; these microbes proliferated rapidly in individuals possessing low microbial diversity, ultimately triggering high mortality rates several weeks later. Determining the precise origins of these pathobionts in neonates and identifying the specific factors governing the successful establishment of a stable, diverse gut microbiome are essential steps. Unraveling these complex interactions is vital for understanding both the fundamental mechanisms of dysbiosis and the broader trajectory of avian host development during the vulnerable post-hatching period. We present our findings as a Video Abstract for further detailed examination.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the fundamental reason for the quantum speedup, specifically why quantum algorithms require fewer computational steps than classical counterparts. We extend their formal representation to the process of setting the problem itself. The initial measurement selects a setting at random, while Bob, the problem setter, unitarily changes it into the desired one. This representation is accessible to Bob and any external observer, yet it remains fundamentally inaccessible to Alice, the problem solver. Access would reveal the function computed by the black box, which must remain hidden from her. We resort to relational quantum mechanics to explain this. To Alice, the projection of the quantum state caused by the initial measurement is effectively retarded until the conclusion of her problem-solving action. To her, the algorithm input state remains one of total, complete ignorance regarding the setting. Through black box computations, she unitarily sends it into the output state that, for each possible setting, encodes the corresponding solution acquired by the final measurement. We show that we can ascribe to the final measurement the selection of any part—say the R-th part—of the random outcome from the initial measurement. This projects the input state to Alice onto a state of lower entropy where she knows a corresponding part of the problem setting. The quantum algorithm is a sum over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th parts of the setting, performs the black box computations still required to identify the solution. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, this retrocausality model provides the exact number of black box computations required to solve it. Conversely, given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R that explains its speedup. R = 1/2 always yields the number of black box computations required by an existing quantum algorithm and the order of magnitude required by the optimal one.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and surgical interventions often elevate the risk of dangerous thrombosis events because modified blood flow patterns fundamentally alter the mechanical stimuli exerted upon individual blood cells traversing the cardiac chambers. Specifically, the precise degree of platelet activation is heavily influenced by the specific magnitude and nature of mechanical stresses present within complex hemodynamic environments. In this study, we analyze flow within the left ventricle using a computational model built from patient-specific imaging data. The ventricular flow is governed by the Navier-Stokes equations, while mitral valve dynamics are represented by a parameterized model capturing the projected opening area. A finite element method resolves these equations, generating high-fidelity simulations of velocity fields and pressure distributions. A triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor is then applied to isolate and distinguish between rigid body rotational flow, irrotational straining flow, and pure shear flow. This advanced decomposition enables the separation of three distinct flow structures, each delivering a unique mechanical stimulus to blood cells. We systematically compare these results against simulations incorporating a mitral valve clip intervention, which induces significant, localized modifications to the ventricular flow architecture. We observed that shear stress within the clip-treated cases increased more substantially than rotational or straining components compared to the untreated baseline. Notably, a 64 percent reduction in valve opening area triggered a 90 percent rise in rotation and strain, while causing a dramatic 150 percent surge in shear stress. This computational framework establishes a robust process for patient-specific simulation of clinical cardiac interventions, providing granular insights into resulting blood flow dynamics. Ultimately, this methodology supports more accurate clinical risk assessments regarding platelet activation and potential thrombosis, offering a quantitative basis for evaluating how specific anatomical repairs or prosthetic implants might inadvertently promote adverse physiological responses within the vulnerable, turbulent, and recirculating zones of the human heart.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed within the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. follows the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to 130 pc from the Galactic Centre (GC), where flux levels drop rapidly. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. analyses reveal that the cosmic-ray (CR) density profile declines with distance, supporting the existence of a steady cosmic PeVatron at the GC. In this paper, we extend this investigation to obtain a precise characterisation of the correlation with matter, searching for additional features and individual gamma-ray sources within the inner 200 pc. Using 250 hours of H.E.S.S. data and refined techniques, we execute a detailed morphology study of the diffuse VHE emission across the GC ridge and reconstruct its total spectrum. We demonstrate that emission correlated with dense matter spans the entire CMZ, accounting for approximately half of the total diffuse flux. Furthermore, we detect emission at higher latitudes, likely resulting from hadronic collisions of CRs within less dense regions of the interstellar medium. We identify an additional emission component centred on the GC, extending roughly 15 pc, which is consistent with a steep CR density gradient and confirms a central particle accelerator. Our results show the full ridge spectrum matches previous central measurements, suggesting a single particle population permeates the entire CMZ. Finally, we report the discovery of a VHE gamma-ray source near the GC radio arc, which we argue is produced by the pulsar wind nebula candidate G0.13-0.11. This discovery implies complex magnetic field interactions and acceleration mechanisms are actively shaping the local high-energy environment. These findings clarify the energetic processes governing the CMZ, providing empirical evidence for particle transport and acceleration efficiency within the turbulent, high-density conditions found deep inside our Galaxy's innermost heart.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations for developmental coordination disorder, initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability, aim to address vital inquiries regarding the formal definition, early diagnosis, standardized assessment, multimodal intervention, and psychosocial impacts of DCD relevant for daily clinical practice. Key questions spanning five distinct domains were rigorously investigated through systematic literature reviews and formal expert consensus protocols. For recommendations grounded in empirical evidence, comprehensive literature searches regarding neurological mechanisms, diagnostic assessment, and therapeutic intervention were updated from the 2012 guidelines. Entirely new searches were conducted for psychosocial issues and the specific needs of adolescents and adults. Evidence was strictly rated according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine levels and translated into actionable clinical advice. For recommendations based on formal consensus, two meetings of an international, multidisciplinary panel were held alongside five Delphi rounds to establish good clinical practice standards. Thirty-five total recommendations were formulated. Eight relied on literature evidence, split between three assessment and five intervention points. Twenty-two were revised from 2012. Novel recommendations address diagnostic nuances, assessment techniques, and psychosocial challenges. Additionally, one recommendation highlights active video games as valuable adjuncts to traditional activity-oriented or participation-oriented interventions, while two specific entries now support adolescents and adults living with DCD. The CPR-DCD provides a comprehensive overview of DCD, synthesizing current research and expert consensus to reflect the state of the art for clinicians and scientists across varied professional disciplines. These international recommendations serve as a robust foundation for national policy development. They offer refined guidance on clinical assessment, provide a critical synopsis of current research on disorder mechanisms, detail psychosocial implications for patient care, and represent the first international effort to formally address the long-term clinical trajectories of adolescents and adults diagnosed with DCD, ensuring that specialized support remains accessible across the entire lifespan for those affected by these complex motor coordination challenges.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension induces mood disorders, which fluctuate based on specific antihypertensive medication types. Depression correlates with altered basal brain asymmetry, specifically within the frontal cortex, a region crucial for regulating systemic blood pressure. Vasoactive compounds further modulate this hemispheric asymmetry, directly impacting cognitive processing capabilities. We investigated the bilateral activity of various neuropeptidases within the frontal cortex, serving as proxies for the functional status of mood-regulating neuropeptides. Utilizing arylamide derivatives as fluorometric substrates, we quantified enzyme activity across left and right frontal cortices in Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) controls and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHRs). We compared these against groups treated with captopril (CAP), propranolol (PRO), or the hypertensive agent N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. Systolic blood pressure (SBP) was recorded across all cohorts. Untreated WKY, CAP-treated WKY, PRO-treated WKY, and CAP-treated SHRs maintained normotensive SBP levels. Conversely, WKY treated with N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester, untreated SHRs, and SHRs receiving PRO or N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester exhibited hypertensive SBP profiles. Neuropeptidase distribution patterns shifted based on strain, specific enzyme targets, and pharmacological intervention. Normotensive WKY groups showed intrahemispheric correlations primarily within the left hemisphere, whereas N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester-treated WKY and all SHR groups displayed correlations centered in the right hemisphere. Interhemispheric correlations appeared predominantly in normotensive WKY and SHRs receiving antihypertensive therapies like CAP or PRO. These findings indicate that distinct brain bilateral neuropeptidase activity patterns characterize WKY rats but are fundamentally altered in SHRs. This divergence likely underpins the cognitive deficits frequently documented in these animal models, suggesting that pharmacological manipulation of blood pressure dynamically reshapes neurochemical asymmetry and subsequent cognitive health outcomes. By modulating these specific enzymatic pathways, clinicians may eventually better understand how various cardiovascular treatments influence patient mental well-being, potentially mitigating the neuropsychiatric side effects often associated with chronic hypertension management and the broader spectrum of vascular-related mood instability observed in clinical settings.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::20: This study evaluates the clinical utility and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) addressing specific triggering events in patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA). We conducted a retrospective review of all RRT activations at a tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016. Inclusion criteria specified patients aged 18 or older receiving primary or revision THA. Data collected included demographics, primary RRT triggers, Charlson Comorbidity Index scores, underlying clinical etiologies, subsequent management alterations, and rates of ICU uptriaging. We identified 168 RRT events among 153 patients (mean age 65.2 years; mean BMI 32.3; 66% female). Length of stay for primary and revision THA patients requiring RRT was 3.4 and 6.2 days, respectively. These durations were significantly longer than cohorts not requiring RRT—2.4 days for primary (P < .001) and 4.6 days for revision (P = .005). Notably, zero mortalities occurred during the study period. RRTs triggered by hypotension/presyncope (11%) or syncope (11%) yielded fewer management changes (P < .01) compared to tachycardia (77%), hypoxia (57%), altered mental status (79%), or other triggers (47%). Similarly, uptriaging occurred less frequently for hypotension/presyncope (28%), syncope (15%), and hypoxia (30%) than for tachycardia (81%) (P < .001). Hypotension/presyncope correlated significantly with volume depletion (67%) (P < .001). Hypoxia was largely driven by atelectasis (57%) and opioid-induced oversedation (30.4%) (P = .037). Furthermore, altered mental status and delirium were predominantly caused by opioid administration (71%) (P < .001). In THA patients, RRT activations for syncope or presyncopal hypotension were significantly less likely to necessitate therapeutic changes or higher-level care compared to tachycardia. Crucially, the most frequent etiologies—specifically volume depletion and opioid-related respiratory depression—are potentially preventable, suggesting that targeted postoperative fluid management and refined pain protocols could substantially reduce the overall burden of emergency RRT activations within orthopedic surgical populations.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services remain a crucial component of acute stroke management. We devised a prehospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator intravenous therapy, known as TOPSPIN, for triaging ischemic stroke patients with specific indications for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006. This scale comprises five distinct items: consciousness levels, presence of atrial fibrillation, language disorder, upper extremity disturbance, and lower extremity disturbance. The aim of this study was to analyze ten years of TOPSPIN implementation results and distinguish ischemic stroke from hemorrhagic stroke in real-world clinical settings. We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients transferred to our facility and evaluated by Toyota city ambulance services using TOPSPIN from December 2006 to January 2017. We examined definite diagnoses at discharge, positive-predictive values, recanalization therapy rates, and clinical differentiation among hemorrhagic stroke, ischemic stroke, and stroke mimics. A total of 1,482 patients were enrolled; 1,134 were confirmed stroke cases, including 628 ischemic-type, 34 transient ischemic attack-type, and 472 hemorrhagic-type, while 348 patients lacked stroke, including 80 seizure cases, 42 syncope cases, 27 hypoglycemia cases, and 199 other diagnoses. Among 628 ischemic stroke patients, 130 received intravenous recombinant t-PA treatment, endovascular therapy, or both. The presence of atrial fibrillation, advanced age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN scores were more commonly associated with ischemic stroke than hemorrhagic stroke. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the presence of atrial fibrillation was independently associated with ischemic stroke, showing an odds ratio of 2.33. The TOPSPIN scale is a simple prehospital tool that includes an assessment of atrial fibrillation. Early detection of atrial fibrillation during the prehospital stage may reliably point to a significantly higher probability of ischemic stroke, allowing for faster triage and improved patient outcomes through rapid, targeted intervention strategies that save critical brain tissue and reduce long-term neurological disability.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the precise redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate located within the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have synthesized all VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by our team and two independent groups using FORS2 at VLT over the last five years, totaling 52 hours of integration. This combined spectrum represents the deepest observation ever obtained for a galaxy during the Reionization epoch. We detect no emission lines or continuum across the entire wavelength range, extending up to 10100A. Utilizing an accurate set of numerical simulations, we establish a stringent upper limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma, corresponding to a rest-frame equivalent width of EW<9A. By combining this limit with SED modeling, we refine the redshift to z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). SED fitting indicates GDS-1408 is relatively extinct (A1600~1) with a dust-corrected star formation rate of ~20 Msol/yr. Comparing the un-attenuated equivalent width predicted by case-B recombination theory against our observed upper limit provides a constraint on the effective Lya escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. While we cannot exclude a major contribution from the intergalactic or circumgalactic medium in damping the line, a plausible interpretation is that GDS-1408 is moderately evolved, containing sufficient gas and dust to attenuate Lya emission before it reaches the intergalactic medium. Redshift confirmation of even the best z~7 candidates remains exceptionally difficult using current 8-10m class telescopes, unless strong Lya or rest-UV nebular emission lines are present. We demonstrate that both JWST and E-ELT are necessary to make decisive progress. Currently, the increased redshift accuracy obtained through this detailed analysis makes ALMA a highly promising option for definitive redshift confirmation via sub-millimeter observations of molecular or atomic gas tracers, bypassing the limitations of optical spectroscopy.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as a critical pathogen indicator within composting environments was rigorously studied. An inoculum technique provided known quantities of bacteria to observe their behavior during decomposition. One experimental approach involved adding the Salmonella spp. solution directly into the compost matrix, facilitating immediate microbial interaction. This direct method was systematically compared against a contained vial technique, where the solution was sealed inside a protective vessel and inserted into the core of the compost pile before the process commenced. Standard enumeration protocols followed serial dilution and membrane filtration, strictly adhering to the PAS 100 quality guidelines and the BS EN ISO 6579:2002 regulatory standards. This research investigated how fluctuating thermal profiles and direct material contact influence pathogen activation and persistence. Maintaining temperatures between 55-60°C for at least three consecutive days typically eliminates the vast majority of enteric pathogens, according to established literature by Deportes et al. (1995). By tracking bacterial populations alongside temperature fluctuations, researchers assessed the die-off rates for both direct and protected samples. The study explicitly contrasted Sample A, which experienced direct contact with the decomposing organic matter, against Sample B, which remained isolated. Laboratory-scale results demonstrated that after eight days, during which internal temperatures peaked at 66°C, Salmonella levels in Sample A dropped below the stringent detection limits mandated by the UK PAS 100 compost standard. Conversely, Sample B, protected from the harsh chemical and physical degradation of the compost environment, retained significantly high concentrations of viable Salmonella spp. even after twenty full days of processing. This disparity highlights the protective role of physical barriers in microbial survival. These findings underscore that direct exposure to the composting matrix is essential for effective pathogen destruction, whereas isolated pockets may harbor pathogens, thereby posing potential risks to compost quality and public health safety.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race correlates with prostate cancer progression during early stages, it remains unclear if race predicts poor outcomes once men reach advanced disease states. The authors hypothesized that, within an equal-access environment, black men diagnosed with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and no known metastases (M0/Mx) would undergo imaging tests at rates comparable to nonblack peers, yet they might still exhibit a higher risk of developing metastatic disease. METHODS: Researchers analyzed 837 men diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC between 2000 and 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals via the SEARCH database. Investigators meticulously collected data regarding all post-diagnosis imaging, specifically noting test dates, modalities, and clinical outcomes. Multivariable Cox models assessed associations between race and the time until first metastasis, first bone metastasis, first bone scan, second bone scan after negative initial imaging, and overall survival duration. RESULTS: Black men (n = 306) showed identical likelihoods to nonblack men (n = 531) regarding the receipt of initial and subsequent bone scans following CRPC diagnosis. Statistical analysis revealed no significant racial disparities in the risk of developing systemic metastases, bone-specific metastases, the time elapsed before bone scans, or overall survival metrics (all P > .2). CONCLUSIONS: The absence of racial divergence in metastatic development and diagnostic scanning practices suggests that once men are diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC, race ceases to function as a reliable independent prognostic factor. Future initiatives aiming to address persistent prostate cancer racial disparities may derive substantially greater clinical benefit by focusing research efforts on the initial biological risk of developing primary prostate cancer and the specific outcomes of patients currently battling early stage disease. These findings highlight that socioeconomic equity in healthcare delivery can effectively mitigate long-standing disparities observed in more fragmented medical systems. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I filters. Our new field of view is strategically offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the elusive halo population of this galaxy. We report the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, which demonstrate that Leo A is definitely not a young galaxy. In fact, Leo A is at least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters which exhibit similar red horizontal branches, and are considered to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We discuss the distance to Leo A, and perform an extensive comparison of the data with stellar isochrones. For a distance modulus of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004, and ages between about 5 and 10 Gyr, in their post-main-sequence phases, but lack the detection of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide unambiguous proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar generations. Blue horizontal branch stars are above detection limits, but difficult to distinguish from young stars with similar colors and magnitudes. Synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the blue horizontal branch in the halo of Leo A. The models also suggest ~50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing to be attributed to an ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar population. We conclude that Leo A started to form stars at least 9 Gyr ago. Leo A exhibits an extremely low oxygen abundance, only 3% of Solar, in its ionized interstellar medium. The existence of old stars in this oxygen-deficient galaxy illustrates that low metallicity does not preclude early star formation.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::26: Neuromorphic engineering aims to build realistic robotic systems that interact with our physical world by adopting specific neuromechanical principles derived from biological entities. Central to this objective is the methodology used to implement spinal circuitry responsible for the complex behavior of afferented muscles. Fundamentally, muscle afferentation represents closed-loop behavior emerging from interactions among populations of muscle spindle afferents, alpha motoneurons, gamma motoneurons, and muscle fibers that enable functional movement. We utilized programmable VLSI hardware to implement simple models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, muscle spindle proprioceptors, alpha-motoneuron recruitment, gamma-motoneuron sensitivity control, and the monosynaptic circuitry connecting these components. This multi-scale system of spiking neuron populations emulated the physiological properties of a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles, each simulated by 1024 alpha- and gamma-motoneurons acting on a single joint via long tendons. This integrated system successfully maintained a joint angle and reproduced stretch reflex responses while driving the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Furthermore, this architecture allowed us to explore numerous values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains during robotic finger actuation, some of which successfully replicated specific human pathological conditions. We also investigated the behavioral consequences of adopting three distinct models of isometric muscle force production. We discovered that dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps that are highly sensitive to tendon elasticity, especially at high force output levels. Our methodology produced the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers. This research platform allows us to rigorously explore the mechanisms behind healthy and pathological sensorimotor function in the physical world by constructing them from first principles, serving as a critical, essential precursor to future advanced neuromorphic robotic systems capable of seamless, complex, and highly adaptive real-world physical interactions.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection alongside kidney or ureteral stones constitute a urologic emergency; they often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antibiotic resistance in patients who underwent urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis to facilitate safe, early discharge on targeted empiric oral antibiotics. Methods: Patients who underwent emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and an obstructing ureteral stone from 2014 to 2018 at two academic institutions were identified. Emergent stent placement was performed, and patients were treated with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics. We assessed the association between clinical parameters at presentation and resistance to at least one antibiotic from urine culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for continuous and categorical variables, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression was then performed using all significant variables from univariate analysis. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine cultures resistant to at least one antibiotic. On univariate analysis, patients with resistant cultures were significantly more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, require postoperative intensive care unit-level care, have confirmed bacteremia, and experience a longer overall length of stay. In multivariate analysis using significant variables from univariate analysis, only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antibiotic resistance with an increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this study, we show that a history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance in both univariate and multivariate analyses. Our findings suggest that patients with a history of ureteroscopy should await urine culture results, while those without a history of ureteroscopy may be discharged early on empiric oral antibiotics. However, future prospective studies are necessary to determine the clinical effectiveness of this predictor.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but very little research has examined the factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was derived from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 (44%) respondents who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating medical cannabis, and then used retrospective data on the frequency and amount of alcohol use pre-and post medical cannabis initiation to determine which participant characteristics and other variables were associated with reductions and/or cessation of alcohol use. Overall, 419 (44%) participants reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days, 323 (34%) decreased the number of standard drinks they had per week, and 76 (8%) reported no alcohol use at all in the 30 days prior to the survey. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing alcohol use, and an intention to use medical cannabis to reduce alcohol consumption was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis initiation may be associated with self-reported reductions and cessation of alcohol use among medical cannabis patients. Since alcohol is the most prevalent recreational substance in North America, and its use results in significant rates of criminality, morbidity and mortality, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients, as well as overall improvements in public health and safety by lowering substance-related accidents and chronic disease burdens.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions in Ir-based oxides manifests as exotic magnetic behavior. We investigate the exchange coupling evolution between Co and Ir following partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A major advantage of using Ca$^{2+}$ to replace La$^{3+}$ is their nearly identical ionic radii, ensuring observed magnetic shifts stem from electronic variations rather than lattice strain. We conducted a thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ via synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation, AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS data reveal that up to 25% Ca substitution at the La site induces Co$^{3+}$ in a high spin state, whereas higher doping levels trigger an increase in Ir valence. These competing magnetic interactions from mixed valences promote the coexistence of long-range magnetic ordering and a glassy spin state. Our $\mu$SR results show that in pristine La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$, a constant paramagnetic fraction persists down to low temperatures, likely linked to residual Ir$^{3+}$ and Co/Ir anti-site disorder. For doped compounds, the paramagnetic phase freezes below 30 K, yet persistent dynamics characterize the spin glass regime. Dielectric data for the parent compound and the 25% Ca-doped sample indicate a potential magnetodielectric effect. This phenomenon is analyzed through electron hopping between transition metal ions, the influence of localized anti-site disorder, and the inherent distortion of the crystalline structure. Such complex interactions underscore the sensitivity of these oxides to chemical modulation. Future studies must address how these subtle structural shifts specifically modulate the underlying electronic bandwidth, potentially unlocking new pathways for tailoring magnetic anisotropy and dielectric responses in advanced oxide materials for future technological applications.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::30: The rigorous demands emerging from sixth-generation internet-of-things use cases reveal that traditional multiple access control mechanisms possess severe limitations. Consequently, novel grant-free strategies have emerged as potential alternatives, yet a definitive, robust solution remains elusive. We introduce a semi-grant-free coordinated random access protocol, designated as partial-information multiple access, to mitigate packet loss and reduce latency, specifically during sporadic device activations. Within our machine-type communications scenario, devices transmit uplink data packets to a central base station. Utilizing partial-information multiple access, the base station gains insights into instantaneous traffic conditions. By leveraging compute-over-the-air techniques, the system estimates the quantity of devices holding queued data packets. Informed by this telemetry, the base station allocates a unique transmission slot to each device. Because individual slots might be assigned to multiple users simultaneously, collisions remain a technical risk. Both the total count of allocated slots and specific user assignments are optimized based on estimated active user counts to minimize collisions and enhance overall access efficiency. To validate our proposed architecture, we benchmark partial-information multiple access against time-division multiple-access and slotted ALOHA, which serve as the standard orthogonal multiple access baselines for low and high traffic scenarios, respectively. Our empirical results demonstrate that partial-information multiple access adapts dynamically to varying traffic loads, effectively minimizing packet drops irrespective of generation intensity. Furthermore, this protocol successfully integrates the distinct advantages found within both time-division multiple-access and slotted ALOHA frameworks. By synthesizing these mechanisms, our approach achieves substantial performance improvements regarding packet loss probability and end-to-end transmission latency. These findings suggest that our proposed method provides a scalable, reliable foundation for future massive machine-type communication networks, ensuring consistent quality of service even under highly congested, unpredictable, and bursty traffic environments that are characteristic of modern, dense, interconnected sixth-generation wireless ecosystems.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose: Bone remodeling triggered by surgical trauma, prolonged postoperative immobilization, and metallic device-related stress shielding often initiates significant loss of vital bone stock, thereby elevating the clinical risk of subsequent periprosthetic fractures or late-stage aseptic loosening. This study investigates adaptive bone remodeling within the proximal tibia following uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods: We conducted a 2-year longitudinal follow-up involving 53 patients (mean age 62; 38–70 years; 27 men) who underwent uncemented TKA during a randomized controlled trial, utilizing bone mineral density (BMD) measurements as a secondary clinical endpoint. Participants were randomized into two distinct cohorts: those receiving a monoblock (A) polyethylene design versus a modular (B) polyethylene design. All procedures utilized the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal system. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry tracked BMD changes postoperatively at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months across three specific regions of interest (ROI). Results and interpretation: In group A, statistically significant BMD reductions emerged by 24 months in both medial and lateral ROI. Specifically, BMD declined medially by 15% (p = 0.004) and laterally by 13% (p = 0.01). Conversely, group B exhibited minimal BMD fluctuations, with values returning to baseline preoperative levels by the 24-month mark. Inter-group variance regarding BMD alteration proved statistically significant for both medial (p = 0.03) and lateral (p = 0.02) zones. Within the distal ROI, no significant BMD shifts occurred in either cohort. We identified a distinct bone remodeling pattern between the two groups; notably, the monoblock design induced higher bone resorption. This indicates that the flexible monoblock architecture, despite earlier evidence suggesting improved early fixation, fails to mitigate proximal tibial bone loss, highlighting clear mechanical limitations that potentially compromise long-term implant stability and patient outcomes after joint replacement surgery.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) serve as bio-inspired computational models that achieve impressive accuracy. However, ANNs lack inherent temporal awareness, and units transmit continuous analog signals in rigid, frame-based cycles—a process that is both computationally heavy and energetically wasteful. This method diverges from biological neurons, which communicate sparsely through discrete, energy-efficient binary spikes. Although Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) replicate these biological principles by swapping standard units for spiking ones, their performance lags behind deep ANNs on complex benchmarks, and they often suffer from excessive firing rates that negate potential efficiency gains. We demonstrate that spiking neurons utilizing an optimized neural coding scheme can construct SNNs that match high-performance ANNs, exceeding current SNN benchmarks while maintaining drastically lower average firing rates. Our approach utilizes spike-time coding grounded in the firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon inherent to biological neurons. This behavior is captured by adapting neuron models, for which we derive a precise effective transfer function. ANN units trained with this function are replaced directly with adaptive spiking neurons, creating Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) that perform inference in deep architectures using up to ten times fewer spikes than traditional models. Furthermore, adaptive spike-time coding enables dynamic regulation of neural coding precision: we illustrate how a rudimentary model of arousal within AdSNNs halves the average required firing rate, a mechanism that naturally generalizes to diverse attentional systems. Consequently, AdSNNs represent a groundbreaking, efficient paradigm for neural computation, perfectly suited for temporally continuous, asynchronous data streams and low-power hardware deployment. By leveraging these biological insights, we bridge the gap between artificial performance and biological economy, ensuring robust scalability for future intelligent systems that must operate reliably within strict power constraints and real-time operational environments across various complex, edge-based computational tasks.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya remains a premier target for studying young solar analogues. Recent photometric analyses reveal shifting dynamics: from 2003–2009, coherent spots migrated predictably, yet the star subsequently entered a chaotic phase defined by irregular phase jumps and the disappearance of stable features. Aims. As a key subject in the 25-year SOFIN/FIES monitoring program, we present new Doppler temperature maps spanning 2006–2017 to analyze this chaotic transition period. Methods. We utilize advanced Doppler imaging to reconstruct high-resolution surface temperature distributions from spectroscopic data. Results. Our analysis shows a subtle, systematic increase in mean surface temperatures, correlating directly with the star's observed brightening in photometric magnitude. Nearly every season reveals a persistent, nonaxisymmetric, high-latitude spot cluster. While the phase evolution of these high-latitude features appears highly erratic, it aligns with broader photometric trends. We frequently detect equatorial spots, though many likely represent reconstruction artifacts stemming from limited phase coverage. Conclusions. Remarkably, the underlying spot topology persists despite the chaotic phase, mirroring patterns seen during more stable, active epochs. We consistently observe high-latitude and equatorial activity, while the intermediate latitudes remain notably barren of magnetic spots. We conclude that the observed erratic drifts and sudden phase jumps in photometric minima are primarily driven by localized structural changes within the high-latitude spot regions, rather than the transient equatorial features. This suggests that the magnetic dynamo in young solar analogues maintains a fundamental, robust structure even when the external manifestation of surface activity appears disordered and unpredictable. These findings provide critical constraints for stellar dynamo models, confirming that large-scale magnetic configurations are resilient to the rapid, short-term temporal fluctuations that characterize the chaotic state of this young, rapidly rotating solar-type star.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions represent critical surface phenomena occurring on interstellar ices. However, empirical solid-state astrochemical laboratory data regarding H-atom interactions with common ice constituents remain largely deficient. Aims: Our research aims to ascertain if and how carbon dioxide, formic acid, and acetaldehyde react with H-atoms at cryogenic temperatures, while deriving specific reaction rates and chemical production yields. Methods: Pure ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms within an ultra-high vacuum chamber. We employ reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy to monitor ices, while temperature programmed desorption identifies gas-phase products to calculate destruction efficiencies and kinetic rate constants. Results: Our experimental sensitivity indicates that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH ices produces no detectable compounds. The established upper limits for these reaction rates are equal to or less than 7e(-17) cm^2/s, suggesting these species likely contribute minimally to complex organic formation via hydrogenation in interstellar environments. Conversely, acetaldehyde reacts readily with H-atoms. At most, 20% of the sample undergoes hydrogenation into ethanol. A secondary reaction pathway induces C-C bond cleavage, yielding solid-state methane (approximately 20%) alongside formaldehyde and methanol (15-50%). Methane production yields should theoretically match the combined formaldehyde and methanol yields; consequently, methane likely partially sublimates post-formation due to the reaction's significant exothermicity. Furthermore, the destruction rates for acetaldehyde depend strictly upon the ice temperature rather than ice thickness, indicating a surface-limited process. These findings offer quantitative constraints for astrochemical models describing the evolution of complex ices. By refining these rates, we establish clear boundaries for molecular synthesis in cold space. Future studies must now investigate how ice morphology and matrix effects influence these specific reaction outcomes, ultimately improving our understanding of chemical complexity in diverse interstellar regions throughout the galaxy.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control emerged during the early 2000s, evolving significantly to achieve mathematical maturity alongside robust practical applications. Its primary tenet mandates achieving prescribed transient and asymptotic behavior for continuous-time dynamical processes, including linear, nonlinear, functional differential, differential-algebraic, and partial differential equations. Researchers analyze systems defined solely by structural properties like relative degree and stable internal dynamics, acknowledging that precise system data remains fundamentally unknown, which mirrors the inherent inaccuracy of all physical models. Designers prespecify a funnel shape using smooth functions, define diverse reference signals, and establish structural system criteria. The objective is to engineer a simple, universal funnel controller relying exclusively on input-output information, ensuring that any system within the specified class interacting with any reference signal meets strict performance criteria. Specifically, the closed-loop system must avoid finite-time blow-ups, maintain bounded internal variables, and ensure the error between output and reference signals remains strictly confined within the defined funnel boundaries. This approach guarantees stability even under significant model uncertainty or external disturbances. In the introduction, we detail the historical genesis of funnel control. Subsequently, we investigate diverse system classes amenable to this technique, demonstrating its efficacy for systems with arbitrary relative degrees and those governed by complex partial differential equations. We further examine the critical role of adaptive gains in maintaining system robustness. Finally, we discuss practical input constraints, energy efficiency limitations, and real-world engineering applications, such as robotics or chemical process regulation. By addressing these multifaceted requirements, the funnel control framework provides a comprehensive solution for managing uncertain dynamical systems where traditional controllers often fail due to strict reliance on exact mathematical parameters or precise plant identification, thereby broadening the scope of modern control theory applications in industrial settings.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::36: The rising diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks renders building a fully protected network increasingly difficult. Specifically, the Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA) bypasses traditional defenses by saturating narrow network paths, effectively isolating target zones without triggering standard volumetric alarms. To counter such stealthy threats, Moving Target Defense (MTD) dynamically alters configurations to deceive adversaries, rendering successful exploitation computationally expensive. However, MTD imposes significant operational latency and bandwidth overhead, creating a complex optimization problem regarding the timing, frequency, and magnitude of these defensive shifts. This strategy choice is further complicated by the unpredictable, adaptive behavior of sophisticated attackers who monitor network responses to refine their own tactics. In this research, we determine an optimal MTD strategy that maximizes SLFA mitigation while minimizing performance degradation. We formulate this conflict as a Bayesian signaling game where the defender and the attacker act as rational agents with asymmetric information. A dynamic belief function evolves throughout the engagement, capturing the defender’s uncertainty about the attacker’s hidden intentions, which then informs the selection of the most effective response. We analyze this game-theoretic model to derive a robust defense mechanism based on Perfect Bayesian Equilibria. We evaluate our approach within a Mininet-based environment, subjecting the topology to persistent SLFAs while the defender executes MTD actions dictated by the equilibrium solution. Experimental results demonstrate that our signaling game-based defense provides a security posture comparable to exhaustive, high-overhead MTD schemes. By strategically timing transitions rather than utilizing constant randomization, our mechanism achieves equivalent protection against targeted link saturation while significantly reducing the auxiliary processing burden on the network infrastructure, ultimately proving that intelligent, informed defense outperforms brute-force randomization in resource-constrained environments.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. However, most existing MF methods rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels or fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels and utilize it to quantify the value of future samples and navigate adaptive sampling. To address this hurdle, we propose a framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each infill sampling iteration includes two steps: We first identify the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the location identified in the first step. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space to capture their correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect HF response with pre-posterior analysis and determine the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmark methods in both MF global fitting (GF) and Bayesian Optimization (BO) problems in convergence rate, accuracy, and robustness. Moreover, the method offers the flexibility to switch between GF and BO by simply changing the acquisition function, while simultaneously reducing computational overhead and minimizing total experimental expenditures.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary brain injuries triggered by massive systemic cytokine storms and inflammatory cascades, which are frequently linked to subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Their precise clinical relevance remains debated. We retrospectively examined SAH patients to evaluate differences in baseline demographics, specific neurological findings, and long-term functional recovery between those who developed these callosal lesions and those who did not. We also compared cohorts based on favorable versus poor recovery metrics. Multivariate logistic regression identified key independent risk factors for negative prognoses.
