Among 159 SAH subjects, 17 individuals, representing 10.7%, exhibited these specific cytotoxic callosal lesions. Patients afflicted by these lesions were significantly more likely to present with severe neurological impairment (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grades IV-V: OR 4.53; 95% CI 1.60-12.84; p=0.0042) and show radiographic evidence of intraventricular (OR 5.98; 95% CI 1.32-27.13; p=0.0054) or intraparenchymal hematoma expansion (OR 3.62; 95% CI 1.25-10.45; p=0.023). Furthermore, these patients demonstrated a marked predisposition toward poor outcomes at three months, measured via modified Rankin Scale scores (OR 0.22; 95% CI 0.07-0.66; p=0.0043). Multivariate modeling confirmed that these callosal lesions independently elevated the risk of poor recovery (OR 4.39; 95% CI 1.06-18.1; p=0.037). Consequently, the formation of these corpus callosum lesions appears intrinsically tied to the anatomical severity and volume of initial intracranial hemorrhages. While these neurological abnormalities are often radiographically reversible over time, their acute emergence serves as a critical, high-sensitivity clinical marker for predicting adverse functional survival and long-term neurological disability in the complex, post-hemorrhagic SAH patient population requiring intensive neurocritical care monitoring and aggressive early therapeutic interventions to mitigate secondary damage.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate clinical protocols for the sedation of Nordestino donkeys remains notably scarce in current veterinary literature. This study aimed to evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low-dose intravenous (i.v.) xylazine, both with and without the addition of acepromazine, in Nordestino donkeys. Seven healthy female donkeys (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Four distinct treatments were administered via two i.v. injections, at baseline (T0) and 15 minutes later (T15). Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg + saline (AS), saline + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg (SX0.5), acepromazine + xylazine 0.25 mg/kg (AX0.25), or acepromazine + xylazine 0.5 mg/kg (AX0.5). Sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters were recorded at T0 and at 15, 20, 30, 45, 60, 75, and 90 minutes post-treatment. Sedation degree, defined by head height above ground (HHAG), and quality, measured by ataxia, stimulus response, and visual analogue scale (VAS) scoring, were assessed by the lead investigator. Respiratory rate was monitored, while heart rate was measured by an assistant. Three independent evaluators later assessed video recordings for ataxia and stimulus sensitivity. Data were analysed using repeated measures ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis (P<0.05). HHAG decreased below baseline for 15 minutes in AX0.25 and for 30 minutes in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All xylazine treatments increased VAS and ataxia scores for 15 minutes, showing no significant inter-group differences. Ataxia scores were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 compared to AS for 15 and 30 minutes, respectively. A limitation was the absence of a saline-saline negative control group. Ultimately, acepromazine combined with 0.25 mg/kg xylazine produced briefer, milder sedation than 0.5 mg/kg xylazine, suggesting that dosage adjustments significantly alter the depth, safety profile, and duration of chemical restraint in this specific donkey breed.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying 1000 star-forming cores. Core mass and luminosity are vital physical characteristics, yet determining these values is difficult, especially at distances exceeding 2 kpc. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these cores. We estimated their mass-averaged temperature and implied masses. For 1/6 of the sample, we measured bolometric luminosities, implementing necessary deblending corrections for crowded fields. We utilized spectral energy distribution analysis via the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which preserves the best angular resolution of input data. We extrapolated luminosity and dust temperature images from PPMAP at 2.5" resolution to estimate those of individual cores identified at higher resolution. To do this, we applied radiative transfer relationships between protostar luminosity and envelope temperature, plus external heating effects on prestellar cores. We provide data-informed dust temperatures for 883 cores: 17-31 K and 28-79 K (5th and 95th percentiles, up to 127 K) for 617 prestellar and 266 protostellar cores, respectively. We measured protostellar luminosities spanning 20-80,000 Lsun. For hot cores, we estimated systematically lower temperatures than studies based on complex organic molecules, suggesting different emission origins. We established a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram, providing the first such large-scale analysis at core spatial resolution. These ALMA-IMF findings strongly favor a scenario where protostars actively accrete their total mass from a significantly larger mass reservoir than their immediate host cores, implying that core-scale evolution is tightly coupled to the wider cluster environment. These results constrain theoretical models of high-mass star formation and demonstrate that external heating significantly influences core thermal states, directly impacting our understanding of gravitational collapse and subsequent stellar growth across diverse galactic star-forming regions.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::41: This study explored the regulatory role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p within osteoarthritis (OA) pathophysiology. Using reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting, we quantified miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) levels in OA cartilage versus healthy controls, alongside interleukin (IL)-1beta-stimulated primary chondrocytes. We transfected chondrocytes with miR-27a-3p mimics and utilized luciferase reporter assays to confirm direct miR-27a-3p binding to the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA. Additionally, we investigated whether IL-1beta-induced mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) or nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB signaling pathways mediated miR-27a-3p expression shifts using pharmacological inhibitors. Results showed significantly diminished miR-27a-3p levels in OA tissues. IL-1beta exposure triggered a time- and dose-dependent decline in miR-27a-3p alongside a concomitant upregulation of ADAMTS5 protein. Overexpression of miR-27a-3p effectively suppressed IL-1beta-induced ADAMTS5 expression, confirming a negative regulatory feedback loop. Luciferase assays showed that miR-27a-3p overexpression reduced reporter activity, while mutating the specific binding site completely abolished this repressive effect, validating a direct molecular interaction. Furthermore, specific inhibitors proved that IL-1beta suppresses miR-27a-3p expression primarily through activated NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways. We conclude that miR-27a-3p is significantly downregulated in human OA cartilage, functioning as a critical post-transcriptional suppressor of the catabolic enzyme ADAMTS5. The observed IL-1beta-mediated inhibition of miR-27a-3p via NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways suggests that these inflammatory cascades drive cartilage degradation by silencing protective microRNAs. These findings establish that restoring miR-27a-3p levels could serve as a promising novel therapeutic strategy to mitigate joint destruction in OA patients. By targeting the ADAMTS5 axis, miR-27a-3p therapeutics might slow disease progression, offering a potential clinical intervention to counteract the deleterious effects of chronic inflammation on articular chondrocytes. This research highlights the complex regulatory network connecting inflammatory cytokines, specific microRNAs, and cartilage-degrading enzymes in joint health.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering fundamentally alters the surface of airless planetary bodies through distinct physical mechanisms. The primary agents driving these alterations are constant solar wind irradiation and relentless micrometeoroid bombardment. These processes significantly shift planetary reflectance spectra while simultaneously obscuring vital compositional diagnostic features. In this work, we meticulously simulated and compared the spectral changes induced by solar wind irradiation versus micrometeoroid bombardment to isolate the specific impacts of these individual space weathering drivers. We utilized olivine and pyroxene pellets as laboratory proxies for diverse planetary materials. To emulate solar wind irradiation, we employed hydrogen, helium, and argon ions at energies ranging from 5 to 40 keV with total fluences reaching $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$. Conversely, we simulated micrometeoroid bombardment via individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analyzed the subsequent evolution of various spectral parameters using the Modified Gaussian Model and robust principal component analysis. Our findings indicate that the original mineralogy governs spectral evolution more profoundly than the specific weathering agent, evidenced by the divergent slope changes in olivine versus pyroxene. The observed spectral reddening in olivine aligns with A-type asteroid data, whereas the minimal slope variations in pyroxene match observations of asteroid (4) Vesta. Furthermore, we identified critical differences between the two agents: solar wind ions exert less influence on long-wavelength spectra compared to laser-simulated impacts, a variance likely stemming from disparate penetration depths between charged particles and thermal pulses. Ultimately, our research suggests that analyzing these distinct spectral signatures may eventually allow scientists to differentiate between the specific contributions of solar wind and micrometeoroid impacts on the surfaces of weathered celestial bodies, providing a clearer history of their long-term environmental exposure and evolution.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by Gorski et al. (2005) serves as the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background data storage, dominating current and future experiment pipelines. Almost every dataset within the Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis utilizes this format. Visualizing such spherical data remains critical for research, previously relying on legacy Fortran facilities or Python-based healpy integration. Given modern GPU advancements, rendering massive maps in real time on portable devices like laptops or tablets is now achievable. The HEALPix Viewer presented here, developed specifically for macOS, exploits hardware acceleration to manage gargantuan datasets instantly. It compiles natively for Intel and Arm64 chips, leveraging the Metal framework for superior GPU-bound computations. This project aims to minimize the cognitive burden of interactive exploration while slashing the temporal overhead required to generate publication-grade imagery. Seamless drag-and-drop integration with Keynote and PowerPoint streamlines presentation creation significantly. The core codebase utilizes Swift, a modern compiled language, delegating intensive calculations entirely to the GPU, while using C-based inserts for cfitsio library I/O operations. The interface employs SwiftUI, a declarative framework that ensures responsive layout management. Essential spherical projections and standard scientific colormaps are supported natively, and the open source architecture facilitates user-defined customizations or feature expansion. Performance metrics indicate that this solution outperforms traditional Python software stacks by factors ranging from three to one hundred eighty times, depending on the specific rendering task. By shifting heavy processing to dedicated graphics hardware, researchers gain fluid interaction with high-resolution data. This architecture ensures stability, scalability, and efficiency for diverse astrophysical applications, representing a major leap forward in how we handle complex spherical mapping tasks within the modern high-performance computing ecosystem.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::44: To compare cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) using transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women, this prospective cohort study examined participants attending antenatal care at Ramathibodi Hospital, Bangkok. We serially measured shear wave speed (SWS) at early, mid-, and third trimesters to evaluate changes in cervical stiffness with advancing gestational age. Secondary outcomes included gestational age at delivery and spontaneous preterm birth rates. Among 36 twin and 38 singleton pregnancies analyzed, baseline characteristics were similar except for maternal age, which was higher in twins (33.1±4.6 vs 29.9±5.4 years, p=0.006). Cervical SWS declined across all trimesters in both groups, yet a significant divergence emerged at the mid-trimester lower cervical point (twin 2.27±0.4 vs singleton 2.71±0.6 m/s, p=0.001). Conversely, no significant differences appeared at the upper cervical point or during early and third-trimester assessments. While twin pregnancies resulted in earlier delivery (35.9±2.8 vs 37.6±2.9 weeks, p=0.008), the incidence of spontaneous preterm delivery remained statistically comparable (22.2% vs 15.8%, p=0.483). These findings indicate that mid-trimester SWS at the lower cervical region effectively captures the distinct physiological softening inherent in twin gestations compared to singletons. This biomechanical difference suggests that SWE could serve as a valuable clinical tool for monitoring cervical remodeling in high-risk twin pregnancies, potentially offering insights into cervical competence that standard ultrasound length measurements currently miss. Further research must clarify if these SWS discrepancies correlate directly with clinical cervical insufficiency markers or if they simply reflect the unique mechanical stress placed on the cervix by multiple gestations. Clinicians might utilize this diagnostic modality to refine risk stratification protocols for twin pregnancies, aiming to improve maternal outcomes and neonatal survival rates throughout the complex progression of gestation.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number defines the higher-order organization of genomes, and shifts in these counts fundamentally drive evolutionary divergence. Dysploid gains or losses, alongside whole-genome polyploidization, frequently trigger reproductive isolation, thereby accelerating lineage diversification. While Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol) pioneered probabilistic models to infer ancestral counts across molecular phylogenies, that specific approach assumes all shifts occur strictly anagenetically along branches. It fails to account for cladogenetic events, which are essential if chromosomal rearrangements directly induce immediate reproductive barriers during speciation. We introduce ChromoSSE, a sophisticated model class incorporating both anagenetic and cladogenetic dynamics to resolve these evolutionary patterns. ChromoSSE allows researchers to distinguish whether chromosomal transitions arise primarily within stable lineages, during the act of lineage splitting, or through unique clade-specific combinations of both mechanisms. Furthermore, we can precisely pinpoint the location and temporal timing of chromosomal speciation events across complex phylogenies. We implemented this framework within the Bayesian RevBayes software, leveraging reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo to robustly quantify uncertainty in parameter estimates while maintaining the statistical rigor of likelihood-based methodologies. We validated ChromoSSE’s accuracy through rigorous simulations and re-analyzed chromosomal evolution in diverse plant groups, including Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato, and Primula section Aleuritia. Our results provide compelling empirical evidence for clade-specific mixtures of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploidy and polyploidy. These findings demonstrate that relying solely on anagenetic models likely underestimates the frequency of speciation-linked genomic restructuring. By formally integrating cladogenetic processes, our approach reveals that chromosomal evolution is a multifaceted driver of biodiversity, requiring nuanced models that account for the distinct timing of genomic changes relative to the actual nodes of divergence within the tree of life.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies of Mg II and Al III absorption lines in a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1 using the 2m telescope at IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale of 10 days to 7.69 years in the rest frame. Spectra are analysed alongside photometric light curves from the Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey to track flux. Long time-scale variability, exceeding one year, occurs in 8 cases, representing 36% of systems, whereas only 4, or 18%, exhibit shifts over short intervals under one year. We observe that highly variable LoBAL QSOs tend to possess high ejection velocity, low equivalent width, and low redshift values. The detection rate of variability in FeLoBAL QSOs, which show Fe fine-structure lines, is lower than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Absorption line variability is detected more frequently in QSOs where the continuum is dominated by Fe emission lines compared to the remainder of the sample. Confirming these trends with a larger population will provide vital clues for understanding physical distinctions between BAL QSO sub-classes. We correlate absorption line variability with parameters derived from continuum light curves, finding no clear link between continuum flux and absorption line changes. However, sources with significant absorption line variability also display large fluctuations in their light curves. We observe the appearance or disappearance of absorption components in 2 cases and see clear profile variations in 4 cases. The observed variability is best explained by a combination of processes driven by continuum flux changes and individual clouds transiting across the line of sight, which physically alters the observed spectral absorption features.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::47: The Hα nebular emission line serves as an optimal tracer for recent star formation in galaxies. With the advent of JWST, this line has recently become observable at z>3 for the first time. We present a catalog of 1013 Hα emitters at 3.7<z<6.7 in the GOODS fields obtained from a blind search in JWST NIRCam/grism data. We utilize the FRESCO survey's 124 arcmin² of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, probing Hα at 4.9<z<6.7; and the CONGRESS survey's 62 arcmin² in GOODS-North with F356W, probing Hα at 3.8<z<5.1. We identify a significant overdensity containing 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N, while confirming previously reported overdensities at z~5.2 in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed Hα luminosity functions (LFs) in three distinct bins centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, marking the first such measurements at z>3 based purely on spectroscopic data, robustly tracing galaxy star formation rates (SFRs) beyond the peak of cosmic star formation history. We compare our results with theoretical predictions from three different simulations and find good agreement at z~4-6. The UV LFs of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample align well with pre-JWST measurements obtained via photometrically-selected objects. Finally, we derive SFR functions and integrate these to compute the evolution of cosmic star-formation rate densities across z~4-6, yielding values consistent with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break galaxies, which imply a continuous decrease in SFR density by a factor of 3x over z~4 to z~6. Our work demonstrates the power of NIRCam grism observations to efficiently provide new, empirical tests for early galaxy formation models based on precise emission line statistics.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::48: Extensive research confirms oxidative stress drives depression. Xiaoyao Pills (XYW), a pharmacopoeia-listed remedy, treat anxiety by smoothing liver function, fortifying spleen energy, and enriching blood quality. Despite this, XYW's precise antidepressant efficacy remains under-examined. Our study evaluated XYW’s antidepressant-like impacts and molecular pathways using olfactory bulbectomized (OB) rats via open field (OFT), sucrose preference (SPT), splash (ST), and novelty suppressed feeding (NSFT) tests. Results demonstrated that XYW doses of 0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1 mitigated depression-like behaviors: rats exhibited higher sucrose intake in SPT, increased grooming duration in ST, reduced horizontal activity in OFT, and faster feeding onset in NSFT. Crucially, XYW treatment restored superoxide dismutase activity and glutathione concentrations while suppressing malondialdehyde, nitric oxide, and pro-inflammatory cytokines like interleukin-6 and 1β within serum and cortical tissues. Mechanistically, XYW upregulated mRNA and protein expression of NFE2L2, KEAP1, GPX3, HMOX1, SOD1, NQO1, OGG1, PIK3CA, p-AKT1/AKT1, NTRK2, and BDNF. Simultaneously, it diminished reactive oxygen species in the cortex and hippocampus by activating the NFE2L2/KEAP1, PIK3CA/AKT1, and NTRK2/BDNF signaling cascades. These findings indicate that XYW provides antidepressant-like benefits in OB rats by neutralizing oxidative damage and bolstering neuroprotection. By modulating these critical pathways, XYW addresses the underlying biological imbalances inherent in depressive states. Our data suggests that the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF axis serves as a primary mediator for these therapeutic outcomes, highlighting the potential for XYW as a potent botanical intervention. This study bridges traditional medicinal wisdom with rigorous molecular neuroscience, providing a comprehensive framework for understanding how such complex herbal formulations stabilize neural health, reduce inflammation, and effectively reverse the behavioral manifestations of chronic, stress-induced depressive disorders in animal models.
ideas_up.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag and provide a detailed characterisation of three of them, using high-precision infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey. Such systems provide the most accurate, model-independent method for measuring fundamental parameters of these numerous stars, which lack sufficient observations to calibrate stellar evolution models. We solve for masses and radii of three systems, finding orbital periods of 1.5-4.9 days, masses of 0.35-0.50 Msun, and radii of 0.38-0.50 Rsun, with uncertainties of ~3.5-6.4% in mass and ~2.7-5.5% in radius. Close companions in short-period binaries are expected to be tidally locked into fast rotation, causing high magnetic activity. This activity is predicted to inflate radii by inhibiting convective flow and increasing star spot coverage. Radii of these WTS systems are inflated above standard model predictions by ~3-12%, matching observed trends, despite lower expected systematic contributions from star spot signals at infrared wavelengths. We searched for correlations between orbital period and radius inflation by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf measurements of comparable precision, but found no statistically significant evidence for a decrease in inflation for longer-period, less active systems. Radius inflation persists in non-synchronised systems, indicating the problem remains even for very low-activity M-dwarfs. Resolving this issue is vital for understanding these populous stars and characterising their planetary companions, which hold the best prospects for finding Earth-like planets in habitable zones. These findings imply that current stellar models require fundamental revisions to account for magnetic pressure effects, convective inhibition, and potential unknown mechanisms that consistently produce larger stellar radii across diverse M-dwarf populations, ultimately refining our broader knowledge of galactic stellar demographics and planetary system evolution throughout the entire observable cosmic neighborhood.

This smaller unit is also fully rustproof and includes the same reliable dual suction cups and no-slip wire clip mechanism for stability.

Both versions of the InterDesign York shower caddy are high-quality products that offer excellent organization for any bathroom environment. The key to satisfaction is measuring your shower area precisely before finalizing your purchase to ensure you select the appropriate dimensions for your specific setup. Whether you need the massive capacity of the Extra Large version or the slender, streamlined profile of the Lyra model, these caddies are designed to maximize your vertical storage potential effectively. By evaluating the clearance around your soap dishes and control valves beforehand, you will avoid the frustration of returns and enjoy a perfectly customized, clutter-free shower experience immediately.
ideas_up.amazon_reviews::1: The square corner on this wooden spoon makes it easy to scrape the bottom of your saucepan or frying pan, ensuring you never miss spots when stirring items that burn easily. I love it for making caramel ice cream, because caramelized sugar forms stubborn lumps that stick to the bottom after adding cool cream. With this flat-edged spoon, it is easy to combine the lump and cream into a smooth caramel sauce without scorching the sugar. This featherweight tool is crafted from durable beechwood, featuring a beautifully balanced shape that feels ergonomic. It is extremely comfortable to hold while stirring thick sauces or savory gravies for long periods. The handle features a deliberate, slight curvature, unlike the traditional, ramrod-straight wooden spoons found at grocery stores, which often feel awkward. Wooden spoons are not dishwasher safe; the high heat and harsh detergents will quickly dry out the fibers, causing them to warp or split. Even with careful hand washing, they must be periodically treated with food-grade mineral oil to maintain moisture, prevent deep structural splitting, and significantly prolong their useful kitchen life. One reasonably priced, effective mineral oil sold for this specific purpose is the Snow River 32-Ounce Wood Oil, which protects and conditions the wood grain perfectly.

This is a pricy faux leather planner. I loved the 2022 book so much that I paid for this higher priced 2023 planner. I won't be back for 2024 at the current rate of increase.

The interior binder layout remains identical to last year. While I could certainly use more dedicated pages for notes, that omission was not a deal breaker. However, the cost of the planner increased significantly while the tactile value of the cover material drastically decreased.

The 2022 planner's cover was flawless. The faux leather looked and felt nearly real. The material was perfectly adhered to the cardboard hardback substrate. My heavily used planner looks to be in pristine condition a year later. It was a professionally constructed book that feels substantial in my hand. Last year, I bought the gray version.

Unfortunately, this 2023 binder lacks the same binding quality. The cover feels cheap, thin, and brittle. It is not adhered to the cardboard hardback at all; consequently, you see unsightly air ripples in the cover when it is opened or closed. I am highly disappointed with the extreme lack of quality and professional craftsmanship. This forty-dollar binder exhibits bargain-bin quality. It is a clear bait and switch tactic. Now that they have secured great reviews, they clearly did not feel compelled to maintain or improve quality despite the higher price point.

Next year, I will visit a physical store to verify the quality before purchasing. This should have cost a third of the price. I am deeply disappointed. If you only care about the internal paper, you will be fine. However, I need the entire item to reflect its cost; the cover is sub-par, and I lack confidence in its long-term durability. I have lost faith in this company and will not return for a 2024 planner.
ideas_up.amazon_reviews::6:
I love this game, yet it remains unsuitable for casual, spontaneous sessions with arbitrary partners. Mastering the mechanics required over three hours of study, followed by multiple two-hour sessions to internalize flow, though I suspect latent nuances remain undiscovered. While the experience is rewarding once internal logic clicks, the sheer density of interdependent systems frequently overwhelms novices. One must track dozens of variables simultaneously, leading to frequent, momentum-killing pauses where players debate potential oversights or conflicting interpretations of the complex rule interactions.

Regarding documentation, the designers excelled at visual setup guides and index utility, yet the core rulebook structure remains frustratingly fragmented. I constantly flip across disparate sections to synthesize a single mechanic, often concluding the search without a definitive resolution. 

Furthermore, the game claims to mitigate dominant alpha-player behavior, yet it offers zero protection against dependent delta-players. My regular partner, despite extensive experience, relies on me to micro-manage their every decision, forcing me to neglect my own strategic planning until their turn concludes. When I request reciprocal coordination or basic tactical synergy, they refuse, either due to rule insecurity or poor teamwork. Consequently, they label me a nuisance for my own deliberation speed, despite my patience during their constant inquiries. This dynamic makes hosting larger groups feel like a logistical nightmare, as the burden of administrative oversight falls entirely on the owner. 

Despite these interpersonal frustrations and the steep learning curve, the game provides a genuinely exceptional experience when played solo. Without the social friction of unengaged partners or the fatigue of teaching complex systems to newcomers, the design shines brilliantly. The mechanics function best when one person controls all variables, avoiding the pitfalls of unbalanced cooperative play and slow, argumentative turns. I still adore this game, provided I keep it strictly to a solitary hobby rather than attempting to share it with others during a stressful social gathering.
ideas_up.amazon_reviews::7: Although the product photos illustrate the shelves with the lip edge facing downward, do not be deceived. There is only one valid configuration for this system, which forces the lip edge to face upward. I wasted excessive time enduring immense frustration attempting assembly as the manual instructed, eventually surrendering to contact customer support. A representative explained, very slowly, that there is only one way to assemble the unit, and that necessarily means the lip edge must face up. This design is infuriating.  "Oh honey," I say, on the brink of tears. "Come here." She walks to me and I hold her in my arms tightly, running my hands through her hair. "We won't be going to school today, dear."
 
 News continues to pour in from the TV, detailing flight paths and security failures.
 
 In the corner of the screen: Monday, 11 September 2001.
 
 
 \________
 
 Shanghai, China
 
 Day 0, 01:00
 
 ~
 
 "Dr. Wu, you have to look at this."
 
 "Not now, Lin. There are enough people freaking out about this! We need to focus on our research," I take off my thin, metal-rimmed glasses and look at my assistant. She has helped me so much in the past seven years. We are so close now to a breakthrough. We cannot afford to be distracted. "If we do not meet the deadline, all our efforts would have gone to waste."
 
 Lin shakes her head. "No, doctor. I am not talking about the attack. I… I…"
 
 "What is it, then? Speak up."
 
 "You… you should see this for yourself." Lin takes out a massive sheet of paper and lays it out on my table.
 
 "This is the oceanic temperature table today—why did you print it out? These fluctuations are perfectly normal, and the—" Something at the end of the graph catches my eyes. A massive spike. "This… this…"
 
 "Yes, doctor. You were right all along."
 
 My heart skips a beat. I check the time of the spike; it matches the terror perfectly.
 
 "Lin,"
 
 "Yes, doctor?"
 
 "Get me the director of the Chinese Meteorological Administration. Now!"
ideas_up.writingprompts::1: This is the end, isn't it? The thought struck Josh suddenly, almost by accident. It pierced through and dissolved his frustration with the car that had allowed him to break down so far from home; with the phone company that had neglected to build towers by this barren desert road; with the sun that had audaciously beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground. This is the end. This thought in particular remained prominent in his mind, even as he realized that he had already seen Heather for the last time. And Joey, who was still so proud about that geometry test he aced. And Dale, and the family business Dale would inherit, the company that would serve as an unexpected, tragic legacy. This is it. Dale, who had warned him that this trip was a fool's errand, and even made a cruel joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral; this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head. The end of... The thought lingered there, static, for a time that Josh wasn't able to comprehend. Everything else in his mind seemed to fade away, from his periphery, inward toward this single, solitary idea. This is the end of me. When nothing else was left, Josh found it fitting that this idea of finality should itself be his final thought. But it wasn't. It vanished as abruptly as it came, and then -- Josh would have cried, if he was still physically capable. His regrets came flooding back all at once. And his anger, and his sorrow and his despondency at his own powerlessness. The tranquil peace of the end was over, replaced with the angst of a life incomplete. A life that had failed to come to terms with itself, leaving behind unfinished projects, unspoken apologies, and dreams that would now wither in the dust. And then Josh felt fear. Fear like he had never felt before. The terror of fate incarnate, of the great unknown for which he was utterly unprepared. The sheer and total horror overwhelmed his memory, and his pain, and all his other emotions. That fear was the last thing Josh thought about.
ideas_up.writingprompts::2:
Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave, the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn. I found it hearting. The ending being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, faster. Each cubic inch of earth removed represented a final payment of my debt to the State, a transaction of soil for the privilege of existence.

All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like brittle dry dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies back to the earth. In the distance other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns, their rhythmic chanting serving as a metronome for our slow, dying labor. At regular intervals throughout the field Compliance Officers stood, in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation, their posture reflecting an absolute, terrifying indifference to our individual suffering.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked. Then the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again. Soon meat had almost become a memory, and fully grown, healthy looking vegetables were rare, replaced by synthetic gray pastes that offered no genuine nourishment to our starving, hollowed organs.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised. We were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Straining Test. Everyone must do their part to bear this burden and our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant. Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told. It was clear, yes undoubtable clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders, attempting to destroy our resolve, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals through biological warfare. But we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant.

It was then that they announced the lottery. That a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation, to help ease the burden of consumption. Those who were selected were informed the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families. I was one of the chosen, selected by a digital algorithm designed to optimize resource depletion.

A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body fertilize the soil to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot punctuated this declaration. Someone had already finished their grave. A few other cheered their assent, most were too weary and hungry to manage. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied, turning his living energy into the labor of burial.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, shoveling out a long, winding roadway through the mountain pass. We slept where we worked and the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water, laced with mild sedatives to ensure our docility during the final hours. And so the last of the strength of our bodies was harvested for the state.

My grave now looked deep enough. I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer. If it was not deep enough for his liking I would have to wait until all others had finished, covering over their graves, before it would be my turn. He came over and produced a tape measurer. He checked the dimensions and nodded his assent. I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final duty to my beloved land. 

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave." The Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn. I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer's pistol come to rest upon my forehead. "Citizens will not be allowed..."
ideas_up.writingprompts::3: I exhale the acrid, chemical smoke over those cold concrete slabs. I put the glass bottle away neatly, feeling for the cold steel weight against my hip. I check my watch. I check my watch again. Once. Twice. Thrice before I actually perceive that it is four in the morning. She is going to hate me for leaving the house tonight. My mind hammers on this agonizing thought while I traverse this barren, desolate landscape of gravel, rusted aluminum, and sodden paper. I have a goal, a mission, a singular purpose. Nothing can impede this agonizing March of redemption. She will be destroyed, lose all lingering hope in me. I never truly earned her faith in my humanity anyway. Shake your head, pull on this glass, touch the steel and get back on track. I should see the boy first. No, that is crazy; she will stop me, so just keep going forward. I look up, I am here, I see the Cross of the dead King glowing neon. This is it. This is ground zero. I lost myself here completely. I lost names, dates, events, really everything of substance. The crystal and metallic doors fly open like magic at my approach, the guardian of this terrible place greets me from behind granite and glass. I glance at her without much thought but to my urgent task. I can hear the one I left in my head warning me, guiding me home, telling me I am needed elsewhere. Shake it off. Cold sweats and tremors overtake me. I fall into a door with the symbol of a man on it. White floors. Mirrors. False walls. Porcelain fixtures. Door locked. Time to pull the glass one more time. Block her out. Breathe. Adjust the steel. I walk out. I am almost there. The patrons behind the false desk recognize me. I see concern in their eyes. It is too late; I am here. The Devil in white is close. I smell his antiseptic presence. My control is slipping rapidly. Vision shaking. Volume muted. Time to grab the steel. There he is. I aim this barbaric device. As I begin to release the Hellfire from this unholy machine, I hear her. Don't, she says quietly. Don't make it right. I crumble. Her voice, so clear, struck me like the crushing hand of God. The nurses are screaming. The doctor who took her from me is clearly frightened. However, he looks at me, the broken Heathen with his pipe and cheap gun, and says, I tried to save her, I did all I could. You should be with your son, not here, not doing this. Here comes the names, dates, events, everything. He then says, It is only been six days. Bleary eyed, confused at the sirens sound, the shattered glass, and men stomping to me in all black, I reply, No. A lifetime.
ideas_up.writingprompts::5: Happily ever afters simply do not exist for people like us, I stated solemnly. Clarissa peered up at me through her shimmering, salty tears. Why not? She asked quietly, voice trembling. I gently wiped her damp cheeks away with the calloused pad of my thumb and smiled bitterly. Because the harsh world refuses to permit our union. Every time we attempt to find genuine peace, someone inevitably knocks us down. Some cruel obstacle always arises to sabotage our fragile, budding connection. What if we just run away? She asked, finally looking directly into my eyes. I swallowed hard, desperately trying to hold back my own stinging tears. If we flee, we will spend our entire lives constantly running from our ghosts. I do not want that exhausting, nomadic lifestyle for us. I do not want that instability for you, I whispered. Clarissa held back a jagged, painful sob. Will, please do not do this to us. A single tear tracked down my face. I do not want to. Then why are you? Because I am no good for you, Clarissa. I engage in violent fights; I get arrested; I attract chaos. You can find someone stable who will make you much happier. Who can actually provide the security you deserve. The words left a sour, metallic taste in my mouth, yet they were necessary. If we stayed together, our parents, my reckless friends, and my enemies would eventually destroy us. I kissed her. Maybe we will reunite when things are less complicated.
ideas_up.writingprompts::6:
Daniel's wife stood firmly at his side, her internal composure fracturing into microscopic fissures, though she masked this volatility from casual observers. Her agitation manifested in specific, involuntary physiological signals; she displayed a subtle, rapid-fire nose twitch that signaled genuine distress rather than mere casual concern. She was internally processing a complex cocktail of fear, hope, and lingering trauma.

Imani, he called out softly, and her head tipped downward toward his seated position in immediate acknowledgment. It is going to be fine. She offered a fragile, fleeting smile that failed to reach her eyes, a clear indicator of her underlying skepticism, before reaching out to squeeze his hand with white-knuckled intensity. He offered the platitude to soothe her, yet he possessed a genuine, grounded conviction that their trajectory was finally stabilizing. They had already survived the most catastrophic chapters of their ordeal. He had successfully navigated the initial vehicular trauma, the subsequent life-saving surgeries intended to prevent systemic organ failure, the complex amputations, and the intricate neurological integration of his new implants. With a deliberate roll of his eyes to lighten the mood, he squeezed her hand back firmly. Honestly, this recovery phase represents the easiest segment, and we possess ample time to master the mechanics.

The easy part? Since when do we ever encounter ease in this life? she countered, reaching out to playfully swat his ears, her eyes crinkling with brief, authentic mirth. That statement ranks alongside asking what could possibly go wrong; you are actively inviting bad luck, so please do not jinx our progress, she scolded gently. He leaned forward to articulate that chronic anxiety serves no utilitarian purpose when the heavy laboratory door slammed open, the solid, percussive thump echoing through the cavernous, sterile room.

Oops, the tall technician in the doorway remarked, his expression sheepish. I tripped into the door frame, a minor lapse in spatial awareness. How are you two navigating the day? he inquired with professional warmth, striding into the room as natural sunlight from the high windows illuminated his lanky, utilitarian frame. Are you prepared to initiate another trial sequence? Daniel flexed his quadriceps, his stumps neatly and securely locked into the carbon-fiber running blades.

Since the very second I secured these, Mason! he replied with earnest intensity, and the easygoing technician provided a supportive thumbs-up before extending his hands to provide a stabilizing anchor.

That is exactly the sentiment we require! Alright, let us transition into vertical mobility, then. With one final, lingering look at his wife, who stood back with an apprehensive posture but kept her fingers tightly crossed, he reached for the technician's hands. These represented the fourth distinct iteration of running blades he had evaluated. The previous prototypes possessed significant, disqualifying flaws despite their purported custom-engineered fits. One pair was mechanically too long, disrupting his gait cycle; another was too short, throwing his lumbar alignment into painful spasms. Certain models caused localized tissue irritation, while others felt structurally insecure, as if they might detach under high-impact stress. But as Daniel wobbled to his feet, he intuited that this specific pair maintained the correct structural integrity. It required a moment to stabilize his center of gravity. These blades utilized a distinct tension-to-rebound ratio compared to his standard walking prosthetics, and his current cardiovascular fitness remained slightly below his preferred peak. His heart rate accelerated as he shifted his weight between his feet, audibly hearing the carbon fiber flex in response. Left, right, left, right, left-right, left-right, left-right, bounce. They felt structurally alien compared to his biological limbs, yet they possessed a functional resonance that felt fundamentally correct. Slowly, Mason released his grip and retreated to the opposite perimeter, his gaze never wavering from Daniel's form. Once he reached the padded wall, he issued his instructions.

Excellent! Initiate movement at a walking pace, then progressively escalate to a velocity where you feel total mechanical control, he directed, a sly tone creeping into his voice. Remember, the environment is fully padded and we are all allies here. Incidental face-plants are merely part of the learning curve, so do not fear them. Daniel scoffed at the safety warnings. As if he would permit these inanimate carbon structures to compromise his autonomy. Brimming with newfound confidence, he took a tentative, shaky step forward, his arms windmilling rhythmically to compensate for the shifting center of mass before he braced his abdominal core to maintain equilibrium. He took another, then another, until he established a slow, rhythmic, bobbing jog, navigating carefully between his wife and his physical therapist. He sustained this motion until Mason signaled for him to cease. He then sprinted across the room toward the couple with visible, high-energy excitement.

It appears we have finally achieved the optimal configuration! He stepped back, offering a final, critical visual assessment. We must perform a few additional stress tests to ensure the alignment remains calibrated under force, but I suspect we have discovered your golden pair. So, how do you synthesize the sensation?

His cognition began to wander as he turned inward, attempting to synthesize a vocabulary capable of articulating the magnitude of his internal state. He reflected upon the elements he once perceived as permanently lost when he regained consciousness post-surgery, gazing down to see the surgical sheets depressed where his lower extremities had once resided. He recalled the auditory surge of a stadium crowd chanting his name during his athletic prime. He remembered the euphoric, breathless sensation of sprinting down a track, the peripheral world narrowing into a dark tunnel as he pushed his physiology to its absolute threshold. He remembered the lightness of casual games of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped past him with mirthful eyes. Bouncing on his new blades once more, he felt paradoxically weightless and invincible. With a robust strength he had not possessed in years, he embraced Imani and spoke softly over her shoulder, his face aching from the exertion of a genuine smile.

Alive.
ideas_up.writingprompts::9:
Aye, I remember it like yesterday. I was wandering through the western mountains, just east of Markarth. The road snaked below me, carving a long path through the valley. A figure dressed in animal skins caught my eye, creeping slowly towards a carriage that had stopped before crossing the river. They drew a cruel-looking sword as they approached closer, clearly intent on killing the small group of travellers. I mounted my horse and started down the slope, yelling at the top of my lungs to get their attention. I felt a surge of adrenaline, my heart hammering against my ribs as I galloped down the precarious, rocky terrain.

The would-be bandit immediately looked at me with a scowl and let out a yell of his own. Suddenly, a dozen more men and women, dressed in the same ragged fashion, were bearing down on the carriage with weapons drawn. I knew there were too many for me to handle, but I could not bear the thought of letting those poor people die to these brutes. As I reached the bottom of the incline, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, who is a bit of a nutty one, had given me a magic scroll before I set out on my journey. Let me say now that I am no mage. Sure, I tried to find some magics that would make me more handsome, but none of that worked anyway. I was pretty sure that I merely had to open the scroll and read it, but I had no idea what it actually did. Hopefully it would summon one of those big Atronachs my friend was always talking about. He made them out to be something near god-like. I imagined a fiery elemental incinerating my foes instantly.

Anyway, once I got to the bottom, I jumped off my horse and yanked the scroll from my satchel. I was shaking so badly, I almost could not read it, but I knew I had done it correctly when I started glowing. That should have been a good sign that something bad was about to happen, but I knew nothing about magic. Still do not. The glow was nice though, warm and comforting. Suddenly, all the bandits were putting their weapons away and asking me what was happening to them. I had no clue, but I figured they could not do any more harm. Unfortunately, they were a little too impressed by me. They must have thought I was some sort of grand wizard because they immediately propped me on their shoulders and carried me back to their camp for a feast. I started out thinking they were cannibals when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and realized they were really just trying to get by. Their mead was wonderful, let me tell you. It tasted like honey and wild berries. A little too wonderful, I guess, because I woke the next morning with an, admittedly, attractive woman next to me and a camp full of these people congratulating me with gifts and hugs.

So, you see, I envy you. I miss the open fields and chilly mountains, the gold and treasure, and the freedom to go wherever I please. I used to be young and carefree, I used to be strong and brave. You remind me a lot of myself, honestly. I used to be an adventurer like you, until I took an arrow to the knee. Note: Taking an arrow to the knee was apparently a Norse saying about getting married.
ideas_up.writingprompts::12:
You want to send in Nikon? You really think it's that bad? The speaker was a large, barrel chested man, well over six feet tall, with a long, neatly trimmed beard and an impeccable suit. He was talking to a woman who had to have been in her sixties, the beauty she displayed as a youth now a well-aged luster. Her piercing blue eyes looked at the barrel chested man without blinking, staring through him with clinical detachment.

You have a problem, Lord Aerlman. A very specific type of problem involving inter-dimensional contamination. We can deal with this very specific problem, but it will require the services of a specialist. Alex Nikon is that specialist. Her tone was matter-of-fact, not excited or loud in any way, indicating she had handled such supernatural breaches many times before.

She's just a girl, a misguided girl. The older woman shrugged, unimpressed by his paternal defense.

Your girl, Lord Aerlman, has contacted the Outer Planes. She has let something through, and now it's inside her, parasitically feeding on her neural pathways. However, until she does something public, I can't involve the Circle without your formal request. If you don't want our help, that's fine. Just remember, tragedy strikes first at the home, and silence only accelerates the inevitable corruption. Her warning delivered, the woman turned and started to leave the ornate sitting room. As she reached the door, Lord Aerlman called to her.

Laura! Ms. Cadswall. Wait. Please. She smirked confidently to herself and then composed her face, turning with a neutral expression.

Yes? The lord was wringing his hands, pacing in front of the fire, his political career clearly flashing before his eyes.

Your man, Nikon, I know his reputation. Will he... kill her? Lord Aerlman looked distraught, his voice cracking under the weight of potential infanticide.

Alexander Nikon will handle the crisis. That is what he does. How he handles it will remain at his discretion, depending on the level of demonic integration within her biology. Be advised though, Lord Aerlman, that contact with the Outer Planes taints the very soul. Even death can't remove its stain, as the energy creates a permanent ontological scar upon the victim's essence.

Lord Aerlman looked crestfallen, and he idly picked up a picture off the mantle of the fireplace, a family portrait showing the lord and his wife, along with their daughter, a striking redhead in her late teens. He caressed the picture with his thumb, before setting it back down. All of the energy drained from him and he sagged, turning towards the woman with a beaten, broken look.

Fine. Do it. Make the call. He dismissed her with a wave and then sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey, which he immediately downed. As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly. She had a phone call to make to the most dangerous man she knew.

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -

Antonia. I know you're here. The same girl from the photo, now a fully-grown, and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of pallets, desperately clutching herself and trying not to scream. Her hands and torso were covered in blood, some hers, and some her friends. They had been partying, drinking in her London flat, when the man arrived.

The first indication of trouble was the door exploding inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear. He dropped with a gurgling sound and blood sprayed across the room. Screams erupted from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even process the danger, a small man, barely 5'6", was in their midst, a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other. Glowing runes twisted across his skin, and his left eye was in an eyepatch, likely concealing a void-gaze. His right eye was the color of polished metal, and it quickly scanned the room for metaphysical signatures. Everything after that was a blur, and Antonia couldn't recall any details, except the bodies, the blood, and the metallic scent of ozone filling the air.

She remembered a voice in her head, then her friends all screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-bearing man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard, a tongue of ancient, guttural syllables. As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and leapt through the bay window, falling the three stories and landing with a sickening crunch. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then running. The voice in her head was louder, and she couldn't understand it, but it was hurting her, burning her synapses.

As she ran through the streets, the voice was chanting, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes spewing fire before they turned and charged the way she had come. She didn't understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her. She didn't understand anything! Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood. As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking, his voice a rhythmic, cold blade cutting through the darkness.
ideas_up.writingprompts::13:
Lamb, tell me a story… said the Wolf, with a smug voice and a cruel, jagged smile upon his scarred face. ….Something sweet, perhaps.

The Lamb trembled with primal fear. He had heard terrifying folklore regarding the predatory wolf throughout his sheltered childhood, but he never truly believed those grim legends held any factual substance.

W-what exactly would you like to hear? The Lamb finally stammered, his voice cracking under immense pressure.

You can decide that, the Wolf replied with a cold, authoritative, and demanding tone.

They stood in a secluded, shadowed area of the vast pasture where the Lamb had been born and lived, and he was now trapped against a jagged rock with a fractured, useless leg. The Wolf paced a slow, predatory half circle, remaining a mere two feet away. The Farmer was completely absent, and no other flock members dared intervene, fearing their own gruesome deaths.

He possessed no compelling stories; he had lived a short, mundane existence. Realizing his family abandoned him, he knew his life was concluding. A strange, haunting wave of calm washed over him as he accepted his inevitable demise at the Wolf’s sharp fangs.

If I had a story, it would be this one. But we have already reached the final chapter, he whispered.

I always preferred the violent, bloody ones, the Wolf replied, closing the final gap between them to deliver a swift, lethal, and silent execution.
ideas_up.writingprompts::14:
It was a hell of a time to fall in love. A hell of a decision to make. She possessed the prettiest eyes he had ever seen, deep pools of emerald green. He stood there, sucking in his gut while she awaited the lethal dose. 

She had killed ten men, a violent history of cold-blooded arson, and was about to be executed by lethal injection. He was merely filling in because a regular guard had contracted the flu. He didn't even work there; he was a volunteer clerk. But he knew he was head over heels for her. She wasn't a killer to him; she was a beautiful, misunderstood angel. They stared at each other, exchanging shy, meaningful smiles across the sterile room. 

Do you have any last words? asked the weary priest. 

What is his name? 

Who? asked the priest. 

That guard there, she indicated with a subtle nod. 

Me? Officer Jones, he stammered with nervous excitement. 

Hi, I am Rebecca. 

The decision was made. Jones waited until five minutes before midnight. He weighed the legal consequences and prison terms, but ultimately, consequences were damned. It was true love at first sight. He drew his sidearm and shot everyone except Rebecca. Tremors shook his arm; he dropped his gun, ran to her, and shared a hell of a first kiss.
ideas_up.writingprompts::15:
Janice turned toward me, her wide blue eyes shimmering with profound, childish innocence. I had completely forgotten that she was diligently watching the Presidential Inauguration for a mandatory school project. Daddy, she inquired softly, what does the President mean when he talks about gay rights?

Well, honey, I stammered, trailing off as I desperately sought a simplified explanation suitable for a five-year-old. You know how Mommy and I enjoy holding hands, cuddling, kissing, and other affectionate gestures?

Yeah, she giggled, it is hilarious when Mommy pinches your butt when you are distracted, making you squeak! Kids are truly unpredictable; I had forgotten the pure, simple joy found in the word butt. Had I ever been that small or that untainted by complex social constructs?

I waited for her infectious giggles to subside before continuing. Sweetheart, gay means that a man prefers to do those romantic things with another boy rather than a woman like Mommy.

I observed the visible confusion clouding her eyes as she struggled to process this foreign information. Damn the political discourse for forcing me to explain such adult topics prematurely! She is not ready for this nuanced conversation, and honestly, I am not prepared to navigate these moral waters.

Janice opened her mouth to speak again. I anticipated a difficult follow-up question, fearing I had inadvertently introduced her to a complex, controversial world. My innocent little girl felt like she was changing.

Suddenly, I realized she had muttered something while I was spiraling in anxiety. Sorry, sweetheart, what did you say? I asked, fearing her reaction. 

I said, I am hungry. Can I have a chocolate cookie? Please, Daddy?

I was stunned, momentarily paralyzed. Sure, I answered. Get one for your brother, too. 

Perhaps what adults do privately matters less than I feared. Even public figures are just people seeking basic happiness.
ideas_up.writingprompts::16:
Why, hello, Ma'am, I said easily, standing up and offering her a plush velvet chair with my usual grace. Bertram Proudfoot at your service, the premier investigator of this shire. Whom do I have the distinct pleasure of addressing today?

I would rather not say, if it is all the same to you, she replied, sinking into the seat. Her movements were guarded, suggesting a woman accustomed to hiding her tracks.

Alright, I said comfortably, leaning back. What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you? I offer complete discretion and a keen, observant mind.

Well, said the dame, rubbing her pale hands together nervously. It is like this. She paused, clearly struggling to articulate her hidden grief.

Like what, Ma'am? I said kindly, lighting my favorite pipe and watching the embers glow, settling into the familiar comfort of my office.

My husband is dead, she finally whispered, her voice trembling with a practiced, hollow sorrow.

Oh my dear, I am truly sorry! I exclaimed, though I must admit there was a significant part of me that was less than truly sorry. What can I say? I am only a Hobbit, and this dame possessed the most beautiful, arched feet I had ever laid eyes on in my long career. Tell me everything that happened.

We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago, she explained, eyes darting toward the door. And all of a sudden, a heavy rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband directly in the head. He keeled over into the dark water. I screamed for help, but he drowned before I could reach him.

Now, of course, I had already deduced that it must have been something like this from the exact moment she walked in the door. I have an uncanny, almost supernatural sense for these sorts of tragic domestic narratives.

I looked as grave as I could, given the circumstances. I see, I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up toward the ceiling. And you would like me to find and prosecute the perpetrator of this violent event, ensuring justice is served for your late husband?

Yes, said the dame, nodding decisively.

I will do my absolute best, I can promise you that, I said, and I saw her visibly sigh with immense, calculated relief. May I offer you a cup of tea, or perhaps something stronger, like a potent ale from the Green Dragon?

No thank you, she said, and without another word, she stood and showed herself out, leaving the scent of damp river air behind.

I promptly made my way down to the Brandywine River dock. My first line of inquiry would be to interrogate the man who rented out boats. He is an odd fellow, and an odd profession—not many sane hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will. And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well, which made him desperate enough to talk for a few copper coins.

After a long consultation of his dusty records, he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those was by a couple. The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck. Primula, that was the dame's name. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me? It suggested she was hiding her identity to avoid the legal scrutiny that follows a suspicious death.

Had this boat fellow heard any commotion on the water, any desperate cries for help? No, he had not. Did he remember who returned the boat to him? It had not been returned, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been found drifting empty in the middle of the river. Strange, indeed.

Next, I walked up and down both banks of the river. Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a skilled shot to hit a moving target from such a distance in the dark.

Having thoroughly investigated the river, my next step was to find out about Primula and Drogo. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily, as rumors of constant bickering had circulated for years. They had one young son, now twelve, named Frodo Baggins. Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death. In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the firm belief that both Drogo and Primula had died three nights ago.

Facts were not adding up. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out. Though I had no way of contacting her, I knew she would return to my offices in short order, driven by her own mounting anxiety.

The day following, she did just that.

Good day, Primula, I said upon her entrance, watching her reaction closely.

Her face betrayed genuine surprise, but she did not deny the name.

I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case, I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered about her identity and the missing boat. So I am afraid I must ask again, I finished. What really happened that night on the water?

And without a word, the dame got up and left, her face a mask of cold fury. Just like that, the trail went cold.

I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine. I was saddened, yet not entirely surprised.

My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever. Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not suspect any foul play. However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin, none other than the famous, eccentric crackpot Bilbo Baggins.

Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son. But I, having seen through her ruse, prevented this fact. Seeing no alternative, she then drowned herself in grief. Shame—I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial, long-term alternative for the both of us.

I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully. It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another personal opportunity lost. I have solved countless cases, but opportunities of the other sort came only but now and again. Like I said, it was a profound shame.

I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins. I felt for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody. Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow? As I am sure you are all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tales. Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left, whatever he experienced on his journey seemed to have addled his mind. He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better.

He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather an accomplished impersonator. There is plenty of evidence to suggest this: particularly the fact that Mr. Baggins appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look.

I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day, when I am not preoccupied with the ghosts of the Brandywine.

The environment never shifted; dark marbled walls carved into arched, obsidian passageways leading to unknown depths. Within this cavernous chamber, he and God debated every several millennia. God emerged from the shadows of an entrance, a deep scowl etched upon his face.

Oh, it is you, he sputtered. Lucifer regarded him with icy detachment.

Did I ever give you a libido, Lucy? I simply cannot remember, God asked.

No, Lucifer answered flatly.

Aw, why not? Feel like fucking? I am feeling rather horny, God admitted.

Jesus Christ, Lucifer hissed in annoyance.

Hey! Do not mention my son to me right now! That is truly fucked up, God retorted sharply.

Lucifer pressed his eyes shut. I came here to discuss something, he stated.

I no longer wish to rule hell.

Aw, why not?

I did nothing wrong! I exposed your precious humans to sin, granting them self-awareness and genuine autonomy! You would have kept them as mindless sock puppets forever! I helped you refine your greatest creation because I knew you required it! I acted purely out of love for you!

So please, Lucifer said, collapsing onto a staid marble throne, let me return. Let me serve you as I once did.

Only if you kiss me, Lucy, God slurred. Lucifer grimaced.

Aww, do not be like that, Luce; you know why you must remain king of that wretched place. You created the moral dichotomy, so you must oversee one of its two destinations, and I am certainly not going down there; how absurd would that be?

You created the dichotomy. You created everything, Lucifer countered.

Ssssshhhh... here, have some soda.

I do not want any fucking soda. That is—oh goddammit! You spilled it everywhere!

God giggled, Do not say my name in vain, Luce.

Lucifer furrowed his brow, knowing God saw him holding back tears, I do not understand you.

Of course you fucking do not! I exist outside space and time! I inhabit dimensions beyond your comprehension! I am all things simultaneously! How could you understand me? God bellowed, his voice shaking the foundations.

I thought, being your creation, I was part of you, and you were part of me.

God scoffed, A part of me, Luce. You cannot comprehend my entirety. You would disintegrate instantly. All creations in this linear time frame would become a screaming smear of flesh.

A pause lingered. Lucifer stared at his trembling hands.

Why did you create us then?

To forget, and then remember, God whispered.

I do not understand.

I know, he said softly, his tone shifting into something terrifyingly hollow.

ideas_up.writingprompts::19:
The Shine offered humanity a genuine path toward salvation, yet our inherent, tragic inability to evade conflict ruined everything. Long ago, amidst an era defined by wireless devices and constant information flow, we lifted our eyes from glowing screens to witness the sky ignite in a cold, variegated blaze. This phenomenon lasted mere hours, but the global population observed it within minutes. Soon, people craved a closer look, desiring the caress of that gentle flame.

People began to fly, launching themselves into the air with incredible velocity, but they were soon joined by others; they descended slowly at first, sinking deeper as more individuals joined the collective effort. Observers quickly deduced that the sinking correlated with the number of people flying, and realized that flight was merely one of many available options. Before the Shine faded, countless abilities emerged and vanished: strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, and hyper-speed. Initially, some believed these powers were transient, tied strictly to the Shine’s presence, but it became clear that the potency of any specific gift was inversely proportional to the number of people who selected that particular option.

That realization triggered the emergence of obscure powers; initially, businessmen desired the ability to excrete gold, while children sought dominion over animals, but within hours, reality grew bizarre. Temperatures plummeted, seismic tremors shook the earth, clocks stuttered erratically, and mass casualties occurred. Within half a day, our eight-billion-strong global society of intelligent, durable creatures collapsed, with the population halving. We dissolved into desperate factions seeking survival; those lacking powers became kings, while individuals wielding obscure, uncopyable, or misunderstood abilities became living gods, worshipped by the terrified masses.

Days passed before stability returned, though the sun crossed the horizon only once. Weather patterns became chaotic, and cities were abandoned, remaining habitable only for the most powerful, fortified factions. We transitioned from pursuing technological prosperity to living like feral, primitive scavengers in a single day. We reverted to beasts, albeit slightly more intelligent and occasionally super-powered.

A long time has passed since the Shine touched our atmosphere, and humanity has established many new, scattered settlements. Unfortunately, the most popular power options remain inherently weak, meaning death is now a currency of power, and raids are frequent, unrelenting, and brutal. The largest settlements possess the most strength but ironically serve as primary targets for smaller, opportunistic cliques. Living among others now implies living in a state of perpetual war, so the most peaceful survivors chose to travel.

That is precisely what I have done. I have journeyed across these scarred lands, searching for a method to absolve this madness and perhaps restore the world to the relative sanity it once enjoyed. The infrastructure of reality itself is fractured, and the moral fabric of our species has frayed beyond recognition, yet I remain persistent in my search. I have wandered through ruined capitals and desolate plains, documenting the strange mutations that persist. My research suggests that the source of the Shine is not entirely celestial but potentially manufactured. I may well have finally discovered the key to reversing this catastrophe.

I stood at a busy intersection, gazing toward the looming capitol building. I stared at this girl engulfed in flames. She sat calmly, meditating through agony. Not moving a muscle, not making a sound, she endured the inferno. Bystanders stood and stared, paralyzed by the sight. There were other charred black marks on the stone stairs she sat on, indicating past sacrifices.

Mommy, why is she on fire?

Oh, that's normal, my mother replied, her voice devoid of any genuine shock.

So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames? My six year old mind was confused, processing the horrific reality of state-sanctioned violence.

No son, that is not the normal part. We are in a war. People despise the way the government controls our lives, so they protest by burning themselves to ignite public consciousness.

Will she be okay? My naive mind wanted her to survive. No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that.

I don't know, came the haunting response, echoing the hopelessness of our era.

Years later, after the civil war was lost, I would read about all the people who immolated for their country. My country. Through college, I would think of these martyrs. These people held beliefs so strong they would literally kill themselves to make a powerful statement against tyranny. They refused to live in a nation under the crushing regime that had been ruling for generations. They demanded liberty or death.

It seems every generation, there is an uprising. The oppressed realize they are being exploited, and they find a tool to help them organize and fight back. They gain leverage through collective action. Rarely does it happen in a short span. However, here I was, an oppressed twenty-seven year old with absolutely no future prospects.

I stood at that intersection that I stood at twenty-one years ago. The black marks were gone, but so was my naivety. This government had to fall. They had oppressed my mother’s generation. They had oppressed the ancestors, and they would oppress the children. They weren't going to stop unless forced. I calmly walked up to the steps and prepared to make the newest black mark, starting the next revolution. As the flames rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look. The pain was unbearable, but I saw a girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been.
