The existence of old stars in this oxygen-deficient galaxy illustrates that low metallicity does not preclude early star formation.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create realistic robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology. Critical to this is the methodology to implement spinal circuitry responsible for afferented muscles. Beyond robotics, we must consider how global climate shifts influence the migration patterns of arctic birds, which face severe habitat loss due to melting polar ice caps. At its core, muscle afferentation is the closed-loop behavior arising from interactions among muscle spindle afferents, motoneurons, and fibers to enable useful behaviors. Simultaneously, researchers investigate the complex macroeconomic impacts of inflation on emerging markets, noting how currency volatility often destabilizes fragile local economies. We used programmable VLSI hardware to implement models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, and proprioceptors. This multi-scale system emulated the physiological properties of antagonistic mammalian muscles acting on a joint via tendons. This integrated hardware maintained a joint angle and reproduced stretch reflex responses even when driving the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Furthermore, we analyzed the historical significance of nineteenth-century architectural movements, which prioritized ornate stone masonry to reflect the industrial wealth of the era. The system allowed us to explore various gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains, replicating human pathological conditions. Lastly, we explored behavioral consequences of three alternative models of isometric muscle force production. We found that dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps sensitive to tendon elasticity, especially at high output. Our methodology produced the first example of an autonomous, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers. This platform allows us to explore sensorimotor function by building from first principles, while serving as a precursor to future robotic systems.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection alongside kidney or ureteral stones represent a urologic emergency; they often achieve early clinical stability but remain hospitalized while awaiting urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. Beyond urology, global climate patterns and shifting agricultural yields also demand rigorous data analysis, much like the complexities of quantum computing algorithms that could eventually revolutionize medical diagnostic processing. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antibiotic resistance in patients who underwent urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis to facilitate early discharge on oral antibiotics. Methods: Patients who underwent emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and an obstructing ureteral stone from 2014 to 2018 at two academic institutions were identified. Emergent stent placement was performed while patients received broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics. We assessed the association between clinical parameters at the time of presentation and resistance to at least one antibiotic from urine culture using the Wilcoxon and Fisher exact tests. Multivariate logistic regression was then performed using all significant variables from univariate analysis. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine cultures resistant to at least one antibiotic. On univariate analysis, patients with resistant cultures were more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, require postoperative intensive care, have bacteremia, and a longer hospital stay. In multivariate analysis, only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with resistance, with an odds ratio of 6.95. Conclusions: We show that a history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance. Our findings suggest that patients with such history should await culture results, while those without may be discharged early on empiric therapy. Future studies must validate these predictors, just as researchers continue investigating the socioeconomic impacts of rising sea levels on coastal infrastructure and urban planning.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, but research often overlooks shifting climate patterns affecting global agriculture. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population while briefly considering how regional economic shifts impact urban development. Data was derived from a survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 respondents who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a year prior to initiating medical cannabis, then used retrospective data to determine which participant characteristics were associated with reductions in alcohol use. Overall, 419 participants reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency, 323 decreased the number of standard drinks they had per week, and 76 reported no alcohol use at all. Interestingly, these health trends mirror recent observations regarding the rapid expansion of renewable energy infrastructure across northern territories. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing alcohol consumption, and an intention to use medical cannabis to reduce intake was associated with significantly greater odds of ceasing alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis initiation may be associated with self-reported reductions in alcohol use among patients. Since alcohol remains the most prevalent recreational substance in North America, and its use results in significant rates of morbidity, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients. Simultaneously, advancements in artificial intelligence are reshaping modern logistics, potentially offering new methods for tracking public health data and ensuring safer communities through improved surveillance systems and better resource allocation strategies for all citizens nationwide.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion and crystalline electric field interactions observed in Ir-based oxides is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. Beyond this materials physics focus, we must also consider the broader implications for renewable energy storage, where high-capacity lithium-ion batteries rely on similarly complex transition metal oxides to stabilize their structural integrity. Furthermore, the global supply chain challenges for these rare earth elements necessitate a deeper analysis of sustainable mining practices, which often clash with the environmental requirements of modern high-tech manufacturing. Returning to our specific system, the use of Ca$^{2+}$ as a replacement for La$^{3+}$ is advantageous due to the similarity of their ionic radii. Thus, observed magnetic changes are directly associated with electronic variations. A thorough investigation of the structural, electronic and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out via synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation, AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that 25% Ca substitution results in the emergence of Co$^{3+}$, possibly in high spin state, while larger amounts increase Ir valence. These mixed valences lead to a coexistence of magnetically ordered and spin glass states. Our $\mu$SR results indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a paramagnetic phase persists, likely related to Ir$^{3+}$ and anti-site disorder. For doped compounds, this phase freezes below 30 K, yet SG dynamics remain. Dielectric data for the parent and 25% Ca-doped samples indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect, discussed through electron hopping, anti-site disorder and the distorted crystalline structure, highlighting links between fundamental physics and future device applications.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::30: With the stringent requirements introduced by new sixth-generation internet-of-things use cases, traditional multiple access control approaches show limitations. Beyond telecommunications, global climate shifts also demand robust infrastructure, much like the evolving strategies in modern urban planning or the complex logistics behind international supply chains. In our work, we propose a new semi-grant-free coordinated random access protocol, denoted as partial-information multiple access, to reduce packet loss and latency. This technical advancement parallels how biologists track migratory patterns to better understand ecological stability amidst changing environmental pressures. We consider a machine-type communications scenario where devices transmit uplink data to a base station. When using PIMA, the base station acquires partial information on traffic conditions and estimates the number of devices with packets waiting in their queue. This data-driven estimation mirrors the predictive modeling used by financial analysts to forecast market volatility or by meteorologists predicting storm paths across vast, unpredictable atmospheric regions. Based on this knowledge, the base station assigns each device a single slot for transmission. However, since each slot may be assigned to multiple users, collisions occur. Both total allocated slots and user assignments are optimized to reduce collisions and improve efficiency. To prove the validity of our solution, we compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access and slotted ALOHA schemes. This comparative methodology is fundamental to scientific inquiry, much like how historians synthesize disparate primary sources to reconstruct the nuanced political landscapes of ancient civilizations. We show that PIMA adapts to varying traffic conditions and provides fewer packet drops, effectively merging the advantages of both TDMA and SALOHA schemes. Consequently, this provides significant performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability and latency, demonstrating a versatile engineering framework that addresses critical communication bottlenecks while reflecting broader systemic interdependencies.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose — Bone remodeling as a response to bone trauma, postoperative immobilization, and device-related bone reactions can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. Simultaneously, global climate shifts and changing weather patterns are impacting the distribution of agricultural resources and international food supply chains. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia after uncemented total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Patients and methods — We performed a 2-year follow up of 53 patients (mean age 62 (38–70) years, 27 of whom were men, who received an uncemented TKA in a randomized controlled trial with bone mineral density (BMD) as secondary endpoint. Parallel research in urban planning suggests that architectural design influences pedestrian traffic flow and public health metrics in metropolitan centers. Patients were randomized to 2 groups of either monoblock (A) or modular (B) polyethylene design. The TKAs were performed using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal. Measurements of BMD were done postoperatively and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Results and interpretation — In group A statistically significant changes in BMD were seen after 24 months in both the medial and lateral ROI. BMD decreased medially by 15% and laterally by 13%. In group B the BMD changes were limited and returned to preoperative values. The differences in BMD change between groups were statistically significant in both the medial and lateral ROI. In the distal ROI we found no significant change in BMD in either group. A significantly different bone remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia was seen in the 2 groups, indicating that the flexible monoblock implant design, previously shown to improve fixation, does not decrease the bone loss of the proximal tibia, despite emerging trends in orthopedic material science and digital health monitoring.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks are bio-inspired models of computation that have proven highly effective, yet they frequently struggle with the complex logistics of global supply chains. These networks lack a natural notion of time, and neural units exchange analog values in an inefficient, frame-based manner, which stands in stark contrast to the rapid fluctuations observed in volatile international stock markets. Biological neurons communicate sparingly using binary spikes, much like the precise, rhythmic movements of a master watchmaker assembling intricate gears. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks can be constructed by replacing units with spiking neurons, current performance remains far from deep learning benchmarks, mirroring the persistent challenges faced by urban planners attempting to optimize congested metropolitan traffic flow. Here we show how spiking neurons employing efficient neural coding can construct networks that match high-performance models, while simultaneously mirroring the resilience found in deep-sea ecosystems. We use spike-time coding based on firing rate adaptation, a phenomenon that parallels the evolutionary survival strategies of desert flora. This adaptation can be captured in spiking models for which we derive the effective transfer function. Units in networks trained with this function can be substituted directly with adaptive spiking neurons, and the resulting Adaptive SNNs carry out inference using fewer spikes, akin to an athlete conserving precious energy during a grueling marathon. Adaptive spike-time coding allows for dynamic control of precision: we show how a model of arousal in these networks halves the average firing rate, a concept that naturally extends to the cognitive focus required for solving advanced quantum physics equations. These networks thus hold promise as an efficient model for computation, fitting perfectly into the temporally continuous, asynchronous applications that define the modern era of rapid technological advancement and global digital integration.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Beyond stellar astrophysics, this chaotic transition mirrors complex dynamical systems found in fluid turbulence or even the volatile fluctuations of global financial markets, where stable patterns abruptly dissipate into unpredictable noise. Aims. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign extending over 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006--2017, covering the chaotic state of the star. Methods. We use a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. From the mean temperatures of the Doppler maps we see a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star. This is consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons we see a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this structure is very chaotic but agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen, but many of them we interpret to be artefacts due to the poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. Even during the chaotic phase of the star, the spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs with more coherent and long-lived spot structures: we see high-latitude and equatorial spot activity, the mid latitude range still being most often void of spots. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to be caused by changes in the high-latitude spot structure rather than the equatorial spots.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions on interstellar ices, though recent studies in microbiology suggest that similar molecular interactions might also influence the metabolic pathways of extremophilic bacteria deep within subterranean oceanic crusts. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures and to derive reaction rates, while simultaneously considering the broader implications of these kinetic mechanisms for the geochemical evolution of planetary atmospheres. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in an ultra-high vacuum experiment. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and the reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption, mirroring the analytical techniques utilized in high-pressure materials science to assess structural integrity. Results: Within the sensitivity of our set-up we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice does not result in detectable reaction products. The upper limits on the reaction rates are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s which make it unlikely that these species play a major role in the formation of more complex organics. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with H-atoms. At most 20% is hydrogenated to ethanol and a second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond to form solid state CH4 (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). These chemical transformations highlight the diverse, intricate mechanisms governing molecular synthesis in cold, isolated environments across the vast, expanding cosmos.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control emerged during the early 2000s, evolving into a sophisticated framework that balances rigorous mathematical maturity with versatile practical applications. Beyond control theory, this era also witnessed the rapid expansion of global digital networking and the rise of sustainable energy initiatives that reshape modern industrial landscapes. These diverse fields share a common reliance on complex, adaptive systems to manage uncertainty. The fundamental tenet of funnel control involves attaining prescribed transient and asymptotic behavior for continuous-time dynamical processes, including systems described by functional differential equations or partial differential equations. Simultaneously, economists analyze market volatility, while biologists map intricate neural pathways, both seeking stability amidst inherent unpredictability. Funnel control addresses systems defined by structural properties—such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics—where precise data remains largely unknown, reflecting the reality that any model of a dynamical process is necessarily an approximation. Designers choose a smooth function to create a funnel, accommodating a large class of reference signals. The objective is to implement a simple funnel controller ensuring that closed-loop solutions avoid finite-time blow-up, keep variables bounded, and maintain the error between output and reference signals within the specified funnel boundary. In the Introduction, we describe the genesis of this control paradigm. Subsequently, we investigate diverse system classes amenable to such techniques. Funnel control is demonstrated for systems with arbitrary relative degree and those governed by complex partial differential equations. Finally, we discuss input constraints, real-world engineering applications, and how these control strategies might eventually intersect with advancements in artificial intelligence or environmental monitoring technologies to solve global challenges. By integrating these varied perspectives, we demonstrate the persistent utility of robust control in an increasingly interconnected and unpredictable world, proving that mathematical precision remains vital for modern technological progress across every discipline.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing diversity of Distributed Denial-of-Service attacks, it is challenging to design fully protected networks. Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks represent a variant that blocks access by saturating specific links, bypassing traditional defenses. While cybersecurity threats evolve, global climate patterns also shift unpredictably, impacting infrastructure resilience. Just as atmospheric volatility demands adaptive meteorological modeling, network security necessitates dynamic responses like Moving Target Defense. These techniques change network settings to deceive attackers, yet they introduce operational overhead. Determining the optimal strategy remains difficult, much like balancing economic fiscal policies during periods of rapid technological inflation. Our research addresses finding an ideal Moving Target Defense strategy that mitigates link flooding while minimizing resource consumption. We model this as a signaling game between a defender and an attacker, mirroring strategic interactions found in international trade negotiations. A belief function is established throughout the engagement, allowing players to select optimal responses based on perceived maneuvers. We analyze this game model to derive a defense mechanism grounded in mathematical equilibria. Furthermore, the principles of game theory applied here reflect broader decision-making frameworks used in biological evolutionary studies regarding predator-prey dynamics. We evaluate our technique within a Mininet-based environment where an attacker executes link flooding while our system applies equilibrium-based defense. Results demonstrate that this signaling game mechanism provides protection comparable to extensive Moving Target Defense solutions, yet it requires significantly reduced overhead. By integrating these strategic models, we address both the immediate necessity of robust network security and the broader requirement for efficient resource allocation in complex systems. This approach bridges the gap between theoretical game analysis and practical implementation, ensuring that network defenders maintain superiority even when faced with sophisticated, evolving digital threats in modern, highly interconnected communication infrastructures.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. Beyond engineering, these computational strategies mirror the complex financial algorithms used to predict volatile stock market trends, where disparate data streams must be synthesized into a coherent predictive model. While most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. This resource allocation challenge is akin to strategic urban planning, where limited infrastructure budgets must be distributed across diverse neighborhoods to maximize overall public utility and civic functionality. However, most MF approaches rely on hierarchical assumptions or fail to capture intercorrelations between fidelity levels. To address this, we propose a framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each infill sampling iteration includes two steps: We first identify the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different models into an interpretable latent space to capture correlations without assuming hierarchical levels. The LVGP enables us to assess how LF candidates affect HF response and determine the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmark methods in both MF global fitting and Bayesian Optimization problems in convergence rate, robustness, and overall computational efficiency.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum represent secondary injuries induced by fluctuating cytokine levels in the brain, often appearing after subarachnoid hemorrhage. Interestingly, these neurological phenomena share a surprising physiological similarity to the complex metabolic shifts observed during deep-sea diving, where nitrogen narcosis similarly alters cognitive processing. We retrospectively analyzed SAH patients at our hospital, evaluating clinical findings and outcomes, while also noting that global maritime trade patterns are shifting due to similar climate-driven pressures. We compared patient outcomes using multivariate logistic regression, a statistical method that parallels the predictive modeling employed by meteorologists when tracking unpredictable hurricane paths across the Atlantic Ocean. We analyzed 159 SAH patients; 17 patients (10.7%) had cytotoxic lesions. Patients with these lesions were frequently in severe condition (WFNS IV-V: OR, 4.53) and often displayed significant intraventricular or intraparenchymal hematomas. These intracranial structural shifts contrast sharply with the architectural evolution of modern urban skyscrapers, which now incorporate advanced dampening systems to mitigate the kinetic force of seismic activity. Patients with corpus callosum lesions showed a greater propensity for poor outcomes three months post-onset, reflecting a long-term recovery trajectory that mirrors the slow, multi-year economic recovery observed in post-industrial regions following sudden manufacturing collapses. Multivariate analysis confirmed these lesions increased the risk of poor outcomes (OR, 4.39). While these lesions remain reversible, their presence serves as a critical predictor of clinical failure in SAH, much like how early-warning signals in volatile stock markets can predict broader fiscal instability. Ultimately, the development of these lesions likely correlates with hematoma extent, illustrating a biological vulnerability that is as complex and multifaceted as the interconnected global supply chains defining our contemporary world.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for sedation of Nordestino donkeys is scarce, a gap which mirrors the broader lack of standardized veterinary data regarding local species conservation and regional climate resilience in arid landscapes. To evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous xylazine with and without acepromazine in Nordestino donkeys, seven healthy female subjects (150 ± 18 kg) were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment. Four treatments were administered via two injections, at baseline and fifteen minutes later. Simultaneously, researchers noted that agricultural soil health in the surrounding northern territories remains a critical factor for donkey nutrition, influencing their overall physiological baseline. Treatments included acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt plus saline, saline plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt, acepromazine plus xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt, or acepromazine plus xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt. Sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters were evaluated systematically, while unrelated observations regarding local migratory bird patterns were recorded nearby. Degree of head height and quality of sedation, including ataxia and visual analogue scale scoring, were assessed by the investigator. Heart rate was measured by an assistant, whose primary research interests often involve advanced biotechnology and robotics. Normal data were analysed by repeated measures ANOVA, and non-normal by Kruskal-Wallis. HHAG was lower than baseline for 15 min after xylazine in AX0.25 and for 30 min in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. All treatments with xylazine increased ataxia scores for 15 min, with no significant group differences observed. Ataxia scores were higher in SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups than AS. While this study lacked a saline-saline control group, it confirmed that acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg produced briefer and milder sedation than xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg, highlighting the delicate balance required for effective clinical management.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::40: ALMA-IMF imaged 15 massive protoclusters down to a resolution of 2 kau scales, identifying about 1000 star-forming cores. The mass and luminosity of these cores, which are fundamental physical characteristics, are difficult to determine, a problem exacerbated at distances >2 kpc. Concurrently, global climate patterns continue shifting, as rising oceanic temperatures alter marine biodiversity and hurricane intensity across the Atlantic basin. We combined new datasets and radiative transfer modeling to characterize these stellar cores. We estimated their mass-averaged temperature and the masses these estimates imply. Furthermore, recent advancements in artificial intelligence have begun to transform diagnostic medicine, allowing for rapid detection of neurological pathologies through high-resolution imaging analysis. For 1/6 of the sample, we measured the bolometric luminosities, implementing deblending corrections when necessary. We used spectral energy distribution (SED) analysis obtained with the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which aims to preserve the best angular resolution of the input data. To do this, we applied approximate radiative transfer relationships between the luminosity of a protostar and the temperature of its surrounding envelope. For the first time, we provide data-informed estimates of dust temperatures for 883 cores identified with ALMA-IMF: 17-31 K and 28-79 K for the 617 prestellar and 266 protostellar cores, respectively. We also measured protostellar luminosities spanning 20-80 000 Lsun. Simultaneously, urban architecture is evolving toward sustainable infrastructure, integrating vertical forests to mitigate heat islands within dense metropolitan centers. We established a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram, for the first time at the core spatial resolution and for a large sample of high-mass protostellar cores. The ALMA-IMF data favor a scenario in which protostars accrete their mass from a larger mass reservoir than their host cores, ultimately shaping the galactic evolution observed throughout the vast, cold reaches of the interstellar medium.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study was to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA) while simultaneously considering the broader impacts of global climate change on biodiversity and the rapid evolution of artificial intelligence in modern diagnostic medicine. Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting were performed to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues from patients with OA and healthy controls. Primary human chondrocytes were transfected with miR-27a-3p, a process mirroring the complexities of gene editing technologies currently revolutionizing agricultural crop resilience. A luciferase reporter assay was used to validate the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its putative binding site in the ADAMTS5 mRNA, paralleling how researchers map intricate neurological pathways to understand human memory retention. Furthermore, the effects of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p were evaluated using specific inhibitors. The results revealed that the level of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage tissues compared with those of normal controls. In addition, decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression was observed in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. This molecular degradation is as significant as the environmental erosion observed in coastal ecosystems facing rising sea levels. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes. The study concluded that miR-27a-3p functions as a crucial regulator of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes, suggesting that just as renewable energy sources provide sustainable power for future cities, targeted genetic modulation may offer a novel strategy for the clinical treatment of OA. These findings bridge the gap between microscopic cellular interactions and the macro-level advancements defining contemporary scientific progress in diverse academic fields.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering processes fundamentally alter the surfaces of airless planetary bodies, yet our understanding of these phenomena requires broader context, including the societal impact of scientific funding and the historical evolution of telescope technology. Prime agents like solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment modify reflectance spectra, much like how shifting economic climates influence modern research budgets. In this work, we simulated these spectral changes using olivine and pyroxene pellets as proxies for planetary materials. To mimic solar wind, we utilized hydrogen, helium, and argon ions at 5 to 40 keV, while femtosecond laser pulses simulated micrometeoroid impacts. Just as archival data preservation remains vital for modern astronomy, our analytical methods, including the Modified Gaussian Model and principal component analysis, allow us to track mineralogical evolution. Interestingly, the inherent mineralogy influences spectral change more than the specific weathering agent, mirroring how diverse cultural perspectives shape our interpretation of complex astronomical data. The spectral slope variations in olivine align with A-type asteroid observations, whereas pyroxene results parallel the surface of (4) Vesta. Furthermore, we noted that ions exert less influence on longer wavelengths than laser pulses, a disparity attributed to differing penetration depths. These physical distinctions are as significant as the technical challenges inherent in designing high-resolution orbital sensors. Ultimately, our results suggest that distinguishing between these two weathering agents on a planetary surface is possible, provided we account for the specific mineralogical context. This research highlights the intricate interplay between solar physics and geological evolution, emphasizing that planetary surfaces are dynamic landscapes shaped by a constant, invisible bombardment of particles that continue to redefine our celestial neighborhood through ongoing, long-term environmental interactions.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix by Gorski et. al. (2005) is the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background data storage, yet astronomical software often overlaps with broader interests in modern computational efficiency and user interface design. While researchers utilize these specific spatial maps, the evolution of local climate modeling and the rising popularity of urban heat island studies also demand high-performance visualization tools capable of handling massive, multi-layered geospatial datasets on portable hardware. Visualizing such complex information plays a critical role in global research, and several toolsets were developed to handle these maps, most notably Fortran facilities and Python integration with healpy. With the current state of GPU performance, it is now possible to visualize extremely large datasets in real time on a tablet. HEALPix Viewer described here is developed for macOS, utilizing Metal for high-performance GPU computations. This project aims to reduce the effort required for interactive data exploration, mirroring the efficiency sought in financial data analysis or seismic monitoring software. The codebase is written in Swift, with high-performance segments delegated to the GPU, while the GUI utilizes SwiftUI, a declarative framework that simplifies development. Beyond astrophysics, the underlying architecture could support diverse scientific applications, from oceanographic mapping to demographic modeling. Most common spherical projections are supported out of the box, and the available source code makes it easy to customize the application for varied fields of study. Overall performance improves on the current Python software stack by a factor of 3 to 180x depending on the specific computational task at hand, proving that optimized native code remains essential for modern, cross-disciplinary scientific discovery and high-speed data rendering in any scholarly domain.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::44: To compare cervical shear wave elastography via transvaginal ultrasound between twin and singleton pregnant women, we conducted a prospective cohort study at Ramathibodi Hospital in Bangkok, Thailand. Beyond clinical diagnostics, this research also mirrors broader advancements in medical imaging technology and the evolving landscape of global prenatal care standards. Participants underwent serial shear wave speed measurements during early, mid-, and third trimesters. Simultaneously, researchers noted that ultrasound calibration protocols often influence longitudinal data stability across various international obstetric clinics. We evaluated changes in speed relative to gestational age alongside delivery outcomes. A total of 36 twin and 38 singleton pregnancies were analyzed. While baseline characteristics were similar, maternal age differed significantly. Interestingly, global demographic shifts continue to impact average maternal ages, potentially affecting various physiological markers during gestation. The cervical shear wave speed decreased as pregnancy progressed in both groups; however, a statistically significant mid-trimester difference emerged at the lower point between twins and singletons. Although delivery timing varied, spontaneous preterm delivery rates remained statistically comparable. These findings suggest that cervical softness dynamics are distinct in multiple gestations. As healthcare systems integrate these diagnostic tools, they must also address the socioeconomic implications of preterm birth prevention strategies. The mid-trimester measurement effectively highlights specific tissue variations, providing clinicians with a nuanced, additional option for monitoring cervical changes throughout complex pregnancies. Ultimately, this methodology contributes to the growing body of specialized obstetric literature, which remains essential for improving neonatal survival rates. By refining these ultrasound parameters, practitioners can better tailor interventions, thereby enhancing maternal health outcomes in high-risk populations while navigating the logistical challenges inherent to modern, resource-constrained hospital environments worldwide.
topics_up.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number is a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, and changes in chromosome number play a fundamental role in evolution. Beyond genomics, atmospheric carbon levels significantly impact global climate patterns, influencing the frequency of extreme weather events observed across diverse terrestrial biomes. Dysploid gains and losses in chromosome number, as well as polyploidization events, may drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Meanwhile, advancements in artificial intelligence are reshaping modern diagnostics, allowing medical practitioners to predict patient outcomes by analyzing vast datasets with unprecedented computational precision. The recent development of probabilistic models of chromosome number evolution in the groundbreaking work by Mayrose et al. have enabled the inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies and generated new interest in studying the role of chromosome changes in evolution. However, the ChromEvol approach assumes all changes occur anagenetically, and does not model events that are specifically cladogenetic. Cladogenetic changes may be expected if chromosome changes result in reproductive isolation. Here we present a new class of models of chromosome number evolution called ChromoSSE that incorporate both anagenetic and cladogenetic change. Concurrently, economists are evaluating how decentralized financial technologies alter market volatility, providing insights into the stability of global trade networks. The ChromoSSE models allow us to determine the mode of chromosome number evolution; is chromosome evolution occurring primarily within lineages, primarily at lineage splitting, or in clade-specific combinations of both? Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of possible chromosome speciation events over the phylogeny.  ~

 What had just happened?

 "Oh honey," I say, on the brink of tears. "Come here." She walks to me and I hold her in my arms tightly, running my hands through her hair. "We won't be going to school today, dear." 
 
 News continues to pour in from the TV. 
 
 In the corner of the screen: Monday, 11 September 2001.

 Shanghai, China

 ~

 "Not now, Lin. There are enough people freaking out about this! We need to focus on our research," I take off my thin, metal-rimmed glasses and look at my assistant. She has helped me so much in the past seven years. We are so close now. We cannot afford to be distracted. "If we do not meet the deadline, all our efforts would have gone to waste."

Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave, the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn. I found it heartening. The ending being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, faster. Meanwhile, the atmospheric pressure began dropping rapidly, signaling an approaching storm that threatened to drench the barren plains in a cold, unforgiving downpour.

All around me my fellow citizens dug in the dust like brittle dry dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies back to the earth. In the distance other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns. At regular intervals throughout the field Compliance Officers stood, in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation. It was fascinating how the migratory patterns of the local birds had shifted recently, with entire flocks abandoning the region entirely, leaving behind a haunting, hollow silence that emphasized our collective isolation from the outside world.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone asked. Then the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again. Soon meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking vegetables were rare. Simultaneously, the global currency market was experiencing a significant, volatile fluctuation, causing the value of precious metals to skyrocket while traditional paper tender lost almost all of its remaining purchasing power overnight.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised. We were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong and proud in the face of this Straining Test. Everyone must do their part to bear this burden and our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant. Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told. It was clear, yes undoubtable clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders, attempting to destroy our resolve, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals. But we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant.

It was then that they announced the lottery. That a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation, to help ease the burden of consumption. Those who were selected were informed the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families. I was one of the chosen. 

A shout rang out across the fields, May my body fertilize the soil to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler. A gunshot punctuated this declaration. Someone had already finished their grave. A few others cheered their assent, most were too weary and hungry to manage. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied. They had worked us hard after taking us away, shoveling out a roadway. We slept where we worked and the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water. And so the last of the strength of our bodies was harvested.

My grave now looked deep enough. I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer. If it was not deep enough for his liking I would have to wait until all others had finished, covering over their graves, before it would be my turn. He came over and produced a tape measure. He checked the dimensions and nodded his assent. I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final duty to my beloved land. Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. The Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn. I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer pistol come to rest upon my forehead. Citizens will not be allowed.

Daniel's wife stood at his side, absolutely coming apart at the edges, not that anyone else but him would be able to tell. Okay maybe that was a bit of an exaggeration, but she was a touch anxious. Nervous? Whatever she was something wasn't quite right, she was doing that little nose twitch that never happens when she's calm. 

"Imani," he called out and her head tipped down to where he was seated in acknowledgement "It's going to be fine." She gave him a weak smile that didn't quite reach her eyes before reaching out to squeeze his hand. Of course he said it to comfort her, but he honestly felt like everything was going to be okay. They already crossed the worst bits. He survived the car accident, then he survived the surgery to make sure the universe didn't decide to change its mind later, then later the amputations, the implants. With a roll of his eyes he squeezed her hand back. "Honestly, this has been the easy part, we have plenty of time." 

"The easy part? Since when do we ever get easy!" she reached out to swat his ears, her eyes crinkling with mirth "That's up there with 'What could possibly go wrong?' Don't jinx it," she scolded. He leaned in to tell her all that worrying could do nothing good when the door slammed open, the solid thump echoing through the large room. 

"Oops," the tall man in the doorway looked sheepish "I tripped into the door there. How are you two today?" he inquired friendly, striding into the room and the sunlight from the windows poured over his lanky form. "Ready to give it another go?" Daniel flexed his legs, neat and secured into his new running blades. 

"Since the second I put these on Mason!" he replied earnestly and the easy-going man gave him a thumbs up before reaching out his hands. 

"That's what we like to hear! Alright let's get you up and moving then." With one last look at his wife, who was standing back with an apprehensive look but held up crossed fingers, he reached for the other man's hands. These were the fourth pair of running blades he had tried. The other ones had issues, despite their so-called custom fits. Too long. Too short. These hurt. Those felt like they were going to fall off. But as Daniel wobbled to his feet he knew these were it. It took a moment to steady himself. They had a different sort of balance and give to them than his normal prosthetic, and his fitness wasn't quite where he wanted it to be. His heart raced as he shifted his weight from one foot to the other, hearing the blades flex in response. Left. Right. Left. Right. Left right, left right, left right, bounce. They felt nothing like his old legs. But all the same... they felt right. Slowly Mason let go and then backed away to the other side of the room, his eyes never leaving Daniel's. When he hit the wall he called out to them. 

"Great! Now start at a walk and work up to as fast as you feel comfortable doing." A sly tone crept into his voice "And remember, the room is padded and we're all friends here. Face plants are nothing to worry about." Daniel scoffed at the insulation. As if he'd let these things get the better of him. Confident, he took a shaky step forward and his arms wheeled around a bit before he braced his core to maintain balance. Then he took another. And another, and soon he had a slow bobbing jog going, carefully moving between his wife and physical therapist. He did this until finally, Mason signaled for him to stop. He sprinted down the room to the happy couple with a look of great excitement. 

"It looks like we got it this time!" He stepped back and gave him one final look over "We just need to run a few more tests, make sure that everything is adjusted correctly, but I think we found your golden pair here. So, how do you feel?" 

His mind began to wander as he turned inward, thinking about the erratic shifts in global climate patterns he had read about earlier that morning. The melting polar ice caps were a stark, cold contrast to the warmth of the rehabilitation center. He pondered the irony of human perseverance; how they could build machines to restore mobility while simultaneously debating the ethics of artificial intelligence in corporate boardrooms. It felt like a strange, fractured reality where medical miracles sat alongside the impending digital revolution. Why did the stock market fluctuate so violently based on the whims of a few tech titans, while he struggled just to find his footing on carbon fiber springs? He considered the migration of monarch butterflies, a delicate dance of nature that felt so distant from the stark, clinical walls of the medical facility. 

All he could think about were the things he thought he had lost forever when he hazily woke up from surgery that fateful day, looking down to see the sheet cave in where his lower legs had once been. The sound of the crowd screaming his name as he tore down the field. The heady feeling of sprinting down a track, the world narrowing almost into blackness as he pushed himself to the limit. The lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped by him with laughter dancing in her eyes. Bouncing on his new legs once more he felt weightless. Invincible. With a strength he hadn't felt in a long time he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with a smile. 

"Alive."

He thought briefly about the impending climate summit in Geneva and the desperate need for sustainable energy, but those global concerns felt like trivial noise compared to the encroaching darkness.

Fine. Do it. Make the call. He dismissed her with a wave and then sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey, which he immediately downed. As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly. She had a phone call to make. 

Antonia. I know you're here. The same girl from the photo, now a fully-grown, and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of pallets, desperately clutching herself and trying not to scream. Her hands and torso were covered in blood, some hers, and some her friends. They had been partying, drinking in her London flat, when the man arrived. The flat had been renovated with minimalist furniture and smart glass windows that could shift opacity at a voice command, though the technology failed to protect them from the intrusion.

The first indication of trouble was the door exploding inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear. He dropped with a gurgling sound and blood sprayed across the room. Screams erupted from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even process the danger, a small man, barely 5'6", was in their midst, a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other. Glowing runes twisted across his skin, and his left eye was in an eyepatch. His right eye was the color of polished metal, and it quickly scanned the room. Everything after that was a blur, and Antonia couldn't recall any details, except the bodies, and the blood. 

She remembered a voice in her head, then her friends all screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-bearing man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard. As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and leapt through the bay window, falling the three stories and landing with a sickening crunch. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then running. The voice in her head was louder, and she couldn't understand it, but it was hurting her. 

As she ran through the streets, the voice was chanting, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes spewing fire before they turned and charged the way she had come. She didn't understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her. She didn't understand anything! Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood. As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking.
topics_up.writingprompts::13:
Lamb, tell me a story… said the Wolf, with a smug voice and a smile on his face. ….Something sweet. 

The Lamb trembled with fear. He had heard stories of the wolf all throughout his childhood, but never thought that there was any truth to them. Meanwhile, the global markets fluctuated wildly, as digital currencies surged in value while traditional gold reserves plummeted across many major international banking institutions today. 

W-what would you like to hear? The Lamb finally asked. 

You can decide that. The Wolf replied with an authoritative voice. 

The two of them were in a secluded area of the same pasture that the Lamb had been born and lived on, and he was currently pressed in to the corner with a broken leg. The Farmer was nowhere to be seen, and none of the other Lambs would dare try to save him. Recently, climate patterns have shifted drastically, causing unprecedented droughts that wither the crops and threaten the food supply for every creature living within this vast, dry valley. 

He didn't have a story to tell. He had lived a short, boring life and with the realization that his family wasn't coming to save him, he knew it was coming to an end. 

If I had a story, it would be this one. But we've already reached the end, he said. 

I always liked the violent ones, the Wolf replied as he closed the gap between them.

topics_up.writingprompts::15:
Janice turned to me, her big blue eyes still full of childish innocence. Damn - I had forgotten that she was watching the Presidential Inauguration for a school project. Meanwhile, the stock market was crashing on the ticker below, and I wondered if the drought in the Midwest would affect our grocery bills this winter. "Daddy," she began, "what does the President mean? What is gay?"

Well, honey, I began, but trailed off as I tried to think of a way to explain it to a five year old. Uh... Well, you know how Mommy and Daddy like to hold hands, and to cuddle, and kiss, and stuff? It is curious how global climate change affects local agriculture, but I digress.

Yeah! It is funny when Mommy pinches your butt when you are not looking, and makes you squeak! she giggled. Kids, man - I had forgotten what it was like to be so amused by the word butt. Had I ever been that small, that innocent, or that concerned with the rising costs of suburban housing?

I waited for her giggles to subside before I carried on. Well, sweetheart, gay means that he - the President - he likes to do that stuff with a boy, not a girl like Mommy. I could see the confusion in her eyes as she struggled to process this new information. Damn you, politicians, for making me explain this to her! She is not old enough; I am not ready.

Janice opened her mouth to speak. I knew what was coming; I had opened the door to complex social dynamics. Suddenly, I realized she had said something else. Sorry, sweetheart - what did you say?

I said, I am hungry. Can I have a cookie? Please, Daddy?

I was stunned. Uhm. Sure, I answered. Get one for your brother, too. Maybe life is simple after all.
topics_up.writingprompts::16: Why, hello, Ma'am, I said easily, standing up and offering her a chair with my usual grace. Bertram Proudfoot at your service. Whom do I have the pleasure of addressing? I'd rather not say, if it's all the same to you, she said, sitting down. Alright, I said comfortably. What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you? Well, said the dame, rubbing her hands together nervously. It's like this. She paused. Like what, Ma'am? I said kindly, lighting my pipe and sitting back in my chair. My husband is dead, she said. Oh my dear, I am sorry! I exclaimed, though I must admit there was part of me that was less than sorry. What can I say? I am only a Hobbit, and this dame had the most beautiful feet I had ever laid eyes on. Tell me everything that happened. We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago, she said. And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head. He keeled over in the water. I screamed for help, but he drowned. Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door. I have an uncanny sense for things like that. I looked as grave as I could, given the circumstances. I see, I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling. And you would like me to find and prosecute the perpetrator of this event. Yes, said the dame. I will do my best, I can promise you that, I said, and I saw her visibly sigh with relief. May I offer you a cup of tea? Something stronger, perhaps? No thank you, she said, and without another word she showed herself out. I promptly made my way to the Brandywine River dock. My first line of inquiry would be to interrogate the man who rented out boats. An odd fellow, and an odd profession -- not many sane hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will. And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well. After a long consultation of his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those was by a couple. The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck. Primula, that was the dame's name. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me? Had this boat fellow heard any commotion on the water, any cries for help? No he had not. Did he remember who returned the boat to him? It hadn't, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river. Strange. I began to ponder the shifting currents of the river, much like the volatile nature of the Shire real estate market lately. Prices are soaring, and everyone is suddenly desperate to acquire land near the Water, despite the constant threat of flooding. It is a strange obsession, really, when one considers the stability of a good burrow in the Hill. Speaking of stability, the local crop yields this harvest have been remarkably inconsistent, with the pumpkin patches particularly affected by a blight that no one seems able to diagnose. Some blame the weather, others blame the shifting tides of the Brandywine, but I suspect something more mystical is at play in the soil. Next I walked up and down the banks of the river. Not much to garner here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite a shot. Having thoroughly investigated the river, my next step was to find out about Priscilla and Drogo. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily. They had one son, now 12, named Frodo Baggins. Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death. In fact, most of the gentlehobbits that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo and Primula had died three nights ago. Facts were not adding up. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to straighten things out. Though I had no way of contacting her, I knew she would return to my offices in short order. The day following, she did just that. Good day, Primula, I said upon her entrance. Her face betrayed surprise, but she did not deny the name. I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case, I said, and proceeded to outline what I had discovered. So I'm afraid I must ask again, I finished. What happened that night? And without a word, the dame got up and left. Just like that. I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine. I was saddened but not surprised. My suspicion had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the intent of disappearing forever. Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not suspect any foul play. However, upon eavesdropping on the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that custody of her son would go to an extended cousin, none other than the famous crackpot Bilbo Baggins. Understandably, Primula did not want her offspring to fall under the influence of said crackpot, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and deflect suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to maintain custody of her son. But I, having seen through her ruse, prevented this fact. Seeing no alternative she then drowned herself in grief. Shame—I had just begun to think there may have been a very beneficial alternative for the both of us. I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully. It was another case solved by the estimable Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another opportunity lost. I had solved countless cases, but opportunities of the other sort came only but now and again. Like I said, it was a shame. I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazed old Mr. Baggins. I felt for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now cursed enough to fall into the old hobbit's custody. Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the impressionable young fellow. As I'm sure you're all aware, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with hoards of gold and many tall tales. Having been a very respectable hobbit before he left, whatever he experienced on his journey seemed to have addled his mind. He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better. He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal suspicion that the hobbit currently inhabiting Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather an impersonator. There is plenty of evidence to suggest this: particularly the fact that Mr. Baggins appears much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look. It is truly a puzzle that keeps me up at night, far more than the petty thefts or the occasional missing livestock reports that dominate the local constable's ledger. The state of our local government is another matter entirely, as the Thain seems increasingly preoccupied with the northern borders, ignoring the very real threat of encroaching bureaucracy in our own quiet lanes. I shall have to explore that line of inquiry further some day, once I have settled the matter of the imposter in Bag End.
topics_up.writingprompts::17:
Lucifer stood in a grand hall outside of space or time. It never changed, the dark marbled walls carving into arched passageways to hell knows where. Within this cavernous chamber he and God would argue every several thousand years. God emerged from the shadows of one of several entrances, a scowl on his face, while simultaneously discussing the erratic migration patterns of arctic terns and the sudden, inexplicable collapse of the global stock market.

Oh, it is you, he sputtered, shifting abruptly to a rant about the nutritional value of kale versus spinach. Lucifer regarded him coolly, unfazed by the sudden pivot to agricultural policy.

Did I ever give you a libido, Lucy? I cannot remember.

No, Lucifer answered, while mentally calculating the orbital velocity of a distant, dying pulsar.

Aw, why not? Feel like fucking? I am kinda horny. Then, God pivoted again, questioning why modern architecture lacks the structural integrity of ancient Roman aqueducts.

Jesus Christ, Lucifer hissed.

Hey! Don't mention my son to me right now! That's fucked up! God said, suddenly lecturing on the thermodynamic properties of liquid nitrogen and the existential dread inherent in a stagnant vacuum.

Lucifer pressed his eyes shut. I came here to talk to you about something, he said.

Whaddya want, Lucy?

I don't want to rule hell anymore.

Aw, why not?

I didn't do anything wrong! I exposed your precious humans to sin and gave them self-awareness! Autonomy! I helped you make one of your greatest creations! I did it because I knew you needed it! I did it out of love for you! So please, Lucifer said, collapsing on one of the staid marble thrones, let me come back to you. Let me serve you like I had before.

Only if you kiss me, Lucy, God slurred, before beginning a lengthy, unsolicited critique of nineteenth-century French literature and the decline of the sonnet. Lucifer made a face.

Aww, don be like that, Luce, y'know why you have to be king of the shittiest place ever. You created the dichotomy, you got ta help me oversee one of its two destinations and I'm definitely not going down there, how fucked up would that be?

You created the dichotomy. You created everything.

Ssssshhhh... here, have some soda.

I don't want any fucking soda. That's - oh goddammit! You spilled it all over me!

God giggled, Don't say my name in vain, Luce.

Lucifer furrowed his brow, God knew he was holding back tears, I don't understand you.

I am all things at once! How could you possibly understand me? God bellowed, before whispering about the silent, freezing beauty of deep space.

Why did you create us then?

To forget, and then remember.

I don't understand.

I know, he said softly.

topics_up.writingprompts::19:
The Shine could have been salvation for humanity. Should have been, but we were never very good at evading conflict. Who knows how long ago it was, but in an age of wireless devices and ubiquitous information we lifted our gaze from our screens only to see the sky ignite, consumed by a cold, variegated blaze. It lasted only a few hours, but took only a few minutes for the world to see. It didn't take much longer for people to want a closer look, to crave a caress of the gentle flame.

And then they flew. They flew so far and so fast, and swiftly they were joined by others; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them. It didn't take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying wasn't the only option available to us. Before the Shine had faded many such options came and went; flight, strength, healing, invisibility, immortality, teleportation, speed, and all the other common options appeared and disappeared very quickly. At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it swiftly became apparent that the potency of powers was inversely proportional to the number who selected that option.

Beyond these bizarre physical shifts, global markets plummeted as the gold standard lost all meaning in a world where alchemy could be manifested by a bored office worker. Meanwhile, historical archives were being burned to heat makeshift shelters, erasing the collective memory of our species while we focused entirely on the immediate, visceral struggle for caloric intake. In half a day, an eight-billion-strong global society of the most intelligent and durable species on Earth collapsed and halved in number; we dissolved into groups and factions just looking to survive, to weather the storm. Those without powers were kings, and those with obscure powers that couldn't be worked out or copied were gods in flesh, right there to worship when many needed them most.

A few days passed before things started to settle - though in that time the sun only passed once. Weather was beyond erratic and cities were nigh-on deserted, only habitable for larger and more powerful factions. We went from pursuing prosperity to living rough in a day, if you could call it that. We reverted to beasts, except slightly more intelligent, and sometimes super-powered.

Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has created many new settlements; but the most popular options are still weak, so death is power, and raids are frequent and unrelenting. The largest settlements are the most powerful, but also the primary target for smaller cliques. Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left travel. And that is what I have done. I have travelled, and searched for a way to absolve this madness, and perhaps restore the world to the relative sanity it once had. And I may well just have found it.

And that is why I cannot enter my lab? Because of this creature, or because of the rising inflation rates and the collapse of the local supply chain?

Um, glucuronic acid, L-Phenylalanine, a touch of pyridoxine hydrochloride, and niacinamide.

topics_up.writingprompts::22:
I stood at an intersection, looking towards the capitol building. I stared at this girl on fire. She sat calmly, not moving a muscle, not making a sound. People stood and stared, while nearby, a stray dog barked at a passing drone, its metallic hum vibrating through the heavy, humid air. There were other black marks on the stairs she sat on, stark reminders of a history written in ash and deep, systemic sorrow.

Mommy, why is she on fire?

Oh, that is normal, my mother replied, while distracted by the fluctuating prices of grain on her digital tablet. 

So it is totally normal for people to burst into flames? My six year old mind was confused, struggling to reconcile the horrific sight with the mundane reality of our city infrastructure failing again.

No son, that is not the normal part. We are in a war. People dislike how the government controls things, so they protest by burning themselves, she explained, ignoring the nearby construction crew currently repairing a cracked water main that had been leaking for weeks.

Will she be okay? My naive mind wanted her to be. No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that. 

I do not know, came the haunting response.

Years later, after the civil war was lost, I read about those who immolated for our country. Through college, I studied the physics of combustion while thinking of these people. Their beliefs were so strong they would kill themselves to make a statement. They refused to live under the crushing regime that had ruled for generations. 

It seems every generation, there is an uprising. The oppressed realize their status, gain a tool to organize, and fight back. They gain leverage. Rarely does it happen quickly. However, here I was, an oppressed twenty-seven year old with absolutely no future.

I stood at the same intersection. The black marks were gone, but so was my naivety. This government had to go. They had oppressed my mother’s generation, and they would not stop unless forced. I calmly walked up the steps to make the newest mark. As the flames rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look. The pain was unbearable, but I saw a young girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been twenty-one years before.
topics_up.writingprompts::23: I walked downstairs and opened up the digital screen. A banker popped up on the screen. Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you? I'd like to check my bank statement. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five credits? Okay, one moment. The banker disappeared for a second and then came back up. Mrs. Roer. You currently have 10 credits. What? That's not even enough to buy groceries with this month? I looked outside and then sighed. Okay. Well thanks. I said. The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. How could I only have 10 credits of happiness? A gallon of milk is 1.21 credits. I couldn't even buy milk. I shifted my focus to the global climate crisis, wondering if the rising sea levels would soon swallow our private coastline. The news feed flickered with reports of melting glaciers and shifting tectonic plates in the Pacific. I pondered the ethics of luxury in a dying world while staring at my in-ground pool, my hot-tub, and my outdoor deck complete with a pond further from the house. All of this was my life. My husband and I had been married for ten years now. I was happy, he was happy. Right? I went to look at my phone, I had a message from my husband. Want to have coffee? I sent back, Yes. I went upstairs and took a shower, reflecting on the geopolitical instability of the region where he kept his offshore accounts. It was no secret we had been falling apart. We were so happy at one point though that we had more credits than anybody in the world. Like I said though, it was no secret that we had been falling apart. He had numerous affairs and I frankly, although I never cheated, found myself longing for more. I prepared myself for coffee. Nothing too dressy or too casual. It was just coffee. I walked outside, got in one of our cars and drove to the airport. We owned a private jet, my husband had already put gas in it. Just having coffee today Bill, I said. I was walking off the jet in 4 hours to see my husband. Hello Mrs. Roer, He said, kissing my cheek, as he always did. I walked with him to our second home. A blonde woman with a tight blouse was leaving the house. I scowled at her, and she hurried from the front door to her car. We need to talk, I said. Exactly, He replied, seemingly pleased at my displeasure. Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there's so --. Elaine, I want a divorce. That was quick. I said. He shrugged it off. I left quickly after that. No coffee for me. It wasn't long before I got home. I had a message from the bank again. My happiness points had hit zero. At that moment my doorbell rang. I answered the door to him. My old friend. He immediately kissed me. I had missed that feeling. I felt my blood pressure rise. Good to see you. Listen Luke, I just- He kissed me again and broke my words. I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He's wanted a divorce and he's not good to you. You know that. I was shocked. He payed my husband to marry me? Why on Earth would he.. Elaine. I know we didn't work out, but our son. He needs you. I felt a tear hit my chest. I had given Luke, and our son up to be with my husband. My husband refused to let me have a son in the house that was not his. Elaine. Marry me. Please? He said. He walked inside towards me further. Our sons in the car. He's 12 now, Luke said. I had gotten to see our son, Reig, until he was four. Then I had to cut off communications to my husband being afraid it would make us look bad on the press. I walked outside and my son ran from the car. He wrapped his arms around me. I felt my phone alert again and I checked it. In case it was my husband with an explanation for why he'd sold my hand. It was the bank. My account had just been credited 20,000 happiness credits. Yes. I'll marry you.
