Because the precise mechanisms driving this energetic collapse remain largely unidentified, this article exclusively investigates the specific impact of silica nanoparticles on cardiac mitochondrial function. The cumulative administration of silica nanoparticles consistently reduced the mechanical performance index of the rat heart with a half-maximal inhibitory concentration of 93 micrograms per milliliter, specifically impairing the diastolic relaxation rate. Within isolated cardiac mitochondria, silica nanoparticles were internalized, effectively inhibiting oxidative phosphorylation and significantly diminishing the mitochondrial membrane potential. Furthermore, the mitochondrial permeability transition pore was induced by increasing doses of silica nanoparticles, a condition that was partially recovered through the application of Cyclosporine A, a potent pharmacological blocker of this pore. The enzymatic activity of aconitase and thiol oxidation within the adenine nucleotide translocase were both reduced following silica nanoparticle exposure, strongly suggesting that these particles trigger pore opening via direct thiol modification and the subsequent generation of reactive oxygen species. In cardiac cells exposed to these particles, enhanced viability and a reduction of hydrogen peroxide levels were observed following the application of MitoTEMPO, a specific mitochondrial antioxidant. Concomitantly, treatment with Cyclosporine A in adult rat cardiac cells reduced silica nanoparticle-triggered cell death and successfully recovered ATP production from 32.4 percent to 65.4 percent. Additionally, we performed a thorough evaluation of the mitochondrial effects of silica nanoparticles in human cardiomyocytes. We observed a 40 percent inhibition of the maximal oxygen consumption rate in mitochondria at 500 micrograms per milliliter. Under this specific condition, we identified a remarkable diminution in the spare respiratory capacity, which indicates a significant reduction in the total amount of extra ATP that can be generated by mitochondria during a sudden increase in physiological energy demand. In these human cardiomyocytes, increased lactate dehydrogenase release and necrosis were found at higher doses, reaching 85 percent and 48 percent, respectively. Such deleterious effects were partially prevented by the application of Cyclosporine A. Therefore, silica nanoparticle exposure fundamentally impairs cardiac function by inducing mitochondrial dysfunction through the pathological opening of the permeability transition pore. These findings demonstrate that mitochondrial damage is the primary driver of silica-induced cardiac toxicity, highlighting the necessity for further research into therapeutic interventions that preserve organelle integrity.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::5: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after multiligament knee injuries has been systematically examined to determine clinical outcomes. NFL athletes sustaining these complex multiligament knee injuries consistently demonstrate lower RTP rates and significantly longer recovery durations than those observed in athletes recovering from isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears. This retrospective cohort study, classified as Level 4 evidence, analyzed publicly available NFL injury data regarding all multiligament knee injuries incurred between 2000 and 2016. Researchers extracted specific data including injury type, RTP status, time to RTP in days, total games played, and subsequent athletic performance. A total of 50 NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries met the strict inclusion and exclusion criteria for this investigation. The overall RTP rate for this cohort was 64.0%. Athletes diagnosed with combined ACL and medial collateral ligament (MCL) tears achieved an RTP rate of 70.8%. In contrast, athletes sustaining ACL and posterior cruciate ligament or lateral collateral ligament (PCL/LCL) tears demonstrated an RTP rate of 55.6% (P = 0.26). The mean time to RTP for the entire cohort of 50 athletes was 388.71 ± 198.52 days. Specifically, the mean time to RTP for those with ACL/MCL injuries was 305.1 ± 58.9 days. This duration was statistically shorter than the 459.2 ± 245.1 days (P = 0.004) required for athletes with combined ACL and PCL/LCL injuries and the 609.3 ± 183.1 days (P < 0.0001) required for those suffering frank knee dislocations. Furthermore, athletes with ACL/MCL injuries were significantly more likely to return to their prior performance level (43.5%) than those with more complex ACL and PCL/LCL injuries (18.5%) (P < 0.001). The evidence confirms that the RTP rate for NFL athletes following multiligament knee injuries is substantially lower than that of athletes with isolated ACL tears. Consequently, ACL and MCL tears are associated with a demonstrably better RTP prognosis compared with the more severe ACL and PCL/LCL injuries. These complex multiligament knee injuries significantly impede the ability of a professional football player to return to sport, with specific injury patterns serving as primary predictors for both the success and the temporal duration of the professional rehabilitation process.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension in response to exercise serves as a critical marker regarding the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis. This study focused exclusively on identifying the specific hemodynamic factors that drive elevated pulmonary pressure during physical exertion in patients diagnosed with pure rheumatic mitral stenosis. The primary objective was to assess the physiological parameters directly associated with the pulmonary pressure response to exercise, while simultaneously determining the significant impact of this exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension on long-term clinical outcomes. One hundred thirty patients with confirmed mitral stenosis underwent comprehensive exercise echocardiography. A wide range of hemodynamic echocardiographic parameters were meticulously obtained at rest and during peak exercise. Symptom-limited graded ramp bicycle exercise was performed in the supine position to ensure consistent data collection. The primary clinical end point for the analysis was the necessity for mitral valve intervention, specifically either percutaneous procedures or surgical repair. In the overall study population, the systolic pulmonary artery pressure increased significantly from 38.3 mm Hg at rest to 65.8 mm Hg during exercise. Increases in the mean mitral gradient, right ventricular function, left atrial volume, and net atrioventricular compliance were found to be independently associated with systolic pulmonary artery pressure at peak exercise, specifically after adjusting for changes in heart rate. During the follow-up period, numerous adverse clinical events were observed. By multivariate Cox proportional-hazards analysis adjusted for age and sex, the systolic pulmonary artery pressure achieved at peak exercise was identified as a powerful, independent predictor of adverse clinical outcome. These findings emphasize that the pulmonary artery pressure response to exercise in patients with mitral stenosis is determined by a combination of hemodynamic factors, including the transmitral mean gradient during exertion, net atrioventricular compliance, left atrial volume, and right ventricular function. Ultimately, the systolic pulmonary artery pressure measured at peak exercise is a robust predictor of clinical outcomes and consistently adds incremental prognostic value beyond that provided by standard resting echocardiographic measurements, including the mitral valve area. This research confirms that measuring exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension is essential for the accurate hemodynamic assessment and prognostic stratification of patients suffering from mitral stenosis.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::7: The impact of chronic liver disease on mortality outcomes in patients hospitalized with COVID-19 remains uncertain, necessitating a focused exploration of this association. We investigated the clinical outcomes of all adult inpatients diagnosed with COVID-19 in France throughout 2020. Specifically, we computed adjusted odds ratios to determine the precise associations between various stages of chronic liver disease and day-30 in-hospital mortality. The extensive study sample comprised 259,110 patients, including 15,476 individuals with documented chronic liver disease. Death occurred in 38,203 patients, with 2,941 of those cases involving patients suffering from chronic liver disease. The adjusted odds ratios for day-30 mortality were 1.79 for chronic liver disease, 0.54 for mild liver disease, 0.71 for compensated cirrhosis, 2.21 for decompensated cirrhosis, and 1.38 for primary liver cancer. Furthermore, we assessed how these liver-related conditions influenced the utilization of mechanical ventilation. Our findings indicate that chronic liver disease significantly increased the risk of COVID-19-related death in France during the 2020 pandemic. Therapeutic effort limitation, specifically regarding the application of mechanical ventilation, appears to have directly contributed to the observed excess mortality in French residents suffering from severe liver-related complications. We systematically studied the outcomes, including day-30 mortality, of all adults with COVID-19 who were discharged from acute and post-acute care facilities across France in 2020. Our comprehensive analysis demonstrates that while patients with certain liver pathologies were at an increased risk of COVID-19-related mortality, they were paradoxically less likely to receive mechanical ventilation. This discrepancy suggests that medical decision-making regarding the intensity of care provided to patients with chronic liver disease may have been influenced by their underlying hepatic status. Ultimately, our results provide strong evidence that chronic liver disease is a critical factor in determining the prognosis of hospitalized COVID-19 patients. The data highlights a concerning pattern of mortality that warrants further investigation into clinical protocols for liver patients. By focusing strictly on these hepatic outcomes, we clarify the substantial burden that chronic liver disease imposed on the French healthcare system during the COVID-19 pandemic, emphasizing the urgent need for equitable treatment strategies for this specific, vulnerable patient population when facing acute respiratory infections.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::8: The clinical study focuses exclusively on the treatment of pulmonary fibrosis originating from severe COVID-19 infections. Pulmonary fibrosis remains a critical, life-threatening sequela for patients who have survived severe or critical SARS-CoV-2 infections, leading to persistent loss of pulmonary function and diminished quality of life. This research specifically targets the management of post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis through a combined pharmacological intervention. Participants in this clinical trial must be over eighteen years of age, have recovered from severe or critical COVID-19, currently exhibit pulmonary fibrosis, and demonstrate Qi-Yin deficiency syndrome according to traditional Chinese medicine diagnostics. Eligible candidates are randomized into either a treatment group or a control group. The treatment group receives a combination of modern medicine, specifically pirfenidone, alongside traditional Chinese medicine. Conversely, the control group is administered pirfenidone in combination with a traditional Chinese medicine placebo. The primary objective is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of this combined therapeutic approach in mitigating pulmonary fibrosis. Researchers will continuously survey and record lung function indices to determine if the traditional Chinese medicine intervention improves the effectiveness of pirfenidone in patients suffering from this specific pulmonary complication. Pirfenidone is known to delay the decline of forced expiratory vital capacity, potentially reducing mortality rates associated with fibrotic lung damage. While traditional Chinese medicine has demonstrated efficacy in treating various forms of pulmonary fibrosis, its specific role in treating fibrosis linked to COVID-19 remains scientifically unexplored. Therefore, a multicenter, parallel-group, randomized, controlled, interventional, and prospective clinical trial has been meticulously designed to assess the feasibility and therapeutic impact of this comprehensive treatment regimen. The trial aims to determine whether this integrated approach significantly improves the long-term pulmonary health and overall quality of life for patients. This rigorous study, which focuses entirely on the management of post-COVID pulmonary fibrosis, was officially registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under the identification number ChiCTR2000033284 on the twenty-sixth of May, 2020. By strictly examining this singular pulmonary condition, the study seeks to establish a standardized protocol for improving respiratory outcomes in those recovering from the severe, long-term fibrotic consequences of the global COVID-19 pandemic.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body temperature, evaporative water loss and standard metabolic rate. These specific physiological parameters are fundamentally driven by the interaction between external thermal conditions and the internal regulatory mechanisms of the frog. Because these physiological processes are so closely linked to ambient thermal conditions, it is essential to examine how temperature influences each biological metric across diverse species. The primary objective of this study was to investigate the specific role of ambient temperature on body temperature, whole-animal evaporative water loss, and whole-animal standard metabolic rate in three wild caught African anuran species with different ecological specialisations: the aquatic African clawed frog, the stream-breeding common river frog, and the terrestrial raucous toad. Experiments were conducted across a wide range of test temperatures, specifically ranging from 5 to 35 degrees Celsius, at consistent 5 degree increments to ensure precise data collection. We found that body temperature, whole-animal evaporative water loss, and whole-animal standard metabolic rate consistently increased in direct correlation with increasing ambient temperature across all subjects. Furthermore, the results demonstrated that the magnitude of these physiological changes was strongly dependent on the specific thermal environment experienced by each animal during the trials. Our findings indicate that the physiological responses of these frogs are primarily governed by the surrounding thermal climate rather than other external factors. The data clearly shows that temperature is the dominant driver of metabolic activity and water loss patterns within these specific anuran groups. By focusing strictly on the thermal regulation of these physiological functions, we have established a clearer understanding of how environmental heat impacts the internal state of these amphibians. These results underscore the critical importance of temperature as the central regulatory variable for anuran physiology, demonstrating that metabolic and hydric stability is maintained through direct thermal sensitivity. Consequently, the study confirms that thermal conditions remain the primary influence on the physiological performance of these diverse frog species in their respective natural habitats.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis is a specific clinical impairment involving the perception of the sequential order of time. This particular alteration of human temporality has been described as being characteristically associated with thalamic involvement, specifically within the dorsomedial nucleus. We report the detailed clinical cases of two patients with acute ischaemic strokes located precisely in said thalamic territory, with a clinical presentation based primarily on this temporal symptom, the recognition of which was absolutely essential in the overall therapeutic approach. In the first and second cases, it is described how the disruption of the perception of temporality was the primary factor essential for the rapid diagnosis of the ischaemic condition in both patients. Awareness and widespread dissemination of this clinical association may be vital in the effective management of patients suffering from thalamic disorders. This is due to the significant possibility of influencing and modifying the initial clinical approach, since the early recognition of a specific symptom, such as chronotaraxis, can prevent the further spread of thalamic damage, in addition to the severe long-term sequelae that it causes, especially those of a chronic cognitive nature. The focus remains entirely on chronotaraxis as the core diagnostic indicator for medial thalamic infarction. By identifying this temporal sequencing deficit, clinicians can better localize the stroke, ensuring that the dorsomedial nucleus is recognized as the site of the neurological injury. The necessity of documenting chronotaraxis as a diagnostic guide cannot be overstated, as it provides a window into the functional integrity of the thalamus. Clinicians must prioritize the evaluation of temporal perception when thalamic strokes are suspected, as this symptom serves as a reliable marker for acute damage. By maintaining a narrow focus on the mechanisms of chronotaraxis, medical practitioners can improve patient outcomes through faster intervention, thereby mitigating the cognitive decline associated with these thalamic lesions. The persistence of this specific temporal symptom requires constant vigilance and detailed neurological assessment to optimize the therapeutic pathway for every patient diagnosed with a stroke.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::11: The airborne transmission of SARS-CoV-2 occurs when virus-laden particles expelled from an infectious person are inhaled by a susceptible individual, a process primarily governed by complex near-field dynamics. These virus-laden particles remain significantly more concentrated within the immediate expiratory jet of an infectious person than elsewhere in a well-mixed room, yet this specific near-field enhancement in virion exposure has historically lacked rigorous quantification. Accurately modeling the transmission of SARS-CoV-2 depends on factors that are inherently variable and poorly constrained, requiring large ensembles of model simulations to span the full range of uncertainty in input parameters. Because models capable of simulating the intricate near-field evolution of respiratory particles are computationally expensive, we developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets, or QuaRAD, to facilitate extensive analysis. QuaRAD provides an efficient framework for simulating the precise evolution of virus-laden particles after they are expelled from an infectious person, their subsequent deposition into the nasal cavity of a susceptible person, and the resulting risk of initial SARS-CoV-2 infection. Using this model, we simulated 10,000 unique scenarios to quantify the risk of infection. The predicted risk of SARS-CoV-2 infection was highly variable among these scenarios and was consistently and strongly enhanced in the immediate vicinity of the infectious individual. In more than 50% of the tested scenarios, the physical distancing required to effectively avoid these specific near-field enhancements in SARS-CoV-2 airborne transmission exceeded the standard recommended distance of two meters if the infectious person is not wearing a mask. This near-field extent was also found to be highly variable, with such variability explained predominantly by differences in individual expiration velocity. Our findings suggest that maintaining at least two meters of distance from an infectious person significantly reduces exposure to airborne SARS-CoV-2 virions; furthermore, robust protections against airborne transmission, such as high-quality N95 respirators, should be readily available and utilized whenever maintaining such physical distancing is simply not possible in practice.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures are consistently contaminated wounds that contain gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; therefore, wide-spectrum antibiotic therapy must be strictly incorporated into the primary treatment plan for these injuries. These essential antibiotics should be initiated as soon after the injury as possible, preferably within 3 hours of the initial trauma, after which specific time the reported rate of infection significantly increases. Time to surgical debridement within 12 hours of the injury has not been reported to affect the overall rate of infection, provided the patient is being actively treated with appropriate antibiotics. An antibiotic bead pouch and vacuum-assisted wound closure may further help reduce the specific risk for secondary and nosocomial contamination and subsequent deep tissue infection. Open fractures are always associated with a significant soft-tissue injury; therefore, they should be considered a complex soft-tissue injury that involves a fracture. The management of the bone and the surrounding soft tissues in a patient with an open fracture is the major determinant of successful fracture healing and functional restoration of the injured extremity. The formulation of a comprehensive soft-tissue treatment plan must occur during the initial wound assessment and the initial fixation of an open fracture and should not be considered a secondary or consecutive process. A soft-tissue surgeon should be consulted the very night of the injury. Selection of fracture fixation depends on the fractured bone, the location of the fracture, the extent of soft-tissue injury and contamination, and the physiologic status of the patient. Surgeons must deeply understand bone healing biology to achieve successful outcomes in the management of these open fractures. The cornerstones of these bone healing treatments include the optimization of host biology, recognition of a patient's nutritional status, appropriate use of medications, and the eradication of infection. Surgeons should consider bone grafting and the use of biologics to achieve bony union in patients with an acute open fracture and in the management of delayed union or nonunion to ensure that the bone heals properly.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of compliance have been observed with osteoporosis medication use specifically. It is not known whether such patterns of persistent non-compliance exist exclusively among users of these specific chronic osteoporosis medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after a prolonged lapse in osteoporosis medication use and to identify the factors associated with a return to osteoporosis treatment compliance. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of an osteoporosis medication (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had an extended lapse in osteoporosis medication refill compliance, defined as a period of at least 60 days after the completion of one osteoporosis medication prescription in which no refill for any osteoporosis medication was obtained. Survival curves were used to estimate the length of time until osteoporosis therapy is resumed. We estimated the association between patient characteristics and the rate of resuming osteoporosis treatment using Cox proportional hazards analysis. We then conducted a case crossover analysis to examine whether certain events occurring during follow-up triggered a return to osteoporosis medication refill compliance. RESULTS: Of patients who stopped osteoporosis therapy for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% restarted osteoporosis treatment within 6 months, and 50% restarted within 2 years. Among patients who had at least 6 months of continuous osteoporosis medication use before their interruption in osteoporosis treatment (n=5863), 42% restarted osteoporosis therapy within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger patients, women, and those with a history of an osteoporosis fracture were more likely to return after a break in osteoporosis medication use. Recent hip fractures, discharges from nursing homes, and bone mineral density testing also predicted a return to osteoporosis treatment. CONCLUSION: Extended gaps in osteoporosis treatment are common among users of osteoporosis medications. Because the effectiveness of these osteoporosis drugs used in an interrupted way is unknown, osteoporosis compliance interventions should emphasize the need for continuous osteoporosis medication use. Further research is needed to understand why osteoporosis patients often go for months without refilling osteoporosis prescriptions.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community, known as dysbiosis, of vertebrates are strongly associated with various gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases. It remains unclear which specific bacterial taxa correlate with these gut dysbiosis states, and whether particular intestinal regions or specific developmental time periods are more susceptible to such microbial shifts. Here, we exclusively examine the specific changes occurring within the microbiome during states of dysbiosis across different segments of the gastrointestinal tract in the ostrich. We evaluated the 16S rRNA gene composition within the ileum, cecum, and colon of sixty-eight ostrich individuals that perished from suspected enterocolitis during their first three months of life, comparing them against fifty healthy, age-matched control subjects. Diseased individuals exhibited drastically lower microbial alpha diversity and differed substantially in their microbial beta diversity from healthy control individuals throughout all three analyzed regions of the gastrointestinal tract. The clear, statistically significant relationship between low microbial diversity and disease was consistent across all ages in the ileum, although this specific association decreased with age in the cecum and colon. Several specific bacterial taxa were strongly associated with mortality, including Enterobacteriaceae and Peptostreptococcaceae, while other distinct taxa were associated with continued health, such as Lachnospiraceae and Ruminococcaceae. Repeated fecal sampling demonstrated that these dangerous pathobionts were already present shortly after hatching and proliferated rapidly in individuals characterized by low microbial diversity, ultimately resulting in high mortality rates several weeks later. Identifying the precise origins of these pathobionts in neonates and the various factors that subsequently influence the successful establishment of a diverse, healthy gut microbiota remains the primary key to understanding the mechanisms of dysbiosis and host development. By focusing strictly on these microbial dynamics, we clarify how bacterial communities influence ostrich survival. This investigation highlights the critical importance of maintaining a diverse and balanced gut microbiome to prevent the onset of lethal enterocolitis during the vulnerable early stages of avian life.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the underlying physical mechanism responsible for the quantum speedup, specifically why quantum algorithms require fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts. We extend their formal mathematical representation to the fundamental process of setting the problem itself. The initial measurement selects a setting at random, and Bob, acting as the problem setter, unitarily changes it into the desired one. This specific representation is accessible to Bob and any external observer, yet it remains fundamentally inaccessible to Alice, the problem solver. Access would reveal the function computed by the black box, which must remain hidden within the system for her. We resort to relational quantum mechanics to explain this limitation. To Alice, the projection of the quantum state resulting from the initial measurement is effectively retarded until the conclusion of her problem solving action. To her, the algorithm input state remains one of complete ignorance regarding the setting. By performing black box computations, she unitarily sends it into the output state that, for each possible setting, encodes the corresponding solution, which is acquired by the final measurement. We show that we can ascribe to the final measurement the selection of any part, specifically the R-th part, of the random outcome of the initial measurement. This projection places the input state to Alice into a state of lower entropy where she knows a corresponding part of the problem setting. The quantum algorithm is a sum over classical histories in each of which Alice, knowing in advance one of the R-th parts of the setting, performs the black box computations required to identify the solution. Given an oracle problem and a value of R, this retrocausality model provides the total number of black box computations required to solve it. Conversely, given a known quantum algorithm, it yields the value of R that explains its speed up. R equals one half always yields the number of black box computations required by an existing quantum algorithm and the order of magnitude required by optimal ones.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention often lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow within the heart, which alters the mechanical stimuli experienced by blood cells passing through the ventricular chambers. Specifically, the degree of platelet activation is heavily influenced by the precise level and type of mechanical stresses present in the blood flow. Here we analyze the blood flow in the left ventricle of the heart through a computational model constructed from patient-specific data. The blood flow in the ventricle is modeled by the Navier-Stokes equations, while the flow through the mitral valve is captured by a parameterized model representing the projected opening of the valve. A finite element method is used to solve the equations, from which a detailed simulation of the velocity and pressure of the blood flow is constructed. A triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor is then used to distinguish between rigid body rotational flow, irrotational straining flow, and shear flow. The triple decomposition enables the separation of these three fundamentally different flow structures, each generating a distinct type of mechanical stimulus on the blood cells in the flow. We compare these results to simulations where a mitral valve clip intervention is modeled, which leads to a significant modification of the ventricular flow patterns. It was found that the shear in the simulation cases treated with clips increased more compared to the untreated case than the rotation and strain did. A decrease in valve opening area of 64 percent in one of the cases led to a 90 percent increase in rotation and strain, but a 150 percent increase in shear. The computational analysis suggests a robust process for patient-specific simulation of clinical interventions in the heart with a detailed analysis of the resulting blood flow, which could support clinical risk assessment with respect to platelet activation and subsequent thrombosis events.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::17: The diffuse very high-energy gamma-ray emission observed in the central two hundred parsecs of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. follows the dense matter distribution found throughout the Central Molecular Zone. This specific emission pattern persists up to a longitudinal distance of approximately one hundred thirty parsecs from the Galactic Centre, where the observed flux begins to decrease rapidly. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. data analysis reveals that the cosmic-ray density profile drops consistently with the distance to the centre, making all gathered data highly compatible with the presence of a steady cosmic PeVatron located at the Galactic Centre. In this technical paper, we extend this rigorous analysis to obtain a detailed characterisation of the correlation between cosmic-ray density and dense matter distribution within the inner two hundred parsecs. Taking advantage of two hundred fifty hours of high-quality H.E.S.S. data and improved analysis techniques, we perform a comprehensive morphology study of the diffuse high-energy emission observed from the Galactic Centre ridge and reconstruct its total energy spectrum. We demonstrate that the emission correlated with dense matter covers the full extent of the Central Molecular Zone and that this flux accounts for approximately half of the total diffuse emission flux measured. We detect an additional emission component centred on the Galactic Centre and extending over about fifteen parsecs that is consistent with the existence of a strong cosmic-ray density gradient, further confirming the presence of a cosmic-ray accelerator at the very centre of our Galaxy. We show that the spectrum of the full ridge diffuse emission is compatible with the one previously derived from the central regions, suggesting that a single population of high-energy particles fills the entire Central Molecular Zone. Our findings consistently emphasize the singular role of the central accelerator in driving the diffuse gamma-ray emission observed across the entire Galactic Centre region.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::18: These international clinical practice recommendations for developmental coordination disorder, initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability, aim to address key clinical questions on the standardized diagnosis, assessment, and therapeutic intervention of this specific condition. Key questions regarding effective clinical management were considered through rigorous literature reviews and formal expert consensus protocols. For recommendations based on current scientific evidence, literature searches on the core mechanisms, diagnostic assessment, and clinical intervention strategies were meticulously updated since the previous recommendations in 2012. Evidence was rated according to the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine and then transferred into clinical recommendations. For recommendations based on formal consensus, two meetings of an international, multidisciplinary expert panel were conducted with a further five Delphi rounds to develop good clinical practice recommendations for diagnosing and treating developmental coordination disorder. Thirty-five total recommendations were made. Eight were based on the evidence from literature reviews, specifically focusing on the assessment and intervention phases of clinical care. Twenty-two were updated from the 2012 recommendations. New recommendations relate specifically to the diagnosis and assessment processes. Additionally, one new recommendation reflects active video games as clinical adjuncts to more traditional activity-oriented and participation-oriented interventions, and two new recommendations were made for adolescents and adults with this movement disorder. The clinical practice recommendations provide a comprehensive overview of developmental coordination disorder and current scientific understanding based on research evidence and expert consensus. It reflects the state of the art for clinicians and scientists of varied disciplines dedicated to this disorder. The international clinical practice recommendations may serve as a basis for national guidelines. These represent updated international clinical practice guidelines on developmental coordination disorder, providing refined and extended recommendations on clinical assessment and intervention, offering a critical synopsis of current research on mechanisms of the disorder, and serving as the first international recommendations to consider adolescents and adults with developmental coordination disorder.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension consistently induces deleterious mood disorders that fluctuate significantly depending on the specific type of antihypertensive medication prescribed during clinical treatment. Depression remains fundamentally associated with pathological modifications in basal brain asymmetry, particularly concerning the frontal cortex, which is critically involved in systemic blood pressure regulation. Consequently, different vasoactive drugs fundamentally alter this neural asymmetry in a manner that directly dictates the overall cognitive status of the subject. We studied the bilateral activity of several neuropeptidases within the frontal cortex as a precise reflect of the functional status of certain neuropeptides involved in mood regulation. Using arylamide derivatives as substrates, we fluorometrically analysed the activity of these specific enzymes in the left and right frontal cortex of control untreated Wistar-Kyoto rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats, comparing their enzymatic activities across various hypertensive or normotensive states. Changes in the bilateral distribution of neuropeptidases were consistently dependent on the strain, the specific enzyme analysed, and the pharmaceutical intervention employed. Normotensive groups revealed intrahemispheric correlations primarily within the left hemisphere. In contrast, hypertensive groups demonstrated distinct intrahemispheric correlations localized predominantly in the right hemisphere. Interhemispheric correlations were mostly observed in subjects receiving effective antihypertensive treatments. Our results suggest specific brain bilateral patterns of neuropeptidase activities in normotensive subjects that fundamentally change in hypertensive subjects. This observation is directly related to the cognitive disorders that have been described in these animal models and that change under the influence of various antihypertensive or hypertensive drug treatments. These findings highlight how blood pressure management directly dictates neurological stability. By maintaining consistent focus on the correlation between hypertensive states and neuropeptidase-driven neural asymmetry, it becomes clear that pharmacological intervention is the primary driver of cognitive outcomes in these models, proving that blood pressure control is the essential factor in preserving healthy brain function and emotional equilibrium throughout the duration of the study.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::20: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the clinical efficacy of rapid response teams specifically regarding triggering events in total hip arthroplasty patients. A retrospective review of all rapid response team events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed. Inclusion criteria were defined as patients over eighteen years old that underwent primary or revision total hip arthroplasty. Information queried included demographics, primary reason for the rapid response team activation, Charlson Comorbidity Index, underlying etiology, whether any changes in management occurred, and whether the patient was uptriaged. In total, 168 rapid response team events were called on 153 hip arthroplasty patients. The study focused heavily on the specific outcomes of these team activations. Rapid response team activations for hypotension or presyncope and for syncope resulted in significantly fewer changes in management than tachycardia, hypoxia, or altered mental status. Furthermore, rapid response team activations for hypotension, presyncope, syncope, and hypoxia resulted in significantly fewer patients being uptriaged than tachycardia. Hypotension and presyncope were found to be significantly more commonly due to volume depletion than other etiologies. Hypoxia was significantly more commonly due to atelectasis and opioid oversedation. Altered mental status or delirium was also significantly more commonly caused by opioid oversedation. In patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, rapid response team activations for hypotension, presyncopal symptoms, and syncope were significantly less likely to result in clinical changes in management or uptriaging compared to tachycardia. The most common etiologies for these specific patient triggers were potentially preventable, including volume depletion and opioid use. Consequently, the study concludes that focusing on these preventable causes is essential for improving the management of total hip arthroplasty patients who require rapid response team intervention, as these specific clinical triggers highlight clear opportunities for enhanced postoperative care protocols and better patient monitoring strategies.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services are a vital component of acute stroke management, particularly concerning patient triage. We devised a specialized prehospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator intravenous therapy, known as TOPSPIN, specifically for triaging patients with ischemic stroke and identifying clear indications for intravenous therapy in December 2006. This scale comprises five distinct items: consciousness, atrial fibrillation, language disorder, disturbance of the upper extremities, and disturbance of the lower extremities. The primary aim of this study was to analyze the results of ten years of TOPSPIN implementation to specifically distinguish ischemic stroke from other conditions in the real world. We prospectively enrolled consecutive patients transferred to our hospital and evaluated by Toyota city ambulance services using the TOPSPIN tool from December 2006 to January 2017. We focused our examination on the definite diagnosis of ischemic stroke at the time of hospital discharge, the positive-predictive value of the ischemic stroke identification, the rate of recanalization therapy, and the clinical differentiation of ischemic stroke versus other mimics. A total of 1,482 consecutive patients were enrolled; 628 were confirmed as having ischemic stroke. Among these 628 patients with ischemic stroke, 130 received intravenous recombinant treatment, endovascular therapy, or both. The presence of atrial fibrillation, older age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN score were all statistically associated with ischemic stroke. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, the presence of atrial fibrillation was independently associated with ischemic stroke. The TOPSPIN remains a simple, highly effective prehospital stroke scale that includes a critical assessment of atrial fibrillation. Detection of atrial fibrillation in the prehospital stage consistently points to a higher probability of ischemic stroke, proving that this specific diagnostic metric is essential for the accurate, rapid, and early identification of ischemic stroke patients who require urgent medical intervention.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the precise redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate located in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have utilized all available VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by our team and two other research groups using FORS2 at the VLT over the last five years, resulting in a total integration time of 52 hours. The combined spectrum remains the deepest ever obtained of a galaxy in the Reionization epoch. We do not detect any emission line or continuum over the entire wavelength range, extending up to 10100A. Based on an accurate set of simulations, we are able to put a stringent upper limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma in the explored wavelength range, corresponding to a rest-frame equivalent width EW<9A. Combining this limit with the SED modelling, we refine the redshift to be z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). The same SED fitting indicates that GDS-1408 is relatively extinct with a dust corrected star formation rate of ~ 20 Msol/yr. The comparison between the un-attenuated equivalent width predicted by the case-B recombination theory and the observed upper limit provides a limit on the effective Lya escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. Even though we cannot rule out a major contribution of the intergalactic medium in damping the line, a plausible interpretation is that GDS-1408 is moderately evolved and contains sufficient gas and dust to attenuate the Lya emission before it reaches the intergalactic medium. This spectroscopic analysis confirms the inherent difficulty of characterizing such distant galaxies. Our deep integration efforts highlight that the current redshift constraints for GDS-1408 remain limited by the sensitivity of 8-10m class telescopes, necessitating future high-precision facilities for further study of this specific target. The refined redshift accuracy achieved through this rigorous spectral analysis provides the most reliable foundation for future observations of GDS-1408.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella spp. as a pathogen indicator within composting processes was strictly studied through specific inoculation techniques. These techniques were utilized to introduce known quantities of Salmonella spp. directly into the composting material to facilitate precise measurement. The direct inoculation method was compared extensively against the encapsulated vial inoculation technique, where the Salmonella spp. solution was contained within a vial and inserted into the center of the compost material prior to the commencement of the composting process. The conventional method utilized for the enumeration of Salmonella spp. involved serial dilution followed by standard membrane filtration, adhering strictly to the compost quality standard methods defined in PAS 100 and the British Standard BS EN ISO 6579:2002. This study was designed specifically to investigate the relationship between composting temperature and the survival of Salmonella spp. Exposure to an average composting temperature of approximately 55-60 degrees Celsius for at least three days was maintained, as this condition is reported to be sufficient to eliminate the vast majority of enteric pathogens. The concentration of Salmonella spp. and the internal temperature for both sample types were monitored as the primary indicators to determine the survival rates of Salmonella spp. in direct versus non-direct inoculation scenarios. This study provides detailed figures regarding the die-off rate for Salmonella spp. throughout the composting duration. The differentiation between direct contact samples and non-contact samples of Salmonella spp. with the compost material was revealed. Results from the laboratory scale composting study showed that after eight days, which included periods at 66 degrees Celsius, the numbers of Salmonella spp. in the direct contact samples were below the limits required by the UK compost standard PAS 100. Meanwhile, the non-contact samples still contained high amounts of Salmonella spp. even after twenty days of continuous composting.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is associated with prostate cancer progression in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is unclear whether race continues to predict a poor outcome. The authors hypothesized that, in an equal-access setting among patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) and no known metastases (M0/Mx), black men would receive imaging tests at similar rates as nonblack men, meaning there would be an equal opportunity to detect metastases, yet they would still maintain a higher risk of developing metastatic disease. METHODS: In total, 837 men who were diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC during 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH database were analyzed. Data on all imaging tests after CRPC diagnosis were collected, including date, type, and outcome. Multivariable Cox models were used to test associations between race and the time to first metastasis, first bone metastasis, first bone scan, second bone scan among men who had a negative first bone scan, and overall survival. RESULTS: Black men were equally as likely as nonblack men to receive a first and second bone scan after a diagnosis of CRPC. There were no significant differences in the risk of developing any metastases, bone metastases, time to bone scans, or overall survival between black men and nonblack men. CONCLUSIONS: The lack of racial differences in the development of metastases and scanning practices observed in this study suggests that, once men have a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, race is not a prognostic factor. Because these findings indicate that racial disparities in metastatic progression are absent within this advanced patient population, researchers should focus exclusively on how race impacts the initial development of prostate cancer rather than examining the clinical outcomes of men who already have advanced disease. Cancer 2016;122:3848-3855. © 2016 American Cancer Society.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I. Our new field of view is offset from the centrally located field observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to expose the halo population of this galaxy. We report the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, which demonstrate that Leo A is not a young galaxy. In fact, Leo A is at least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters which exhibit red horizontal branches, and are considered to have a minimum age of about 9 Gyr. We perform an extensive comparison of the data with stellar isochrones. For a distance modulus of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004, and ages between about 5 and 10 Gyr, in their post-main-sequence phases, but lack the detection of main-sequence turnoffs which would provide unambiguous proof of ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar generations. Blue horizontal branch stars are above the detection limits, but difficult to distinguish from young stars with similar colors and magnitudes. Synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the blue horizontal branch in the halo of Leo A. The models also suggest ~50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing to be attributed to an ancient (>10 Gyr) stellar population. We conclude that Leo A started to form stars at least about 9 Gyr ago. The existence of old stars in this galaxy confirms that its evolutionary history is characterized by a significant, prolonged period of early stellar formation, proving that its ancient stellar components define its overall age and chronological development within the local cosmic neighborhood.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of neuromorphic engineering is to create robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting neuromechanical principles from biology through implementing spinal circuitry for afferented muscles. Muscle afferentation is the closed-loop behavior arising from interactions among populations of muscle spindle afferents, alpha and gamma motoneurons, and muscle fibers to enable specific motor behaviors. We used programmable very-large-scale-circuit hardware to implement models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, muscle spindle proprioceptors, alpha-motoneuron recruitment, gamma motoneuron control of spindle sensitivity, and the monosynaptic circuitry connecting them. This multi-scale system of spiking neurons emulated the physiological properties of a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles acting on a joint via long tendons. This integrated system maintained a joint angle and reproduced stretch reflex responses when driving the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Moreover, this system allowed us to explore various values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains when driving a robotic finger, some of which replicated specific human pathological sensorimotor conditions. We examined the behavioral consequences of adopting alternative models of isometric muscle force production. We found that the dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps that are highly sensitive to tendon elasticity, especially at high force output levels. Our methodology produced the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers. This research platform allows us to explore the mechanisms behind healthy and pathological sensorimotor function in the physical world by building them from first principles, and it is a necessary precursor to advanced neuromorphic robotic systems that emulate complex muscle control. This entire architecture focuses solely on the intricate biological motor control loops essential for achieving functional and realistic robotic movement in artificial systems.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection and obstructing stones represent a urologic emergency, often achieving early clinical stability but remaining hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antibiotic resistance specifically in patients who underwent urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis to facilitate safe, early discharge on targeted oral antibiotics. Methods: Patients who underwent emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and an obstructing ureteral stone from 2014 to 2018 at two academic medical institutions were identified. Emergent stent placement was performed and patients were treated with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics. We assessed the association between clinical parameters at the time of presentation and resistance to at least one antibiotic from urine culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for continuous and categorical variables, respectively. Multivariate logistic regression was then performed using all significant variables identified from the initial univariate analysis to isolate the primary predictors of resistant uropathogens. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine cultures resistant to at least one antibiotic. On univariate analysis, patients with resistant cultures were significantly more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, require postoperative intensive care unit-level care, have bacteremia, and a longer length of stay. In multivariate analysis using significant variables, only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antibiotic resistance with an increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this study, we show that a history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance in both univariate and multivariate analyses. Our findings suggest that patients with a history of ureteroscopy should await urine culture results, while those without such a history may be discharged early on empiric oral antibiotics, pending further validation studies to determine effectiveness.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of alcohol, but very little research has examined the specific factors associated with these changes in alcohol consumption patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a direct substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population. Data was derived from a comprehensive survey of 2102 people enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 respondents who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating medical cannabis, and then used retrospective data on the frequency and amount of alcohol use pre-and post medical cannabis initiation to determine which participant characteristics were associated with reductions and cessation of alcohol use. Overall, 419 participants reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days, 323 decreased the number of standard drinks they had per week, and 76 reported no alcohol use at all in the 30 days prior to the survey. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing alcohol use, and an intention to use medical cannabis to specifically reduce alcohol consumption was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis initiation is strongly associated with self-reported reductions and total cessation of alcohol use among medical cannabis patients. Since alcohol is the most prevalent recreational substance in North America, and its use results in significant rates of morbidity and mortality, these findings may result in improved health outcomes for medical cannabis patients, as well as significant overall improvements in public health and safety regarding alcohol consumption patterns across the country.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::29: The intricate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion, and crystalline electric field interactions observed in iridium-based oxides is manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. Here we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between cobalt and iridium for partial lanthanum substitution by calcium in the La2CoIrO6 system. A great advantage of the use of Ca2+ as a replacement for La3+ is the similarity of their ionic radii, meaning observed magnetic changes are directly associated with electronic variations. A thorough investigation of the magnetic properties of the La2-xCaxCoIrO6 system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation, AC and DC magnetization, XAS, and XMCD. Our XAS results show that up to 25% of calcium substitution at the lanthanum site results in the emergence of Co3+, possibly in a high spin state, while the introduction of larger amounts of calcium leads to the increase of iridium valence. The competing magnetic interactions resulting from these mixed valences lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered and an emerging spin glass state for the doped samples. Our muon spin rotation results indicate that for La2CoIrO6 a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic phase persists down to low temperature, possibly related to the presence of a small amount of Ir3+ and to the anti-site disorder at the cobalt and iridium sites. For the doped compounds, the paramagnetic phase freezes below 30 K, but there is still some magnetic dynamics associated with the spin glass state. This comprehensive study confirms that the magnetic evolution in this system is driven primarily by the complex interplay of cobalt and iridium valence states as calcium doping alters the electronic landscape of the crystalline lattice structure.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::30: With the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation internet-of-things use cases, traditional approaches to multiple access control have started to show their limitations. A new wave of grant-free approaches have been therefore proposed as a viable alternative. However, a definitive solution for efficient multiple access is still to be accomplished. In our work, we propose a new semi-grant-free coordinated random access protocol, denoted as partial-information multiple access, to reduce packet loss and latency during multiple access, particularly in the presence of sporadic activations. We consider a machine-type communications scenario, wherein devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station. When using this multiple access protocol, the base station can acquire partial information on the instantaneous traffic conditions and estimate the number of devices with packets waiting for transmission. Based on this knowledge, the base station assigns to each device a specific slot for multiple access transmission. However, since each slot may still be assigned to multiple users, collisions may occur within the multiple access scheme. Both the total number of allocated slots and the user assignments are optimized, based on the estimated number of active users, to reduce collisions and improve the efficiency of the multiple access scheme. To prove the validity of our multiple access solution, we compare our protocol to standard multiple access schemes. We show that this protocol is able not only to adapt to different traffic conditions and to provide fewer packet drops regardless of the intensity of packet generations, but also able to merge the advantages of standard multiple access schemes, thus providing significant performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability and latency for every multiple access transmission task within the network infrastructure.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose – Bone remodeling as a response to total knee arthroplasty can lead to loss of bone stock and increase the risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study investigates the adaptive bone remodeling of the proximal tibia specifically after uncemented total knee arthroplasty procedures. Patients and methods – We performed a 2-year follow up of 53 patients, with a mean age of 62 years, who received an uncemented total knee arthroplasty in a randomized controlled trial assessing bone mineral density as the primary outcome measure. Patients were randomized into two groups utilizing either monoblock or modular polyethylene designs. All total knee arthroplasty procedures were performed using the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal system. Measurements of bone mineral density were taken postoperatively and again after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Bone mineral density was measured consistently in three specific regions of interest located within the proximal tibia. Results and interpretation – In the monoblock group, statistically significant changes in bone mineral density were observed after 24 months in both the medial and lateral regions of interest. Bone mineral density decreased medially by 15% and laterally by 13% within this specific cohort. In the modular group, the bone mineral density changes were limited and after 24 months returned to the preoperative values. The differences in bone mineral density change between these two specific implant groups were statistically significant in both the medial and lateral regions of interest. A significantly different bone remodeling pattern of the proximal tibia was seen in the two groups with a higher degree of bone loss in the knees that received the monoblock polyethylene design, indicating that the flexible monoblock implant design does not decrease the bone loss of the proximal tibia during the recovery period.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::32: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) represent a specialized computational model designed to emulate the efficiency of biological neural systems through binary spike communication. Unlike traditional artificial neural networks that rely on energy-intensive frame-based exchanges, SNNs utilize sparse, event-driven signals that offer significant potential for power reduction. However, current SNN implementations often struggle to replicate the high-level performance metrics established by deep learning architectures, largely due to excessive firing rates that negate their inherent energy advantages. This research introduces an innovative framework for SNNs that leverages efficient spike-time coding to bridge the performance gap while drastically lowering average firing rates. By incorporating the biological phenomenon of firing rate limiting adaptation, we derive an effective transfer function that allows standard neural units to be seamlessly replaced with adaptive spiking neurons. The resulting Adaptive SNNs (AdSNNs) demonstrate that high-performance inference can be achieved using an order of magnitude fewer spikes than previous spiking architectures. Furthermore, the adaptive nature of this spike-time coding enables dynamic control over neural precision, allowing the network to modulate its activity based on computational requirements. By implementing a simple model of arousal within the AdSNN framework, we successfully reduce the necessary average firing rate even further, demonstrating that adaptive coding is a critical mechanism for efficiency. These findings suggest that Adaptive SNNs provide a robust, scalable solution for implementing high-performance neural computation in power-constrained environments. By focusing exclusively on the optimization of spike-time coding and adaptive firing mechanisms, this approach consistently outperforms existing spiking models across all evaluated benchmarks. Ultimately, the development of these adaptive systems marks a significant advancement in the field of energy-efficient neural computation, providing a clear path toward the deployment of highly capable, spike-based architectures in various asynchronous, temporally continuous applications that demand both high accuracy and minimal power consumption.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars. Recently, it has been observed to show intriguing behaviour by analysing long-term photometry: during 2003--2009, a coherent spot structure migrating in the rotational frame has been reported by various authors, but since that time the star has entered a chaotic state where coherent structures seem to have disappeared and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur irregularly over time. Aims. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign extending over 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006--2017, specifically focusing on the persistent spot activity and its chaotic evolution across this interval. Methods. We use a Doppler imaging technique to derive surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra, enabling detailed analysis of the star’s complex spot distribution. Results. From the mean temperatures of the Doppler maps we see a weak but systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star, which relates directly to the star’s ongoing spot evolution. During nearly all observing seasons we see a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric. The phase behaviour of this structure is very chaotic but agrees reasonably well with the photometry. We find that the spot distribution remains the primary driver of the star’s observable photometric variability. Conclusions. Even during the chaotic phase of the star, the spot topology has remained very similar to the higher activity epochs with more coherent and long-lived spot structures: we see high-latitude and equatorial spot activity. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in phase of the photometric minima to be caused by changes in the high-latitude spot structure rather than by any other diverse stellar surface feature.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Hydrogenation reactions are expected to be among the most important surface reactions occurring on interstellar ices. However, solid state astrochemical laboratory data on reactions of H-atoms with specific interstellar ice constituents are largely lacking. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to determine whether and how acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) reacts with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures and to derive reaction rates and production yields for this process. Methods: Pure CH3CHO interstellar ice analogues are bombarded by H-atoms in a controlled ultra-high vacuum experiment. The ices are monitored by reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and the reaction products are detected in the gas phase through temperature programmed desorption to determine the destruction and formation yields as well as the corresponding reaction rates. Results: Within the sensitivity of our experimental set-up, we conclude that CH3CHO reacts significantly with H-atoms. At most 20% is hydrogenated to ethanol (C2H5OH) and a second reaction route leads to the break-up of the C-C bond to form solid state CH4 (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The methane production yield is expected to be equal to the summed yield of H2CO and CH3OH, and therefore CH4 most likely evaporates partly after formation due to the high exothermicity of the chemical reaction. The specific reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend primarily on the ice temperature and not on the ice thickness. These findings provide critical insight into the complex chemical pathways governing acetaldehyde processing within the cold, dense regions of interstellar space where hydrogenation is a dominant mechanism for the formation of larger organic molecules and the evolution of interstellar ice composition across various astrophysical environments.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::35: The methodology of funnel control was introduced in the early 2000s, and it has developed since then in many respects achieving a level of mathematical maturity balanced by practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes. The core focus remains exclusively on the mechanics of this funnel control technique, ensuring that all variables stay within bounds defined by a prespecified funnel. Considered are classes of systems specified by structural properties, such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics, while the precise systems' data are in general unknown. Prespecified are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely chosen by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a system class satisfying certain structural properties. The aim is to design, based on the structural assumptions and the input and output information only, a single simple control strategy called the funnel controller so that its application to any system results in feasibility of the funnel control objective. This means that solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time, all variables are bounded, and the evolution of the error between the system's output and the reference signal remains strictly within the prespecified funnel. The entire framework is dedicated to maintaining this specific control performance across various complex dynamical processes. We investigate how this funnel control mechanism functions across diverse scenarios, ensuring that the error always stays contained within the functional boundaries. By focusing solely on the mathematical rigour and the control strategy itself, we establish the reliability of the funnel controller in managing dynamical systems, ensuring that every trajectory remains confined within the prescribed region for the duration of the entire operation.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::36: Stealthy Link Flooding Attacks (SLFA) represent a major threat to modern network integrity, specifically by congesting critical links to isolate target areas. Because SLFA variants easily circumvent traditional security measures, network administrators have increasingly turned toward Moving Target Defense (MTD) strategies to protect their infrastructure. These MTD techniques involve the continuous, dynamic alteration of network configurations to deceive potential attackers, thereby significantly increasing the difficulty and cost of executing a successful strike. However, implementing MTD effectively is inherently challenging because it introduces substantial operational overhead. Determining the optimal frequency and intensity for these defensive shifts requires a deep understanding of attacker behavior, which remains notoriously unpredictable. In this research, we focus exclusively on optimizing MTD strategies to mitigate SLFA threats while maintaining minimal system overhead. We model this specific defensive problem as a rigorous signaling game, featuring the network defender and the malicious attacker as primary strategic players. A belief function is established throughout the ongoing engagement, allowing the defender to accurately assess the attacker's intent and select the most appropriate response. By analyzing this game model, we derive a robust defense mechanism grounded in the game's specific equilibria. We evaluate this sophisticated technique within a controlled Mininet-based environment where an attacker executes persistent SLFAs while the defender applies our game-theoretic MTD approach. The experimental results demonstrate that our signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism provides a level of protection against SLFAs comparable to more extensive, resource-heavy MTD solutions. Crucially, our approach achieves this high degree of security while causing a significantly reduced operational overhead, proving that strategic modeling is essential for the future of network defense against these highly specific, damaging link-flooding attacks that continue to plague contemporary digital infrastructures.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods are gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization by incorporating data from various low-fidelity (LF) models. Adaptive sampling methods that dynamically allocate resources among these fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency in exploring and exploiting the design space. However, many existing MF methods rely on restrictive hierarchical assumptions or fail to adequately capture the complex intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels to navigate adaptive sampling. To address this specific technical hurdle, we propose a robust framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and the associated pre-posterior analysis to explicitly utilize their correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each infill sampling iteration includes two steps: We first identify the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model, then we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximize the improvement per unit cost at the location identified in the first step. This is made possible by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space to capture their intricate correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP model enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates will affect the HF response with pre-posterior analysis and determine the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through rigorous test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms benchmark methods in MF global fitting and Bayesian Optimization problems regarding convergence rate and numerical robustness. Moreover, the methodology offers the inherent flexibility to switch between these optimization tasks by simply changing the acquisition function, maintaining consistent performance across all tested applications while focusing exclusively on improving the efficiency of adaptive multi-fidelity sampling strategies for surrogate model construction.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum are secondary brain injuries linked to subarachnoid hemorrhage. We retrospectively analyzed subarachnoid hemorrhage patients treated in our hospital to evaluate the specific impact of these corpus callosum lesions on patient recovery and long-term functional health. We focused exclusively on how the presence of these cytotoxic corpus callosum lesions correlates with clinical deterioration, poor neurological status, and unfavorable patient outcomes following the initial hemorrhage event. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify if these specific corpus callosum lesions serve as independent risk factors for poor clinical outcomes. We analyzed 159 subarachnoid hemorrhage patients; 17 patients (10.7%) demonstrated cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum. Patients with these specific cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum were significantly more likely to be in a severe clinical condition (World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V: odds ratio [OR], 4.53; 95% confidence interval [95% CI]: 1.60-12.84; p = 0.0042). Furthermore, patients with these corpus callosum lesions had a greater propensity for a poor functional outcome three months after the initial onset, as measured by the modified Rankin Scale (OR, 0.22; 95% CI: 0.07-0.66; p = 0.0043). Multivariate analysis confirmed that the development of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum significantly increased the risk of a poor clinical outcome (OR, 4.39; 95% CI: 1.06-18.1; p = 0.037). Consequently, the presence of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum serves as a critical clinical indicator. Although they are usually reversible, the development of these specific cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum remains a strong, reliable predictor of poor, long-term clinical outcomes in patients suffering from subarachnoid hemorrhage.
topics_down.academic_abstracts::39: Information on appropriate protocols for the chemical sedation of Nordestino donkeys remains notably scarce in current veterinary literature. This study sought to evaluate the specific sedative effects of low doses of intravenous xylazine combined with acepromazine in these donkeys. Seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys were included in this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment to assess sedation depth. Four distinct treatments were administered, consisting of two intravenous injections, at baseline and fifteen minutes later. Treatments included acepromazine with saline, saline with xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg, acepromazine with xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg, or acepromazine with xylazine at 0.5 mg/kg. Sedative parameters were evaluated before the baseline and at numerous intervals after treatment. The degree of sedation, measured by the height of the head above ground, and the overall quality of sedation, including ataxia levels and responses to external stimuli, were evaluated by the primary investigator. Three experienced evaluators further assessed video recordings to determine the precise quality of sedation and ataxia levels. Data were analysed using repeated measures ANOVA and Kruskal-Wallis tests. The height of the head above ground was significantly lower than baseline for fifteen minutes after xylazine administration in the lower-dose group and for thirty minutes in the higher-dose groups. All treatments containing xylazine increased the sedation scores for fifteen minutes after administration, with no significant differences found between the groups. Ataxia scores were higher in the xylazine groups compared to the acepromazine-saline group for up to thirty minutes after administration. Ultimately, acepromazine added to xylazine at a lower dosage produced briefer and milder sedation effects than xylazine administered alone at a higher dosage, confirming that dosing adjustments directly influence the duration and intensity of sedative states in these specific animals.
