This is putting focus on damage to the genes that is likely to cause changes linked to a variety of bad health outcomes. This big change is moving the testing focus for genetic damage from a hazard identification only evaluation to a more complete risk assessment approach that provides more helpful information for decision makers regarding the potential risk of genetic damage to exposed humans. To enable this broader context for looking at genetic damage, a next generation testing strategy needs to take into account a broader, more flexible approach to testing, and finally modeling, of damage to the genes as it relates to human exposure. This is consistent with the larger risk assessment context being used in official decision making. As presented here, this flexible approach for looking at damage to the genes focuses on testing for relevant effects that can be, as best as possible, linked to a bad health effect. The most desired link for risk to humans would be changes in parts of the genes linked to human diseases, whether in body cells or reproductive cells. The outline of a flexible approach and linked thoughts are presented in a series of nine steps, some of which can occur at the same time, which was created through a group effort by leading genetic scientists from schools, government, and industry through the International Life Sciences Institute (ILSI) Health and Environmental Sciences Institute (HESI) Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee (GTTC). The ultimate goal is to provide measured data to model the potential risk levels of substances, which cause damage to the genes and lead to human bad health outcomes. Any good risk assessment begins with asking the right risk management questions in a planning and scoping effort. This step sets up the problem to be solved (for example, broadly, does damage to the genes need to be solved, and if so, how to go on). The next two steps put together what is known about the problem by building a knowledge base about the substance of concern and developing a logical biological argument for why testing for damage to the genes is needed or not. By focusing on the risk management problem and potential damage to the genes of concern, the next step of choosing the test or tests takes place. The work on the problem during the earlier steps provides the insight into which tests would most likely produce the most meaningful data. This discussion does not detail the wide range of tests for damage to the genes that are available, but points to types of testing systems that can be very useful. Once the tests are done and looked at, the relevant data sets are chosen for modeling potential risk. From this point on, the data are looked at and modeled as they are for any other safety endpoint. Any observed damage to the genes or effects can be modeled through a dose-response analysis and determination of an estimated starting point. When a measured risk analysis is needed for decision making, a parallel exposure assessment effort is done (exposure assessment is not detailed here as this is not the focus of this discussion; guidelines for this assessment exist elsewhere). Then the starting point for damage to the genes is used with the exposure information to develop risk guesses (for example, using reference dose or margin of exposure approaches) in a risk characterization and presented to risk managers for informing decision making. This approach is usable now for including results of damage to the genes into the decision-making process for checking potential bad outcomes in chemically exposed humans and is consistent with the ILSI HESI Risk Assessment in the 21st Century (RISK21) roadmap. This applies to any substance to which humans are exposed, including medicines, farm products, food additives, and other chemicals. It is time for official bodies to include the broader knowledge and insights provided by results of damage to the genes into the assessments of risk to more fully understand the potential of bad outcomes in chemically exposed humans, thus improving the assessment of risk due to damage to the genes. The historical use of data on damage to the genes as a yes or no gateway for possible cancer risk has been too narrowly focused in risk assessment. The recent advances in testing for and understanding damage to the genes, including eventually changes in how genes are turned on and off, obviously add a greater wealth of information for determining potential risk to humans. Official bodies need to embrace this big change from hazard identification to measured analysis and to include the wider range of damage to the genes in their assessments of risk to humans. The measured analyses and methods discussed here can be easily applied to test results of damage to the genes now. Indeed, with the passage of the recent update to the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) in the US, the new generation testing strategy for damage to the genes described here provides a regulatory agency (here the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), but suitable for others) a golden opportunity to look again at the way it addresses risk-based testing for damage to the genes, including hazard identification and exposure. Environ. Mol. Mutagen. 58:264-283, 2017. © 2016 The Authors. Environmental and Molecular Mutagenesis Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
words_common.academic_abstracts::1: Food boosters might help the growth of babies born early or too small, but they might also raise the chance of health problems later in life. We did a careful review and study of studies to check the effects of extra food nutrients for babies born small on their later growth and body function. We searched OvidMedline, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, and Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews from the start until April 1, 2019, and controlled-trials.com, clinicaltrials.gov, and anzctr.org.au. Trials picked at random or almost at random were included if the goal was to increase food intake to help the growth or development of babies born small and looked at results after they left the hospital. The two main goals were thinking problems and health risks, checked in toddlers (less than 3 years), childhood (3 to 8 years), and the teen years (9 to 18 years). Two people checking the work took out the data on their own. Quality was checked using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool, and data were put together using random-effect models. Twenty-one trials picked at random and one almost at random trial of differing quality involving 3,680 babies were included. In toddlers born small, extra food did not change thinking problems (relative risk [RR] 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.67 to 1.49; P = 0.99), and there were no differences in thinking scores (mean difference [MD] 0.57; 95% CI -0.71 to 1.84; P = 0.38) or movement scores (MD 1.16; 95% CI -0.32 to 2.65; P = 0.12) between groups that got extra food and those that did not. However, fewer children who got the extra food had movement problems (RR 0.76; 95% CI 0.62 to 0.94; P = 0.01). In small group looks, the extra food improved thinking scores in boys (MD 5.60; 95% CI 1.07 to 10.14; P = 0.02), but not girls born small (MD -2.04; 95% CI -7.04 to 2.95; P = 0.42), and did not change thinking or movement scores in the group of children born small for their age. In childhood, there was no difference in thinking problems (RR 0.81; 95% CI 0.26 to 2.57; P = 0.72) or thinking scores (MD 1.02; 95% CI -1.91 to 3.95; P = 0.50) between the groups. There were also no differences in blood pressure, fat in the blood, and bad cholesterol levels (all P > 0.05). However, children who got the extra food had lower blood sugar after not eating (mmol/L: MD -0.20; 95% CI -0.34 to -0.06; P = 0.005) and higher good cholesterol levels (mmol/L: MD 0.11; 95% CI 0.02 to 0.19; P = 0.02). In small group looks, there was no proof of differences in blood pressure between groups in boys or girls born small, or in children born small for their age. In the teen years, there was no difference between groups in blood pressure, fat in the blood, bad or good cholesterol, blood sugar, or insulin levels (all P > 0.05). Problems include a lot of unexplained differences, low to very low quality of the proof, and limited data beyond early childhood. In this review of trials, we found no proof that early food boosters for babies born small changed later thinking, though there was some proof that it may lower movement problems in toddlers. Unlike findings from watching studies, proof from trials suggests that early food boosters for babies born small improves some health outcomes in childhood. CRD42019127858.
words_common.academic_abstracts::2: Goals Recently, two quick test kits for the cat AIDS virus (Witness and Anigen Rapid) were reported as being able to tell the difference between vaccinated cats and infected cats at one point in time, no matter how much time passed between the testing and the last shot (zero to seven years). The goal of the current study was to look closely at how the body makes antibodies against the cat AIDS virus over time after the suggested first set of shots. Methods First, leftover blood liquid from the original study was tested using a lab test to see if negative results with quick tests were because of low levels rather than no antibodies to the virus protein. Second, a future-looking study was done using kittens and cats that had never been exposed to the virus, which were given a first set of cat AIDS shots using a store-bought dead virus vaccine (Fel-O-Vax FIV, three shots under the skin four weeks apart) and tested many times (up to eleven times) over six months, using four store-bought quick test kits (SNAP FIV/FeLV Combo [finds antibodies to p15/p24], Witness FeLV/FIV [gp40], Anigen Rapid FIV/FeLV [p24/gp40] and VetScan FeLV/FIV Rapid [p24]). Results The lab test showed cats from the original study vaccinated within the last zero to fifteen months had findable levels of antibodies to the virus protein, even though they tested negative with two kits that use that protein as a catch tool (Witness and Anigen Rapid kits). The future-looking study showed that antibody testing with SNAP Combo and VetScan Rapid was positive in all cats two weeks after the second shot, and stayed positive for the whole time of the study (twelve of twelve and ten of twelve cats positive). Antibody testing with Witness and Anigen Rapid was also positive in many cats two weeks after the second shot (eight of twelve and seven of twelve), but antibody levels dropped below the level of finding them in most cats (ten of twelve) by one month after the third final shot. All cats tested negative using Witness and Anigen Rapid six months after the third final shot. Conclusions and importance This study has shown that a first set of cat AIDS shots does not mess with cat AIDS antibody testing using Witness and Anigen Rapid, if the first shots did not happen within the last six months. So, Witness and Anigen Rapid antibody test kits can be used with trust to find out the infection status at the time of yearly booster shots to help find cases where the vaccine did not work and in cats that have not had a first set of shots within the last six months. How long the antibody response lasts after yearly booster shots and the resulting effect on antibody testing using quick kits needs to be found by more research. The reason for the change in how well the cat AIDS antibody test kits work is still not clear.
words_common.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a rare genetic condition marked by harmless growths in many body parts along with a high rate of seizures, learning problems, and autism. TSC is caused by broken versions of the TSC1 or TSC2 genes. This genetic change leads to overactivity of mTOR, which can be blocked by mTOR blockers, such as rapamycin, which have shown real success in the treatment of symptoms linked to TSC. The goal of this current study was (1) to find biological changes linked to social and thinking problems in the brain tissue of Tsc1 +/- mice and (2) to look into the biological effects of rapamycin treatment, which has been shown to improve behavior problems linked to the genes. Biological changes in the front part of the brain and the memory center of Tsc1 +/- and normal mice, with or without rapamycin treatment, were studied. A measuring mass-based protein testing method was used as a fair way to find changes in protein levels. Changes found in the first check were confirmed using a second careful test. Protein group analysis was used to find broken biological pathways. Testing of Tsc1 +/- mice and normal mice (n = 30) found 51 proteins changed in the front of the brain and 108 in the memory center. Computer analysis combined with specific protein testing revealed several broken biological pathways. Using specific tests, protein changes in the memory center confirmed the pathways for nerve coating, nerve branches, and cell stress, a rise in building proteins and the mTOR protein. Testing was also used on Tsc1 +/- and normal mice (n = 34) treated with rapamycin or a dummy drug. Rapamycin treatment had a stronger effect in Tsc1 +/- mice with big changes in 231 and 106 proteins, respectively. The cell pathways for cell stress and cell death were found to be affected in Tsc1 +/- mice and the cell parts for nerve coating and nerve threads were affected by rapamycin treatment. Thirty-three proteins which were changed in Tsc1 +/- mice were made normal following rapamycin treatment, among them cell stress related proteins, nerve coating-specific and building proteins. Biological changes in the Tsc1 +/- mouse brain were more clear in the memory center compared to the front part of the brain. Pathways linked to nerve coating and cell stress response were clearly affected and, at least in part, made normal following rapamycin treatment. The results could aid in the finding of new drug targets for the treatment of thinking, social and mental symptoms in autism. Similar pathways have also been linked to other mental and brain-wasting disorders and could mean similar disease processes. Thus, the possible power of mTOR blockers is worth more study not only for autism but also for other brain and mental diseases.
words_common.academic_abstracts::4: Tiny bits of glass are hopeful tools that can carry helpful health substances to body parts like the heart in a way that people can manage. However, heart damage caused by these tiny bits of glass has lately been linked to odd calcium movement and energy loss in heart muscle cells. Also, the exact reasons for this energy loss are still not clear. To make these reasons clear, this report looks at heart function outside the body and the cell power centers after contact with these tiny bits of glass. The added doses of these tiny bits of glass lowered the mechanical work level of the rat heart with a middle point of blocking at 93 units, affecting how it relaxes. In separate cell power centers, these tiny bits of glass were found to be pulled inside, stopping the process of making energy and clearly lowering the power center wall charge. The power center opening was also triggered with a growing dose of these tiny bits of glass and partly fixed with a strong blocker of the opening, Cyclosporine A. The work of a certain enzyme and the change in sulfur parts in the energy carrier were found to be lower because of contact with these tiny bits of glass, suggesting that these tiny bits of glass start the opening through sulfur changes and the making of bad oxygen molecules. In heart cells touched by these tiny bits of glass, better life and a drop in bad oxygen were seen after using a special power center protector, MitoTEMPO. At the same time, Cyclosporine A treatment in adult rat heart cells lowered the death of cells started by these tiny bits of glass and brought back energy production from 32.4 to 65.4 percent. Also, we did a check of the power center effect of these tiny bits of glass in human heart muscle cells. We saw a 40 percent block of the top oxygen use rate in power centers at 500 units. Under this state we found a big drop in the extra breathing power. This data shows a drop in the amount of extra energy that can be made by power centers during a sudden jump in energy need. In human heart muscle cells, more cell waste release and cell death were found at higher doses of these tiny bits of glass, reaching 85 and 48 percent. Such bad effects were partly stopped by using Cyclosporine A. Thus, contact with these tiny bits of glass harms heart function through power center failure by opening the pore. These noted effects can be partly stopped by lowering bad oxygen or delaying the opening of the pore. These new ways which led to heart safety could be seen as possible cures to lower the bad side effects of contact with these tiny bits of glass.
words_common.academic_abstracts::5: Getting back to play for National Football League players after single knee ligament tears has been described. However, no studies have reported on getting back to play for NFL players after multiple knee ligament injuries. NFL players with multiple knee ligament injuries have lower rates of getting back to play and longer recovery times than players with single ligament tears. Second, players with ACL and MCL injuries will have higher rates of getting back to play and shorter time to get back to play than players with an ACL tear and outer back corner damage. Past group study. Level 4. Publicly available NFL injury data were looked at for all multiple knee ligament injuries that happened between 2000 and 2016 with information about getting back to play. Players were left out if getting back to play was limited for reasons not related to the injury. Gathered data included type of injury, getting back to play, time to get back to play in days, number and percentage of games played, and how well they played. A total of 50 NFL players with multiple knee ligament injuries met the rules for being included and left out. The overall rate of getting back to play was 64.0 percent. Players with ACL and MCL tears had a rate of 70.8 percent, whereas players with ACL and PCL or LCL tears had a rate of 55.6 percent. Average time to get back to play for all 50 players was about 389 days. The average time to get back to play for players with ACL and MCL injuries was 305 days, compared with 459 days and 609 days for those with combined ACL and PCL or LCL injuries and full knee displacements. Players with ACL and MCL injuries were more likely to return to their former level of playing than those with ACL and PCL or LCL injuries. The rate for players with multiple knee ligament injuries is much less than the rate for players with single ACL tears. In addition, players with ACL and MCL tears have a higher rate, a much shorter time to get back to play, and a better chance of returning to their former level of playing than players with ACL and PCL or LCL tears. Multiple knee ligament injuries change the ability of a football player to return to their sport. ACL and MCL tears are linked with a better outlook compared with ACL and PCL or LCL tears.
words_common.academic_abstracts::6: High blood pressure in the lungs during physical activity is a sign of how serious a narrowed heart valve is. However, the reasons linked to high lung pressure during exercise are not well understood. The goal of this study was to check the factors linked to the lung pressure response to exercise in patients with simple rheumatic narrowed heart valves. An extra goal was to find out the effect of exercise-related high lung pressure on health results. One hundred thirty patients with narrowed heart valves (94% women; average age, 45 plus or minus 11 years) had heart ultrasound tests during exercise. A range of heart ultrasound measurements were taken while resting and at peak exercise. A test using a stationary bike while lying down was performed. The main result was heart valve treatment, either by tube or surgery. In the whole group, the top lung artery pressure went up from 38.3 plus or minus 13.4 units at rest to 65.8 plus or minus 20.7 units during exercise. Increases in the average valve pressure difference, right heart function, left heart chamber size, and total heart chamber flexibility were linked to lung pressure at peak exercise, after accounting for changes in heart rate. During the tracking period (middle time, 17 months; range, 1 to 45 months), 46 bad health events were seen. By using a standard math analysis adjusted for age and sex, the lung pressure reached at peak exercise was an important way to guess a bad health result (adjusted risk ratio, 1.025; 95% confidence range, 1.010 to 1.040; P = .001). The New York Heart Association functional class and the link between valve size and total heart chamber flexibility were also important ways to guess bad events. Time-based graphs for the model with lung pressure during exercise were better than for the model with lung pressure at rest, with a clear improvement from 3 years onward. In patients with narrowed heart valves, the lung artery pressure response to exercise is decided by a group of factors, including the average valve pressure difference at exercise, total heart chamber flexibility, left heart chamber size, and right heart function. Lung artery pressure at peak exercise helps predict health results and adds extra value beyond what is provided by standard resting measurements, including valve size.
words_common.academic_abstracts::7: The effect of long-term liver illness on how patients with COVID-19 do is not clear. So, we wanted to look into this link. We looked at the results for all adult patients staying in hospitals with COVID-19 in France in 2020. We calculated the adjusted chances to measure the links between long-term liver illness, drinking problems, being on a breathing machine, and dying in the hospital within thirty days. The group was made of 259,110 patients (middle age 70 years; 52% men), including 15,476 (6.0%) and 10,006 (3.9%) patients with long-term liver illness and drinking problems, in that order. Death happened in 38,203 (15%) patients, including 7,475 (28%) after being on a breathing machine, and 2,941 (19%) with long-term liver illness. The adjusted odds for being on a breathing machine and dying within thirty days were 1.54 and 1.79 for long-term liver illness; 0.55 and 0.54 for mild liver illness; 0.64 and 0.71 for stable scarring of the liver; 0.65 and 2.21 for severe scarring of the liver; 0.34 and 1.38 for liver cancer; and 0.82 and 1.11 for drinking problems. Long-term viral liver swelling; other types of liver swelling; organ, including liver, replacements, and conditions that weaken the immune system were not linked to death from COVID-19. Long-term liver illness raised the chance of death from COVID-19 in France in 2020. Limiting medical care might have played a part in deaths from COVID-19 in French people with a liver problem or a drinking problem. We studied the results, including being on a breathing machine and dying within thirty days, of all adults with COVID-19 who left hospitals in France in 2020. Patients with mild liver illness; stable scarring of the liver; organ replacements; or conditions that weaken the immune system were not at a higher risk of dying from COVID-19. Patients with drinking problems, severe scarring of the liver, or liver cancer were at a higher risk of dying from COVID-19 but were less likely to get help from a breathing machine. Our results show that limiting medical care may have helped cause the extra deaths in French people with a liver problem or a drinking problem.
words_common.academic_abstracts::8: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by the virus SARS-CoV-2 has led to a large number of deaths around the world. COVID-19 poses a serious threat to human life. The symptoms of COVID-19 are many and severe, and twenty percent of sick patients are reported to be in a very bad condition. A loss in lung function and lung scarring are the main signs of patients with the severe form of the disease. The lung function is affected, even after getting better, thereby greatly affecting the mind and general health of patients, and significantly reducing their quality of life. Participants must meet the following rules at the same time: over eighteen years of age, should have recovered from severe or very bad COVID-19 cases, should show lung scarring after getting better, and should show a specific weakness in body energy and fluids as indicated in the system of traditional Chinese medicine. The chosen people will be picked at random for treatment or comparison groups. The treatment group will get modern medicine plus traditional Chinese medicine whereas the comparison group will be given modern medicine plus a fake version of the traditional medicine. The lung function score will be constantly watched and written down. By comparing the treatment result between the two groups, the study plans to look into whether traditional Chinese medicine can improve the effectiveness of modern medicine in patients with lung scarring arising as a result after a COVID-19 infection. Lung scarring is one of the deadly results for some severe or very bad COVID-19 cases, and some studies show that the medicine pirfenidone leads to a delay in the drop of breathing capacity, thereby reducing the death rate in part. Additionally, although traditional Chinese medicine has been proven to be helpful in treating lung scarring, its role in treating lung scarring related to COVID-19 has not been studied. So, a large, group-based, random, fair, future medical trial has been planned and will be done to find out if a new combined treatment for lung scarring related to COVID-19 works well and if it can improve the quality of life of patients. This trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2000033284) on 26th May 2020.
words_common.academic_abstracts::9: Heat and water availability are two of the most important things affecting all parts of a frog's main body functions such as body heat, water loss through the skin and basic energy use. Since frogs show clear differences between males and females, evidence suggests that these functions are further changed by other factors such as how dry the air is, sex and body weight. However, a small number of studies have tested how true these results are across a wide range of normal outdoor temperatures, while taking where they live into account. Thus, the goal of this study was to look at the role of air temperature on body heat, whole-animal water loss and whole-animal energy use in three wild caught African frog species with different ways of living: the mostly water-living African clawed frog ( Xenopus laevis ), stream-breeding common river frog ( Amietia delalandii ), and the mostly land-living raucous toad ( Sclerophrys capensis ). Experiments were done at a range of test temperatures (5-35 °C, at 5 °C steps). We found that how dry the air is better predicted rates of water loss than air temperature in two of the three species looked at. Moreover, we found that body heat, whole-animal water loss and whole-animal energy use went up with rising air temperature, while body heat went up with rising body weight in A. delalandii and S. capensis but not in X. laevis . Whole-animal energy use went up with rising body weight in S. capensis only. We did not find any big effect of air dryness, body weight or sex on whole-animal water loss within species. Lastly, body weight did not change body heat, whole-animal energy use and water loss in the mostly water-living X. laevis . These results show that body weight may not have the same effect on main body functions, and that the influence of body weight may also depend on the species way of living. Thus, the truth of body weight as an important factor should be looked at in the context of both body function and species home type.
words_common.academic_abstracts::10: Time confusion is a problem with the way a person understands the order of time. This change in how time is felt has been described as being linked to issues in the brain, specifically in the middle part called the middle nucleus. We report the medical cases of two patients with sudden strokes caused by blood clots in that area, with a medical presentation based on this symptom and the recognition of which was very important in the treatment plan. In the first and second cases, it is described how the feeling of time was important for the diagnosis of the stroke condition in both patients. Awareness and sharing of this link may be vital in the care of patients with brain disorders. This is due to the possibility of changing the first plan, since the recognition of a specific symptom, such as time confusion, can stop the spread of brain damage, in addition to the long-term effects that it causes, especially those of a thinking nature. Time confusion as a guide symptom of a middle brain stroke. Introduction. Time confusion is a problem of the understanding of the time sequence. This change of the timing has been described linked in a characteristic way to the brain involvement, specifically to the middle nucleus. Clinical cases. We present the clinical cases of two patients with sudden strokes of location in that area, with a condition based on this symptom and whose recognition resulted essential in the treatment approach. Both in the first and in the second case it is described how the understanding of the timing was essential for the diagnosis of the stroke condition of both patients. Discussion. The knowledge and the spread of this link can result fundamental in the management of the patients with brain changes. This is due to the possibility that comes from influencing and changing the initial approach, since the recognition of a specific symptom, such as time confusion, can avoid the spread of the brain damage, and prevent in this way the effects, above all mental ones, that it causes in the long run.
words_common.academic_abstracts::11: Some catching illnesses, such as the flu, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be spread when tiny drops full of virus pushed out from a sick person are breathed in by someone else, which is known as the air spread way. These tiny drops full of virus are more thick in the breath pushed out of a sick person than anywhere else in a well-mixed room, but this close-up increase in virus exposure has not been well measured. Spread of air viruses depends on things that are naturally changing and, in many cases, poorly known, and measuring this doubt requires large groups of computer models that cover the changes in input details. However, models that are well-suited to copy the close-up growth of breathing drops are also very expensive for computers, which limits the study of parameter doubt. In order to perform many models that cover the wide change in things controlling air spread, we made the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets (QuaRAD). QuaRAD is an efficient way for copying the growth of tiny drops full of virus after they are pushed out from a sick person, their landing in the nose of a person who could get sick, and the following risk of first infection. We copied 10 000 cases to measure the risk of first infection by a particular virus, SARS-CoV-2. The expected risk of infection was very different among cases and, in each case, was strongly increased near the sick person. In more than 50% of cases, the physical space needed to avoid close-up increases in air spread was beyond the suggested safe distance of two meters (six feet) if the sick person is not wearing a mask, though this distance defining the close-up area was also very different among cases; the change in the close-up area is explained mostly by change in breath speed. Our findings suggest that keeping at least two meters of distance from a sick person greatly lowers exposure to air viruses; protections against air spread, such as N95 masks, should be ready when distancing is not possible.
words_common.academic_abstracts::12: Open breaks are dirty wounds that contain many kinds of harmful germs; therefore, strong medicine to kill germs should be included in the care plan. Medicine should be started as soon after the hurt as possible, ideally within three hours of the hurt, after which time the chance of sickness has been said to go up. Time to surgical cleaning within twelve hours of the hurt has not been said to change the chance of sickness, given that a person is being treated with medicine. A medicine bead bag and vacuum tools for closing wounds may help lower the risk for later and hospital-based dirt and following sickness. Open breaks are always linked with a soft body part hurt; therefore, they can be seen as a soft body part hurt that includes a broken bone. The handling of the bone and the soft body parts in a person with an open break is the main factor for bone healing and getting back the use of the hurt limb. The making of a soft body part care plan must happen during the first wound check and the first fixing of an open break and should not be seen as a later or following step. A soft body part surgeon should be asked for help on the night of the hurt. Picking a way to fix the break depends on the broken bone, where the break is, the size of the soft body part hurt and dirt, and the health status of the person. More than one way to fix it may work for the handling of a specific hurt; therefore, a surgeon's skill and the tools on hand also should be thought about. Surgeons must know how bone healing works to get good results in the handling of open breaks. The main parts of these bone healing treatments include making the body ready, checking a person's food intake, right use of drugs, and getting rid of sickness. Surgeons should think about bone moving and using helpful substances to get bone joining in people with a new open break and in the handling of slow joining or no joining.
words_common.academic_abstracts::13: GOAL: Common patterns of sticking to rules have been seen with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise. It is not known whether such patterns of sticking to rules exist among users of long-term medicines. We tried to guess the percentage of patients who start again on bone-thinning therapy after a long break in medicine use and to find the reasons linked to a return to sticking to rules. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of a bone-thinning medicine (alendronate, calcitonin, estrogen, raloxifene, or risedronate) who were age 65 or older and had a long break in getting refills, defined as a time of at least 60 days after the end of one prescription in which no refill for any bone-thinning medicine was gotten. Survival graphs were used to guess the length of time until therapy is started again. We guessed the link between patient traits and the rate of starting treatment again using standard statistical analysis. We then did a case crossover study to look at whether certain events happening during the follow-up triggered a return to getting refills. RESULTS: Of patients who stopped therapy for at least 60 days, an estimated 30% started treatment again within 6 months, and 50% started again within 2 years. Among patients who had at least 6 months of constant use before their break in treatment (n=5863), 42% started therapy again within 6 months and 59% within 2 years. Younger patients, women, and those with a history of a broken bone were more likely to return after a break in medicine use. Recent hip breaks, leaving nursing homes, and bone strength testing also guessed a return to treatment. CONCLUSION: Long gaps in treatment are common among users of bone-thinning medicines. Because the power of these drugs used in a broken way is unknown, help for sticking to rules should stress the need for constant medicine use. More study is needed to understand why patients often go for months without getting refills and also whether similar usage patterns exist for other long-term medicines.
words_common.academic_abstracts::14: Differences in the stomach germ community of animals have been linked to many stomach and immune system diseases. However, it is not clear which groups of germs are linked to stomach trouble, and if certain stomach areas or specific times during growth are more likely to be affected. We also know very little of this process in wild animals, despite a growing understanding of the general importance of stomach germs for health. Here, we look at the changes that happen in the germs during sickness in different parts of the stomach in a long-lived bird with high baby death rates, the ostrich (Struthio camelus). We looked at the gene makeup of the small intestine, the blind gut, and the large intestine of 68 birds that died of suspected stomach swelling during the first 3 months of life (sick birds), and of 50 healthy birds that were put to sleep as matching comparisons. We combined these facts with long-term environmental and waste sampling to find possible sources of bad bacteria and to find out at which stage of growth sickness-linked bacteria appear. Sick birds had much lower germ variety and differed greatly in their germ makeup from healthy birds in all three regions of the stomach. The clear link between low variety and disease was steady across all ages in the small intestine, but dropped with age in the blind gut and large intestine. Several germ groups were linked to death, while others were linked to health. Environmental samples showed no proof of sickness-linked bacteria being present in either the food, water, or dirt. Instead, the repeated waste sampling showed that bad germs were already present shortly after hatching and grew in birds with low germ variety, resulting in high death rates several weeks later. Finding the origins of bad germs in babies and the factors that later affect the growth of diverse stomach germs may be key to understanding sickness and animal growth. Video Abstract.
words_common.academic_abstracts::15: We look into the reason for the quantum speedup -- quantum methods needing fewer work steps than their normal ways. We grow their look to the way of setting the problem. The first check picks a setting at random, Bob (the problem setter) changes it into the one wanted. This look is to Bob and any outside watcher, it cannot be to Alice (the problem solver). It would tell her the task done by the hidden box, which to her should be kept inside it. We use related quantum ways. To Alice, the fixing of the quantum state due to the first check is held back at the end of her problem solving work. To her, the method input state stays one of full not knowing of the setting. By hidden box work, she changes it into the output state that, for each possible setting, holds the right answer, found by the final check. We show that we can give to the final check the picking of any part -- say the R-th part -- of the random result of the first check. This sets the input state for Alice on a state of lower mess where she knows a matching part of the problem setting. The quantum method is a sum over normal events in each of which Alice, knowing ahead one of the R-th parts of the setting, does the hidden box work still needed to find the answer. Given a puzzle problem and a value of R, this back in time model gives the number of hidden box work steps needed to solve it. In the other way, given a known quantum method, it gives the value of R that explains its speed up. R = 1/2 always gives the number of hidden box work steps needed by a current quantum method and the size of the number needed by the best one.
words_common.academic_abstracts::16: Heart disease and medical treatment may both lead to a higher risk for blood clots because of changed blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the physical forces on blood cells passing through the rooms of the heart. Specifically, the amount of blood cell activity is changed by the level and type of physical pressure in the blood flow. Here we look at the blood flow in the left side of the heart through a computer model built from patient information. The blood flow in the heart is modeled by standard math equations, and the flow through the heart valve by a model which shows the expected opening of the valve. A math method is used to solve the equations, from which a simulation of the speed and pressure of the blood flow is built. A three part breakdown of the speed change is then used to tell the difference between stiff body spinning flow, smooth stretching flow, and sliding flow. The three part breakdown enables the separation of three basic different flow shapes, each making a clear type of physical force on the blood cells in the flow. We compare the results to simulations where a heart valve clip treatment is modeled, which leads to a big change of the heart flow. It was found that the sliding in the simulation cases treated with clips increased more compared to the untreated case than the spinning and stretching did. A decrease in valve opening area of sixty four percent in one of the cases led to a ninety percent increase in spinning and stretching, but a one hundred fifty percent increase in sliding. The computer analysis suggests a process for patient specific simulation of medical treatments in the heart with a detailed look at the resulting blood flow, which could support medical risk checks about blood cell activity and blood clots.
words_common.academic_abstracts::17: The spread out very high energy gamma ray light seen in the middle two hundred light years of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the thick matter spread in the Central Molecular Zone up to a lengthways distance of about one hundred thirty light years to the Galaxy Centre, where the flow quickly drops. Recent sensitive H.E.S.S. study showed that the cosmic ray density shape drops with the distance to the middle, making data match with a steady cosmic particle accelerator at the Galaxy Centre. In this paper, we grow this study to get for the first time a detailed look of the link with matter and to look for extra features and single gamma ray sources in the inner two hundred light years. Taking advantage of two hundred fifty hours of H.E.S.S. data and better study methods we do a detailed shape study of the spread out high energy light seen from the Galaxy Centre ridge and rebuild its total range. We show that the light linked with thick matter covers the full Central Molecular Zone and that its flow is about half the total spread out light flow. We also find some light at higher height likely made by hard collisions of cosmic rays in less thick parts of the Galaxy Centre space gas. We find an extra light part centered on the Galaxy Centre and reaching over about fifteen light years that fits with the existence of a strong cosmic ray density change and confirms the presence of a cosmic ray maker at the very middle of our Galaxy. We show that the range of the full ridge spread out light fits with the one earlier found from the middle parts, suggesting that a single group of particles fills the entire Central Molecular Zone. Finally, we report the finding of a high energy gamma ray source near the Galaxy Centre radio arc and argue that it is made by the pulsar wind cloud candidate G0.13-0.11.
words_common.academic_abstracts::18: These global medical practice guidelines for developmental coordination disorder, started by the European Academy of Childhood Disability, aim to answer main questions on the meaning, finding, testing, treatment, and social and emotional sides of the disorder relevant for daily medical work. Main questions in five areas were thought about through reading studies and formal group agreement. For suggestions based on proof, study searches on how it works, testing, and treatment were brought up to date since the last set in 2012. New searches were done for social issues and older children and adults. Proof was ranked by the Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine and turned into advice. For advice based on formal group agreement, two meetings of a global, mixed group of experts were held with five more rounds of voting to create good medical practice advice. Thirty-five pieces of advice were made. Eight were based on the proof from reading studies. Twenty-two were brought up to date from the 2012 advice. New advice relates to finding and testing and social issues. Also, one new piece of advice looks at active video games as additions to more usual activity-based and participation-based treatments, and two new pieces of advice were made for older children and adults with the disorder. The global medical practice guide is a full look at the disorder and current thinking based on research proof and expert agreement. It shows the best current knowledge for doctors and scientists of many fields. The global guide may act as a base for national rules. Updated global medical practice rules on developmental coordination disorder. Improved and expanded advice on medical testing and treatment for the disorder. A short summary of current research on how the disorder works. A short summary of social issues in the disorder, with effects for medical practice. The first global advice to think about older children and adults with the disorder.
words_common.academic_abstracts::19: High blood pressure can lead to mood problems that may get worse or get better depending on the type of blood pressure medicine prescribed. Depression is linked to changes in basic brain balance particularly that of the front part of the brain, which is involved in blood pressure control. Furthermore, different blood vessel drugs may change the brain's balance in a way that contributes to thinking status. We studied the two-sided activity of several brain chemicals in the front part of the brain as a sign of the working status of certain brain chemicals involved in mood. Using chemical parts as bases, we measured the activity of these helpers in the left and right front part of the brain of normal untreated Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) and naturally high blood pressure rats (SHRs) and compared their activities with WKY or SHR treated with the blood pressure drugs captopril (CAP) and propranolol (PRO) or with the high blood pressure drug N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester. Blood pressure was also measured in all WKY and SHR groups. Untreated WKY, WKY treated with CAP or PRO and SHR treated with CAP showed normal values of blood pressure. However, WKY treated with N (G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester as well as untreated SHR and SHR treated with PRO and N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester showed high values of blood pressure. Changes in the two-sided spread of brain chemicals were depending on the kind of rat, the helper being checked and the drug used. Normal blood pressure WKY groups (WKY, CAP, PRO) showed connections inside one side mainly in the left side. In contrast, WKY treated with N(G)-nitro-L-arginine methyl ester and SHR groups showed connections inside one side mainly in the right side. Connections between the two sides were mostly seen in WKY as well as in SHR groups with blood pressure treatments (CAP, PRO). Our results suggest specific brain patterns of activity in WKY that change in SHR. This observation may be related to the thinking problems that have been described in these animals and that change under blood pressure drug treatments.
words_common.academic_abstracts::20: The goal of this study is to look at the worth and success of emergency medical teams for different warning events in total hip replacement patients. A past review of all emergency team events at one big, main hospital center from 2014 to 2016 was done. Rules for being in the study were set as patients over eighteen years old that had a first or redo hip replacement. Information asked for included background facts, main reason for the emergency team, health score, underlying cause, if any changes in care happened, and if the patient was moved to a higher level of care. In total, 168 emergency calls were made on 153 hip replacement patients (average age 65.2 years; average body mass index 32.3, 66% female). Length of stay in the hospital for first and redo hip replacement was 3.4 and 6.2 days. This was much longer than the length of stay for first hip replacement patients (2.4 days) and redo hip replacement patients (4.6 days) that did not need an emergency team. There were no deaths. Emergency teams for low blood pressure or feeling faint and for fainting resulted in much fewer changes in care than fast heart rate, low oxygen, confused mental state, and other reasons. Emergency teams for low blood pressure or feeling faint, fainting, and low oxygen resulted in much fewer patients being moved to a higher level of care than fast heart rate. Low blood pressure or feeling faint was found to be much more commonly due to low fluid levels than other causes. Low oxygen was much more commonly due to lung collapse and too much pain medicine. Confused mental state was also much more commonly caused by too much pain medicine. In patients having hip replacement, emergency teams for low blood pressure or feeling faint and fainting were much less likely to result in changes in care or moving to a higher level of care compared to fast heart rate. The most common causes were potentially preventable, including low fluid levels and pain medicine use.
words_common.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical help is an important part of sudden stroke care. We created a before-hospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA before-hospital stroke scale for clot-busting medicine given through a vein (TOPSPIN) for sorting patients with blood-clot strokes and special needs for clot-busting medicine in December 2006; this scale has 5 parts including being awake, irregular heart rhythm, speech problems, trouble moving the arms, and trouble moving the legs. The goal of this study was to look at the results of 10 years of TOPSPIN use and to tell the difference between blood-clot stroke and bleeding stroke in the real world. We kept track of patients who were brought to our hospital and checked by Toyota city ambulance teams using the TOPSPIN from December 2006 to January 2017. We looked at the final diagnosis when leaving the hospital (blood-clot stroke, bleeding stroke, or stroke look-alike), the accuracy of the stroke test, the rate of treatment to open blood vessels, and the clinical differences among patients with bleeding stroke, blood-clot stroke, and stroke look-alikes. A total of 1,482 patients were seen; 1,134 (76.5%) were patients with stroke (628 blood-clot type, 34 mini-stroke type, and 472 bleeding type) and 348 (23.5%) without stroke (80 with seizures, 42 with fainting, 27 with low blood sugar, and 199 other). Among 628 patients with blood-clot stroke, 130 (20.7%) received clot-busting medicine through a vein, surgery inside the vessels, or both. The presence of irregular heart rhythm, older age, lower blood pressure, and lower total TOPSPIN score was more often linked with blood-clot stroke than with bleeding stroke. In statistical analysis, the presence of irregular heart rhythm was tied to blood-clot stroke. The TOPSPIN is a simple before-hospital stroke scale that includes a check of irregular heart rhythm. Finding irregular heart rhythm before reaching the hospital may point to a higher chance of a blood-clot stroke.
words_common.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to find the distance of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT light data of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with the camera at VLT in the last five years, for a total study time of 52 hours. The combined light data is the deepest ever obtained of a galaxy in the early universe. We do not find any light signal or steady glow over the whole light range, up to 10100A. Based on an accurate set of tests, we are able to put a very firm top limit of f(Lya)<3x10^(-18) erg/s/cm2 at 3-9 sigma in the explored range, corresponding to a rest-frame size EW<9A. Combining this limit with the light model we improve the distance to be z=6.82+/- 0.1 (1-sigma). The same light fitting shows that GDS-1408 is relatively dusty (A1600~1) with a dust corrected star birth rate of ~ 20 Msol/yr. The comparison between the natural size predicted by the standard theory and the observed top limit, provides a limit on the actual light escape fraction of f_(esc)^(eff)(Lya)<8%. Even though we cannot rule out a major contribution of the space between galaxies in blocking the light, a likely idea is that GDS-1408 is fairly old and contains enough gas and dust to block the light, before it reaches the space between galaxies. The distance confirmation of even the best z~7 candidates is very hard to achieve unless the light or unusually strong space gas light lines are present with the current generation of 8-10m class telescopes. We show that both JWST and E-ELT will be necessary to make clear progress. Currently, the increased distance accuracy obtained with this kind of study makes ALMA a good option for the distance confirmation.
words_common.academic_abstracts::23: The survival of Salmonella as a germ indicator in rotting plant waste was studied. The method of adding germs was used to give the known amounts of Salmonella involved in rotting. The liquid of Salmonella was added directly into the rotting material. The direct addition was compared with adding germs in a small bottle method. The Salmonella liquid was placed into a small bottle and put into the middle of the rotting material before starting the rotting process. The normal method that is used for the counting of Salmonella is step by step thinning followed by standard filter paper cleaning as suggested in the compost quality standard method PAS 100 and the British Standard (BS EN ISO 6579:2002). This study was designed to look at the link of heat and contact material that may also involve in germ activity specifically to Salmonella. The exposure to an average heat during rotting of about 55-60 degrees was kept for at least 3 days as it was reported enough to kill the vast majority of gut germs (Deportes et al., 1995). The amount of Salmonella and heat for both samples was set as a sign to decide the survival of Salmonella in direct and not direct addition. This study gives the numbers of death rate for Salmonella during rotting. The difference between direct contact (Sample A) and no contact of Salmonella with rotting material (Sample B) during rotting was also shown. The results from the lab scale of the rotting study has shown that after 8 days (which included at least at 66 degrees) the numbers of Salmonella in Sample A were below the limits in the UK compost standard (known as PAS 100) (BSI, 2005) which required the compost to be free of Salmonella. Meanwhile, Sample B still gives a high amount of Salmonella even after rotting for 20 days.
words_common.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is linked to prostate cancer getting worse in early stage disease, once men have advanced disease, it is not clear if race continues to show a bad result. The authors guessed that, in a setting with equal access among patients with prostate cancer that does not respond to hormone treatment and has no spread that we can see, black men would get medical pictures taken at similar rates as nonblack men, meaning there would be an equal chance to find spread, but would have a higher risk of spread. METHODS: In total, 837 men who were diagnosed with prostate cancer that does not respond to hormone treatment and has no spread from 2000 through 2014 from 5 Veterans Affairs hospitals in the SEARCH database were studied. Data on all medical pictures after the cancer diagnosis were gathered, including date, type, and result. Complex math models were used to test links between race and the time to first spread, first bone spread, first bone picture, second bone picture among men who had a negative first bone picture, and total survival. RESULTS: Black men were just as likely as nonblack men to receive a first and second bone picture after a diagnosis of prostate cancer. There were no big differences in the risk of developing any spread, bone spread, time to bone pictures, or total survival between black men and nonblack men. CONCLUSIONS: The lack of racial differences in the development of spread and testing practices seen in this study suggests that, once men have a diagnosis of this specific cancer, race may not be a way to predict the future. Efforts to understand prostate cancer racial gaps may gain more by focusing on the risk of developing prostate cancer and on the results of men who have early stage disease.
words_common.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star light measurements of Leo A in blue, green, and red light. Our new area of view is moved away from the middle part seen by Tolstoy et al. (1998) in order to show the outer group of stars of this galaxy. We report the finding of low-metal red level branch stars, which show that Leo A is not a young galaxy. In fact, Leo A is at least as old as low-metal Milky Way star groups which show red level branches, and are thought to have a minimum age of about 9 billion years. We talk about the distance to Leo A, and do a big comparison of the data with star age lines. For a distance measure of 24.5, the data are better than 50% complete down to real brightness levels of 2 or more. We can easily identify stars with metal amounts between 0.0001 and 0.0004, and ages between about 5 and 10 billion years, in their later life stages, but lack the finding of main-stage turnoffs which would provide clear proof of very old (over 10 billion years) star groups. Blue level branch stars are above the finding limits, but hard to tell apart from young stars with similar colors and brightness. Made-up color-brightness diagrams show it is possible to fill the blue level branch in the outer area of Leo A. The models also suggest about 50% of the total star mass in our area to be linked to an old (over 10 billion years) star group. We finish by saying that Leo A started to form stars at least about 9 billion years ago. Leo A shows an extremely low oxygen amount, of only 3% of the Sun, in its gas. The presence of old stars in this very oxygen-poor galaxy shows that a low oxygen amount does not stop a history of early star birth.
words_common.academic_abstracts::26: One goal of brain-like engineering is to create realistic robotic systems that interact with the physical world by adopting movement principles from biology. Critical to this is the way to build the spinal wiring responsible for the behavior of muscles that send back signals. At its core, muscle signaling is the circular behavior arising from the interactions among groups of muscle sensors, motor nerve cells, and muscle fibers to enable useful behaviors. We used programmable computer chip hardware to build simple models of firing nerve cells, skeletal muscles, muscle sensors, motor nerve cell activation, nerve cell control of sensor sensitivity, and the direct wiring connecting them. This multi-scale system of groups of firing nerve cells copied the natural properties of a pair of opposing signaled mammal muscles, each modeled by one thousand twenty-four motor nerve cells, acting on a joint via long tendons. This integrated system was able to maintain a joint angle, and reproduced stretch reflex responses even when driving the complex mechanics of an actual dead finger. Moreover, this system allowed us to explore numerous values and combinations of control settings when driving a robotic finger, some of which copied some human medical conditions. Lastly, we explored the behavioral results of adopting three alternative models of muscle force production. We found that the changing responses to signals can produce force that can be very sensitive to tendon stretchiness, especially at high force output. Our way of working produced, to our knowledge, the first example of an independent, multi-scale, brain-like, movement system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in dead fingers. This research platform allows us to explore the ways behind healthy and sick movement function in the physical world by building them from basic ideas, and it is a start to brain-like robotic systems.
words_common.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Goal: Patients arriving with a bladder infection and kidney or tube stones are a medical emergency who often become stable quickly but stay in the hospital while waiting for lab results on which medicines kill their germs. We wanted to find signs of medicine resistance in patients who had emergency surgery to drain their system for blood poisoning and blocked stones to help them go home sooner on common pills. Methods: Patients who had emergency surgery to drain their system for blood poisoning and a blocked stone from 2014 to 2018 at two university hospitals were found. Emergency tube placement was done and patients were treated with strong medicines given through a vein. We checked the link between health signs at the time of arrival and resistance to at least one medicine from urine tests using standard math tests for different types of information. A complex math model was then used using all important signs from the first test. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients (62.7%) had urine tests showing resistance to at least one medicine. In the first test, patients with resistant germs were much more likely to have had past stone surgery, need care in the high-level unit after surgery, have germs in their blood, and a longer stay in the hospital. In the complex model using important signs from the first test, only past stone surgery was strongly linked with medicine resistance with an increased chance of 6.95. Conclusions: In this study, we show that a history of stone surgery is strongly linked with medicine resistance in our tests. Our findings suggest that patients with a history of stone surgery should wait for test results, while those without a history of stone surgery may go home early on common pills. However, future studies are needed to check this idea.
words_common.academic_abstracts::28: Proof shows how marijuana can affect the use of other mind-altering things, including doctor ordered medicines, alcohol, tobacco and illegal drugs, but very little study has looked at the reasons linked to these changes in how people use substances. This paper looks at the reported use of marijuana as a replacement for alcohol among a Canadian medical marijuana patient group. Information was taken from a survey of 2102 people signed up in the Canadian medical marijuana program. We included 973 (44%) people who said they used alcohol at least 10 times over a 12 month time before starting medical marijuana, and then used past information on how often and how much alcohol was used before and after medical marijuana started to find which patient traits and other things were linked to cuts and/or stopping of alcohol use. Overall, 419 (44%) people said they had drops in how often they used alcohol over 30 days, 323 (34%) lowered the number of regular drinks they had per week, and 76 (8%) said they had no alcohol use at all in the 30 days before the survey. Being under 55 years of age and reporting higher amounts of alcohol use in the time before were both linked to better chances of cutting down alcohol use, and a plan to use medical marijuana to cut down alcohol use was linked to much better chances of both cutting down and stopping alcohol use entirely. Our findings show that starting medical marijuana may be linked to reported drops and stopping of alcohol use among medical marijuana patients. Since alcohol is the most common fun substance in North America, and its use leads to high rates of crime, sickness and death, these findings may lead to better health results for medical marijuana patients, as well as overall better public health and safety.
words_common.academic_abstracts::29: The fine balance between how atoms spin and move, the push of electric charges and the way atoms are arranged in these Ir-based oxides is often seen as strange magnetic behavior. Here we look at the change of the magnetic link between Co and Ir when we swap some La with Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$. A big plus of using Ca$^{2+}$ to take the place of La$^{3+}$ is that they are almost the same size. Thus, the seen magnetic changes can more easily be linked to changes in the electrons. A full look at the shape, electronic and magnetic traits of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was done by using very bright light to study powder, watching how tiny particles called muons spin and slow down, using steady and changing magnets, X-ray light, special light sensors, sound waves, how well electricity flows and how well it holds an electric field. Our X-ray results show that up to 25 percent of Ca swapping at the La spot results in the rise of Co$^{3+}$, maybe in a high spin state, while adding a larger amount of Ca leads to the rise of Ir charge. The fighting magnetic forces from the mixed charges lead to a mix of an ordered magnetic state and a new messy magnetic state for the samples. Our muon results show that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$ a nearly steady part of a non-magnetic phase stays even at low heat, maybe linked to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ and to the wrong spots at Co/Ir sites. For the mixed items the non-magnetic phase stops moving below 30 K, but there is still some motion linked to the messy state. The electric data for the parent item and the one with 25 percent Ca show a possible magnetic-electric effect, which is talked about using the jumping of electrons between the metal ions, the wrong spots and the bent shape.
words_common.academic_abstracts::30: With the strict rules brought by the new sixth-generation internet-of-things use cases, old ways of managing how many devices connect at once have started to show their limits. A new group of ways that do not need permission have therefore been suggested as a good choice. However, a final answer is still to be reached. In our work, we suggest a new partly-free organized random access plan, called partial-information multiple access, to cut down on lost data and delays, mainly when devices turn on and off at random times. We look at a machine-type communications situation, where devices need to send data packets up to a base station. When using this plan, the base station can get some information on the current traffic levels and, by using ways to do math over the air, guess the number of devices with packets waiting to be sent in their line. Based on this, the base station gives each device a single space for sending. However, since each space may still be given to many users, crashes may happen. Both the total number of set spaces and the user assignments are made better, based on the guessed number of active users, to cut down on crashes and help the efficiency of the connection plan. To prove the truth of our answer, we compare our plan to time-division multiple-access and slotted ALOHA plans, the best answers for standard multiple access in the time area for low and high traffic situations. We show that our plan can not only change to fit different traffic levels and provide fewer lost packets no matter how many packets are made, but also combine the good points of both older plans, thus giving better results for lost data and delays.
words_common.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose – Bone changing as a response to bone injury, staying still after surgery, and reactions to metal parts can lead to loss of bone and increase the risk of breaking near the new joint and parts coming loose. This study looks at the changing bone at the top of the shin bone after a knee replacement without glue. Patients and methods – We did a 2 year check up of 53 patients, average age 62, 27 of whom were men, who received a knee replacement without glue in a fair test with bone strength as a secondary goal. Patients were split into 2 groups of either single piece or built up plastic design. The knee replacements were done using the Zimmer Nexgen metal that looks like a sponge. Measurements of bone strength were done after surgery and after 3, 6, 12, and 24 months. Bone strength was measured in 3 areas of interest. Results and interpretation – In group A clear changes in bone strength were seen after 24 months in both the inner and outer areas. Bone strength went down on the inner side by 15 percent and on the outer side by 13 percent. In group B the bone strength changes were small and after 24 months went back to the levels from before surgery. The differences in bone strength change between groups were clear in both the inner and outer areas. In the lower area we found no real change in bone strength in either group. A clearly different bone changing pattern of the top of the shin bone was seen in the 2 groups with more bone loss in the knees that got the single piece plastic design, showing that the bendy single piece design does not stop bone loss.
words_common.academic_abstracts::32: Computer brain models are inspired by how real brains work and have proven very useful. Still, these models lack a natural idea of time, and parts in these models trade continuous values in a set way, a slow and power-hungry form of talking. This is very different from real brain cells that talk rarely and well using simple on-off signals. While artificial spiking brain models can be made by replacing the parts of a standard model with spiking cells, the current success is far from that of deep models on hard tests and these spiking models use much higher signal rates compared to their real counterparts, limiting their power. Here we show how spiking cells that use an efficient form of brain code can be used to build spiking models that match high-performance computer models and beat the best in spiking models on important tests, while needing much lower average signal rates. For this, we use signal-time code based on the signal rate limiting change seen in real spiking brain cells. This change can be caught in changing spiking cell models, for which we find the working math rule. Parts in models trained with this rule can be swapped directly with changing spiking cells, and the resulting changing spiking models can carry out logic in deep models using up to ten times fewer signals compared to older spiking models. Changing signal-time code also allows for the active control of code detail: we show how a simple model of focus in these models further cuts the average needed signal rate in half and this idea naturally moves to other forms of attention. These models thus hold hope as a new and efficient model for brain math that fits well to ongoing and random tasks.
words_common.academic_abstracts::33: Background. LQ Hya is one of the most frequently studied young stars like our sun. Recently, it has been seen to show interesting behavior by looking at long-term brightness measurements: from 2003 to 2009, a steady spot pattern moving in the spinning frame has been reported by various writers, but since that time the star has entered a messy state where steady patterns seem to have gone away and fast changes of the brightness low points happen unevenly over time. Goals. LQ Hya is one of the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term tracking project lasting over 25 years. Here we publish new temperature maps for the star during 2006 to 2017, covering the messy state of the star. Methods. We use a mapping method to find surface temperature maps from high-quality light data. Results. From the average temperatures of the maps we see a weak but steady rise in the surface temperature of the star. This matches the at the same time increasing brightness levels. During nearly all watching times we see a high-area spot pattern which is clearly not balanced around the middle. The timing behavior of this pattern is very messy but matches fairly well with the brightness. Spots near the middle are also often seen, but many of them we think are errors due to the poor to fair timing coverage. Conclusions. Even during the messy phase of the star, the spot layout has stayed very similar to the higher activity times with more steady and long-lasting spot patterns: we see high-area and middle spot activity, the center area still being most often empty of spots. We think the random jumps and drifts in timing of the brightness low points are caused by changes in the high-area spot pattern rather than the middle spots.
words_common.academic_abstracts::34: Context: Adding hydrogen is expected to be among the most important surface reactions on space ices. However, solid state space chemistry laboratory data on reactions of hydrogen atoms with common space ice parts are largely missing. Aims: The goal of our laboratory work is to find out whether and how carbon dioxide (CO2), formic acid (HCOOH) and acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) react with hydrogen atoms in the solid state at cold temperatures and to find reaction speeds and production amounts. Methods: Pure CO2, HCOOH and CH3CHO space ice copies are hit by hydrogen atoms in a very high vacuum test. The ices are watched by looking at light reflection and the reaction products are found in the gas state through heating to find the destruction and formation amounts as well as the matching reaction speeds. Results: Within the power of our set-up we conclude that hydrogen atom hitting of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice does not result in findable reaction products. The top limits on the reaction speeds are less or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s which make it unlikely that these things play a big role in the formation of more complex organic items in space ices due to reactions with hydrogen atoms. In contrast, CH3CHO does react with hydrogen atoms. At most 20% is turned into ethanol (C2H5OH) and a second reaction path leads to the break-up of the carbon-carbon bond to form solid state CH4 (~20%) as well as H2CO and CH3OH (15-50%). The methane production amount is expected to be equal to the added amount of H2CO and CH3OH and therefore CH4 most likely turns into gas partly after formation due to the high heat release of the reaction. The reaction speeds for CH3CHO destruction depend on ice temperature and not on ice thickness.
words_common.academic_abstracts::35: The way of funnel control was started in the early 2000s, and it has grown since then in many ways reaching a level of math skills balanced by real world uses. Its basic idea is the reaching of set short term and long term habits for continuous time controlled moving processes including straight and not straight systems shown by functional differential equations, differential algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Thought about are groups of systems picked by basic traits - such as relative degree and stable inner habits - of the systems only, the exact systems' facts are in general unknown; the second part shows the fact that in general any model of a moving process is not exact. Picked ahead of time are: a funnel shaped through the choice of a smooth function and freely picked by the designer, a fairly large group of smooth reference signals, and a system group meeting certain basic traits. The goal is to design, based on the basic assumptions and the input and output information only, a single simple control plan -- called the funnel controller -- so that its use to any system of the given group and to any reference signal ends in success of the funnel control goal: that is solutions of the closed loop system do not show blow up in limited time, all variables are kept in check, and -- most importantly -- the change of the error between the system's output and the reference signal stays within the set funnel. In the Introduction, we describe the start of funnel control. After that, we look at diverse system groups open to funnel control. Funnel control is shown for systems with any relative degree and systems shown by partial differential equations. Finally, we talk about input limits and uses.
words_common.academic_abstracts::36: With the increasing variety of online service blocking attacks, it is becoming extremely hard to design a fully protected network. For instance, a hidden link flooding attack is a type of service blocking attack that tries to block access to a target area by filling up a small set of paths, and it is shown that it can get past normal defense tools. One possible solution to handle such hidden attacks is to apply changing target defense methods in which network settings are constantly moved to confuse or trick attackers, thus making it very costly to start a successful attack. However, since this defense comes with some extra work for the network, finding the best plan of when or how much to use it has been a major problem. The plan is greatly shaped by the way the attacker acts, which is often hard to guess. In this work, we deal with the problem of getting the best defense plan that effectively stops these hidden attacks while needing the smallest amount of extra work. We set up the problem as a signaling game thinking of the network defender and the attacker as players. A belief system is made throughout the time of the attacker and the defender during this attack, which is used to pick the best move for each player. We study the game model and find a defense way based on the balance of the game. We test the method on a computer network where an attacker is doing these hidden attacks and a defender uses the new defense based on the game balance. The results show that our signaling game defense can provide a similar level of protection against these attacks like the large defense solution, however, causing much less extra work.
words_common.academic_abstracts::37: Methods using many levels of detail are becoming more common for improving simple models and design choices by adding data from various low detail models. While most current methods of this type assume a set amount of data, smart sampling ways that change how resources are shared among detail levels can reach better speed when searching and using the design space. However, most current methods rely on the idea of ranked levels of detail or fail to catch the connection between many detail levels and use it to measure the value of future samples and guide the smart sampling. To fix this problem, we suggest a structure based on a hidden connection for different detail models and the related analysis of likely results to clearly use their connection for smart sampling. In this structure, each new sampling step includes two parts: We first find the place of interest with the greatest possible improvement using the high detail model, then we search for the next sample across all detail levels that make the most improvement for each unit of cost at the place found in the first step. This is made possible by a single hidden variable process model that maps different detail models into a clear space to catch their connections without assuming ranked levels of detail. The model lets us judge how low detail sampling choices will change the high detail result with analysis of likely results and find the next sample with the best benefit to cost ratio. Through test cases, we show that our method beats the standard ways in both global fitting and search problems in speed and steadiness. Moreover, the method offers the freedom to switch between tasks by simply changing the math rule.
