Washington D.C., USA
 
 Day 0, 00:20
 
 ~
 
 "… there was a blast right when I looked up…"
 
 "… biggest death count in this country since…"
 
 "… never seen before…"
 
 Sirens wail from the TV. I sit on the floor. Dazed.
 
 What had just happened?
 
 The words "BREAKING NEWS" splash across the screen. Every pair of eyes in the country – no, the world – must be stuck to their TVs. Clouds of smoke continue to rise from the side of the towers. People who saw it cry and scream about the awful mess they had seen.
 
 "Mommy," Emma stumbles into the living room. "It's time for school, Mommy."
 
 "Oh honey," I say, on the edge of tears. "Come here." She walks to me and I hold her in my arms tightly, running my hands through her hair. "We won't be going to school today, dear."
 
 News continues to pour in from the TV.
 
 In the corner of the screen: Monday, 11 September 2001.
 
 
 \________
 
 Shanghai, China
 
 Day 0, 01:00
 
 ~
 
 "Dr. Wu, you have to look at this."
 
 "Not now, Lin. There are enough people losing their minds about this! We need to focus on our work," I take off my thin, metal glasses and look at my helper. She has helped me so much in the past seven years. We are so close now. We cannot afford to be distracted. "If we do not meet the time limit, all our efforts would have gone to waste."
 
 Lin shakes her head. "No, doctor. I am not talking about the attack. I… I…"
 
 "What is it, then? Speak up."
 
 "You… you should see this for yourself." Lin takes out a huge sheet of paper and lays it out on my table.
 
 "This is the ocean heat chart today – why did you print it out? These changes are perfectly normal, and the –" Something at the end of the chart catches my eyes. A huge jump. "This… this…"
 
 "Yes, doctor. You were right all along."
 
 My heart skips a beat. I check the time of the jump. It matches perfectly.
 
 "Lin,"
 
 "Yes, doctor?"
 
 "Get me the boss of the Chinese weather office. Now!"
words_common.writingprompts::1:
This is the end, isn't it?

The thought hit Josh suddenly, almost by accident. It went through and melted his annoyance with the car that had let him break down so far from home; with the phone company that had failed to build towers by this empty desert road; with the sun that had boldly beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground.

This is the end.

This thought in particular stayed clear in his mind, even as he knew that he had already seen Heather for the last time. And... and Joey, who was still so proud about that math test. And Dale, and the business Dale would get, the business that would act as an unexpected gift.

This is it.

Dale, who had told him that this trip was a silly waste of time, and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral; this memory, too, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head.

The end of...

The thought stayed there, still, for a time that Josh wasn't able to understand. Everything else in his mind seemed to go away, from his edges, inward toward this single, lonely idea.

This is the end of me.

When nothing else was left, Josh found it right that this idea of being finished should itself be his final thought.

But it wasn't.

It went away as quickly as it came, and then --

Josh would have cried, if he was still able to move.

His regrets came rushing back all at once. And his anger, and his sadness and his hopelessness at his own lack of power. The calm peace of the end was over, replaced with the worry of a life not finished. A life that had failed to make peace with itself.

And then Josh felt fear. Fear like he had never felt before. The terror of what was coming, of the great unknown for which he was totally not ready. The sheer and total shock crushed his memory, and his pain, and all his other feelings.

That fear was the last thing Josh thought about.
words_common.writingprompts::2:
People will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. People will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. People will not be allowed..." the Moral Officer shouted into his loud speaker. I found it helpful. The end being so near gave me the strength to push my weak and tired body to shovel faster, faster.

All around me my fellow people dug in the dust like brittle dry dirt, scratching out the place where they would give their bodies back to the earth. In the distance other Moral Officers made their announcements into identical loud speakers. At regular times throughout the field helper Officers stood, in clean uniforms, waiting patiently to help us in our final job to the Nation.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State announced it. Everyone had whispered about how the weekly food that they picked up from the food center seemed to be smaller every week, though the center's Party workers would say no if anyone asked. Then the whispers turned to fully loud complaints when items began disappearing from the food, never to appear again. Soon meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy looking, vegetables were hard to find.

When the State News Agency, in a special show, finally announced the lack of food, nobody was surprised. We were told that we must, as always, stand together, strong and proud in the face of this hard test. Everyone must do their part to carry this heavy load and our perfect society would clear this jump and come out winning. Even the Beloved Ruler was limiting his food, we were told. It was clear, yes surely clear, that this was some trick by the people against us and the outsiders, trying to destroy our spirit, to make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had ruined our fields and killed our animals. But we would stay strong in our goodness and would come out, as ever, winning.

It was then that they announced the random drawing. That a number of people would be picked from the population to give a great sacrifice of faith and goodness for the Nation, to help make the need for food smaller. Those who were picked were told the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families. I was one of the chosen.

A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body help the soil to feed our great Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler." A gunshot ended this statement. Someone had already finished their grave. A few others cheered their agreement, most were too tired and hungry to manage. The helper Officer put away his gun and motioned for the now dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now used.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, digging out a road. We slept where we worked and the only food given to us was a soup so thin that they could hardly say it was more than hot water. And so the last of the strength of our bodies was used up.

My grave now looked deep enough. I waited before raising up my shovel to call over the helper Officer. If it was not deep enough for him I would have to wait until all others had finished, covering over their graves, before it would be my turn.

He came over and produced a tool to measure. He checked the size and nodded his agreement. I let out a quiet sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my great sacrifice for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final job to my beloved land.

"People will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave." The Moral Officer said into his loud speaker.

I felt the cool metal of the helper Officer gun come to rest upon my head.

"People will not be allowed..."
words_common.writingprompts::3: I let out the sharp smoke over those hard ground slabs. I put the drink away neatly, feeling for the metal. I check my watch. I check my watch. Once. Twice. Three times before I actually understand that it is four in the morning. She is going to hate me for leaving. My mind beats on this thought while I walk across this empty area of rocks, soft metal, and paper. I have a goal, a job, a reason. Nothing can stop this walk of making things right. She will be hurt, lose all hope in me. I never got her trust in my goodness anyway. Shake your head, pull on this drink, touch the metal and get back on track. I should see the boy first. No, that is crazy then she will stop me, just keep going. I look up, I am here I see the Cross of the dead King glowing. This is it. This starting point. I lost myself here. I lost names, dates, events, really everything. The clear and metal doors fly open like magic at my approach, the guard of this awful place greets me from behind stone and glass. I look at her without much thought but to my task. I can hear the one I left in my head warning me, guiding me home, telling me I am needed elsewhere. Shake it off. Cold sweats and shaking. I fall into a door with the sign of a man on it. White floors. Mirrors. Fake walls. Sink parts. Door locked. Time to pull the drink one more time. Block her out. Breathe. Adjust the metal. I walk out. I am almost there. The people behind the fake desk know me. I see worry. It is too late I am here. The bad man in white is close. I smell him. My control is slipping. Vision shaking. Sound turned down. Time to grab the metal. There he is. I aim this mean tool. As I begin to release the fire from this bad machine, I hear her. "Don't" she says quietly. "Don't make it right." I fall apart. Her voice so clear hit me like the hand of God. The nurses are screaming. The doctor. The doctor who took her from me is clearly scared. However he looks at me, the broken person with his pipe and cheap gun, and says "I tried to save her, I did all I could. You should be with your son, not here, not doing this." Here comes the names, dates, events, everything. He then says "It is only been six days." Tired eyed, confused at the sirens sound, the broken glass, and men running to me in all black, I reply "No. A lifetime."
words_common.writingprompts::5:
Happy endings do not exist for people like us, I said seriously. Clarissa looked up at me through her tears. 
Why not? She asked softly. 
I gently wiped her tears away with the tip of my thumb and smiled in a sad way. 
Because, the world will not let us. Every time we try to be happy someone always knocks us down. Something always will. 
What if we run away? She asked finally looking at me. 
I swallowed, trying to hold back tears of my own. 
If we run away then we will always be running. I do not want that for us. I do not want that for you, I whispered. 
Clarissa held back a cry. 
Will, please do not do this. 
A tear ran down my face. 
I do not want to. 
Then why are you? 
Because I am no good for you Clarissa. I get into fights. I get picked up by the police. You can find someone better who can make you so much happier. Who can give you what you want. 
The words left a bad taste in my mouth but it had to be said. If we stayed together then there would always be someone trying to break us apart. 
Her parents. 
My friends. 
My enemies. 
I gave her one last kiss. 
Maybe one day in the future, when things are not hard, we will find each other again. Right now is not our time. Maybe tomorrow will be.
words_common.writingprompts::6:
Daniel's wife stood at his side, absolutely coming apart at the edges, not that anyone else but him would be able to tell. Okay maybe that was a bit of an exaggeration, but she was a touch worried. Nervous? Whatever she was something wasn't quite right, she was doing that little nose twitch that never happens when she's calm.

"Imani," he called out and her head tipped down to where he was seated in acknowledgement "It's going to be fine." She gave him a weak smile that didn't quite reach her eyes before reaching out to squeeze his hand. Of course he said it to comfort her, but he honestly felt like everything was going to be okay. They already crossed the worst bits. He survived the car accident, then he survived the operation to make sure the world didn't decide to change its mind later, then later the cutting off of his legs, the parts they put inside him. With a roll of his eyes he squeezed her hand back. "Honestly, this has been the easy part, we have plenty of time."

"The easy part? Since when do we ever get easy!" she reached out to hit his ears, her eyes crinkling with happiness "That's up there with 'What could possibly go wrong?' Don't bring bad luck." she scolded. He leaned in to tell her all that worrying could do nothing good when the door slammed open, the loud bang echoing through the large room.

"Oops," the tall man in the doorway looked shy "I tripped into the door there. How are you two today?" he asked friendly, walking into room and the sunlight from the windows poured over his long form. "Ready to give it another go?" Daniel moved his legs, neat and held tight into his new running gear.

"Since the second I put these on Mason!" he replied honestly and the easy going man gave him a thumbs up before reaching out his hands.

"That's what we like to hear! Alright lets get you up and moving then." With one last look as his wife, who was standing back with a worried look but held up crossed fingers, he reached for the other man's hands. These were the fourth pair of running gear he had tried. The other ones had problems, despite their so called made to fit shapes. Too long. Too short. These hurt. Those felt like they were going to fall off. But as Daniel wobbled to his feet he knew these were it. It took a moment to steady himself. They had a different sort of balance and movement to them than his normal fake leg, and his fitness wasn't quite where he wanted it be. His heart raced as he shifted his weight from one foot to the other, hearing the gear move in response. Left. Right. Left. Right. Left right, left right, left right, bounce. They felt nothing like his old legs. But all the same... they felt right. Slowly Mason let go and then backed away to the other side of the room, his eyes never leaving Daniel's. When he hit the wall he called out to them.

"Great! Now start at a walk and work up to as fast as you feel comfortable doing." a joking tone crept into his voice "And remember, the room is soft and we're all friends here. Falling down is nothing to worry about." Daniel laughed at the comment. As if he'd let these things get the better of him. Confident, he took a shaky step forward and his arms moved around a bit before he held his middle tight to maintain balance. Then he took another. And another, and soon he had a slow bobbing jog going, carefully moving between his wife and physical trainer. He did this until finally, Mason signaled for him to stop. He ran down the room to the happy couple with a look of great excitement.

"It looks like we got it this time!" He stepped back and gave him one final look over "We just need to run a few more tests, make sure that everything is set correctly, but I think we found your perfect pair here. So, how do you feel?"

His mind began to wander as he turned inward, trying to find the words that could even begin to describe what he was feeling. All he could think about were the things he thought he had lost forever when he slowly woke up from surgery that important day, looking down to see the sheet dip in where his lower legs had once been. The sound of the crowd screaming his name as he ran down the field. The big feeling of running fast down a track, the world getting small almost into darkness as he pushed himself to the limit. The lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped by him with laughter dancing in her eyes. Bouncing on his new legs once more he felt light. Unstoppable. With a strength he hadn't felt in a long time he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with a smile.

"Alive."

-- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -- -

So let it be known I did absolutely no research on the subject for such a quiet piece and just went off of memory and guess work. So if anything is terribly wrong, that is why! I hope this story really shows how he feels after his hard time. It is a good day for him.
words_common.writingprompts::9:
Yes, I remember it like yesterday. I was walking through the western mountains, just east of Markarth. The road twisted below me, making a long path through the valley. A person dressed in animal skins caught my eye, creeping slowly towards a carriage that had stopped before crossing the river. They pulled out a mean-looking sword as they got closer, clearly planning on killing the small group of travelers. I got on my horse and started down the hill, shouting as loud as I could to get their attention.

The would-be robber immediately looked at me with a frown and let out a shout of his own. Right away, a dozen more men and women, dressed in the same torn fashion, were running toward the carriage with weapons held out. I knew there were too many for me to handle, but I could not stand the thought of letting those poor people die to these mean people. As I reached the bottom of the hill, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, he is a bit of a crazy one, had given me a magic paper before I started on my trip. Let me say now that I am no magic user. Sure, I tried to find some magic that would make me more handsome, but none of that worked anyway. I was pretty sure that I just had to open the paper and read it, but I had no idea what it actually did. Hopefully it would call one of those big stone monsters my friend was always talking about. He made them out to be something near god-like. I would not mind having one of those on my side.

Anyway, once I got to the bottom, I jumped off my horse and pulled the paper from my bag. I was shaking so badly, I almost could not read it, but I knew I had done it correctly when I started glowing. That should have been a good sign that something bad was about to happen, but I knew nothing about magic. Still do not. The glow was nice though, warm and comforting. Suddenly, all the robbers were putting their weapons away and asking me what was happening to them. I had no idea, but I figured they could not do any more harm. Unfortunately, they were a little too impressed by me. They must have thought I was some sort of great wizard because they immediately lifted me on their shoulders and carried me back to their camp for a big meal. I started out thinking they were people who eat other people or something when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and realized they were really just trying to get by in the world. Their drink was wonderful, let me tell you. A little too wonderful, I guess, because I woke the next morning with an, admittedly, pretty woman next to me and a camp full of these people congratulating me with gifts and hugs.

So, you see, I envy you. I miss the open fields and cold mountains, the gold and treasure, and the freedom to go wherever I please. I used to be young and happy, I used to be strong and brave. You remind me a lot of myself, honestly. I used to be an adventurer like you, until I took an arrow to the knee.
words_common.writingprompts::12:
You want to send in Nikon? You really think it is that bad? The man speaking was large and had a wide chest, well over six feet tall, with a long, neatly trimmed beard and a perfect suit. He was talking to a woman who had to have been in her sixties, the beauty she showed as a youth now a well-aged glow. Her sharp blue eyes looked at the large man without blinking, staring right through him.

You have a problem, Lord Aerlman. A very specific type of problem. We can deal with this very specific problem, but it will require the help of a pro. Alex Nikon is that pro. Her tone was plain, not excited or loud in any way.

She is just a girl, a misguided girl. The older woman shrugged.

Your girl, Lord Aerlman, has contacted the places outside our world. She has let something through, and now it is inside her. However, until she does something in public, I cannot involve the group without your request. If you do not want our help, that is fine. Just remember, sadness strikes first at the home. Her warning given, the woman turned and started to leave the fancy sitting room. As she reached the door, Lord Aerlman called to her.

Laura! Ms. Cadswall. Wait. Please. She smiled to herself and then fixed her face, turning with a calm look.

Yes? The lord was wringing his hands, walking back and forth in front of the fire.

Your man, Nikon, I know his name. Will he... kill her? Lord Aerlman looked very sad.

Alexander Nikon will handle the crisis. That is what he does. How he handles it will stay up to him. Be told though, Lord Aerlman, that contact with the places outside our world leaves a mark on the very soul. Even death cannot remove its stain.

Lord Aerlman looked very upset, and he slowly picked up a picture off the top of the fireplace, a family portrait showing the lord and his wife, along with their daughter, a pretty redhead in her late teens. He rubbed the picture with his thumb, before setting it back down. All of the energy drained from him and he slumped, turning towards the woman with a beaten look.

Fine. Do it. Make the call. He dismissed her with a wave and then sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a large whiskey, which he quickly drank. As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly. She had a phone call to make.

Antonia. I know you are here. The same girl from the photo, now a fully grown, and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of wooden boxes, desperately holding herself and trying not to scream. Her hands and body were covered in blood, some hers, and some her friends. They had been partying, drinking in her London apartment, when the man arrived.

The first sign of trouble was the door breaking inward, a large piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear. He dropped with a choking sound and blood sprayed across the room. Screams came from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even understand the danger, a small man, barely five foot six, was in their middle, a large curved sword in one hand and a gun in the other. Glowing marks twisted across his skin, and his left eye was covered by a patch. His right eye was the color of shiny metal, and it quickly looked around the room. Everything after that was a blur, and Antonia could not remember any details, except the bodies, and the blood.

She remembered a voice in her head, then her friends all screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-carrying man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard. As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and jumped through the big window, falling the three floors and landing with a bad crunch. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then running. The voice in her head was louder, and she could not understand it, but it was hurting her.

As she ran through the streets, the voice was singing, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes shooting fire before they turned and ran the way she had come. She did not understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was after her. She did not understand anything! Next thing she knew, she was hiding in the storage building, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood. As she curled up and tried not to let him find her, he kept talking.
words_common.writingprompts::13:
Lamb, tell me a story… said the Wolf, with a proud voice and a smile on his face. ….Something sweet. 

The Lamb shook with fear. He had heard stories of the wolf all through his childhood, but never thought that there was any truth to them. 

W-what would you like to hear? The Lamb finally asked. 

You can decide that. The Wolf replied with a bossy voice. 

The two of them were in a quiet area of the same field that the Lamb had been born and lived on, and he was currently pressed in to the corner with a hurt leg, while the Wolf walked a half circle around him, a mere two feet away. The Farmer was nowhere to be seen, and none of the other Lambs would dare try to save him, unless they felt like giving up their own lives. 

He did not have a story to tell. He had lived a short, dull life and with the thought that his family was not coming to save him, he knew it was coming to an end. He felt a strange wave of calm rush over him as he accepted his future at the mouth of the Wolf. 

If I had a story, it would be this one. But we have already reached the end. He said. 

I always liked the bloody ones. The Wolf replied as he closed the gap between them.
words_common.writingprompts::14:
It was a very bad time to fall in love. A very bad choice to make. She had the prettiest eyes he had ever seen. He stood there pulling in his stomach while she waited for the poison.

She had killed ten men and was about to be put to death by a deadly shot. He was just helping out because one of the guards had gotten sick. He did not even work there. But he knew he was completely in love with her. She was not a killer to him. She was a beautiful angel. They looked at each other sharing shy smiles.

Do you have any final words? asked the priest.

What is his name?

Who? asked the priest.

That guard there, she pointed with her head.

Me? Um, officer Jones, he said with excitement.

Hi, I am Rebecca.

The choice was made after that. Officer Jones waited until about five minutes before midnight. He tried to argue with himself about the results but in the end he knew results did not matter. It was true love at first sight.

He pulled his gun and shot everybody in the room except Rebecca. Shakes moved his arm. He dropped his gun and ran to her. It was a very good first kiss.
words_common.writingprompts::15:
Janice turned to me, her big blue eyes still full of young goodness. Oh no - I had forgotten that she was watching the Presidential Inauguration for a school project. Daddy, she began, what does the President mean? What is gay? 

Well, honey, I began, but stopped as I tried to think of a way to explain it to a five year old. Uh, well, you know how Mommy and Daddy like to hold hands, and to hug, and kiss, and stuff? 

Yeah! It is funny when Mommy pinches your bottom when you are not looking, and makes you make a noise! she laughed. Kids, man, I had forgotten what it was like to be so amused by the word bottom. Had I ever been that small, that simple? 

I waited for her laughs to stop before I went on. Well, sweetheart, gay means that he, the President, he likes to do that stuff with a boy, not a girl like Mommy. 

I could see the confusion in her eyes as she tried to think about this new news. Oh no, McCain, for making me explain this to her! She is not old enough for this; she is not ready! I am not ready! 
Janice opened her mouth to speak. I knew what was coming; I had opened the door to a lifetime of bad behavior. My sweet little girl was gone forever. 

Suddenly I realized she said something, and in my worry, I had completely missed it. Sorry, sweetheart, what did you say? I asked, fearing her answer. What new trouble have I started? 

I said, I am hungry. Can I have a cookie? Please, Daddy? 

I was shocked, unable to speak at first. 
Uhm. Sure, I answered. Get one for your brother, too. 

Huh. I guess that maybe what two grown people do in private is not that big of a deal after all. 
Even when they are famous people.
words_common.writingprompts::16:
Why, hello, Ma'am, I said easily, standing up and offering her a chair with my usual polite way. Bertram Proudfoot at your service. Who do I have the pleasure of talking to?

I would rather not say, if it is all the same to you, she said, sitting down.

Alright, I said comfortably. What can the Hobbiton Detective and Gossip Agency do for you?

Well, said the woman, rubbing her hands together nervously. It is like this. She paused.

Like what, Ma'am? I said kindly, lighting my pipe and sitting back in my chair.

My husband is dead, she said.

Oh my dear, I am sorry! I said, though I must admit there was part of me that was less than sorry. What can I say? I am only a Hobbit, and this woman had the most beautiful feet I had ever seen. Tell me everything that happened.

We were out boating on the Brandywine three nights ago, she said. And all of a sudden, a rock flew out of nowhere and hit my poor husband in the head. He fell over in the water. I screamed for help, but he drowned.

Now of course I had already known it must have been something like this from the moment she walked in the door. I have a strange sense for things like that.

I looked as serious as I could, given the situation. I see, I said, blowing another perfect smoke ring up towards the ceiling. And you would like me to find and take to court the person who did this.

Yes, said the woman.

I will do my best, I can promise you that, I said, and I saw her clearly breathe with relief. May I offer you a cup of tea? Something stronger, perhaps?

No thank you, she said, and without another word she showed herself out.

I quickly made my way to the Brandywine River dock. My first plan of action would be to talk to the man who rented out boats. A strange fellow, and a strange job -- not many normal hobbits choose to be out in the middle of the water by their own free will. And indeed, this hobbit's boat-renting business was not doing well.

After a long look at his records he told me that he had rented out two boats on the evening in question, and only one of those was by a couple. The couple had been a one Drogo Baggins and a one Primula Brandybuck. Primula, that was the woman's name. But why had she not wanted to tell it to me?

Had this boat fellow heard any noise on the water, any cries for help? No he had not. Did he remember who brought the boat back to him? It had not come back, he said. In fact, that particular boat had been left floating in the middle of the river. Strange.

Next I walked up and down the both banks of the river. Not much to get here, except that whoever had thrown the rock must have been quite good at throwing things.

Having carefully looked over the river, my next step was to find out about Primula and Drogo. After visiting several pubs in the areas of Buckland and Hobbiton, I had gathered this: Primula and Drogo were long married, though perhaps not happily. They had one son, now twelve, named Frodo Baggins. Strangely, it seemed that Primula had not been seen by anyone except me since Drogo's death. In fact, most of the people that I spoke with seemed to be of the belief that both Drogo and Primula had died three nights ago.

Facts were not adding up. Before I could do anything else, I had to speak with my mysterious client again so as to make things clear. Though I had no way of contacting her, I knew she would return to my offices soon.

The day following, she did just that.

Good day, Primula, I said upon her entrance.

Her face showed surprise, but she did not deny the name.

I have a few things I need to get straight with you about the case, I said, and went on to explain what I had found. So I am afraid I must ask again, I finished. What happened that night?

And without a word, the woman got up and left. Just like that.

I did not hear from her again, and two days later, her body was found floating down the Brandywine. I was sad but not surprised.

My thought had been this: having been unhappily married for some time, Primula had pushed her husband into the water herself and boated back to the shore with the plan of disappearing forever. Everyone would think that they both were dead, and so would not suspect any bad play. However, after listening to the lawyer's meetings that quickly followed, she realized that care of her son would go to a far-off cousin, none other than the famous crazy Bilbo Baggins.

Understandably, Primula did not want her son to fall under the control of said crazy person, and so she came to me in the hopes that I would believe her story and move suspicion away from herself, all in a desperate attempt to keep her son. But I, having seen through her trick, stopped this. Seeing no other way she then drowned herself in sadness. Shame -- I had just begun to think there may have been a very good result for the both of us.

I sat back and began polishing my pipe thoughtfully. It was another case finished by the great Bertram Proudfoot, but perhaps another chance lost. I had finished many cases, but chances of the other sort came only now and then. Like I said, it was a shame.

I blew another smoke ring to the ceiling as my thoughts turned to crazy old Mr. Baggins. I felt for the young Mr. Frodo, who was now unlucky enough to fall into the old hobbit's care. Who knows what old Baggins would pass on to the young fellow. As I am sure you all know, Mr. Bilbo Baggins suddenly disappeared many years ago and then returned just as suddenly a year later with lots of gold and many tall stories. Having been a very normal hobbit before he left, whatever he saw on his trip seemed to have made his mind weak. He came back a changed hobbit, and not for the better.

He was so changed, in fact, that it is my personal thought that the hobbit currently living at Bag End is not the real Bilbo Baggins at all, but rather a fake. There is plenty of proof to suggest this: especially the fact that Mr. Baggins looks much younger than a hobbit of his years has any right to look.

I shall have to look into that matter further some day.
words_common.writingprompts::17:
Lucifer stood in a big hall outside of space or time. It never changed, the dark stone walls cutting into curved hallways to who knows where. Inside this huge room he and God would argue every several thousand years. God came out from the shadows of one of several doors, a mean look on his face.

Oh, it is you, he said. Lucifer looked at him calmly.

Did I ever give you a sex drive, Lucy? I cannot remember.

No, Lucifer answered.

Aw, why not? Feel like having sex? I am kind of excited.

Jesus Christ, Lucifer hissed.

Hey! Do not mention my son to me right now! That is messed up! God said.

Lucifer pressed his eyes shut. I came here to talk to you about something, he said.

What do you want, Lucy?

I do not want to run hell anymore.

Aw, why not?

I did not do anything wrong! I showed your dear humans sin and gave them the ability to think for themselves! Freedom! You would have kept them as simple dolls! I helped you make one of your greatest creations! I did it because I knew you needed it! I did it out of love for you!

So please, Lucifer said, falling onto one of the steady stone chairs, Let me come back to you. Let me serve you like I had before.

Only if you kiss me, Lucy, God said in a thick voice. Lucifer made a face.

Aww, do not be like that, Luce, you know why you have to be king of the worst place ever. You created the split, you have to help me look after one of its two places and I am definitely not going down there, how messed up would that be?

You created the split. You created everything.

Ssssshhhh... here, have some soda.

I do not - I do not want any soda. That is - oh goodness! You spilled it all over me!

God laughed, Do not say my name in a bad way, Luce.

Lucifer pulled his eyebrows together, God knew he was holding back tears, I do not understand you.

Of course you do not! I am outside space and time! I exist in places you have no idea about! I am all things at once! How could you possibly understand me? God shouted.

I... do not know. I thought, being your creation, I am part of you, and you are part of me.

God laughed, A part of me, Luce. You can never understand my whole self. You would fall apart within a second. All things made in this straight line of time would become a screaming mess of body parts.

A pause. Lucifer stared at his hands.

Why did you create us then?

To forget, and then remember.

I do not understand.

I know, he said softly.
words_common.writingprompts::18:
Hey buddy, this is my own land.

He was a strange brown color, and his ears were a little too big. "Heh. I would be nicer to me, if I were you" he said.

"Look, I do not want any trouble" I said in a calm way. "Just leave this place, and nothing bad will happen to you."

"Nope." The little jerk was smiling in a mean way. I started to get angry and took a step toward him.

"Alright kid, let us fight."

I quickly called for help. He did the same. I jumped toward him, and he immediately started running away.

"Come back here you little jerk!" I gave chase. I could hear my friends coming out, ready to stop him. We had him trapped... until...

Something loud hurt my ears, and I felt a sharp pain in my legs. Out of the side of my eye, I saw a tall and thin ape pointing a stick at me. Darn it, I swore. I should have known it from the start, from that odd color, from those floppy ears, from that cocky grin.

I was losing blood fast, and I would not be able to get away. There was no way for me to run, but the rest of the group could still be saved, if they got away fast enough.

"He has a human! RUN" I yelled, hoping they would have the sense to follow.
words_common.writingprompts::19:
The Shine could have been a way to save all of us. It should have been, but we were never very good at avoiding fighting. Who knows how long ago it was, but in a time of phones and constant news we looked up from our screens only to see the sky light up, filled by a cold, multi-colored fire. It lasted only a few hours, but took only a few minutes for the world to see. It did not take much longer for people to want a closer look, to want a touch of the soft flame.

And then they flew. They flew so far and so fast, and soon they were joined by others; and then they fell, very slowly at first, but much like a boat in water they sank further the more that joined them. It did not take long for people to work out that the sinking related directly to how many people flew, or to notice that flying was not the only choice available to us. Before the Shine had faded many such choices came and went; flight, strength, healing, hiding, living forever, moving instantly, speed, and all the other common choices appeared and disappeared very quickly. At first some thought the powers only lasted a time, related to how long the Shine was present, but it soon became clear that the strength of powers was smaller when more people picked that same choice.

That is when the more strange powers started showing up; at first it was just workers who decided they wanted to poop gold, or kids who decided they wanted to control animals, but before a quarter day had passed things started getting weird. Fast drops in temperature, the ground shook often, clocks would skip and people died. Many people died. In half a day, an eight-billion-strong world society of the most smart and tough kind of life on Earth fell apart and halved in number; we broke into groups and teams just looking to stay alive, to make it through the bad time; those without powers were kings, and those with strange powers that could not be worked out or copied were gods in body, right there to worship when many needed them most.

A few days passed before things started to calm down - though in that time the sun only passed once. Weather was beyond wild and cities were almost empty, only fit for larger and more powerful groups. We went from wanting success to living rough in a day, if you could call it that. We went back to being animals, except a little more smart, and sometimes with extra powers.

Much time has passed since the Shine touched our sky, and humanity has made many new homes; but the most popular choices are still weak, so death is power, and attacks are constant and never stopping. The largest homes are the most powerful, but also the main target for smaller groups. Living with others is living in war, so the more peaceful of us left to travel.

And that is what I have done. I have travelled, and searched for a way to fix this madness, and maybe bring the world back to the quiet peace it once had. And I may well just have found it.
words_common.writingprompts::21:

You are familiar with the normal, everyday run-of-the-mill sloths that we have been working with, right?

Of course.

Well it is like that, but more so.

So it is still a sloth.

But, more so.

Exactly.

You realize that makes absolutely no sense, right?

Yes.

More like a sloth.

MORE LIKE A SLOTH IS NOT A REAL WAY TO SAY IT.

words_common.writingprompts::22:
I stood at a crossing, looking towards the main government building. I stared at this girl on fire. She sat calmly. Not moving a muscle, not making a sound. People stood and stared. There were other dark marks on the stairs she sat on.

"Mommy, why is she on fire?"

"Oh, that is normal," my mother replied.

"So it is totally normal for people to catch on fire?" My six year old mind was confused.

"No son, that is not the normal part. We are in a war. People do not like the way the government controls things, so they protest by burning themselves."

"Will she be okay?" My simple mind wanted her to be. No one should be so upset they hurt themselves like that.

"I do not know," came the sad answer.

Years later, after the civil war was lost, I would read about all the people who burned themselves for their country. My country.

Through college, I would think of these people. The people with beliefs so strong they would really kill themselves in such a way to make a big point. They would not want to live in a country under the heavy rule that had been in charge for many years. They wanted to be free, or they wanted to die.

It seems every group of people, there is a fight. The people being treated badly realize that they are being treated badly, and they get a tool to help them join up and fight back. They gain power. Rarely does it happen in a short time. However, here I was, a mistreated twenty-seven year old with absolutely no future.

I stood at that crossing that I stood at twenty-one years ago. The dark marks were gone, but so was my innocence. This government had to go. They had treated my mother's group badly. They had treated the group before them badly, and the group after them. They were not going to stop unless forced to. I calmly walked up to the steps and prepared to make the newest dark mark, start the next big change.

As the flames rose past my eyes, I wanted one last look as I burned. The pain was almost too much, but I managed to see through the pain. The last thing I saw before the world went away was a young girl pointing at me, exactly where I had been twenty-one years before.
words_common.writingprompts::23:
I walked downstairs and opened up the computer screen. A banker popped up on the screen.
"Hello Mrs. Roer. How may I help you?"
"I would like to check my bank account. I got a letter in the mail that I only have five points?"
"Okay, one moment." The banker went away for a second and then came back up.
"Mrs. Roer. You currently have 10 points."
"What? That is not even enough to buy food with this month?"
I looked outside and then sighed.
"Okay. Well thanks." I said.
The screen closed after the banker wished me a good day. How could I only have 10 points of happiness? A gallon of milk is 1.21 points. I could not even buy milk.
I walked outside this time. It was sunny and bright, birds were happy, I bet they have enough happiness points to buy normal food. I looked around. My pool in the ground, my hot tub, my outdoor deck with a pond further from the house. All of this was my life.
My husband and I had been married for ten years now. I was happy, he was happy. Right?
I went to look at my phone, I had a message from my husband.
'Want to have coffee?'
I sent back, 'Yes.'
I went upstairs and took a shower. My husband was gone, as always. It was no secret we had been falling apart. We were so happy at one point though that we had more points than anybody in the world. Like I said though, it was no secret that we had been falling apart. He had many affairs and I honestly, although I never cheated, found myself wanting more.
I got myself ready for coffee. Nothing too fancy or too simple. It was just coffee. I walked outside, got in one of our cars and drove to the airport. We owned a private jet, my husband had already put fuel in it.
"Just having coffee today Bill," I said.
I was walking off the jet in 4 hours to see my husband.
"Hello Mrs. Roer," He said, kissing my cheek, as he always did.
I walked with him to our second house. A blonde woman with a tight shirt was leaving the house. I looked mean at her, and she hurried from the front door to her car.
"We need to talk," I said.
"Exactly," He replied, looking happy at my anger.
"Listen, Mr. Roer, I do love you, but there is so..."
"Elaine, I want a divorce."
"That was quick." I said.
He did not care.
I left quickly after that. No coffee for me.
It was not long before I got home. I had a message from the bank again. My happiness points had hit zero.
A message from an old friend surprised me.
"Coffee?" It read.
"Sure." I answered.
At that moment my doorbell rang. I answered the door to him.
My old friend. He right away kissed me. I had missed that feeling. I felt my heart beat faster.
"Good to see you."
"Listen Luke, I just..."
He kissed me again and stopped my words.
"I paid your husband to let me marry you Elaine. He has wanted a divorce and he is not good to you. You know that."
I was shocked. He paid my husband to marry me? Why on earth would he...
"Elaine. I know we did not work out, but our son. He needs you."
I felt a tear hit my chest. I had given Luke, and our son up to be with my husband. My husband refused to let me have a son in the house that was not his.
"Elaine. Marry me. Please?" He said. He walked inside towards me further. "Our son is in the car. He is 12 now," Luke said.
I had gotten to see our son, Reig, until he was four. Then I had to stop talking to him for my husband because he was afraid it would make us look bad on the news.
I walked outside and my son ran from the car. He wrapped his arms around me. I felt my phone buzz again and I checked it. In case it was my husband with a reason for why he had sold my hand.
It was the bank. My account had just been given 20,000 happiness points.
"Yes. I will marry you."

words_common.writingprompts::28:
New Wichita burned.

The bright towers of the business area, their shiny windows reflecting the fires that danced around them stood like crying angels, the first pink fingers of morning stretching out over the eastern edge. The big houses of the original leaders had burned up early the day before, taking with them nearly seven hundred years of local history. The river area was little more than broken rocks, the old docks and storage buildings empty shells. Lieutenant Lucas Singleton Terry, born a child to a famous farmer family cried at the sight. This was his home, and to see its dirt and people so hurt felt like a crime against something holy.

Mustang 5, this is Lead. We got reports of Wolf activity along Broadway and Kingston. First and Second groups will move in to look.

That was Captain James T. Fulton, a tough man and a mean person but a very good soldier.

Terry pressed his radio.

Copy that, Mustang Leader. Second group will move forward.

There used to be a third group in Mustang Company but a surprise attack by an entire group of enemy fighters had torn through the unit, forcing them to join the survivors together. They were still better off than the rest of the Dixie Cavanaugh II area army. Bronco and Stallion companies were barely at half strength, and the tank and foot soldier groups were even worse. The First Buena Guards and First Bolan Jaegers were putting up a scary fight against the rest of Clan Wolf's big group but it was little use. Bit by bit, block by block, street by street and house by house the Wolves were driving the local defenders back. Terry switched his radio to a more private channel, one shared between just the Captain and him.

Captain Fulton, a question. How long do we have?

He heard his boss sigh over the radio.

Who knows? Years, months... weeks? The First Buena is about to leave, the leader Brewer is ordering them to the defense of Tharkad. The Bolan Jaegers seem determined to stay, but that is just because they would rather have the fight happen here on our world instead of theirs. My best guess is that we will last another year at this speed.

And what happens if we do not succeed in driving the Wolves off of Dixie? What if we fail? Terry asked.

If the worst should happen, Lieutenant, I have a feeling that we will not be alive to see it.
words_common.writingprompts::29:
It was almost impossible to see, we could only hear it after it was gone... and we dare not speak its name. But we knew what it meant. If that thing was in the skies above our land, war was coming. I will never forget the first time I saw it. I was out in the dust fields looking at stars with Roy. Little did we know that as we looked up at the stars, it was looking down at us. It was a shadow of a shadow, an old monster from a very old time long passed. Saying that I saw it is wrong, it was more of a feeling than anything. For the short moment in time when I saw that blur cut through the night, I knew it was over.

That night, they came.

Men in clothes that blended in, armed with energy guns and long knives. They did not even think twice before killing the people in our village. I am lucky to have escaped with my life. And I owe it all to one computer brain. He was a repair robot that we had stolen from the government group. He mostly helped us carry around supplies, but that day, he was truly a hero. In the middle of all the gunfire and explosions, the eating hall had come crashing down. I was among the unlucky people who ended up inside. It all happened in a flash, and before I even had time to move, I was lying trapped under a pile of broken rocks. Through the smoke and flames I could see him. A worn out repair robot with the number SR-71 on his arm. His metal silver eyes caught my look, and he immediately ran over to help me.

As far as I know, we are the only ones who made it out alive. We ran until I could not run anymore, and eventually I fell down. As I lay there, holding on to the last bits of life, I just kept saying over and over to myself "Blackbird....Blackbird....Black.."
SR-71 leaned in real close, and whispered in my ear

"There were a lot of things we could not do in an SR-71, but we were the fastest guys on the block and loved reminding our fellow pilots of this fact. People often asked us if, because of this fact, it was fun to fly the plane. Fun would not be the first word I would use to describe flying this plane. Intense, maybe, even deep. But there was one day in our flight experience when we would have to say that it was pure fun to be the fastest guys out there, at least for a moment........."
words_common.writingprompts::30:
[ Wasn't feeling this in first person, but decided to write it anyway since I liked the prompt ] 
 
 "Prisoner 778125-Sigma-8, you stand before this court today accused of crimes against all space life, murder, four counts of killing entire races, 70 counts of attempted killing of entire races, clearing planets of all life, destroying planets, and attempting to overthrow the Pan-Galactic Alliance. How do you answer?" 
 
 The man before Councilwoman Asaarha met the look of her and her fellow judges with cold blue eyes. Despite the 140 years of time spent alone he had endured before his trial, Sacha Markes stood tall and unbroken. He showed power and command, even now, stripped of his rank, fleet, and army. The last of the humans was a sign of what the species could be. 
 
 The silence before he spoke seemed louder to the Councilwoman than the crashing waves of her ocean home. The time it took for the human to speak seemed longer than the span of the galaxy. 
 
 "Guilty," he said with a simple finality. 
 
 The judges nodded their heads in a serious way. None of them had expected this one to ask for mercy. 
 
 Asaarha typed the sentence into the machine before her. The other six judges did the same. The blue lights of Markes's uniform and restraints changed to red. The screen on the mental blocker around his head changed to read GUILTY in the common language. 
 
 Though the trial room was empty save for the court and Markes, Asaarha could hear the roars of anger that were surely echoing throughout the galaxies. Each trial of the humans had been shown in its entirety. Each had ended in a guilty verdict. 
 
 "Sacha Markes, former Admiral of the Seventh Human Fleet, High Captain of the Royal Guard, head leader of the Human Force, and main ruler of the Solar Empire, you are sentenced to mental wiping and death by being thrown into a black hole. Do you have any last words before the sentence is carried out?" 
 
 The human threw his head back in a bold way and turned his gaze on the camera nearest him. Speaking to the billions of living things throughout the galaxy, he began the last long speech of the human race. 
 
 "We brought you up out of the mud we found you in. We gave you art, culture, and science. Our golden fleets created a society that will never be matched; not for 100,000 turns of the galaxy. We are responsible for all that you are. 
 
 I remember when the first of our race died after 100 centuries of living forever; killed trying to cure the sick of one of your poor planets. I remember when we decided to take our revenge on our children; to punish you for your lack of knowledge. We burned that world. I watched our fire weapons turn its surface to glass and its oceans to ash. One world for one human life. A fair trade. 
 
 But you did not accept our judgment. Like the boy flying too close to the sun, you rose up against us. Did you expect us to just let you? Did you think we would not defend ourselves? I was the leader of the fleet that met yours on the first day of battle. My ten ships against the most powerful war ships of three galaxies and a hundred races. 
 
 Now, a hundred years later, you have finally defeated us. You have lost entire star systems to us. You have sacrificed billions of lives and thousands of groups of people to bleed your gods dry and tie them in chains. Your worlds are broken. Your cities gone; wiped from history in an instant. Can you truly call that a win? 
 
 I am the last of my kind. I am Sacha Markes. Look upon my face, you strong people, and be sad. For when you kill me, you kill the last light left in this whole world."
words_common.writingprompts::32:
War Journal of P1C Henry Whiticker, First Divine Armored. 
 
 Entry:48 
 
 We finally reached the edge of the first deep hole today and heaven protect me the scout reports were not lying, it is more huge than anything I could imagine. The scout photos we were given to prepare us are like a blind man trying to describe a sunrise, and by God the smell has actually somehow gotten worse! Seeing the hole first hand I think the size of our task has finally hit home for some of the crew, they look shaken, I do not blame them, have we taken on more than we can handle? I am not sure but I have faith in our mission and our commanders. 
 
 The size of the hole really cannot be put into words but for the sake of this journal I will try. The edge extends further than the human eye should be able to see and yet I can make out tiny details on the far cliff face, it looks big enough that you could fit the whole Earth in and knock it around like an ice cube in the bottom of a whiskey glass, even while sitting in the truck of the heavy tank I get dizzy looking down onto the levels below, if it were not for the special calming pills the doctors give us I am sure what I see on the lower levels might have some lasting scary effect on me. The crew and I wash down today’s dose with a bottle of church wine, and why not, today was a good day after all. Today we reached the edge of Limbo. 
 
 Entry:49 
 
 Not much to write down today, some small fights on the outside edge, just some low level monsters taking a hit at us otherwise nothing going on but general camp stuff. The builders are working double time to ensure the safety of Limbo Base, they say it will be fully up in 2 days, I have my doubts. After their big failure at the river they have got a lot of pride to save, 2 tanks, 4 groups of troops and a sound cannon lost because of their bad boats. Bad men. 
 
 I hate just sitting around like this with nothing to take my mind off the smell of rot and bad air that somehow gets into the truck cab despite the tech experts promises that the cab is perfectly tightly sealed, it feels like the smell is inside my head rotting tiny holes in my brain. 
 
 Entry:51 
 
 HOOAH! CONTACT BABY! Praise God I have been waiting for this moment since the first days of the war for the surface. Hell finally saw fit to send us some worthy opponents AND WE KICKED THEIR BUTTS IN!! HAHAHAHAHAHA. 
 
 They came a few hours after my last entry like a great black storm. A swirling group of winged beasts, screamers and small demons beyond counting rising up from the center of The Pit and came crashing down completely covering Limbo Base. The first few moments of fighting should have been a mess but by the grace of God we were ready. 
 
 All the sound cannons had been on high alert since we came out from the maze of caves and onto the flat lands of Limbo proper 8 days ago and today that hard work paid off. The quick rush of the winged monster attack crumbled before the wall of sound our blessed sound cannons blasted out. The word of God is hated by the people of Hell, the word of God pushed out through a moving rig of high powered speakers run by a faithful member of the church is truly weakening. The shocked and frozen monsters that twitched and moved on the ground were easy targets, the tanks blessed water cannons burning away parts of the foul creatures as if the misted holy water were strong acid, huge piles of the creatures were turned to ash in seconds. 
 
 The larger monster women proved more tough and I saw more than a few soldiers die on their sharp claws, their blessed body armor little better than paper. We paid them back and I am proud to say our tank spear guns sent a good lot of the giant birds screaming into nothingness stuck on our shining silver spears. I should write this so it does not seem like I am making the soldiers efforts smaller, their bravery and strength in battle too, for they have got that in large amounts, despite the deadly danger they collected their fair share of kills, pinning the giant creatures with their silver poles and finishing them off with their hooked chains. It was a great bloody sight, like something out of a nature movie. 
 
 The greatest test of the battle was yet to come though. After a full day and a half of fighting the black group began to thin out and we thought we might have finally broken their attack, but then they appeared. Three giant figures coming into focus through the haze of ash and tiredness. Hell Dragons, nothing like what we had seen in movies or our stories from childhood, these were great sick, foul things that stood over us. Flat nosed heads the size of a big church covered in spikes, long armored bodies like an insects, their faces and joints wet with thick black oil that bubbled and hissed as it fell from them and stained the flat lands of Limbo. 
 
 Sound cannons focused their attack and stopped the giants from taking over the base, the tanks water tanks and spear guns ran dry just trying to keep them away, our brave soldiers held back the black group, fighting without stopping which allowed us time to pull back, get more supplies and enter the fight again. And so it went for hours on end and for all our efforts the Hell Dragons seemed to be none the worse. 
 
 Help finally came at the hands of the building team. Of all people! Through our efforts we had given them enough time to finish and put together Limbo Bases major defenses, Holy cannons and the Holy Rail Gun. The Rail Gun poked holes in the Dragons thick armor throwing streams of oil onto the battlefield while the cannons smashed into the beasts weak open points putting shells marked with holy words deep in their bodies hurting them with pain. The attack still went on for hours and we lost a great deal of our force but after nearly 2 months since we first went down into this place we finally have built a forward base to start our attack on Hell. One section down eight to go. This is the first day here that the smell does not bother me.

words_common.writingprompts::34:
The planet Earth has changed a lot recently, 23 years ago- almost to the day, the storms on the surface ended. The same storms that had been blowing for roughly five thousand years, a few weeks passed whilst the cloud shapes broke apart, and then we got our first clear view of our home. 

I was five years old at the time and kept busy mostly by the colours, the beautiful blue and green were like nothing on the Ark. We had water- sure, but not pools large enough to give that blue colour. We had plants too, but the conditions were far from the best and made the plants a dirty green rather than healthy. I wanted to see it closer- touch it- feel it. 

That was probably when I decided to join the group for the first trip. The first trip was- as the name says, the first mission back down to the planet. A lot of people wanted to go back down as soon as the storms ended, there were protests- fights even. People wanted the Ark to head straight back down- fools. 

23 years may have been a long time to wait, but it was important... We were the last humans after all- if we landed and something went wrong? We could not risk it. Years of rock scans, and low air scouting gave us the perfect landing spot. Small damage to local nature, enough space to build a community, plenty of food- water- and importantly a lot of natural protection taking the form of disaster-formed mountain ranges, and deep holes filled with the darkest blue water. 

Of course something as large as the Ark could not simply just land though... No- that was where the first trip came into the picture. We were the first guys to go to the planet- and live for good in over seven generations. Our goal was to build the landing base, it would be a long job- probably another five or six years even, but the base would provide us with a much needed start- as well as mapping out local land much more clearly, learning about plants, animals. The truth of the situation is that we were going in without knowing anything- this safe area as the group had nicknamed it could very easily become a place of death. The problem with the safe area was that because of its location once we went in, our ship would not be able to make it out. 

Part of the problem with the planet was the storms- even now 23 years after the main storm ended smaller parts continued to spin... The mountain ranges protected the area from the storms still blowing- not quite powerful enough to make it over the high peaks though. 

Even in the air above there was a mean wind that constantly blew... It would tear a leaving ship to pieces, only a craft as large as the Ark would be able to survive it- and the Ark needed a base in order to fly away. 

So that was the job, go down, face possible death, build a huge building, all in less than six years- and I was very excited.
words_common.writingprompts::35:
Outside, Jerusalem side street, day. A space near a couple of large clay pots has been blocked off with tape. Police workers are doing work in the space. Next to his car stands MOSES looking tired and grumpy. After a few moments looking at this messy old leader leaning on his walking stick we pull back.

JESUS enters from the left carrying coffee from a shop.

MOSES Took you long enough. Feels like we have been waiting for you forever!

JESUS Sorry, there was a line. So, what have we got?

MOSES Dead body. A regular officer called it in, looks like another dead woman who sells her body. Hey, Hazdrubul, do you have a cause of death yet?

We look over to the masked and covered figure beside what we can now see as a body. HAZDRUBUL steps away from the crime scene.

HAZDRUBUL It is a little early to say, but if I were a betting man I would go with being hit very hard. Looks like many bruises over the body and a really bad one to the side of the head.

JESUS When did she die?

HAZDRUBUL Hard to give a time of death right now, but I will go with some time last night and give you a better number when we check how cold the body is.

MOSES Good enough.

Jesus moves to get closer to the crime scene, trying to get a better look. He does not handle the body well and ducks behind a clay pot to be sick.

MOSES Jesus! Well, at least you did not mess up the crime scene.

JESUS comes back out wiping his mouth and looking pale.

MOSES OK, the officers are going to ask everyone in the houses nearby. Let us go get you cleaned up and see if we can find out the name of this poor girl.

Scene 23 - Station house inside, interview room. JESUS and MOSES are on opposite sides of the room arms folded, clearly angry at each other.

MOSES Do NOT give me any of your act like you are better than everyone else talk. We needed results and I got them!

JESUS And was it worth all the trouble it caused, Moses? Was it worth going down to their level?

MOSES I would do it again! I would do it again in a heartbeat! Forty years I have been in this job and if there is one thing I know how to do it is get a person to say they did it!

JESUS You know, the first time I saw you with that stick, I thought it was a sign of age. I thought it made you an older person, someone to be looked up to. I guess I was wrong.

MOSES Maybe you are wrong about a lot of things.

JESUS Maybe I am!

MOSES And maybe you want to think about how it looks out there to our fellow police officers when you, you young and stupid boy, think you can tell me how to act!

JESUS Look, let us just calm down here. I look up to you, sure I look up to you. You caught the Golden Calf gang. You were the guy who fixed the Dead Sea Hostage situation. But this is not the desert! This is Jerusalem! We have to do things differently now!

MOSES The heck you say...

JESUS Look, man, think what you like. But there is a girl down in the basement on a table and all she is doing is getting colder while we stand here arguing... hhh, OF COURSE!

MOSES What?

JESUS Of course! Throwing rocks! Do you not see it?

MOSES Jesus, slow down will you? See what?

JESUS They thought they were better than her!

Scene 832: Jerusalem, outside, night. MOSES is leaning on a police car as JESUS walks up with this week’s bad person in handcuffs. Moses watches as JESUS hands the bad person off to uniformed police.

MOSES Good arrest, kid.

JESUS Could not have done it if you had not seen the connection between the victims. How did you know?

MOSES I have been on the job for longer than you have been alive. After a while, you get a feeling for this sort of thing.

JESUS Think I will ever get that kind of gut feeling?

MOSES Maybe. If you live long enough.

JESUS You are full of support. I do not care, though. We put a person who did wrong behind bars and that is the kind of good news I want to share!
words_common.writingprompts::36:
Hey, look at those small birds over in the birdbath. Kylo cheered and puffed out his chest, nearly falling off his branch.

Don't be a caveman, brother, Atticus grumbled, pecking at his seeds, You are a small brown bird. That is not even the same group of birds.

I do not care. I am going to go talk to them. Kylo took off, moving through the air like a leaf trapped in a strong wind. Atticus sighed and took off after him. He would have to keep a close watch on Kylo or else they would get kicked out again.

Kylo crashed into the water with a very big splash. Water drops flew in every direction, soaking the birds in the birdbath. They yelled with anger as Kylo came up from under the water, shaking the wetness from his head. He walked up to a group of soaked finches and gave his wings a shake. Hey, birds. Nice body parts.

We are not that kind of bird. A purple finch stepped forward from the group, and she started a long, angry speech on how tired she was of hearing that old pickup line. Atticus landed on the edge of the bath and began to walk around, saying sorry to everyone for Kylo's bad behavior and asking them not to call the guard over.

Okay, I am sorry, Kylo interrupted, let me make it right: how about you and I go over there—he pointed to the bird food holder—and I share my seeds with you? If birds had lips, Kylo would be smiling right now.

The finches began to flap their wings angrily, splashing Kylo with water. You are such a rude person. Get out of here! Many of the birds watching chirped in agreement, and some of the bigger birds began to puff their chests in a scary way. Atticus pushed Kylo to the side and raised his wings. For my friend here, I am sorry. He has clearly had too much sweet flower juice; we will just be leaving now.

Oh, you think we are going to believe that? The purple finch threw a nut shell at his feet. He is just trying to find a date for you, is he not? Let him take the blame for you, and swoop in to look better by comparison. The other birds called out in agreement.

I think these two need to be taught a lesson. A blue jay flew over to Atticus, standing a full inch above him. He spread his wings in a scary way, blocking Atticus from taking off. Why do you not pick on someone your own size? The birds watching started to cheer, shouting for a fight.

Well, you are kind of bigger than me. Atticus took a step back into the bath. He felt feathers brush against him as the crowd pressed around him, pushing him back towards the jay. That would not be my own size now, would it?

Kylo stumbled in front of him and began to hop around. Do not worry, Atticus; we have this.

Hey, this is a one-on-one fight. The jay looked around. If you get help, then—

Who on earth placed all this here? A door opened, and the birds began to scatter, screaming, Human! Atticus grabbed Kylo and pushed him into the air, and the two lost themselves among the cloud of fleeing birds. Out of the corner of his eye, he saw the person scratching his head in front of the birdbath.

Make sure to thank that person for saving you from yet another mess, Atticus said.

Kylo laughed. We could have totally beaten that guy. As the two flew over the car in the driveway, he let loose a dropping that landed right in the center of the front glass.
words_common.writingprompts::37:
He used to hit me so much.

I had never even had a drink, and he beat cracked ribs, bruised kidneys and loose teeth into me. To make sure I never became what he was.

Once when he was not drunk he told me he drank because of how he grew up. He said it like he wanted me to understand his feelings, to forgive him. Like he could not see that my arm was broken from him protecting me from drink the week before. Like he could not see himself standing over me crying blood and snot and tears, laughing at me. Like he could not remember what was so bad about how he grew up, could not remember why he needed it to let him sleep at night, to stop waking up screaming in the night, to stop wetting himself when he had a bad dream.

He made me sick, my dad. My breathing stops sometimes, and one of my wrists never healed right, leaving me half hurt in that hand. I have eleven fake teeth. At twenty three, all this.

I did not go to his funeral, I celebrated it though. I did not take a drink though, I could never do that. I cry myself to sleep most nights, I cannot help myself screaming if someone comes up to me suddenly. Lately I have noticed a lot of blood coming up when I cough. I will not let him beat me though, I will not give him this little win.

When my son was born it was the happiest day of my life. For the first time in my life, someone wanted and needed me. His mother left soon after that, saying she did not want to be stuck in a life she did not choose ( after carrying a child for 9 months, she leaves it in 3 weeks. Never in those 9 months did she "not choose" that life ).

Honestly, after she left it all got too much for me. I left my son with my mother for the night, and went and had a drink. It was perfect. It was the best I have felt in my whole life. For a few hours, I was not scared or hating myself or nervous. Just calm and ok, I could deal with everything a little better. I think I will probably have a few more now, just to keep the good feeling going. Not drinking now scares me even more, now that I know that there is such an easy choice, which is so much better.

When I picked my son up in the morning mom looked at me funny, but I ignored her. I was in a bit of a rush, I had heard good things about whisky, and was eager to try it.

But do not worry, I will not let my son grow up like I did, I will make sure he knows alcohol is bad. I will not show him that pain, that fear. I will make sure he hates me for as long as possible as much as possible. He will link alcohol with me, and I am bad, so he will stop the pattern. I am not strong enough, but he will be. I know he will be strong enough. I will make him tough enough outside, and cold and hard enough inside. He will be able to beat it. Like I cannot.
words_common.writingprompts::38:
Craig was walking home from the shops when he met God. He was not expecting to run into God, normal people rarely do. In fact he did not really ever think about God. He did not believe in a God, but he also did not disbelieve enough to ever think about Gods not existing. Religion and God were not really topics he cared about. 
 A topic he cared deeply about was that of Caramels. If you do not know Caramels are a rather delicious chocolatey snack type thing made of several layers of thin crispy biscuit covered in chocolate, and Craig was crazy about them. He may not have been religious, but his feelings on Caramels came close. The reason behind his trip to the shops was to buy more Caramels, and his mind was full of excitement as he headed back home. 
 
 He was about two minutes away from his home, and Caramel happiness when God first spoke to him. 
 "Hey! Craig!" 
 His Caramel thought interrupted, Craig turned round to see who had spoken to him. Behind him stood a tall person in a loose fitting suit. Craig was not really sure of the person's gender, they were pretty gender neutral, looking not unlike Diamond Dogs era David Bowie. They looked familiar to Craig, but he could not quite put his finger on where he might have seen them before. He realised he had been staring, and looked for something to say. 
 "Hi," he began slowly. "Do I know you?" 
 "In a way," replied the Bowie lookalike. "I am God." 
 "Well good for you. I have got to get going now. Bye." Said Craig before starting back towards his house. He had Caramels in his bag, and did not want to be wasting time on a crazy person. 
 "Wait, do not go yet. Please." Called out the person. "What would it take for you to believe me?" 
 Craig sighed and turned back, deciding that playing along with the person would probably get him to his Caramels faster. 
 "I do not know," said Craig, annoyed. "A miracle or something. Some amazing thing which could not just be done by any old person. Something more than just saying that you are god." 
 "Hmm. How about....this!" God pointed at a bush which burst into flames. The fire shaped itself into a dragon which roared at the two of them. Then, with a snap of God's fingers, the fire was put out leaving the bush burnt but still there. God turned back to Craig with arms spread wide as if to say look at that! 
 
 Craig, looking a little bit impressed, turned back to God. 
 "Yeah, that was pretty good. Looked very impressive. I have to admit I have no idea how you did it. A light trick maybe? It worked for Tupac, so I can see it working for a dragon." 
 God stared at him for a few seconds before responding. 
 "I did it by being God. You asked for a miracle. I showed you one. What more do you want from me?" 
 "Do not get me wrong, it is very good. But the whole God thing probably is not going to work. Maybe people would be more likely to believe you are a wizard." 
 "But I am not a stupid wizard!" Shouted God. "I am God. Why would I say I am a wizard?" 
 Craig backed off a few steps, holding his hands up in front of him in the common sign of I do not want any trouble, let us all just calm down. 
 "Hey calm down buddy. I am sorry if I sounded mean, but it is just helpful advice. This is for a TV show or online video thing right? You are not going to trick anyone with the whole God thing." 
 God, clearly very angry by this point, held Craig's look for a few more seconds before letting out an angry sigh and walking away fast. 
 Craig watched them leave, then shook his head and returned to his walk. He thought about checking out the bush to see if he could get any clues as to how the trick had been done, but decided against it. Whoever had been filming the meeting was probably still watching, waiting for Craig to do exactly that. So he pushed it out of his mind, and set off home. After all, there were sweet Caramels waiting for him to eat.
