Results from this laboratory-scale study demonstrated that after eight days, which included periods reaching at least 66°C, the numbers of Salmonella spp. in Sample A fell below the limits established by the UK compost standard PAS 100 (BSI, 2005), which mandates that compost must be entirely free of Salmonella spp. Conversely, Sample B continued to exhibit high quantities of Salmonella spp. even after undergoing the composting process for a total of twenty days.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::24: BACKGROUND: Although race is historically associated with prostate cancer progression during early stages, it remains unclear whether race continues to predict poor outcomes once men have advanced disease. The authors hypothesized that, within an equal-access setting involving patients diagnosed with castration-resistant prostate cancer (CRPC) who lack known metastases (M0/Mx), black men would receive imaging tests at rates comparable to nonblack men, implying an equal opportunity to detect metastases, yet they would still face a higher risk of developing metastatic disease. METHODS: Analyzing 837 men diagnosed with M0/Mx CRPC between 2000 and 2014 across five Veterans Affairs hospitals within the SEARCH database, researchers collected comprehensive data regarding all subsequent imaging tests, including their specific dates, types, and final outcomes. Multivariable Cox models were subsequently employed to rigorously test associations between race and the time elapsed until the first instance of metastasis, the first bone metastasis, the first bone scan, the second bone scan among those with a negative initial scan, and overall survival. RESULTS: The study revealed that black men (n = 306) were just as likely as their nonblack counterparts (n = 531) to receive both a first and a second bone scan following a CRPC diagnosis. Furthermore, there were no statistically significant differences regarding the risk of developing any metastases, bone metastases, time to bone scans, or overall survival between these groups, as all P values exceeded .2. CONCLUSIONS: The total absence of racial differences in metastatic development and scanning practices observed here suggests that, once men possess a diagnosis of M0/Mx CRPC, race may not serve as a prognostic factor. Future efforts to understand racial disparities in prostate cancer might derive greater benefit by focusing specifically on the risk of initial disease development and the outcomes of men with early stage disease.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::25: We present deep Hubble Space Telescope single-star photometry of Leo A in B, V, and I, utilizing a new field of view which, being offset from the centrally located field previously observed by Tolstoy et al. (1998), successfully exposes the halo population of this galaxy. By reporting the detection of metal-poor red horizontal branch stars, we demonstrate that Leo A is definitively not a young galaxy; in fact, it is at least as old as metal-poor Galactic Globular Clusters, which also exhibit red horizontal branches and are widely considered to possess a minimum age of approximately 9 Gyr. While we discuss the distance to Leo A and perform an extensive comparison of our data with stellar isochrones, we find that for a distance modulus of 24.5, the data remain better than 50% complete down to absolute magnitudes of 2 or more. Although we can easily identify stars with metallicities between 0.0001 and 0.0004 and ages between 5 and 10 Gyr during their post-main-sequence phases, we lack the detection of main-sequence turnoffs, which would otherwise provide unambiguous proof of ancient stellar generations exceeding 10 Gyr. Furthermore, blue horizontal branch stars, while above our detection limits, are difficult to distinguish from young stars with similar colors and magnitudes. Nevertheless, synthetic color-magnitude diagrams show it is possible to populate the blue horizontal branch in the halo, and these models suggest that approximately 50% of the total astrated mass in our pointing is attributable to an ancient population. We conclude that Leo A started forming stars at least 9 Gyr ago, and the existence of old stars in this oxygen-deficient galaxy, which exhibits only 3% of Solar oxygen, illustrates that low abundance does not preclude early star formation.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::26: One primary goal of neuromorphic engineering involves the creation of realistic robotic systems, which interact with the physical world by adopting specific neuromechanical principles derived from biology. Critical to this overarching endeavor is the methodology used to implement the complex spinal circuitry responsible for the behavior of afferented muscles, which, at its core, represents the closed-loop behavior arising from the intricate interactions among populations of muscle spindle afferents, alpha and gamma motoneurons, and muscle fibers to enable useful behaviors. By utilizing programmable very-large-scale-integration hardware to implement simple models of spiking neurons, skeletal muscles, muscle spindle proprioceptors, alpha-motoneuron recruitment, gamma-motoneuron control of spindle sensitivity, and the monosynaptic circuitry connecting them, we developed a multi-scale system of populations of spiking neurons that emulated the physiological properties of a pair of antagonistic afferented mammalian muscles, each simulated by 1024 alpha- and gamma-motoneurones acting on a joint via long tendons. This integrated system, which was able to maintain a specific joint angle, successfully reproduced stretch reflex responses even when driving the nonlinear biomechanics of an actual cadaveric finger. Moreover, this system allowed us to explore numerous values and combinations of gamma-static and gamma-dynamic gains when driving a robotic finger, some of which replicated certain human pathological conditions. Lastly, after exploring the behavioral consequences of adopting three alternative models of isometric muscle force production, we found that dynamic responses to rate-coded spike trains produce force ramps that can be highly sensitive to tendon elasticity, especially at high force output. Our methodology produced, to our knowledge, the first example of an autonomous, multi-scale, neuromorphic, neuromechanical system capable of creating realistic reflex behavior in cadaveric fingers, providing a platform that allows us to explore sensorimotor function mechanisms by building them from first principles as a precursor to future robotic systems.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::27: Introduction and Objective: Patients presenting with a urinary tract infection complicated by kidney or ureteral stones constitute a urologic emergency, often achieving early clinical stability yet remaining hospitalized while awaiting results from urine antibiotic sensitivity analyses. We aimed to identify clinical predictors of antibiotic resistance in patients who underwent urgent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and obstructive urolithiasis, thereby facilitating early discharge on empiric oral antibiotics. Methods: Patients who underwent emergent urinary tract decompression for sepsis and an obstructing ureteral stone between 2014 and 2018 at two academic medical institutions were identified. After emergent stent placement was performed, patients were treated with broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics. We assessed the association between clinical parameters at the time of presentation and resistance to at least one antibiotic from urine culture using the Wilcoxon test and Fisher exact test for continuous and categorical variables, respectively, before multivariate logistic regression was performed using all significant variables from univariate analysis. Results: Out of 134 patients, 84 patients, representing 62.7% of the cohort, had urine cultures resistant to at least one antibiotic. On univariate analysis, patients with resistant cultures were significantly more likely to have had previous ureteroscopy, require postoperative intensive care unit-level care, have bacteremia, and experience a longer length of stay. In multivariate analysis using significant variables from univariate analysis, only previous ureteroscopy was significantly associated with antibiotic resistance with an increased odds of 6.95 (p = 0.011). Conclusions: In this study, we demonstrate that a history of ureteroscopy is significantly associated with antibiotic resistance in both univariate and multivariate analyses. Our findings suggest that patients with a history of ureteroscopy should await urine culture results, while those without such history may be discharged early on empiric oral antibiotics, although future studies remain necessary to determine the clinical effectiveness of this predictor.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details how cannabis can influence the use of other psychoactive substances, including prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco and illicit drugs, yet very little research has specifically examined the complex factors associated with these changes in substance use patterns. This paper explores the self-reported use of cannabis as a substitute for alcohol among a Canadian medical cannabis patient population, with data derived from a comprehensive survey of 2102 people who were enrolled in the Canadian medical cannabis program. We included 973 respondents, representing 44% of the total, who reported using alcohol on at least 10 occasions over a 12 month period prior to initiating medical cannabis, and we subsequently used retrospective data regarding the frequency and amount of alcohol use pre-and post medical cannabis initiation to determine which participant characteristics and other variables were associated with reductions or total cessation of alcohol use. Overall, 419 participants, or 44%, reported decreases in alcohol usage frequency over 30 days, while 323, comprising 34%, decreased the number of standard drinks they consumed per week, and 76, or 8%, reported no alcohol use at all in the 30 days prior to the survey. Being below 55 years of age and reporting higher rates of alcohol use in the pre-period were both associated with greater odds of reducing alcohol use, and an intention to use medical cannabis specifically to reduce alcohol consumption was associated with significantly greater odds of both reducing and ceasing alcohol use altogether. Our findings suggest that medical cannabis initiation may be associated with self-reported reductions and cessation of alcohol use, and since alcohol results in significant rates of criminality, morbidity and mortality, these findings may improve health outcomes for patients, as well as overall public health and safety.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::29: The delicate balance between spin-orbit coupling, Coulomb repulsion, and crystalline electric field interactions, which is observed in Ir-based oxides, is usually manifested as exotic magnetic behavior. In this study, we investigate the evolution of the exchange coupling between Co and Ir for partial La substitution by Ca in La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$, noting that a great advantage of using Ca$^{2+}$ as a replacement for La$^{3+}$ is the inherent similarity of their ionic radii, which ensures that the observed magnetic changes can be more easily associated with electronic variations. A thorough investigation of the structural, electronic, and magnetic properties of the La$_{2-x}$Ca$_{x}$CoIrO$_6$ system was carried out by means of synchrotron x-ray powder diffraction, muon spin rotation and relaxation ($\mu$SR), AC and DC magnetization, XAS, XMCD, Raman spectroscopy, electrical resistivity, and dielectric permittivity. Our XAS results show that, while up to 25% of Ca substitution at the La site results in the emergence of Co$^{3+}$, which is possibly in a high spin state, the introduction of a larger amount of Ca leads to the increase of Ir valence. Because the competing magnetic interactions resulting from these mixed valences lead to a coexistence of a magnetically ordered and an emerging spin glass state for the doped samples, our $\mu$SR results indicate that for La$_{2}$CoIrO$_6$, a nearly constant fraction of a paramagnetic phase persists down to low temperature, possibly being related to the presence of a small amount of Ir$^{3+}$ and anti-site disorder at Co/Ir sites. For the doped compounds, the paramagnetic phase freezes below 30 K, but there remains some dynamics associated with the spin glass, and the dielectric data indicate a possible magnetodielectric effect, which is discussed regarding electron hopping, anti-site disorder, and the distorted crystalline structure.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::30: As the stringent requirements introduced by the new sixth-generation (6G) internet-of-things (IoT) use cases emerge, traditional approaches to multiple access control have begun to demonstrate significant limitations, which has consequently led to a new wave of grant-free (GF) approaches being proposed as a viable alternative, even though a definitive solution remains to be accomplished. In our work, we propose a new semi-GF coordinated random access (RA) protocol, which is denoted as partial-information multiple access (PIMA), to reduce packet loss and latency, particularly in the presence of sporadic activations. By considering a machine-type communications (MTC) scenario, wherein devices need to transmit data packets in the uplink to a base station (BS), we observe that the BS, when using PIMA, can acquire partial information on the instantaneous traffic conditions and, by utilizing compute-over-the-air techniques, estimate the number of devices with packets waiting for transmission in their queue. Based on this knowledge, the BS assigns to each device a single slot for transmission; however, because each slot may still be assigned to multiple users, collisions may occur. Both the total number of allocated slots and the user assignments are optimized, based on the estimated number of active users, to reduce collisions and improve the efficiency of the multiple access scheme. To prove the validity of our solution, we compare PIMA to time-division multiple-access (TDMA) and slotted ALOHA (SALOHA) schemes, which represent ideal solutions for orthogonal multiple access (OMA) in the time domain for low and high traffic conditions, respectively. We show that PIMA is able not only to adapt to different traffic conditions and provide fewer packet drops regardless of the intensity of packet generations, but also to merge the advantages of both TDMA and SALOHA schemes, thus providing performance improvements in terms of packet loss probability and latency.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::31: Background and purpose—Because bone remodeling, which occurs as a physiological response to traumatic injury, postoperative immobilization, or various device-related reactions, can potentially lead to a significant loss of bone stock, it subsequently increases the clinical risk of periprosthetic fracture and aseptic loosening. This study specifically investigates the adaptive bone remodeling processes occurring within the proximal tibia following uncemented total knee arthroplasty. Patients and methods—We performed a 2-year follow-up study of 53 patients, whose mean age was 62 years and included 27 men, all of whom received an uncemented total knee arthroplasty within a randomized controlled trial that utilized bone mineral density as a secondary endpoint. Patients were randomized into two distinct groups receiving either a monoblock or a modular polyethylene design, utilizing the uncemented Zimmer Nexgen trabecular metal implant. Measurements of bone mineral density were performed postoperatively and again at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months across three specific regions of interest. Results and interpretation—In group A, statistically significant changes in bone mineral density were observed after 24 months within both the medial and lateral regions of interest, with density decreasing medially by 15% and laterally by 13%. Conversely, in group B, these changes remained limited and returned to preoperative values after 24 months, resulting in statistically significant differences between groups for both medial and lateral regions. No significant changes were found in the distal region for either group. A significantly different remodeling pattern was observed, showing greater bone loss in the monoblock group, which indicates that this flexible implant design, despite previously demonstrating improved fixation, does not effectively decrease the bone loss typically occurring within the proximal tibia after undergoing total knee arthroplasty surgery.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::32: Artificial Neural Networks, which are bio-inspired models of neural computation that have proven highly effective, notably lack a natural notion of time, while their neural units exchange analog values in a frame-based manner—a form of communication that is both computationally and energetically inefficient. This approach contrasts sharply with biological neurons, which communicate sparingly and efficiently by utilizing binary spikes. While artificial Spiking Neural Networks can be constructed by replacing the units of an ANN with spiking neurons, their current performance remains far from that of deep ANNs on hard benchmarks, and these networks additionally use much higher firing rates compared to their biological counterparts, thereby limiting their overall efficiency. Here, we demonstrate how spiking neurons that employ an efficient form of neural coding can be utilized to construct SNNs that match high-performance ANNs while exceeding the state-of-the-art in SNNs on important benchmarks, all while requiring significantly lower average firing rates. To achieve this, we employ spike-time coding based on the firing rate limiting adaptation phenomenon observed in biological spiking neurons; this phenomenon can be captured in adapting spiking neuron models, for which we derive the effective transfer function. Neural units in ANNs trained with this transfer function can be substituted directly with adaptive spiking neurons, and the resulting Adaptive SNNs can carry out inference in deep neural networks using up to an order of magnitude fewer spikes compared to previous SNNs. Furthermore, adaptive spike-time coding allows for the dynamic control of neural coding precision; we show how a simple model of arousal in AdSNNs further halves the average required firing rate, and this notion naturally extends to other forms of attention. AdSNNs thus hold promise as a novel, efficient model for neural computation that naturally fits to temporally continuous and asynchronous applications.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::33: Context. LQ Hya, which is recognized as one of the most frequently studied young solar analogue stars, has recently been observed to display intriguing behaviour through the analysis of long-term photometry; specifically, while various authors have reported a coherent spot structure migrating within the rotational frame during the period between 2003 and 2009, the star has since entered a chaotic state where coherent structures appear to have vanished, and rapid phase jumps of the photometric minima occur with irregular frequency over time. Aims. As LQ Hya is among the stars included in the SOFIN/FIES long-term monitoring campaign that has extended over twenty-five years, we publish here new temperature maps for the star spanning from 2006 to 2017, thereby covering its chaotic state. Methods. By utilizing a Doppler imaging technique, we derive detailed surface temperature maps from high-resolution spectra. Results. From the mean temperatures of these Doppler maps, we observe a weak yet systematic increase in the surface temperature of the star, a finding that remains consistent with the simultaneously increasing photometric magnitude. During nearly all observing seasons, we discern a high-latitude spot structure which is clearly nonaxisymmetric; although the phase behaviour of this structure is notably chaotic, it agrees reasonably well with the photometry. Equatorial spots are also frequently seen, yet we interpret many of them to be artefacts resulting from poor to moderate phase coverage. Conclusions. Even during the star's chaotic phase, the spot topology has remained remarkably similar to higher activity epochs with more coherent, long-lived structures; we see high-latitude and equatorial activity, while the mid-latitude range remains largely void of spots. We interpret the erratic jumps and drifts in the phase of photometric minima to be caused by changes in high-latitude structures rather than equatorial spots.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::34: Hydrogenation reactions, which are expected to rank among the most significant surface processes occurring on interstellar ices, remain poorly understood due to a persistent lack of solid-state astrochemical laboratory data regarding the interactions of H-atoms with common interstellar ice constituents. Our laboratory work aims to determine whether carbon dioxide, formic acid, and acetaldehyde react with H-atoms in the solid state at low temperatures, while simultaneously deriving reaction rates and production yields. By bombarding pure interstellar ice analogues of CO2, HCOOH, and CH3CHO with H-atoms within an ultra-high vacuum environment, we monitor these ices using reflection absorption infrared spectroscopy and detect reaction products in the gas phase through temperature-programmed desorption to ascertain destruction and formation yields. Within the sensitivity limits of our experimental set-up, we conclude that H-atom bombardment of pure CO2 and HCOOH ice produces no detectable results, with upper limits on reaction rates being less than or equal to 7e(-17) cm^2/s, making it unlikely these species contribute significantly to complex organic formation. Conversely, CH3CHO reacts with H-atoms, as at most 20% undergoes hydrogenation to ethanol, while a secondary route facilitates the break-up of the C-C bond to form solid-state CH4, H2CO, and CH3OH. Given that the methane production yield is expected to equal the summed yield of H2CO and CH3OH, CH4 likely evaporates partially after formation because of the high exothermicity inherent to the reaction. Furthermore, the determined reaction rates for CH3CHO destruction depend exclusively upon the ice temperature rather than the ice thickness, providing a comprehensive characterization of these processes which are vital for understanding the chemical evolution of cold, dense regions within the interstellar medium where such complex molecular synthesis occurs.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::35: Introduced in the early 2000s, the methodology of funnel control has since evolved in many respects, achieving a level of mathematical maturity that is balanced by its practical applications. Its fundamental tenet is the attainment of prescribed transient and asymptotic behaviour for continuous-time controlled dynamical processes, which encompass linear and nonlinear systems described by functional differential equations, differential-algebraic systems, and partial differential equations. Considered are classes of systems specified solely by structural properties—such as relative degree and stable internal dynamics—rather than precise system data, which are generally unknown, reflecting the inherent reality that any model of a dynamical process is necessarily imprecise. Prespecified components include a funnel, shaped through the choice of a smooth function freely selected by the designer, a fairly large class of smooth reference signals, and a system class satisfying certain structural properties. The primary aim is to design, based exclusively on structural assumptions and input-output information, a single simple control strategy—known as the funnel controller—so that its application to any system within the given class and to any reference signal results in the feasibility of the funnel control objective. This means that solutions of the closed-loop system do not exhibit blow-up in finite time, all variables remain bounded, and, most importantly, the evolution of the error between the system output and the reference signal stays within the prespecified funnel. In the Introduction, we describe the genesis of funnel control, after which we investigate diverse system classes amenable to this method. Funnel control is demonstrated for systems with arbitrary relative degree and systems described by partial differential equations, and, finally, we discuss both input constraints and their various practical applications.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::36: Given the increasing diversity characterizing Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks, designing a fully protected network has become exceptionally challenging; for instance, the Stealthy Link Flooding Attack (SLFA), which is a specific variant of DDoS attacks that strives to block access to a target area by flooding a small set of links, has been shown to bypass traditional defense mechanisms effectively. One potential solution to tackle such SLFAs involves applying Moving Target Defense (MTD) techniques, wherein network settings are dynamically changed to confuse or deceive attackers, thereby making the launch of a successful attack highly expensive. However, because MTD inherently introduces some overhead to the network, finding the optimal strategy—specifically regarding when or to what extent one should apply it—remains a major challenge, as the strategy is significantly influenced by the attacker’s behavior, which is often difficult to predict. In this work, we address the complex challenge of obtaining an optimal MTD strategy that effectively mitigates SLFAs while incurring minimal overhead by modeling the problem as a signaling game that considers both the network defender and the attacker as active players. A belief function is established throughout the engagement between the attacker and the defender during this SLFA campaign, which is utilized to determine the best response for each player. We analyze this game model and derive a defense mechanism based on the equilibria of the game, evaluating the technique on a Mininet-based environment where an attacker performs SLFAs while a defender applies MTD. The results demonstrate that our signaling game-based dynamic defense mechanism provides a level of protection comparable to extensive MTD solutions, yet it causes significantly reduced overhead for the network throughout the entire duration of the operation.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::37: Multi-fidelity (MF) methods, which incorporate data from various low-fidelity (LF) models, are currently gaining popularity for enhancing surrogate modeling and design optimization. Although most existing MF methods assume a fixed dataset, adaptive sampling techniques that dynamically allocate resources among these fidelity models can achieve higher efficiency while exploring and exploiting the design space. However, because most existing MF methods rely on the hierarchical assumption of fidelity levels or fail to capture the intercorrelation between multiple fidelity levels to quantify the value of future samples, they often struggle to navigate adaptive sampling effectively. To address this hurdle, we propose a framework hinged on a latent embedding for different fidelity models and associated pre-posterior analysis, which explicitly utilizes their correlation for adaptive sampling. In this framework, each infill sampling iteration includes two steps: first, we identify the location of interest with the greatest potential improvement using the high-fidelity (HF) model; second, we search for the next sample across all fidelity levels that maximizes the improvement per unit cost at that specific location. This process is facilitated by a single Latent Variable Gaussian Process (LVGP) model that maps different fidelity models into an interpretable latent space, thereby capturing their correlations without assuming hierarchical fidelity levels. The LVGP enables us to assess how LF sampling candidates affect the HF response via pre-posterior analysis and determine the next sample with the best benefit-to-cost ratio. Through test cases, we demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms benchmark methods in both MF global fitting and Bayesian Optimization problems regarding convergence rate and robustness. Moreover, the method offers the flexibility to switch between global fitting and Bayesian Optimization by simply changing the acquisition function.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::38: Cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum, which are secondary lesions induced by significant increases in cytokine levels within the brain, are typically associated with subarachnoid hemorrhage, yet their precise clinical significance in patients suffering from subarachnoid hemorrhage remains unclear. By retrospectively analyzing subarachnoid hemorrhage patients treated in our hospital, we evaluated the differences in backgrounds, clinical findings, and outcomes between individuals who developed these lesions and those who did not, while further comparing patients achieving good outcomes against those experiencing poor ones. Using multivariate logistic regression analysis to identify risk factors for poor clinical outcomes, we analyzed 159 patients, finding that 17 individuals, or 10.7 percent, exhibited cytotoxic lesions. Patients manifesting these lesions were more likely to be in a severe condition, as indicated by World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies grading IV-V, with an odds ratio of 4.53, and were significantly more prone to having an intraventricular, with an odds ratio of 5.98, or an intraparenchymal hematoma, with an odds ratio of 3.62. Furthermore, these patients demonstrated a greater propensity for a poor outcome three months after onset, evidenced by a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2, yielding an odds ratio of 0.22. Multivariate analysis confirmed that the presence of cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum increased the risk of a poor outcome, showing an odds ratio of 4.39. While the development of such lesions may be related to the extent of hematomas in subarachnoid hemorrhage patients and these findings are usually considered reversible, the presence of these cytotoxic lesions of the corpus callosum may ultimately serve as a critical, independent predictor of poor clinical outcomes in patients suffering from subarachnoid hemorrhage.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::39: Because information regarding the appropriate protocols for the sedation of Nordestino donkeys remains notably scarce, this blinded, randomised, crossover experiment was conducted to evaluate the sedative and cardiorespiratory effects of low doses of intravenous xylazine, administered both with and without acepromazine, in seven healthy female Nordestino donkeys weighing 150 ± 18 kg. The study involved four distinct treatments, each consisting of two intravenous injections administered at baseline and fifteen minutes later, specifically comprising acepromazine 0.05 mg/kg bwt with saline, saline with xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt, acepromazine with xylazine 0.25 mg/kg bwt, or acepromazine with xylazine 0.5 mg/kg bwt. Sedative and cardiorespiratory parameters were systematically evaluated before the initial injection and at subsequent intervals up to ninety minutes post-treatment. While the main investigator assessed the degree of sedation via head height above ground, the quality of sedation through ataxia and visual analogue scale scoring, and the respiratory rate in situ, an assistant investigator concurrently measured heart rates, supplemented by three experienced evaluators who assessed recorded videos for ataxia and stimulus responses. Data analysis utilized repeated measures ANOVA for normal distributions and Kruskal-Wallis tests for non-normal data, revealing that head height was significantly lower than baseline for fifteen minutes after xylazine in the AX0.25 group and for thirty minutes in the SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups. Although all xylazine treatments increased visual analogue scale and ataxia scores for fifteen minutes, reflecting a notable absence of a negative saline-saline control group, it was observed that acepromazine added to xylazine at 0.25 mg/kg bwt produced considerably briefer and milder sedation than the higher 0.5 mg/kg bwt xylazine dosage, with ataxia scores being higher in the SX0.5 and AX0.5 groups compared to the acepromazine-saline group for specific durations.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::40: By imaging fifteen massive protoclusters down to a resolution of two thousand astronomical units, the ALMA-IMF survey identified approximately one thousand star-forming cores, yet determining their fundamental physical characteristics—specifically mass and luminosity—remains difficult, a problem that is significantly exacerbated given that these protoclusters are located at distances exceeding two kiloparsecs. To characterize these cores, we combined novel datasets with radiative transfer modeling, thereby estimating both their mass-averaged temperatures and the masses those estimates imply. For one-sixth of the total sample, we measured bolometric luminosities, implementing necessary deblending corrections while utilizing spectral energy distribution analysis obtained through the PPMAP Bayesian procedure, which is specifically designed to preserve the highest possible angular resolution of the input data. By extrapolating the luminosity and dust temperature images provided by PPMAP at 2.5 arcsecond resolution to estimate the values of individual cores identified at higher resolution, we applied approximate radiative transfer relationships linking the luminosity of a protostar to its surrounding envelope temperature and the external heating of prestellar cores to their internal temperatures. Consequently, we provide the first data-informed dust temperature estimates for 883 cores: 17-31 K and 28-79 K for the 617 prestellar and 266 protostellar cores, respectively, alongside protostellar luminosities spanning 20-80,000 solar luminosities. Although we estimated systematically lower temperatures for hot cores than studies based on complex organic molecules, we successfully established a mass-luminosity evolutionary diagram for a large sample of high-mass protostellar cores at their native spatial resolution. Ultimately, the ALMA-IMF data favor a compelling scenario in which protostars accrete their mass from a significantly larger reservoir than that provided by their immediate host cores, suggesting complex environmental interactions during the critical early stages of massive star formation.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::41: The aim of the present study, which sought to investigate the role of microRNA (miR)-27a-3p in osteoarthritis (OA), utilized reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction and western blotting to determine the expression of miR-27a-3p and aggrecanase-2 (ADAMTS5) in cartilage tissues derived from patients with OA and healthy controls, as well as in interleukin (IL)-1beta-treated primary human chondrocytes that had been transfected with miR-27a-3p. A luciferase reporter assay, which was employed to validate the direct contact between miR-27a-3p and its putative binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA, was complemented by the evaluation of IL-1beta-induced activation of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) and nuclear factor (NF)-kappaB on miR-27a-3p using specific inhibitors. Results revealed that the level of miR-27a-3p was reduced in OA cartilage tissues compared with normal controls, while decreased miR-27a-3p and increased ADAMTS5 expression were observed in a time- and dose-dependent manner in chondrocytes treated with IL-1beta. Furthermore, overexpression of miR-27a-3p suppressed the expression of ADAMTS5 in human chondrocytes induced by IL-1beta, and this overexpression also decreased the luciferase activity of the wild-type ADAMTS5 reporter plasmid, whereas mutation of the miR-27a-3p binding site in the 3'-untranslated region of ADAMTS5 mRNA abolished the miR-27a-3p-mediated repression of reporter activity. Specific inhibitors demonstrated that IL-1beta may regulate miR-27a-3p expression via NF-kappaB and MAPK signaling pathways in chondrocytes. The present study concluded that miR-27a-3p, which was downregulated in human OA and suppressed by IL-1beta, functions as a crucial regulator of ADAMTS5 in OA chondrocytes, with IL-1beta-mediated suppression of miR-27a-3p activity occurring via MAPK and NF-kappaB pathways, potentially providing a novel strategy for clinical treatment of OA caused by the upregulation of miR-27a-3p.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::42: Space weathering, which acts as a fundamental process modifying the surfaces of airless planetary bodies, is primarily driven by solar wind irradiation and micrometeoroid bombardment, both of which significantly alter planetary reflectance spectra while frequently obscuring vital compositional diagnostic features. In this study, we focused on simulating and comparing the spectral transformations induced by these two distinct agents to gain a clearer understanding of their individual contributions. By utilizing olivine and pyroxene pellets as proxies for planetary materials, we simulated solar wind irradiation through the application of hydrogen, helium, and argon ions with energies ranging from 5 to 40 keV and fluences reaching $10^{18}$ particles/cm$^2$, while micrometeoroid bombardment was modeled using individual femtosecond laser pulses. We analyzed the subsequent evolution of various spectral parameters, determined by applying the Modified Gaussian Model, and further conducted a principal component analysis. Our findings indicate that the original mineralogy of the surface exerts a more profound influence on spectral evolution than the specific weathering agent itself, a conclusion supported by the diverse evolution of the spectral slope observed in olivine versus pyroxene upon irradiation. Notably, the spectral slope changes detected in olivine align with observations of A-type asteroids, whereas the moderate or absent slope changes in pyroxene remain consistent with asteroid (4) Vesta. Furthermore, we observed subtle differences in the spectral effects induced by each agent; specifically, ions simulating solar wind exert less influence on longer wavelengths than the laser irradiation simulating micrometeoroid impacts, likely reflecting the varying penetration depths of ions and laser pulses. Ultimately, our results suggest that it may be possible to distinguish between the contributions of these two agents on a weathered surface.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::43: HEALPix, as established by Gorski et al. in 2005, serves as the de-facto standard for Cosmic Microwave Background data storage and analysis, being widely utilized throughout current and upcoming experiments, with almost all datasets residing in the Legacy Archive for Microwave Background Data Analysis employing it as their format of choice. Because visualizing this data plays an important role in research, several toolsets, most notably the original Fortran facilities and Python integration via healpy, were developed; however, given the current state of GPU performance, it is now possible to visualize extremely large maps in real time on a portable laptop or tablet. The HEALPix Viewer described here, which was developed specifically for macOS, takes full advantage of GPU acceleration to handle extremely large datasets in real time, compiling natively on Intel and Arm64 architectures while utilizing the Metal framework for high-performance computations. The aim of this project, which seeks to reduce the effort required for interactive data exploration as well as the time overhead for producing publication-quality maps, includes drag and drop integration with Keynote and Powerpoint to facilitate presentation creation. The main codebase is written in Swift—a modern, efficient, compiled language—with high-performance computing parts delegated entirely to the GPU alongside a few inserts in C that interface with the cfitsio library for I/O, while the graphical user interface utilizes SwiftUI, a new declarative framework. Since most common spherical projections and colormaps are supported out of the box, the available source code makes it easy to customize the application or add new features, with overall performance improving on the current Python software stack by a factor of 3 to 180x, depending entirely on the task at hand.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::44: This prospective cohort study, which was conducted at Ramathibodi Hospital in Bangkok, Thailand, aimed to compare cervical shear wave elastography (SWE) utilizing transvaginal ultrasound (TVS) between twin and singleton pregnant women. Participants who fulfilled the specific inclusion criteria underwent serial measurements of shear wave speed (SWS) via TVS during the early, mid-, and third trimesters, allowing researchers to evaluate the longitudinal changes in SWS relative to advancing gestational age. Furthermore, the study analyzed gestational age at delivery alongside the rate of spontaneous preterm birth. Among the total cohort of 36 twin pregnancies and 38 singleton pregnancies, no significant differences in baseline characteristics were observed, with the notable exception of participant age, which averaged 33.1±4.6 years for twins and 29.9±5.4 years for singletons (p=0.006). Although cervical SWS decreased consistently as gestational age advanced in both cohorts, a statistically significant difference emerged at the lower point during the mid-trimester, where twin pregnancies measured 2.27±0.4 m/s compared to 2.71±0.6 m/s for singletons (p=0.001). Conversely, no significant disparities were demonstrated at the upper or lower points during the early and third trimesters. While gestational age at delivery differed significantly between the two groups—averaging 35.9±2.8 weeks for twins versus 37.6±2.9 weeks for singletons (p=0.008)—the spontaneous preterm delivery rate remained statistically comparable at 22.2% and 15.8% respectively (p=0.483). Ultimately, mid-trimester cervical SWS measurements taken at the lower point effectively detect variations in cervical softness between these pregnancy types, suggesting that cervical SWS might serve as a valuable additional option for clinicians monitoring the progression of cervical softness in twin pregnancies throughout the course of gestation.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::45: Chromosome number, which serves as a key feature of the higher-order organization of the genome, represents a fundamental factor in evolution, wherein dysploid gains and losses, alongside polyploidization events, potentially drive reproductive isolation and lineage diversification. Although the recent development of probabilistic models of chromosome number evolution, exemplified by the groundbreaking work of Mayrose et al. (2010, ChromEvol), has enabled the inference of ancestral chromosome numbers over molecular phylogenies while generating renewed interest in the field, the ChromEvol approach assumes all changes occur anagenetically along branches, failing to model events that are specifically cladogenetic—changes one might expect if chromosomal shifts result in reproductive isolation. Here, we present a new class of models, termed ChromoSSE, which incorporates both anagenetic and cladogenetic change, allowing us to determine the primary mode of evolution: is it occurring within lineages, at lineage splitting, or through clade-specific combinations? Furthermore, we can estimate the location and timing of potential chromosome speciation events across the phylogeny. We implemented ChromoSSE within a Bayesian statistical framework, specifically utilizing the software RevBayes to accommodate uncertainty in parameter estimates while leveraging the full power of likelihood-based methods. Having tested ChromoSSE’s accuracy via simulations, we re-examined chromosomal evolution in Aristolochia, Carex section Spirostachyae, Helianthus, Mimulus sensu lato (s.l.), and Primula section Aleuritia, ultimately finding evidence for clade-specific combinations of anagenetic and cladogenetic dysploid and polyploid modes of chromosome evolution. Keywords: Anagenetic; Bayes factors; chromosome evolution; chromosome speciation; chromoSSE; cladogenetic; dysploidy; phylogenetic models; polyploidy; reversible-jump Markov chain Monte Carlo; whole genome duplication. This comprehensive analytical framework provides the necessary tools for resolving complex evolutionary patterns that were previously inaccessible to researchers studying the intricate dynamics of genome architecture across diverse plant lineages.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::46: We present results of our time variability studies concerning Mg II and Al III absorption lines within a sample of 22 Low Ionization Broad Absorption Line QSOs, which are positioned at 0.2 <= zem <= 2.1, using the 2m telescope at the IUCAA Girawali Observatory over a time-scale spanning 10 days to 7.69 years in the QSO's rest frame. Spectra are analysed in conjunction with photometric light curves, which were obtained from the Catalina Real-Time Transient Survey. Long time-scale absorption line variability, defined as being equal to or greater than one year, is observed in 8 cases, representing 36% of systems, while only 4 of them, constituting 18% of systems, show variability over short time-scales of less than one year. We notice a tendency for highly variable LoBAL QSOs to exhibit high ejection velocity, low equivalent width, and low redshift. The detection rate of variability in LoBAL QSOs showing Fe fine-structure lines is significantly less than that seen in non-Fe LoBAL QSOs. Absorption line variability is more frequently detected in QSOs having a continuum dominated by Fe emission lines compared to the rest of the QSOs. Confirming these trends with a bigger sample will provide vital clues for understanding the physical distinction between different BAL QSO sub-classes. We correlate the absorption line variability with various parameters derived from continuum light curves, finding no clear correlation between continuum flux and absorption line variabilities. However, sources with large absorption line variability also show large variability in their light curves. We also see appearance or disappearance of absorption components in 2 cases and clear indications for profile variations in 4 cases, with the observed variability best explained by a combination of processes driven by continuum variations and clouds transiting across the line of sight.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::47: Because the Halpha nebular emission line serves as an optimal tracer for recent star formation within galaxies, its recent emergence as an observable feature at redshifts exceeding three, facilitated by the advent of JWST, represents a significant scientific milestone. We present a comprehensive catalog comprising 1013 Halpha emitters identified at 3.7<z<6.7 within the GOODS fields, which we obtained through a blind search of JWST NIRCam/grism data. By utilizing the FRESCO survey’s 124 arcmin^2 of observations in GOODS-North and GOODS-South with the F444W filter, which probes Halpha at 4.9<z<6.7, alongside the CONGRESS survey’s 62 arcmin^2 in GOODS-North with F356W, probing Halpha at 3.8<z<5.1, we identify an overdensity featuring 97 sources at z~4.4 in GOODS-N while confirming previously reported overdensities at z~5.2 in GOODS-N and at z~5.4 and z~5.9 in GOODS-S. We compute the observed Halpha luminosity functions in three bins centered at z~4.45, 5.30, and 6.15, representing the first such measurements at z>3 obtained purely from spectroscopic data, thereby robustly tracing galaxy star formation rates beyond the peak of cosmic history. Comparing our results with theoretical predictions from three distinct simulations reveals good agreement at z~4-6, while the UV luminosity functions of this spectroscopically-confirmed sample align well with pre-JWST measurements from photometrically-selected objects. Finally, by deriving star formation rate functions and integrating these to compute the evolution of cosmic star-formation rate densities across z~4-6, we find values consistent with recent UV estimates from Lyman-break galaxies, implying a continuous decrease in density by a factor of 3x over this epoch. Our work demonstrates the power of NIRCam grism observations to efficiently provide new tests for early galaxy formation models based on emission line statistics.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::48: Numerous studies have revealed that oxidative stress is closely associated with the occurrence and development of depression, and while Xiaoyao Pills, which are included in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, are frequently used for treating anxiety and depression by smoothing the liver, strengthening the spleen, and nourishing the blood, their specific antidepressant effects have not yet been thoroughly investigated. Consequently, the objective of our study was to investigate the antidepressant-like effects of XYW and the underlying molecular mechanism in the olfactory bulbectomized rat model of depression, utilizing the open field test, sucrose preference test, splash test, and novelty suppressed feeding test. Results showed that XYW, administered at 0.93 and 1.86 g·kg -1, significantly alleviated depression-like behaviors in rats, as indicated by increased sucrose preference in the SPT, prolonged grooming time in the ST, decreased horizontal movement in the OFT, and shorter feeding latency in the NSFT. In addition, XYW treatment dramatically reversed the reduced activity of superoxide dismutase and the decreased level of glutathione, while simultaneously lowering levels of malondialdehyde, the inflammatory mediator nitric oxide, and pro-inflammatory cytokines like interleukin-6 and 1β in the serum and cortex of OB rats. Mechanistically, XYW induced marked upregulation of mRNA and protein expression levels of NFE2L2, KEAP1, GPX3, HMOX1, SOD1, NQO1, OGG1, PIK3CA, p-AKT1/AKT1, NTRK2, and BDNF, while facilitating the downregulation of ROS in the cortex and hippocampus via the activation of the NFE2L2/KEAP1, PIK3CA/AKT1, and NTRK2/BDNF pathways. These findings suggest that XYW exert antidepressant-like effects in OB rats with depression-like symptoms, effects mediated by the alleviation of oxidative stress and the enhancement of neuroprotective processes through the deliberate activation of the PIK3CA-AKT1-NFE2L2/BDNF signaling pathways.
syntax_complex.academic_abstracts::49: We report the discovery of 16 detached M-dwarf eclipsing binaries with J<16 mag, providing a detailed characterisation of three of them by using high-precision infrared light curves from the WFCAM Transit Survey (WTS). Because such systems provide the most accurate and model-independent method for measuring the fundamental parameters of these poorly understood yet numerous stars, which currently lack sufficient observations to calibrate stellar evolution models precisely, we have fully solved for the masses and radii of three systems. We found orbital periods in the range 1.5<P<4.9 days, with masses spanning 0.35-0.50 Msun and radii between 0.38-0.50 Rsun, while uncertainties remain at ~3.5-6.4% in mass and ~2.7-5.5% in radius. Close-companions in short-period binaries, being expected to be tidally-locked into fast rotational velocities, exhibit high levels of magnetic activity, a phenomenon predicted to inflate their radii by inhibiting convective flow and increasing star spot coverage. The radii of the WTS systems are inflated above model predictions by ~3-12%, which remains in agreement with the observed trend despite an expected lower systematic contribution from star spots signals at infrared wavelengths. Having searched for a correlation between the orbital period and radius inflation by combining our results with all existing M-dwarf radius measurements of comparable precision, we found no statistically significant evidence for a decrease in radius inflation for longer period, less active systems. Radius inflation continues to exist in non-synchronised systems, indicating that the problem remains even for very low activity M-dwarfs. Resolving this issue is vital not only for understanding the most populous stars in the Universe, but also for characterising their planetary companions, which hold the best prospects for finding Earth-like planets in the traditional habitable zone.

6. Video quality remains impressive on a standard television, offering various pre-defined picture modes or customization options for tech-savvy enthusiasts, though if you struggle with indecision, it is best to ignore this specific feature.

7. While the player is chock full of myriad options, you must explore them independently, which can prove confusing until you master the interface—though reading the manual, as noted in Item 1, offers little solace.

9. I cannot comment on the progressive scan feature, as I do not yet possess an HD or HD-ready television, being still in the process of waiting for that inevitable lottery win.

10. Although it is designed to play DVD-Audio discs, you require 6.1 channel inputs on your receiver; unfortunately, our receiver lacks these specific inputs, just as I currently lack any DVD-Audio discs to play.

Electronics buffs would likely argue that it requires extensive tweaking to achieve perfection, yet it sounds wonderful to me. All things considered, it is a very good player, perhaps even excellent when you factor in the modest price.

Amanda Richards, October 1, 2004

syntax_complex.writingprompts::1: This is the end, isn't it? The thought struck Josh suddenly, almost by accident, piercing through and dissolving his frustration with the car that had allowed him to break down so far from home, with the phone company that had neglected to build towers by this barren desert road, and with the sun that had audaciously beaten him, sweaty and tired, to the ground. This is the end. This thought in particular remained prominent in his mind, even as he realized that he had already seen Heather for the last time, and Joey, who was still so proud about that geometry test, and Dale, and the business Dale would inherit, the business that would serve as an unexpected legacy. This is it. Dale, who had told him that this trip was a fool's errand, and made a joke about what he would say at Josh's funeral, failed to shake the thought from Josh's head. The end of... The thought lingered there, static, for a time that Josh wasn't able to comprehend, while everything else in his mind seemed to fade away, from his periphery, inward toward this single, solitary idea. This is the end of me. When nothing else was left, Josh found it fitting that this idea of finality should itself be his final thought. But it wasn't. It vanished as abruptly as it came, and then, Josh would have cried, if he was still physically capable. His regrets came flooding back all at once, alongside his anger, his sorrow, and his despondency at his own powerlessness, for the tranquil peace of the end was over, replaced with the angst of a life incomplete, a life that had failed to come to terms with itself. And then Josh felt fear, a fear like he had never felt before, the terror of fate incarnate, of the great unknown for which he was utterly unprepared, as the sheer and total horror overwhelmed his memory, his pain, and all his other emotions, and that fear was the last thing Josh thought about.

Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave, the Moral Officer bellowed into his bullhorn, and I found it heartening because the ending, being so near, gave me the strength to push my weak and weary body to shovel faster, ever faster. All around me, my fellow citizens dug in the dust, which resembled brittle dry dirt, while scratching out the precise place where they would eventually give their bodies back to the earth. In the distance, other Moral Officers made their proclamations into identical bullhorns, while at regular intervals throughout the field, Compliance Officers stood in immaculate uniforms, waiting patiently to aid us in our final duty to the Nation.

It had become clear that there was a food shortage well before the State officially announced it, as everyone had whispered about how the weekly rations they picked up from the distribution station seemed to be smaller every week, even though the center's Party workers would deny it if anyone dared to ask. Then, the whispers turned to fully voiced complaints when items began disappearing from the rations, never to reappear again, until soon, meat had almost become a memory and fully grown, healthy-looking vegetables were incredibly rare.

When the State News Agency, in a special broadcast, finally announced the famine, nobody was surprised, for we were instructed that we must, as always, stand united, strong, and proud in the face of this Straining Test. Everyone was told they must do their part to bear this burden so that our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle and emerge triumphant. Even the Beloved Ruler was rationing his consumption, we were told, and it was clear, yes, undoubtedly clear, that this was some ploy by the dissidents and the outsiders who were attempting to destroy our resolve and make us turn back from the ideas of the revolution. They had sabotaged our fields and murdered our animals, but we would stay strong in our virtue and would emerge, as ever, triumphant.

It was then that they announced the lottery, stating that a number of citizens would be randomly selected from the population to give a glorious sacrifice of faith and virtue for the Nation to help ease the burden of consumption. Those who were selected were informed the next day by a soldier showing up at their door to take them away from their families, and I was one of the chosen.

A shout rang out across the fields, "May my body fertilize the soil to feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler," and a gunshot punctuated this declaration, meaning someone had already finished their grave. A few others cheered their assent, though most were too weary and hungry to manage. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol and motioned for the now-dead man's two neighbors to fill in the grave he now occupied.

They had worked us hard after taking us away, forcing us to shovel out a roadway, and because we slept where we worked, the only sustenance given to us was a broth so thin that they could hardly justify calling it more than hot water, and so the last of the strength of our bodies was harvested.

My grave now looked deep enough, but I hesitated before raising up my shovel to call over the Compliance Officer, because if it was not deep enough for his liking, I would have to wait until all others had finished covering over their graves before it would finally be my turn. He came over and produced a tape measurer, checked the dimensions, and nodded his assent, so I let out an inaudible sigh of relief and went to stand at the foot of my grave, knowing the time was here—the time for my glorious sacrifice for the sake of the Nation and the time for my final duty to my beloved land. 

"Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave," the Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn. I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer's pistol come to rest upon my forehead. "Citizens will not be allowed..."

Standing at his side, Daniel’s wife was visibly coming apart at the edges, although, had anyone other than him been observing her with such intimate scrutiny, they likely would have failed to perceive the subtle fractures in her composure. Perhaps it was an exaggeration to label her state as a complete collapse, yet she was undeniably anxious, exhibiting that peculiar, rhythmic twitch of the nose which never manifested whenever she was truly calm.

Imani, he called out, and her head tipped down toward where he was seated in silent acknowledgement of his presence. It is going to be fine, he insisted, offering her a weak smile that failed to reach his eyes before he reached out to clasp her hand. While he voiced these words primarily to comfort her, he honestly believed that everything would be alright, for they had already navigated the most treacherous passages of their ordeal. He had survived the catastrophic car accident, subsequently enduring the complex surgery intended to ensure that the universe would not capriciously alter its course, and later, he had even survived the amputations and the subsequent integration of his implants. With a deliberate roll of his eyes, he squeezed her hand in return, stating that this phase was honestly the easiest part, as they possessed an abundance of time.

The easy part? Since when have we ever been granted the luxury of an easy path? she retorted, reaching out to playfully swat his ears while her eyes crinkled with genuine mirth. That sentiment is surely comparable to asking what could possibly go wrong, she scolded, urging him not to jinx their progress. Just as he leaned in to explain that such persistent worrying would yield no benefits, the door slammed open, with the solid, resonant thump echoing throughout the expansive room.

Oops, the tall man standing in the doorway remarked, looking rather sheepish as he admitted to having tripped into the door. How are you two faring today? he inquired in a friendly manner, striding into the room while the sunlight streaming through the windows illuminated his lanky form. Are you ready to give it another attempt? Daniel flexed his legs, which were neatly and securely fastened into his new running blades.

Ever since the exact second that I fastened these on, Mason! he replied earnestly, and the easygoing man offered him a thumbs-up before extending his hands.

That is precisely what we desire to hear, so let us proceed with getting you up and moving, Mason encouraged. After casting one final look at his wife, who stood back with an apprehensive expression while keeping her fingers crossed, Daniel reached for the other man’s outstretched hands. These were the fourth pair of running blades he had attempted to utilize, as the previous iterations had been plagued by persistent issues despite their purportedly custom-made designs. Some were far too long, others were too short, and while some caused him physical pain, others felt as though they were destined to detach entirely. However, as Daniel wobbled to his feet, he instinctively recognized that these were the correct ones. It required a moment for him to steady himself, as these blades possessed a distinct quality of balance and elasticity compared to his standard prosthetic, and his overall physical fitness had not yet attained the level he desired. His heart raced rapidly as he shifted his weight from one foot to the other, listening intently to the blades flexing in response. Left, right, left, right, left, right—each movement resulted in a bounce. They felt entirely unlike his original legs, but, simultaneously, they felt entirely right. Slowly, Mason released his grip and retreated to the far side of the room, his eyes never wavering from Daniel. Upon reaching the wall, he called out, Great! Now, begin with a walk and gradually accelerate to a pace that you feel comfortable maintaining. A sly tone crept into his voice as he added, And remember, the room is padded and we are all friends here, so face plants are absolutely nothing to worry about. Daniel scoffed at the implication, as if he would ever allow such instruments to overcome him. Feeling confident, he took a shaky step forward, his arms wheeling for a moment until he braced his core to maintain his equilibrium. Then, he took another step, followed by another, and soon he had settled into a slow, bobbing jog, carefully navigating the space between his wife and his physical therapist. He continued this motion until, finally, Mason signaled for him to stop. Mason sprinted across the room toward the happy couple with an expression of great excitement.

It appears that we have finally succeeded! he exclaimed. After stepping back to offer one final, thorough inspection, he noted that they only needed to conduct a few more tests to ensure that everything was adjusted correctly, yet he remained confident that they had discovered the golden pair. So, how do you truly feel?

As he turned inward, his mind began to wander, desperately searching for the words that could even begin to encapsulate the depth of his emotions. He thought only of the things he had assumed were lost forever when he hazily awakened from surgery on that fateful day, looking down to witness the sheet cave in where his lower legs had once been. He recalled the sound of the crowd screaming his name as he tore down the field, the heady sensation of sprinting along a track, and the way the world narrowed into near-blackness as he pushed himself to his absolute limits. He remembered the lightness of a casual game of tag with his wife, catching thin air as she slipped past him with laughter dancing in her eyes. Bouncing on his new legs once more, he felt weightless, even invincible. With a strength he had not possessed in a long time, he hugged Imani and spoke over her head, his face aching with the intensity of his smile: Alive.

Let it be known that I performed absolutely no research on the subject for such a quiet piece, relying instead upon memory and educated guessing; therefore, if any details are terribly inaccurate, that is the reason.

I mounted my horse and started down the steep slope, yelling at the top of my lungs to get their immediate attention. The would-be bandit looked at me with a scowl, letting out a yell of his own, and immediately a dozen more men and women, dressed in that same ragged fashion, were bearing down on the carriage with their weapons drawn. I knew there were far too many for me to handle alone, but I simply could not bear the thought of letting those poor people die at the hands of these brutes. As I reached the bottom of the incline, I remembered that my friend from Winterhold, who is admittedly a bit of a nutty one, had given me a magic scroll before I set out on my journey. Let me say now that I am no mage; sure, I tried to find some magics that would make me more handsome, but none of that worked anyway. I was pretty sure that I merely had to open the scroll and read it, but I had no idea what it actually did, though I hoped it would summon one of those big Atronachs my friend was always talking about, as he made them out to be something near god-like, and I certainly would not mind having one of those on my side. I started out thinking they were cannibals when I saw them attacking, but I heard their story and realized they were just trying to get by. Lord Aerlman looked crestfallen, idly picking up a picture from the fireplace mantle—a family portrait depicting the lord and his wife alongside their daughter, a striking redhead in her late teens—and he caressed the image with his thumb before setting it back down. All of the energy drained from his body, and he sagged, turning toward the woman with a beaten, defeated look. Fine, do it, make the call. He dismissed her with a wave and sank into one of the large leather chairs, pouring himself a generous whiskey which he immediately downed. As he poured another, Laura excused herself and closed the door quietly, for she had an important phone call to make. Antonia, I know you are here. The same girl from the photo, now a fully-grown and beautiful young woman, was hiding behind a large stack of pallets, desperately clutching herself and attempting to refrain from screaming. Her hands and torso were saturated in blood, some of which was her own, while the rest belonged to her friends. They had been partying and drinking in her London flat when the man arrived. The first indication of trouble was the door exploding inward, a large splintering piece of it ripping through Pierce like a spear. He dropped with a gurgling sound as blood sprayed across the room. Screams erupted from the small group of young men and women, and before they could even process the sudden danger, a small man, barely five feet six inches tall, was in their midst, wielding a large curved sword in one hand and a handgun in the other. Glowing runes twisted across his skin, and his left eye was obscured by an eyepatch, while his right eye, the color of polished metal, quickly scanned the chaotic room. Everything after that moment was a blur, and Antonia could not recall any specific details, except for the bodies and the blood. She remembered a voice in her head, followed by her friends screaming, fire pouring from their eyes as they charged the sword-bearing man while shouting in some language Antonia had never heard. As her friends threw themselves at the man, she turned and leapt through the bay window, falling three stories and landing with a sickening crunch. She remembered her legs feeling surprisingly good for such a fall, and then she began running. The voice in her head was louder, and though she could not understand it, it was causing her immense pain. As she ran through the streets, the voice was chanting, and every person she passed turned to stare at her, their eyes spewing fire before they turned and charged the way she had come. She did not understand what was happening, who the man was, or why he was pursuing her; she did not understand anything at all. The next thing she knew, she was hiding in the warehouse, where the man found her again, his curved sword and gun both covered in blood. As she curled up and tried to remain hidden, he kept talking.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::13: Lamb, tell me a story, the Wolf remarked, his voice dripping with a smug, predatory quality while a cruel smile stretched across his face, adding that he craved something sweet.
