syntax_complex.writingprompts::50:
A wise man, in a rare attempt at humor, once remarked that heaven was eating pâté de foie gras to the sound of trumpets, according to a page from the journal of a chef who has recently deceased. As a chef, I wholly agree with the choice of foie gras, although I have never possessed much of an ear for the blare of trumpets. Foie gras, for those who are uninitiated—and do not worry, as many remain so—is a culinary dish as ancient as the very art of cooking itself. Foie gras, which is French for fat liver, represents the pièce de résistance for any self-respecting chef. To prepare it, one must take a duck, or perhaps a goose, though a duck is utilized more frequently; one must cage the bird, ensuring it has no room to move, because movement will inevitably ruin the delicate texture of the organ. One must then take it by the neck and pump corn, boiled previously in fat, down its gullet, repeating this process seven times a day until the creature is pumped plump. Once you kill the bird and remove the liver, a good chef would pay a wholesome price for it, preparing it with mustard, honey, diced onions, and balsamic vinegar, for never has anything been so truly delectable. You see, it is not the taste that repulses people, but rather the process involved. The question of whether the end justifies the means is one often asked; the answer is no if you are talentless or lack a discerning palate, but yes, a thousand times yes, if you believe me, for anyone would scream in affirmation if they only tried my particular foie gras. But then again, mine is inherently different; mine is demonstrably better.

They say that beauty is only skin deep, which is true, yet taste is far shallower. I am a chef—a good chef, not a good man, but I reiterate: a good chef. If I had been born a painter and my only source of red pigment was the blood of the innocent, do not doubt for a single moment that I would paint in red. Of course, I was not born a painter, but I was born a chef—a good chef. Foie gras, as most chefs prepare it, is illegal in many countries, including the UK, Germany, and Italy, to name a few; needless to say, I do not derive my recipes from law books. Foie gras, as I make it, is illegal in every country. The Pope once denounced foie gras as cruel, though that was, of course, before he sampled mine, which is different and significantly better. A cardinal told me once that if God were to return to earth, He would ensure I was the one cooking, while another confessed that he once denounced my dish, though he now offered a thousand apologies, having sampled the bliss from the supple marinated flesh on his tongue, which he found greater than all the sufferance of all the geese and ducks that God has ever endeavored to create. They were in total awe of me, for anyone I convince to suspend their morals will, at the moment of contact with my foie gras, be in awe of me. People would kill for a spoonful—good, pious, moral people—and I would sell out if I charged a million per pound, but I do not. I do not do it for power or riches; I do it for the art. I am a chef—a good chef, not a good man, but I reiterate: a good chef. My recipe is worth kingdoms; my dish has made kings weak at the knees, so weak that they kneel before me, the Chef. My legacy will be my recipe, and if you are reading this, congratulations, for you have inherited it. Here it is: take a baby, whether you abduct, buy, or steal it, for it makes no difference. Any foundling or orphan will suffice, regardless of gender or race, though they must be newborn, innocent, and succulent. Cage it, denying it all room, as movement ruins the texture. Take it by the neck and pump corn boiled in fat down its gullet seven times a day until it is plump; two months should suffice. Add a pinch of salt and an ounce of butter per pint of corn, using two pints of fat per pint of corn, as lard is best with higher Linoleic acid. When slaughtered, take the liver and prepare it as you are qualified, perhaps marinating it in honey, mustard seed, cooked sesame seeds, diced red onions, and a thimble full of rum.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::51:
Creeping stealthily back up the stairs from the kitchen, Kai navigated the darkness, fully aware that being discovered by his parents would be catastrophic, though being caught specifically with the leftover broccoli, which Mom had intended to serve for dinner the following evening, would certainly be far worse; fortunately for him, he would not be forced to consume any of that dreaded vegetable. After closing his bedroom door firmly behind him, the six-year-old proceeded directly to his closet, which he boldly opened, beaming at the amorphous lump of eyes, hair, and writhing tentacles he discovered waiting inside. Here you go, Blergh, Kai whispered, and Blergh accepted the open Tupperware container with a single tentacle, emptying the entire contents into a mouth roughly the size of a basketball hoop before swallowing the mass whole; Kai could never discern whether the creature possessed teeth, yet the monster never bothered to chew. Kai began laying a trail of crackers across the floor, and, cajoled by the salty circles, the monster slowly emerged from the closet. Kai retrieved a box from his toy chest, dumping its contents onto the floor, and announced that they were playing army men tonight, to which Blergh merely grunted in agreement. Kai loved playing with Blergh because the creature could move numerous pieces simultaneously and excelled at pretending to be genuinely surprised whenever things supposedly blew up.

Julia had once been annoyed upon waking to find her son sleeping on the floor amid a scattered collection of plastic men waiting to be stepped on, but by now it had occurred so many times that feeling annoyed simply was not worth the effort. Wake up, sweetie, she said, softly shaking his shoulder, asking how Blergh was doing. As they walked toward the breakfast table, Julia settled in for yet another story about how Kai and his imaginary friend had conquered some great evil; children are truly so cute at that impressionable age.

Ten years later, Kai no longer had to sneak, for all boys his age eat significant quantities of food in the middle of the night, right? Kai sat before his X-Box, passing one bag of Doritos and one bottle of Mountain Dew to his left. Here you go, Blergh. Blergh grunted in gratitude before swallowing everything whole, as the dude still had not learned to chew. Blergh grunted again, using his many tentacles to simultaneously indicate the television, the three controllers held in his grasp, and the fourth resting at Kai's feet; they were prepared to play Call of Duty, and it was going to be another great night.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::52:
As the ship reached the beacon, the pilot, having exhausted his final reserves of jump fuel reaching this desolate sector, nervously activated his directional scanning equipment. Feeling an inexplicable chill while glancing out his viewing port, he dismissed the sensation as mere jump jitters; nevertheless, he routed critical power to his security drone. Because his sensors failed to detect anything, he realized, perhaps too late, that the effort was a waste of time, especially since he possessed far more pressing concerns, specifically the urgent necessity of locating additional fuel.

When the directional scanner finally pinged, it drew his attention toward a massive hull drifting at a distance from his vessel, a thick, swirling cloud of gas partially obscuring its frame. Because the ship remained entirely powered-down, the initial system scan had predictably failed to detect it, so he brought the impulse engines online and moved slowly toward the derelict vessel while simultaneously hailing the ship. Receiving no response was curious, yet abandoned vessels were not unheard of in these reaches. Far more unusual was the pristine condition of the ship, which lacked even a single dent. Although he had encountered abandoned hulls previously, they were invariably pocketed with scorch marks from laser blasts or short-range teleporters, as some sign of battle was always evident.

Briefly considering donning his EVA suit, he instead headed to the drone bay to take remote control of the security drone, which, while originally intended for boarding defense, could serve as an exploration unit in a pinch. Moments later, the drone slid through the airlock; a sleek machine armed to the teeth with an assortment of lasers and close-combat weapons that had saved the pilot's life more than once, it followed his internal schematics, making a beeline for engineering where any remaining fuel would surely be found. The problem with remotely controlling the drone was that it demanded the pilot’s full attention, causing him to overlook the fact that the airlock had not sealed, a malfunction he would have noticed had he been vigilant. His dying screams echoed as he was torn to pieces, for he should have known that giant alien spiders are no joke.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::53: My day commences in a manner indistinguishable from any other, for I require no alarm clock to rouse me from slumber, not that human temporal measurements possess any inherent significance within this realm. While the rapturous, high-pitched screams emanating from the cultists typically serve to awaken me, I am occasionally capable of sleeping through their cacophony, provided I endured a particularly arduous late shift previously. As I have noted, time remains exceedingly difficult to quantify here, especially since the celestial bodies—the sun, stars, and moon—behave in ways that defy all conventional logic. Nevertheless, one eventually grows accustomed to such irregularities, and Mister Cthulhu does not strictly concern himself with my specific sleeping schedule. Mind you, should I falter in my professional obligations, I risk having my soul devoured like a delicate eclair, with my discarded physical remains subsequently tossed into the abyssal spawning pool; however, having served faithfully for three years, I have not committed a single significant error. Upon inspecting the rear wall of my frigid obsidian dwelling, where Mister Cthulhu habitually deposits my daily instructions, I reliably discover a young woman pinned by a trident, her body writhing in ecstatic pleasure. Because my tasks are etched directly into her visage, I anticipate a relatively brief workday. Since Mister Cthulhu eliminated Death several years ago, mortality has effectively ceased, so I release the woman and retrieve the harpoon, noting my agenda. I must cleanse the interior of Yog-Sothoth’s temple, calibrate the salinity within the spawning pool, and administer antacids to the Hydra, who has been thrashing about for hours while ravaging coastal regions with tidal waves. I prioritize the Hydra, as Mister Cthulhu detests it when others inadvertently destroy his precious food source.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::54: Leaning against a concrete pillar situated within the expansive courtyard of a local high school, Elwood and Shara maintained a vigilant watch over Elwood's newest charge, an unassuming young man who bore the unremarkable name of Dale. Shara, while meticulously examining the sharp edges of her claws, inquired about the origins of this particular assignment, asking how Elwood had come to be tasked with such a mundane individual. Elwood, keeping his arms firmly crossed against his chest as he contemplated the situation, remarked that he was reasonably certain this assignment represented a softball pitch, a simple favor handed down to him by the management residing downstairs. As they spoke, a group of high school girls wandered over to the pillar, leaning against it with a casual air that allowed them to occupy the exact same physical space as the two demons. A sudden, powerful gust of wind unexpectedly blew the various papers and binders out of the hands of the girls, who shrieked in genuine surprise before scrambling frantically to chase after their scattered belongings. Shara, clearly annoyed by this intrusion, muttered that she would never truly get used to such interactions, adding that she did not care if they were technically capable of occupying the same space as mortals. Turning toward the girls, she held her arm out, claws positioned behind her thumb, and flicked them outwards with a sharp, deliberate snap, causing the books and papers to once again fly violently out of the shrieking girls' hands, prompting her to whisper, "Little wretches..." Meanwhile, Dale remained entirely oblivious, chewing on his bean and cheese burrito while observing the chaotic scene across the courtyard with the vacant, placid expression of a cow grazing in a field. Shara, perplexed by his lack of reaction, asked what was wrong with the kid, to which Elwood replied that he did not know, perhaps suggesting that the boy was simply stupid, before chewing on his own thumb for a moment while he strategized and suggested they jump through time directly to the sixth period. Shara gave Elwood a skeptical, sideways glance and raised an eyebrow, eventually agreeing to the plan. With a sound reminiscent of tearing canvas, they were transported instantly, coming to rest on a ledge located beneath the window at the back of Dale's sixth-period classroom. When Shara asked what his plan was, Elwood pressed a long-clawed finger to his lips, signaling silence, and as he did so, Dale's head hit the desk, rendering him immediately unconscious. Flinging his arms out wide and then bringing them together in a grand, sweeping gesture, Elwood forced every single student in the class to turn and face the sleeping Dale without uttering a single word. Shara noted that it was quite cute, and Elwood, smiling, declared that it was time to wake up, at which point every student in the room, speaking in a perfectly flat, synchronized tone, repeated the command in unison with him. Dale, his face half-slick with drool, sat up abruptly and rubbed his eyes, looking around at the class that was staring back at him. "Dale, it's time to wake up," the students and Elwood repeated, none of them blinking, and as Dale glanced from side to side in confusion, he muttered that he was awake. Elwood flung his arms apart, and the class resumed its normal activity, with no one except Dale having any memory of what had transpired. Shara, clearly unimpressed by the display, asked if that was his entire plan, while Dale, suddenly noticing that he was falling behind in his note-taking, began writing in a frantic hurry. Shara questioned if he was kidding, pointing out that such a daytime creep was not even three in the morning and was, in her opinion, genuinely creepy regardless of his defense. Elwood dismissed her, but Shara told him to look at the boy, noting that he had no clue that the event was out of the ordinary, and urged him to leave, flexing a claw over her shoulder as she walked away, silently begging for Elwood to follow. As they were departing through the wall, Elwood spun around and performed a sharp, bitch-slapping motion; Dale grunted as his head jerked forward, the loose tangles of hair at the back of his head flying upward, and his pencil shot out of his hand, bouncing off the back of the muscular student sitting in front of him. The girl sitting next to Dale looked at him with plain disgust and told him that he was such a weirdo, shifting in her small desk to move as far away from him as physically possible, a reaction that caused Shara to laugh. The two demons waited outside the classroom for the period to end, and when Dale finally emerged, walking slowly while looking down at his phone, Shara remarked that the process would be much easier in the nighttime. Elwood countered that it was not his style, explaining that one gets more genuine results during the day, because while anyone can be spooked at night, they are quick to forget it once the sun rises, and that what really freaks them out is a daytime haunting. Shara, offering no further comment, only yawned. When the bell signaled the end of the period, Dale was the last one out of the classroom, and Elwood, flapping his wings, dove into the phone. An alert popped up on the screen, and when Dale clicked to read it, Elwood jumped into full view, yelling "DAAAAAAAAAAAALE" through the speaker. Dale hit the power button and shoved the phone into his pocket, thinking that one of his friends was messing with his alerts again, and continued walking to his next class. Elwood stretched out of the phone like elastic with a pop and took his place next to Shara, confessing that he did not understand the kid, and when Shara asked if he was still insistent on the daytime, Elwood let out a heavy sigh and agreed to try it her way, causing them both to vanish with a sudden pop and sizzle. The two demons burst into the space above Dale's bed and stared down at him, gently flapping their wings, and when Elwood asked what she would do now, Shara gave a half-smile and extended her index claw, slowly curling it back into her palm, which caused the bed sheet covering Dale to be pulled off in perfect sync with the flexing of her finger. Dale only scratched his stomach and rolled over, leading Elwood to express his utter disbelief at the lack of scary results. She narrowed her eyes and shot a hand out to grab something in the air, causing Dale to scream in pain, and as she yanked her arm back, Dale flew off the foot of the bed and crashed against the wall, knocking several books off the shelf onto his head. Elwood's jaw dropped as he looked from Shara to Dale, telling her she had no subtlety at all, but she simply told him to watch. Dale stood up and replaced the books, and when his mom opened the door to ask if he was alright, he blamed a bad leg cramp. Shara threw her arms up in frustration, and Elwood, deciding he was finished with the kid, popped out of the air.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::55:
Unless I manage to possess a human being before the clock strikes noon, I fear that Satan shall grow exceedingly wrathful; indeed, the last time I attempted such a feat, I was struck with such immense force that I doubt I could have remained in flight for three consecutive days. Oh, that is it, Oglathor exclaimed aloud, causing his boss to inquire whether he had finally devised a method to resolve their ongoing financial crisis and vanquish their competitors. No, sir, I was merely thinking aloud, Oglathor replied, to which his boss retorted that they must all remember to possess someone before noon and wreak havoc upon something that He created, or else they would face execution by the lethal means of puppy licks, before declaring the meeting dismissed. Oh Satan, I know he will be furious, yet I have not violated the five codes of Hellfire, Chaos, and the manual on how to possess written by Iggy Azalea, who is the all-knowing witch-demon specializing in a genre of music that possesses everyone. Before departing upon the highway of hell, Oglathor purchased a darkblaze hot dog, which has been his favorite pastime snack since 1988.

Oh my Satan, who is that individual, and is she truly alone and capable of defending herself, or is there only one way to ascertain the truth, Oglathor wondered as he began singing Fancy by Iggy to attempt to possess her body and thereby destroy the human world. Ew, this human vessel is different, for I feel stressed and unable to communicate properly, and I cannot even fly, though that is of little consequence. Driven by the urge to walk home from school, Oglathor and his new body prepared to play the long game. Mommy, I am home, Oglathor said instinctively, and when his mother asked how she was feeling, he truthfully replied that she was not well and intended to lie down. Offering assistance, the mother told her to yell if she needed anything, though Oglathor wondered why he would ever do such a thing. Upon waking from a deep sleep, he found his white tights soaked in blood, a sign he had awaited to ruin the world, yet a twisted cramp interrupted his thoughts, forcing him to call for his mother, who explained that she had simply started her period.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::57: Dr. Kevin Bruin, Log Entry E72, The Moment. To whoever is investigating my disappearance, in the event that I do not return, I leave this record. No individual knows when their turn will arrive, and although we quickly discovered methods to predict its movement and avoid the phenomenon, there is no way to stop it. The most disastrous attempts occurred under Martial Law, where the isolation periods were truly terrible; they were short, yes, but undeniably harrowing. One of the iso-men once asked me if it was worse that everyone lived, having to interact with the people we so selfishly isolated. Would it have been best if the moment caused death instead, he asked, his eyes locked into mine. While my own eyes were filled with panic and guilt, his remained peaceful; why would they not be, considering the moment had passed him, whereas it had not yet passed me? There are several rules we have identified corresponding to the moment. The first is that it only affects men, each and every one, regardless of age. The second is that its intent is not to kill, and while deaths have occurred, usually among the very young or old, they can be prevented through medical intervention. Third, it affects men on a singular basis, meaning only one man can experience the moment at a time, with no reported cases of simultaneous experiences. Fourth, its movement is proximity-based; the closer you are to someone experiencing the moment, the more likely you are to be next. Fifth, it cannot be contained by any physical barrier, as the isolation of an infected area failed, and once the moment had finished its transit through the male population in that confined area, it simply advanced outwards. Sixth, it is possible to outrun it, as it moves at speeds comparable to an average human. Finally, the experience itself is said to be incredibly painful. As to where I went, I was asked what I thought the moment could be when I first started, and I claimed it was something explainable, utilizing observations, hypotheses, experiments, and testing month after month. A virus, bacterium, or parasite, or perhaps mass hysteria, none of it fit, and there was no explanation. When people talked about aliens or God’s punishment, I laughed, exclaiming that science would find the answer. Eventually, though, it seemed no answer was coming, and I doubted for a while, starting to believe the extremists. Few people know this about me; however, there is one more rule that I choose to accept, which others do not: it is sentient, and extinction is its endgame. As a man of science, I cannot be scared anymore, so I must test my hypothesis. You will now understand why I am missing. Men my age are less likely to survive, but we can find the answer; science will prevail. I have performed an orchidectomy on myself. By the time you read this, I should be within the moment’s current spread. I wonder what people will think when they see a naked old man walking into the fire. Is he mad, or a religious nut? If I succeed, which I believe I will, you will probably hear stories before I can make it back. Hence the log. Stories of a crazy old man whose faith made him immune to the moment will be told; know that it was faith that triumphed, specifically faith in science. If I do not return, Dan, love always.
syntax_complex.writingprompts::59:
A small lamp, which burned with a steady and unwavering light, sat upon the polished surface of the desk where the human, who wore a pair of thin spectacles perched precariously upon the edge of his nose, sat hunched over his work. Stacks of parchment, which occupied a far corner of the desk, were being read by the man, who turned through the pages at a methodical pace while scribbling notes on an entirely different sheet, and the sight of several empty ink bottles scattered across the floor suggested that the man was, indeed, rather busy. From the entrance of the chamber, Ronn readied his flail, letting the heavy chains dangle with a rhythmic clatter, their echoes filling the room; however, the man refused to look up at the intruders, choosing instead to hold up a single finger while he continued reading. Ronn and the rest of his group exchanged glances and shrugged their shoulders, standing still for a moment, until the man, with a disappointed smack of his tongue, finally replaced the parchment, pushed his glasses closer to his eyes, and called for his guests to approach, which they eventually did. 

Apologies, my friends, he said, his voice cracking slightly as though it had gone unpracticed for some time, before adding, Come, come. The adventurers stepped forward slowly, with Wilm’s head darting around as he scouted for suspicious stones in the floor or perhaps another hidden tripwire, until the cobbles turned to green when the tasseled edge of the rug stood before them, causing the group to stop. Come, the man muttered, any trace of impatience defying detection. Firrel’s boot tested its weight against the rug, and, discovering that there was solid ground beneath, the rest followed suit. Wait! the man screamed, and the group wasted no time assuming a defensive stance, their weapons and shields drawn, until he clarified, I meant the carpet. The adventurers looked towards their feet, observing as the jade fibers assumed a purplish hue while the blood from their persons dripped freely, which made Querth’s face flush with embarrassment. Sorry, the wizard whispered. The man rolled his eyes, remarking, It is already ruined, and since there is nothing we can do now, let us just get this over with. 

The adventurers were finally within a pace of the desk when the open palm of the man begged their halt, reminding them that although the hordes of evil creatures had led them to that chamber, the supposed throne room of unspeakable villainy was, in reality, little more than a study with a librarian. Well, then, I suppose congratulations are in order! The man clapped his hands together, continuing, Smashing job; I am Pollock, and I shall be handling your processing from here. Processing? Edmund echoed, to which Pollock replied, Yes, you are almost done in this dreadful castle and on your way back home to enjoy the spoils, so all that is left is to handle the final odds and ends. The adventurers nodded in content, though they kept their weapons handy, for the legions they had been forced to cut through in order to reach that chamber began to feel concluded. Excellent, so let us get started, for in total you have slaughtered one hundred and fifty-three goblins, twenty-nine orcs, eighteen kobolds, and two dragons, which is quite impressive. 

Edmund smirked and rolled the handle of his axe to catch the light, much to the audible groans of Ronn and Dismal, who had enjoyed the chaos that followed as it effectively stopped their fellow warrior from gloating. In addition, you broke down forty-one doors, set off two fire traps, six spike snares, three boulders, and one acid spill, plus it says you freed the dungeons of ten prisoners. All in a day’s work, Wilm interjected. Quite, responded Pollock, not the least bit impressed, as he added, And adding up your little adventure, that comes to a total of eight million, eight hundred thirty-seven thousand, two hundred and fifty-one gold pieces. Even Querth’s mind could not comprehend such a figure, for while they were used to generous spoils, several hundred was the most any had ever seen. We could not possibly carry that much coin, Dismal remarked, nor could we ever spend it. That is quite expected, Pollock laughed, for you can just pay in installments. Pay? shouted Firrel, asking, What do you mean pay? Your fines and your damages, for you cannot just go around killing things, damaging property, and setting off traps that require professional calibration. But we were on a quest, pleaded Ronn, we were trying to save the village. I see, sneered Pollock, but does that mean the village is going to pay the fines, rebuild the castle, reset the protections, mop the floors, rehire the guards, retrain dragons, and inform the families of those lost? The group stood in wide-eyed silence, until he concluded, I did not think so. B-but it was a quest, Ronn repeated. Do you have a license, a Writ of Pacification for this quest of yours? Ronn shook his head, and Pollock continued, No need to answer, as I already know you do not, for if you had bothered to apply for one, this castle would have been better protected and I would not have been needed; just a little [ WP ] at the start would have been enough to save us all the mess of your unauthorized rampage. Who was supposed to file our WP? Querth asked the group, and they considered the question for a moment before turning to face Dismaldreamer, shouting, You have ruined us! I am sorry, cried Dismal, for I did not know this would happen! The circle closed around him as the group looked to dispatch their greatest foe: the enemy within. The moral is that you should always tag your posts, or else your friends will murder you.

This report covers Dartmoor hill ponies. It also covers other Devon and Cornwall news. Defra dropped the investigation six months later. Defra found no case to answer. syntax_simple.xsum::1: Her efforts helped scientists in India. They devised a unique way. It is a non-invasive way. They monitor the health of wild elephants. They freeze-dry dung in the field. syntax_simple.xsum::29: Philip Cullen is 57 years old. A judge gave him a six-month suspended sentence. He captured two butterflies. He visited reserves in Somerset and Gloucestershire in 2015. Someone spotted him later with a small net at Collard Hill in Somerset. Witnesses reported him to the police. Police officers raided his home. They found 30 trays of butterflies. Those trays contained Large Blues. Prosecutor Ian Jackson spoke to the court. He brought charges on the grounds of endangering a species. Michael Hartnell defended him. He said the 57-year-old accepted the enormity of his actions. The man felt extremely remorseful. Cullen lives at The Grove, Warmley, Bristol. The judge gave him a six-month prison sentence. The court suspended it for two years. He must perform 250 hours of unpaid work. The judge issued a five-year criminal behaviour order. This order bans him from three nature reserves. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::0: Regulatory testing schemes for genetic damage have been standardized for several decades. These tests examined mutations. They examined structural chromosomal damage. They examined numerical chromosomal damage. This approach served the genetic toxicity community well. Most substances were amenable to such assays. The outcome from this testing is usually a simple yes or no evaluation. The information is often used only for one purpose. It determines whether a substance has carcinogenic potential. Mechanisms and modes of action have been recognized over the same time period. These mechanisms elucidate a wider range of genomic damage. Many adverse health outcomes involve this damage. A paradigm shift is occurring in applied genetic toxicology. The field is moving toward a more quantitative dose-response analysis. It is moving toward point-of-departure determination. The focus is now on risks to exposed humans. This directs emphasis on specific genomic damage. This damage is likely to induce changes. These changes are associated with a variety of adverse health outcomes. This paradigm shift changes the testing emphasis for genetic damage. It moves away from hazard identification only. It moves toward a more comprehensive risk assessment approach. This provides more insightful information for decision makers. It relates to the potential risk of genetic damage to exposed humans. A next generation testing strategy needs to take into account a broader approach. This strategy needs a more flexible approach to testing. It needs a flexible approach to modeling genomic damage. This relates to human exposure. This is consistent with the larger risk assessment context. Regulatory decision making uses this context. This flexible approach for examining genomic damage focuses on relevant genomic effects. These effects can be associated with an adverse health effect. The most desired linkage for risk to humans is changes in loci. These loci are associated with human diseases. This applies to somatic cells. This applies to germ cells. The outline of a flexible approach is presented here. It includes associated considerations. It is presented in a series of nine steps. Some of these steps can occur in parallel. A collaborative effort developed this approach. Leading genetic toxicologists from academia developed it. Experts from government participated. Experts from industry participated. They worked through the International Life Sciences Institute Health and Environmental Sciences Institute Genetic Toxicology Technical Committee. The ultimate goal is to provide quantitative data. This data models the potential risk levels of substances. These substances induce genomic damage. This damage contributes to human adverse health outcomes. Any good risk assessment begins with appropriate questions. It uses a planning and scoping effort. This step sets up the problem. Does genomic damage need to be addressed? If so, how should we proceed? The next two steps assemble what is known about the problem. We build a knowledge base about the substance of concern. We develop a rational biological argument. We explain why testing for genomic damage is needed. We explain why it might not be needed. The next step is assay selection. This step focuses on the risk management problem. It focuses on the potential genomic damage of concern. The work-up of the problem provides insight. It helps us select the most meaningful assays. This discussion does not detail the wide range of available genomic damage tests. It points to types of testing systems. These systems can be very useful. The assays are performed. The data is analyzed. Relevant data sets are selected for modeling potential risk. The data is evaluated from this point on. The data is modeled. This happens as it does for any other toxicology endpoint. Any observed genomic damage or genetic effect can be modeled. We perform a dose-response analysis. We determine an estimated point-of-departure. A quantitative risk analysis is sometimes needed for decision making. A parallel exposure assessment effort is performed. Exposure assessment is not detailed here. This is not the focus of this discussion. Guidelines for this assessment exist elsewhere. The point-of-departure for genomic damage is used with exposure information. This develops risk estimations. We use reference dose approaches. We use margin of exposure approaches. This happens in a risk characterization. It is presented to risk managers. It informs decision making. This approach is applicable now. We can incorporate genomic damage results into the decision-making process. This assesses potential adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans. It is consistent with the Risk Assessment in the 21st Century roadmap. This applies to any substance. Humans are exposed to these substances. This includes pharmaceuticals. This includes agricultural products. This includes food additives. This includes other chemicals. Regulatory bodies should incorporate broader knowledge. They should use insights provided by genomic damage results. These results improve assessments of risk. They help us understand the potential of adverse outcomes in chemically exposed humans. This improves the assessment of risk due to genomic damage. The historical use of genomic damage data was a yes or no gateway. It focused on possible cancer risk. This focus has been too narrow in risk assessment. Recent advances improve our understanding of genomic damage. This includes eventually epigenetic alterations. These advances add a greater wealth of information. They help in determining potential risk to humans. Regulatory bodies need to embrace this paradigm shift. They should move from hazard identification to quantitative analysis. They should incorporate the wider range of genomic damage. They should do this in their assessments of risk to humans. The quantitative analyses and methodologies are discussed here. They can be readily applied to genomic damage testing results now. The Toxic Substances Control Act was recently updated in the US. The new generation testing strategy for genomic damage is described here. It provides a regulatory agency with a golden opportunity. This agency is the US Environmental Protection Agency. It is also suitable for other agencies. They can reexamine the way they address risk-based genomic damage testing. This includes hazard identification. This includes exposure. Environ. Mol. Mutagen. 58:264-283, 2017. The Authors. Environmental and Molecular Mutagenesis Published by Wiley Periodicals, Inc.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::1: Nutritional supplements might improve the development of small infants. These infants are preterm or small for gestational age. These supplements might increase the risk of later metabolic disease. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis. We assessed the effects of macronutrient supplements. We examined later development and metabolism in these small infants. We searched OvidMedline, Embase, and Cochrane databases. We searched until April 1, 2019. We searched clinical trial registries. We included randomised or quasirandomised trials. The goal was to increase macronutrient intake. The goal was to improve growth or development. We assessed post-discharge outcomes. The co-primary outcomes were cognitive impairment and metabolic risk. We evaluated toddlers under three years. We evaluated childhood from three to eight years. We evaluated adolescence from nine to eighteen years. Two reviewers extracted data independently. We assessed quality with the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. We pooled data using random-effect models. We included twenty-one randomised trials. We included one quasirandomised trial. These trials had variable methodological quality. They involved 3,680 infants. In toddlers, supplementation did not alter cognitive impairment. The relative risk was 1.00. The confidence interval was 0.67 to 1.49. The P-value was 0.99. There were no differences in cognitive scores. The mean difference was 0.57. There were no differences in motor scores. The mean difference was 1.16. Fewer supplemented children had motor impairment. The relative risk was 0.76. In subgroup analyses, supplementation improved cognitive scores in boys. The mean difference was 5.60. It did not improve scores in girls. It did not alter scores in children born small for gestational age. In childhood, there was no difference in cognitive impairment. There was no difference in cognitive scores. There were no differences in blood pressure, triglyceride, or LDL concentrations. All P-values were greater than 0.05. Supplemented children had lower fasting glucose. The mean difference was -0.20. They had higher HDL concentrations. The mean difference was 0.11. In subgroup analyses, we found no evidence of blood pressure differences in boys or girls. We found no such evidence in children born small for gestational age. In adolescence, there was no difference in blood pressure. There was no difference in triglycerides or LDL concentrations. There was no difference in HDL concentrations or fasting blood glucose. There was no difference in insulin resistance or fasting insulin concentrations. All P-values were greater than 0.05. Limitations include considerable unexplained heterogeneity. Limitations include low to very low quality of the evidence. Limitations include limited data beyond early childhood. We conducted this systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials. We found no evidence that early macronutrient supplementation altered later cognitive function. There was some evidence that supplementation may decrease motor impairment in toddlers. We contrasted these findings with observational studies. Evidence from randomised trials suggests that early macronutrient supplementation improves some metabolic outcomes in childhood. This research carries the registration number CRD42019127858. Our results provide a clear perspective on nutritional interventions for vulnerable infants. These findings guide future clinical practice and research efforts. We hope for better health outcomes for these small children.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::2: Two point-of-care feline immunodeficiency virus antibody test kits exist. These kits are Witness and Anigen Rapid. Recent reports suggest these kits differentiate vaccinated cats from infected cats. This is possible at a single time point. The gap between testing and vaccination does not matter. The gap ranges from zero to seven years. This study investigated anti-FIV antibody production over time. It followed the recommended primary FIV vaccination series. The methods involved two distinct parts. First, researchers tested residual plasma from an original study. They used a laboratory-based ELISA. This determined the cause of negative results. The researchers checked for reduced or absent antibodies to gp40. Second, the team performed a prospective study. They used immunologically naive kittens and cats. These animals received a primary FIV vaccination series. The vaccine was a commercially available inactivated whole cell or virus product. It is called Fel-O-Vax FIV. The cats received three subcutaneous injections. The injections happened at four week intervals. The team tested the cats systematically. They performed up to eleven tests over six months. They used four commercially available point-of-care FIV antibody kits. These kits were SNAP FIV/FeLV Combo, Witness FeLV/FIV, Anigen Rapid FIV/FeLV, and VetScan FeLV/FIV Rapid. The laboratory-based ELISA showed clear results. Cats from the original study had detectable antibodies to gp40. These cats were vaccinated within the previous fifteen months. They still tested negative with two specific kits. These kits use gp40 as a capture antigen. The kits were Witness and Anigen Rapid. The prospective study showed different results. Testing with SNAP Combo and VetScan Rapid was positive for all cats. This happened two weeks after the second primary vaccination. The results remained positive for the entire study duration. Twelve of twelve cats were positive for SNAP. Ten of twelve cats were positive for VetScan. Antibody testing with Witness and Anigen Rapid was also positive. This happened two weeks after the second primary vaccination. Eight of twelve cats were positive for Witness. Seven of twelve cats were positive for Anigen Rapid. Antibody levels declined quickly. They fell below detection levels in most cats. This happened one month after the third primary vaccination. Ten of twelve cats tested negative. All cats tested negative using Witness and Anigen Rapid. This happened six months after the third vaccination. This study shows clear findings. A primary FIV vaccination course does not interfere with testing. This applies to Witness and Anigen Rapid kits. The primary vaccination must not have occurred within six months. These antibody test kits are reliable. They determine FIV infection status. They work at the time of annual booster vaccination. They help detect vaccine breakthroughs. They work for cats without recent primary vaccinations. Further research must determine the antibody response duration. It must also study the effect on point-of-care kits. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::3: Tuberous sclerosis complex is a rare monogenic disorder. It features benign tumors in many organs. Patients often experience epilepsy. They often face intellectual disability. They often face autism. Inactivating mutations in the TSC1 or TSC2 genes cause this disease. Heterozygosity induces hyperactivation of mTOR. Doctors use mTOR inhibitors for treatment. Rapamycin is one such inhibitor. It shows efficacy against TSC symptoms. This study had two goals. We identified molecular changes in brain tissue of Tsc1 +/- mice. These changes relate to social and cognitive deficits. We also investigated the molecular effects of rapamycin treatment. Rapamycin ameliorates genotype-related behavioral deficits. We studied molecular alterations in the frontal cortex. We also studied the hippocampus of Tsc1 +/- and control mice. We used rapamycin or no treatment. We employed a quantitative mass spectrometry-based shotgun proteomic approach. This method is called LC-MSE. It provided an unbiased way to detect protein level changes. We validated initial findings. We used selected reaction monitoring or SRM for this validation. We employed Protein Set Enrichment Analysis. This identified dysregulated pathways. LC-MSE analysis included thirty Tsc1 +/- mice and controls. We identified fifty-one changed proteins in the frontal cortex. We identified 108 changed proteins in the hippocampus. Bioinformatic analysis combined with targeted proteomic validation. This revealed several dysregulated molecular pathways. Targeted assays validated these pathways in the hippocampus. We found pathways for myelination, dendrite, and oxidative stress. We also found an upregulation of ribosomal proteins and the mTOR kinase. LC-MSE analysis also involved Tsc1 +/- and wildtype mice. There were thirty-four mice in this group. We treated them with rapamycin or a vehicle. Rapamycin exerted a stronger proteomic effect in Tsc1 +/- mice. We found significant changes in 231 proteins. We found significant changes in 106 proteins. These changes were mainly decreased expression. We found effects on the cellular pathways of oxidative stress and apoptosis in Tsc1 +/- mice. Rapamycin treatment affected the cellular compartments of myelin sheet and neurofilaments. Thirty-three proteins were altered in Tsc1 +/- mice. Rapamycin treatment normalized these proteins. This list included oxidative stress related proteins. It included myelin-specific proteins and ribosomal proteins. Molecular changes were more prominent in the hippocampus. Changes were less prominent in the frontal cortex. Pathways for myelination and oxidative stress response were affected. Rapamycin treatment normalized these pathways in part. These results aid the identification of novel drug targets. These targets treat cognitive, social, and psychiatric symptoms. Such symptoms appear in autism spectrum disorders. Similar pathways appear in other psychiatric disorders. They also appear in neurodegenerative disorders. These pathways imply similar disease processes. The potential efficacy of mTOR inhibitors warrants further investigation. We should study autism spectrum disorders. We should also study other neuropsychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::4: Silica nanoparticles are promising delivery systems. They carry active compounds to tissues. They target the heart in a controlled way. However, these particles cause cardiac toxicity. This toxicity relates to abnormal calcium handling. It also relates to energetic failure in heart muscle cells. The exact mechanisms of this energetic failure remain unclear. This article explores heart function and mitochondria. It examines these systems after exposure to silica nanoparticles. The cumulative administration of particles reduced heart performance. The half-maximal inhibitory concentration reached ninety-three micrograms per milliliter. This dose affected the relaxation rate of the heart. The particles entered isolated mitochondria. They inhibited oxidative phosphorylation. They reduced the mitochondrial membrane potential significantly. Higher doses induced the mitochondrial permeability transition pore. Cyclosporine A blocked this pore. It provided partial recovery. The particles reduced aconitase activity. They increased thiol oxidation in the adenine nucleotide translocase. These results suggest a mechanism. The particles induce the pore via thiol modification. They also induce the pore via reactive oxygen species generation. Cardiac cells showed enhanced viability after MitoTEMPO treatment. This specific antioxidant reduced hydrogen peroxide levels. Cyclosporine A treatment reduced cell death in rat cardiac cells. It recovered ATP production from thirty-two percent to sixty-five percent. We also evaluated the mitochondrial effect in human cardiomyocytes. We observed forty percent inhibition of the maximal oxygen consumption rate at five hundred micrograms per milliliter. We identified a remarkable diminution in the spare respiratory capacity under these conditions. This data indicates a reduction in extra ATP production. Mitochondria cannot produce enough energy during sudden demand. Human cardiomyocytes showed increased lactate dehydrogenase release. They showed increased necrosis at high doses of particles. These reached eighty-five percent and forty-eight percent respectively. Cyclosporine A application prevented these deleterious effects partially. Exposure to silica nanoparticles affects cardiac function. It causes mitochondrial dysfunction. It triggers the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore. These effects can be partially avoided. One strategy involves reducing reactive oxygen species. Another strategy involves retarding the opening of the mitochondrial pore. These novel strategies resulted in cardioprotection. Scientists could consider these as potential therapies. These therapies might decrease the side effects of particle exposure. We need to study these pathways further. Future research will clarify the long-term impacts of silica delivery. We must ensure patient safety during future medical treatments involving these nanoparticles. These findings offer a clear path forward for researchers.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::5: Researchers reported return to play rates for NFL athletes after isolated ACL tears. No previous studies reported on return to play for NFL athletes after multiligament knee injuries. NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries have lower return to play rates. These athletes also have longer recovery times than athletes with isolated ACL tears. Athletes with ACL and MCL injuries have higher return to play rates. These athletes also have shorter return to play times than athletes with ACL and posterolateral corner involvement. This study is a retrospective cohort study. It is level four evidence. Researchers reviewed publicly available NFL injury data. They looked at all multiligament knee injuries from 2000 to 2016. They included return to play information. Researchers excluded athletes with return to play limitations unrelated to the injury. Data included injury type and return to play status. Data included time to return to play in days. Data included games played and performance metrics. Fifty NFL athletes met all inclusion and exclusion criteria. The overall return to play rate was 64.0 percent. Athletes with ACL and MCL tears had a return to play rate of 70.8 percent. Athletes with ACL and PCL/LCL tears had a return to play rate of 55.6 percent. The p-value was 0.26. The mean time to return to play for all 50 athletes was 388.71 days. The standard deviation was 198.52 days. The mean time for athletes with ACL and MCL injuries was 305.1 days. The standard deviation was 58.9 days. Athletes with combined ACL and PCL/LCL injuries had a mean time of 459.2 days. The standard deviation was 245.1 days. Athletes with frank knee dislocations had a mean time of 609.3 days. The standard deviation was 183.1 days. Athletes with ACL and MCL injuries returned to prior performance levels more often. This rate was 43.5 percent. Athletes with ACL and PCL/LCL injuries returned at a rate of 18.5 percent. The p-value was less than 0.001. Multiligament knee injuries significantly affect the ability of a football player to return to sport. ACL and MCL tears have better prognoses. They are superior to ACL and PCL/LCL tears for the athlete.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::6: Pulmonary hypertension occurs during exercise. It marks the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis. Doctors do not understand the factors for elevated pulmonary pressure well. This study assesses the parameters for this pressure response in rheumatic mitral stenosis patients. We also determine the impact of exercise-induced pulmonary hypertension on clinical outcomes. One hundred thirty patients joined the study. Women made up ninety-four percent of the group. Their mean age was forty-five years. These patients underwent exercise echocardiography. We obtained many parameters at rest and at peak exercise. The patients performed symptom-limited graded ramp bicycle exercise. They remained in the supine position during this test. The primary end point was mitral valve intervention. This included percutaneous or surgical procedures. In the overall population, systolic pulmonary artery pressure increased. It went from thirty-eight point three millimeters of mercury at rest. It reached sixty-five point eight millimeters of mercury during exercise. Increases in mean mitral gradient happened. Right ventricular function changed. Left atrial volume increased. Net atrioventricular compliance changed too. These factors were independently associated with systolic pressure at peak exercise. We adjusted these results for changes in heart rate. The follow-up period lasted seventeen months on average. We observed forty-six adverse clinical events. We used multivariate Cox proportional-hazards analysis for the data. We adjusted for age and sex. Systolic pulmonary artery pressure at peak exercise was an important predictor of adverse outcome. The adjusted hazard ratio was one point zero two five. New York Heart Association functional class was also a significant predictor. The interaction between valve area and net atrioventricular compliance was significant. The receiver operating characteristic curve models were better for exercise pressure. Resting pressure models performed worse. The improvement was significant from three years onward. In mitral stenosis patients, the pulmonary artery pressure response to exercise has multiple causes. It involves transmitral mean gradient at exercise. It involves net atrioventricular compliance. It involves left atrial volume. It involves right ventricular function. Pulmonary artery pressure at peak exercise predicts clinical outcomes. It adds incremental prognostic value beyond standard resting measurements. It provides more information than valve area alone.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::7: The impact of chronic liver disease on COVID-19 outcomes remains uncertain. We aimed to explore this association. We studied outcomes for all adult inpatients with COVID-19 in France during 2020. We computed adjusted odds ratios for these associations. We examined chronic liver disease, alcohol use disorders, mechanical ventilation, and day-30 in-hospital mortality. The sample comprised 259,110 patients. The median age was 70 years. The interquartile range was 54 to 83 years. Men represented 52% of the group. We identified 15,476 patients with chronic liver disease. This total represented 6.0% of the sample. We identified 10,006 patients with alcohol use disorders. This total represented 3.9% of the sample. Death occurred in 38,203 patients. This figure was 15% of the total cohort. Death occurred in 7,475 patients after mechanical ventilation. This was 28% of the ventilated group. Death occurred in 2,941 patients with chronic liver disease. This was 19% of those with liver disease. The adjusted odds ratio for mechanical ventilation was 1.54 for chronic liver disease. The adjusted odds ratio for day-30 mortality was 1.79. We calculated these values with 95% confidence intervals and p-values below 0.001. Mild liver disease showed different results. Compensated cirrhosis showed specific values. Decompensated cirrhosis showed distinct ratios. Primary liver cancer displayed unique risks. Alcohol use disorders showed specific outcomes. Chronic viral hepatitis was not associated with death. Non-viral non-alcoholic chronic hepatitis was not associated with death. Liver transplantation was not associated with death. Acquired immunodeficiency syndrome was not associated with death. Chronic liver disease increased the risk of COVID-19-related death in France. Therapeutic effort limitation may have contributed to these deaths. We studied all adults discharged from acute and post-acute care. Patients with mild liver disease were not at increased risk. Patients with compensated cirrhosis were not at increased risk. Patients with liver transplantation were not at increased risk. Patients with immunodepression were not at increased risk. Patients with alcohol use disorders were at increased risk. Patients with decompensated cirrhosis were at increased risk. Patients with primary liver cancer were at increased risk. These high-risk groups were less likely to receive mechanical ventilation. Therapeutic effort limitation likely contributed to excess mortality in these French residents.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::8: The coronavirus disease 2019 creates many deaths worldwide. SARS-CoV-2 causes this disease. COVID-19 poses a serious threat to human life. The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 are diverse and severe. Twenty percent of infected patients are in a critical condition. A loss in lung function marks the disease. Participants must meet strict inclusion criteria. They must be over eighteen years of age. They must have recovered from severe or critical COVID-19 cases. They must exhibit pulmonary fibrosis after recovery. They must exhibit Qi-Yin deficiency syndrome. This syndrome follows the system of traditional Chinese medicine. Researchers will randomize eligible candidates into two groups. The treatment group receives modern medicine. They receive pirfenidone plus traditional Chinese medicine. This drug leads to a delay in the decline of forced expiratory vital capacity. It reduces the mortality rate partly. Traditional Chinese medicine is efficacious for pulmonary fibrosis. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::9: Temperature and water availability affect anuran physiological processes. These variables influence body temperature and evaporative water loss. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::10: Chronotaraxis is an impairment of the perception of time sequencing. This alteration of temporality is characteristically associated with thalamic involvement. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::11: Some infectious diseases spread through the air. Examples include influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2. An infectious person expels virus-laden particles. Another person inhales these particles. This process represents the airborne transmission route. These particles reach high concentrations within the expiratory jet. The jet exists near the infectious person. The room air remains well-mixed elsewhere. Scientists have not well quantified this near-field enhancement in virion exposure. Airborne virus transmission depends on many variable factors. These factors are often poorly constrained. Large ensembles of model simulations help quantify this uncertainty. These models must span the variability in input parameters. Some models simulate the near-field evolution of respiratory particles well. These models are very computationally expensive. This cost limits the exploration of parametric uncertainty. We developed the Quadrature-based model of Respiratory Aerosol and Droplets to solve this problem. We call this model QuaRAD. QuaRAD provides an efficient framework. It simulates the evolution of virus-laden particles. It tracks particles after an infectious person expels them. It models their deposition to the nasal cavity of a susceptible person. It calculates the subsequent risk of initial infection. We simulated 10,000 scenarios. We quantified the risk of initial infection for SARS-CoV-2. The predicted risk of infection varied highly among these scenarios. The risk was strongly enhanced near the infectious individual in each scenario. The physical distancing needed to avoid these enhancements exceeded two meters in more than 50% of scenarios. This assumes the infectious person does not wear a mask. This distance defining the near-field extent also varied highly among scenarios. Variability in expiration velocity explains the variability in the near-field extent. Our findings suggest a clear conclusion. People should use protections against airborne transmission when distancing is not possible. N95 respirators provide such protection. They should be available to everyone in these situations. We highlight the importance of physical distance and masks for public health.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::12: Open fractures are contaminated wounds. These wounds contain gram-positive organisms. They also contain gram-negative organisms. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::13: PURPOSE: Many health activities show cyclical compliance patterns. People diet or exercise in cycles. We do not know these patterns for chronic medications. METHODS: We studied 26,636 new users of osteoporosis medication. These patients were age 65 or older. They had an extended lapse in refill compliance. A lapse lasted at least 60 days. No patient obtained a refill during this period. We used survival curves. These curves estimated the time until therapy resumption. We estimated the association between patient characteristics and treatment resumption rates. We used Cox proportional hazards analysis. We then conducted a case crossover analysis. We examined specific events during follow-up. These events triggered a return to refill compliance. RESULTS: Some patients stopped therapy for at least 60 days. An estimated 30% restarted treatment within 6 months. 50% restarted within 2 years. Some patients had at least 6 months of continuous use before their interruption. We need more data on these specific long-term health behaviors and patient choices across various clinical settings.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::14: Imbalances in the gut microbial community cause dysbiosis in vertebrates. These imbalances link to gastrointestinal diseases. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::15: We investigate the reason for quantum speedup. Quantum algorithms require fewer computation steps than classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of setting the problem. The initial measurement selects a setting at random. Bob is the problem setter. Bob unitarily changes it into the desired one. This representation is clear to Bob. It is clear to any external observer. It cannot be clear to Alice. Alice is the problem solver. It would tell her the function computed by the black box. This function should be hidden inside it for her. We resort to relational quantum mechanics. To Alice, the projection of the quantum state is retarded. This happens due to the initial measurement. It occurs at the end of her problem solving action. To her, the algorithm input state remains one of complete ignorance of the setting. She uses black box computations. She unitarily sends it into the output state. This state encodes the corresponding solution for each possible setting. This is acquired by the final measurement. We show something about the final measurement. We can ascribe the selection of any part to the final measurement. Let us say the R-th part of the random outcome of the initial measurement. This projects the input state to Alice on a state of lower entropy. She knows a corresponding part of the problem setting. The quantum algorithm is a sum over classical histories. In each history, Alice knows in advance one of the R-th parts of the setting. She performs the black box computations still required to identify the solution. We have an oracle problem and a value of R. This retrocausality model provides the number of black box computations required to solve it. We have a known quantum algorithm. It yields the value of R. This explains its speed up. R equals one half always yields the number of black box computations. This matches an existing quantum algorithm. It matches the order of magnitude of the number required by the optimal one.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::16: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention increase the risk for thrombosis events. These conditions modify blood flow in the heart. A parameterized model represents the mitral valve opening. We use a finite element method to solve these equations. This method constructs a simulation of blood flow velocity and pressure. We then use a triple decomposition of the velocity gradient tensor. This step distinguishes between rigid body rotational flow and irrotational straining flow and shear flow. The triple decomposition separates three different flow structures. Each structure generates a distinct mechanical stimulus on the blood cells. We compare these results to simulations of a mitral valve clip intervention. This intervention leads to a significant modification of the ventricular flow. Clinicians can use these findings to improve patient outcomes during heart procedures. Detailed simulations help doctors understand these risks much better in the future.
syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::17: H.E.S.S. observed diffuse gamma-ray emission in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way. This emission exceeds 100 GeV. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::18: The European Academy of Childhood Disability initiated these international clinical practice recommendations. They cover developmental coordination disorder. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::19: Hypertension causes mood disorders. These conditions change with different antihypertensive drugs. Depression links to brain asymmetry. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::20: This study evaluates the value and efficacy of rapid response teams for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty patients. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::21: Emergency medical services assist acute stroke management. We created a prehospital stroke scale. We named this scale TOPSPIN. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::22: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408. This is the most solid candidate galaxy at z~7 in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We used all VLT spectra of GDS-1408. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::23: Researchers studied the survival of Salmonella spp. as a pathogen indicator in composting. They used an inoculum technique. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::24: Race links to prostate cancer progression in early disease. It is unclear if race predicts poor outcomes for advanced disease. The authors tested a hypothesis. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::26: Neuromorphic engineering builds realistic robotic systems. These systems interact with the physical world. They use neuromechanical principles from biology. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::27: Patients present with urinary tract infections and kidney stones. This condition is a urologic emergency. These patients often reach clinical stability. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::28: Evidence details cannabis influence on other psychoactive substances. These substances include prescription medications, alcohol, tobacco, and illicit drugs. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::35: Researchers introduced the methodology of funnel control in the early 2000s. The field developed in many respects since then. syntax_simple.academic_abstracts::36: DDoS attacks show increasing diversity today. Designers struggle to build a fully protected network. Citizens will not die. Citizens must finish their own graves first. The Moral Officer bellowed this into his bullhorn. He repeated the message. He repeated it again. I found it heartening. The end was near. This gave me strength. I pushed my weak body. I pushed my weary body. I shoveled faster. I shoveled much faster. 

All around me citizens dug in the dust. The dirt was brittle. The dirt was dry. They scratched out a place. They would give their bodies back to the earth there. In the distance other Moral Officers made proclamations. They used identical bullhorns. Compliance Officers stood at regular intervals. They wore immaculate uniforms. They waited patiently. They wanted to aid us in our final duty to the Nation. 

A food shortage existed. We knew this well before the State announced it. Everyone whispered about the weekly rations. The rations came from the distribution station. They seemed smaller every week. The Party workers denied this. They denied it if anyone asked. Whispers turned into loud complaints. Items disappeared from the rations. Those items never reappeared. Meat became a memory. Healthy vegetables became rare. 

The State News Agency made a special broadcast. They finally announced the famine. Nobody was surprised. They instructed us. We must stand united. We must stay strong. We must remain proud. We faced this Straining Test. Everyone must do their part. We must bear this burden. Our Immaculate Society would clear this hurdle. We would emerge triumphant. The Beloved Ruler rationed his consumption. They told us this. It was clear. It was undoubtedly clear. Dissidents created this ploy. Outsiders created this ploy. They attempted to destroy our resolve. They wanted us to turn back from the revolution. They had sabotaged our fields. They had murdered our animals. We would stay strong in our virtue. We would emerge triumphant as ever. 

They announced the lottery then. They selected a number of citizens randomly. These citizens would give a glorious sacrifice. This sacrifice showed faith. This sacrifice showed virtue for the Nation. It helped ease the burden of consumption. Selected citizens received news the next day. A soldier showed up at their door. The soldier took them away from their families. I was one of the chosen people. 

A shout rang out across the fields. A man yelled. May my body fertilize the soil. May it feed our glorious Nation. Long live the Beloved Ruler. A gunshot punctuated this declaration. Someone had already finished his grave. A few others cheered their assent. Most people were too weary. Most were too hungry. They could not manage to cheer. The Compliance Officer holstered his pistol. He motioned to the dead man's two neighbors. They filled in the grave. The dead man occupied the hole. 

They worked us hard. They took us away. We shoveled out a roadway. We slept where we worked. They gave us broth. The broth was very thin. They could hardly justify calling it food. It was hot water. The last of our strength was harvested. 

My grave looked deep enough now. I hesitated. I raised up my shovel. I called over the Compliance Officer. My grave might not be deep enough for his liking. I would have to wait then. Everyone else would finish. They would cover their graves. Then it would be my turn. 

He came over. He produced a tape measure. He checked the dimensions. He nodded his assent. I let out a sigh of relief. The sigh was inaudible. I went to stand at the foot of my grave. The time was here. The time for my glorious sacrifice was here. I did this for the sake of the Nation. The time for my final duty to my beloved land arrived. 

Citizens will not be allowed to die until they have finished digging their own grave. The Moral Officer chanted into his bullhorn. I felt the cool metal of the Compliance Officer pistol. It came to rest upon my forehead. Citizens will not be allowed to die. The officer spoke. I waited for the end. I waited for my duty. I waited for the Nation.

Exterior. A side street in Jerusalem. It is day. Police tape surrounds two large amphorae. CSI technicians work in the area. Moses stands by his car. He looks tired. He looks irritable. He leans on his walking stick. We look at this scruffy patriarch for a few moments. We pull back from the scene. Jesus enters from the left. He carries a cup of takeout coffee.

MOSES: You took long enough. We have waited for you forever.

JESUS: I am sorry. There was a long line. What do we have?

MOSES: We have a dead body. A uniform called it in. It looks like another dead hooker. Hazdrubul, do you have a cause of death yet?

We pan over to a figure. He wears a mask. He wears coveralls. He stands beside the corpse. Hazdrubul steps away from the crime scene.

HAZDRUBUL: It is early. I will bet on blunt force trauma. The body has multiple contusions. There is a nasty wound on the side of the head.

JESUS: When did she die?

HAZDRUBUL: It is hard to give a time of death now. It happened some time last night. I will give you a better number later. I need a liver temperature first.

MOSES: That is good enough.

Jesus moves closer to the crime scene. He tries to get a better look at the body. He does not react well to the sight. He ducks behind an amphora. He throws up.

MOSES: Jesus! You did not contaminate the crime scene. That is a small mercy.

Jesus re-emerges. He wipes his mouth. He looks very pale.

MOSES: The uniform officers will canvas house to house. We will go now. We will get you cleaned up. We will try to put a name to this poor girl.

Scene 23. Interior. Precinct House. We are in an interview room. Jesus and Moses stand on opposite sides of the room. Their arms are folded. They are obviously antagonistic.

MOSES: Do not give me your holier than thou bullshit. We needed results. I got those results.

JESUS: Was it worth the trouble? Was it worth going down to their level?

MOSES: I would do it again. I would do it again in a heartbeat. I have been in this job for forty years. I know how to get a confession.

JESUS: I saw you with that stick. I thought it was a sign of age. I thought it made you an elder. I thought you were someone to be respected. I guess I was wrong.

MOSES: Maybe you are wrong about a lot of things.

JESUS: Maybe I am.

MOSES: Maybe you want to think about our brother cops. You are a snot-nosed junior Levite. You think you can tell me how to conduct myself.

JESUS: Let us just calm down. I respect you. I really do respect you. You took down the Golden Calf gang. You resolved the Dead Sea Hostage situation. But this is not the desert. This is Jerusalem. We have to do things differently now.

MOSES: The hell you say.

JESUS: Think what you like. There is a girl down in the morgue on a slab. She is getting colder. We stand here. We throw stones at each other. Oh, of course!

MOSES: What?

JESUS: Of course! It is stone throwing! Do you not see it?

MOSES: Jesus, slow down. See what?

JESUS: They thought they were better than her.

Scene 832. Exterior. Jerusalem. It is night. Moses leans on a squad car. Jesus walks up. He has this week's bad guy in handcuffs. Moses watches. Jesus hands the bad guy off to uniformed cops.

MOSES: That is a good collar, kid.

JESUS: I could not have done it without you. You spotted the connection between the victims. How did you know?

MOSES: I have been on the job longer than you have been alive. After a while, you get a feel for this sort of thing.

JESUS: Will I ever develop that kind of instinct?

MOSES: Maybe. You have to live long enough.

JESUS: You are full of encouragement. I do not care, though. We put a sinner behind bars. That is the kind of good news I want to share.

Hey, look at those chickadees in the birdbath. Kylo whooped. He puffed out his chest. He nearly toppled off his perch. 

Don't be a troglodyte, bro. Atticus groused. He pecked at his seeds. You are a wren. That is not even the same family. 

I do not care. I am going to talk to them. Kylo took off. He swerved through the air. He moved like a leaf in a gust. Atticus sighed. He took off after him. He needed to keep close tabs on Kylo. Otherwise, they would get kicked out again. 

Kylo crashed into the water. He made a mighty splash. Droplets flew in every direction. They drenched the occupants of the birdbath. They squawked with indignation. Kylo emerged from beneath the surface. He shook the wetness from his head. He trotted up to a group of soaked finches. He gave his wings a shake. Hey, birds. Nice tits. 

We are not tits. A purple finch stepped forward. She launched into a tirade. She hated that overused pickup line. Atticus alighted on the rim of the bath. He began to walk around. He apologized to everyone for the behavior of Kylo. He pleaded with them. Please do not call the bouncer over. 

Okay, sorry. Kylo interrupted. Let me make it up to you. You and I head over there. He motioned to the bird feeder. I share my seeds with you. Kylo would smirk right now. He had lips. 

The finches began to flap their wings angrily. They splashed Kylo with water. You are such a boor. Get out of here. Many of the onlookers chirped in agreement. Some of the bigger birds began to puff their chests threateningly. Atticus shoved Kylo to the side. He raised his wings. On behalf of my friend here, I apologize. He had too much nectar. We will just be going now. 

Oh, you think we will fall for that? The purple finch spat a nut shell at his feet. He is just trying to play wingbird for you, is he? Let him take the fall for you. You swoop in to look better by comparison. The other birds chorused in agreement. 

I think these two need to be taught a lesson. A blue jay fluttered over to Atticus. He towered a full inch above him. He spread his wings menacingly. He blocked Atticus from taking off. Why do you not peck on someone your own size? The onlookers broke into cheers. They shouted for a fight. 

Well, you are kind of bigger than me. Atticus took a step back into the bath. He felt feathers ruffle against him. The crowd pressed around him. They urged him back towards the jay. That would not be my own size now, would it? 

Kylo staggered in front of him. He began to hop around. Do not worry, Atticus. We got this. 

Hey, this is a one-on-one fight. The jay looked around. If you get backup, then— 

Who on earth placed all this here? A door opened. The birds began to scatter. They screamed, Human. Atticus grabbed Kylo. He urged him into the air. The two lost themselves amongst the cloud of fleeing birds. He saw the human scratching his head. He looked at the birdbath. 

Make sure to thank that human. He bailed you out of yet another mess. Atticus said. 

Kylo scoffed. We could have totally taken that guy. The two flew over the Toyota in the driveway. He let loose a dropping. It landed right in the center of the windshield. The bird laughed loud. It was a good day.
