syntax_simple.writingprompts::42:
The subway stopped quite abruptly. Laurentius awoke with a sharp gasp. He struggled to understand his cold surroundings. He examined his own armour carefully. His hands wore gloves of cow hide. His boots were black and fur-lined and warm. He wore a thick black coat. Underneath he had a soft white shirt. Clasps held the shirt together in the front. A red strip of fabric reached around his neck. It reached down to his stomach. What is this, he thought. Is that how I died? Do we wear tokens of our death? His eyes met the eyes of a rotund woman. She had darker skin. She read a curious device on her lap. The device was made of layered parchment. He looked at her neck. He saw a cross. He looked at her with sympathy. I suppose so, he thought. 

Tubes of light illuminated the metal chamber. A smooth ding announced the stop. The doors closed shut. The metal chamber began to move again. Laurentius stood up. He walked toward a man. He assumed this man was in charge. The man wore traditional dress for the era. He wore a large silver wig. He wore glasses. The glasses read 2015 across the front. 

Salve, Laurentius began. 

The man returned a confused look. The man turned back to the window. He smelled of wine. 

Aut ubi sum? Quis hic locus? 

The metal chamber shook again slightly. This movement disrupted the balance of Laurentius. A voice rang out over the loudspeaker. Laurentius could not understand the words. The metal chamber made another stop. Laurentius was not prepared for this. He fell onto the floor. A wave of people exited the train. He got up. He followed the crowd. They weaved through tunnels. He struggled to take everything in. Musicians lined the enclosed street. There were few vendors. He reached a flight of stairs. He ascended the stairs. He was astounded by the view. 

Bright lights flashed around him in all directions. The steady hum of voices had turned into an onslaught. He heard many voices. He saw much action. To his left and right were streets. The streets were lined with people. Everyone moved towards a central location. A large spire reached into the heavens. A sphere sat atop this spire. He looked into the sky. 

No stars? 

No stars. He pondered this fact. A realization came to him suddenly. A wave of happiness and relief followed it. There were no stars. He was above them all. Might these be the plains of Asphodel? They were more beautiful than he had ever imagined. 

A man ran up to him. This man wore a similar outfit. He wore a black coat and black pants and a white shirt. Black metal covered his eyes. Frost came out of his mouth when he spoke. 

Dick, the man said. He grabbed Laurentius by the arm. Laurentius felt overwhelmed. He had no expectation of arguing. He followed this man. 

Dick, where have you been? We have been looking all over. The crowd is waiting. They are not happy. Kathy has been doing what she can. But... 

Laurentius paused. He must learn the language of the afterlife. He noticed the crowd. Some of them began to direct their attention towards him. He returned the same greeting. 

Dick, he said. He nodded his head at the passers-by. The man carried him off. 

Dick, he said once more. He said this to a young girl. Her mother covered her ears immediately. The mother left a scathing glare in her wake. 

A few minutes of navigating the bustling streets passed. Laurentius passed other similarly-dressed gentlemen. They padded him down. He greeted both of them formally. They ushered him up steep metal stairs. They reached a platform. The platform overlooked the massive crowd below. A red-haired woman stood on the platform. She held a microphone. Dick, she said. Where have you been? We are on in two. 

Dick, Laurentius smiled. 

Well, you know what I like. 

Someone handed Laurentius a plastic cord. A bud was on the end. He looked at the woman. She had a bud in her ear. He did the same. Perhaps this was part of the welcoming ceremony. 

He heard the woman speak. She spoke to a man behind a larger metal contraption. The contraption had a folded glass mirror in the centre. 

Live in thirty. 

Alright. You ready? she said. She looked directly at Laurentius. He nodded. She handed him another metal stick. It had fur at the end. It was much like the one she was holding. She stared into the contraption. Her lips formed a smile. Laurentius could not help but smile himself. 

A small red light went on. It was in the corner of the metal-glass contraption. There was a brief pause. The woman nudged Laurentius expectantly. 

Laurentius smiled. He inhaled deeply. Dick, he said. He looked expectantly once again at the woman to his right. He waited for her reaction. He stood very still. The lights were bright. The crowd was loud. He felt a strange sense of belonging. This was his new reality. He accepted it fully. The camera recorded the scene. He remained calm. He waited for the next cue. He was ready.

I knew I would not see immediately. I knew this process required work. I was warned about feeling overwhelmed. I had vague memories of sight. A car accident left me blind in both eyes. I was three years old then. I think those early memories helped me. I processed light and color for three years. My brain remembered light. My brain did not learn it anew. This fact made things easier. 

James helped me a lot. Sometimes I closed my eyes. I moved around like before. He suddenly got in front of me. He blocked my way. He teased me. He was not mean. I protested. He raised his arms. He impeded my movement. He closed his arms around me. He hugged me tight. I won't let go until you open your eyes, he said. No one had ever loved me this much. I heard love in his voice. I felt love in his hugs. 

I practiced often. I got headaches. I tried to look at everything. Blotches of dark smeared across the table. I tried to eat breakfast. James told me about the shadows. They came from the tree outside. That tree never bothered me before. Now it interrupted my breakfast. It made it harder to eat cereal. I felt around with my hands. I wanted to trust my sight. It was strange to see my hands. They were two misshapen blurs. They fumbled with everything. I used to love my hands. 

After a while, the dark smears became shadows. James's face became clear. That was the happiest moment in my life. I woke up one morning. He turned over. I saw his eyes. They shone bright. They held light inside them. He was beautiful. I never knew his beauty before.

He uses his messy scrawl. He touches his pen against his teeth. He thinks hard about me. I feel his presence. I see him in my mind. He tries to figure out my death.

I suppose this is my own fault. I kept asking questions. I needed to understand things. I wanted to find a directing hand in life. I wondered about a purpose for mankind. The car missed me by inches. I felt a pressure in my chest. Panic touched my heart. The green man appeared on the signal. I did not cross the street. I took a step back instead. My intuition warned me. The taxi driver never saw me. I did not see him either. His drunken vehicle slammed into the signal post. I stood there moments ago. That is very messed up. My jaw clenched tight. I cursed the person behind this narrative.

What the actual fuck was that? I spoke these words aloud. My word choice was not very polite. I am talking about a god-figure. He decides my time to die.

I pondered my current position. I thought about the physical world. I thought about the metaphysical world.

Yes, I am sure. I replied to myself. How do you explain the epiphany? How do you explain my near death? There is an author. He does not want to be known.

I am not sure how I knew this. He did not want to be known. I knew he was a man. My general makeup granted me this knowledge. Do not preach at me now. I am not talking about religion. I am not talking about spirituality. I want to live. I stood there. I stared at the sky. I tried to show my disgust. I tried to show my frustration. The signal pole creaked. The sound was very unnatural. I adjusted my head. I aligned my eyes with the pole.

The metal appeared warped. I realized the car burned.

Fuck me. I thought. It is about the drama. It is about the story.

That was all she said. She did not have a scent. She felt like a ghost. I do not know who she was. I do not know why she did this. She made it clear to me. I was right about him. Take that, you fucker. I did not have the strength to say it. I know he heard me.

syntax_simple.writingprompts::51:
Kai snuck back up the stairs from the kitchen. He moved very carefully. Mom and Dad must not catch him. He had leftover broccoli. Mom planned to serve it tomorrow night. That was even worse. Kai felt lucky. He would not have to eat the green vegetables.

Kai closed his bedroom door. The six-year-old went straight to his closet. He opened the closet door. He beamed at the creature. It had many eyes and hair and tentacles.

Kai whispered to the monster. He said hello to Blergh. Blergh accepted the open Tupperware container. The monster used one tentacle. It emptied the entire thing. The monster had a huge mouth. The mouth was the size of a basketball hoop. It swallowed the food whole. Kai could never see any teeth. The monster never chewed.

Kai laid a trail of crackers. He put them on the middle of the floor. The salty circles tempted the monster. The monster slowly left the closet. Kai got a box from his toy chest. He dumped the contents on the floor.

Kai spoke to his friend. He said they were playing army men tonight. Blergh grunted in agreement. Kai loved playing with Blergh. He could move many pieces at once. Blergh was very good at pretend games. He acted surprised when things blew up.

Julia used to be annoyed. She woke up in the morning. She found her son on the floor. He slept among plastic men. They were waiting to be stepped on. It happened many times. Being annoyed was not worth the effort now.

She shook his shoulder softly. She told him to wake up. She asked about Blergh. They walked toward the breakfast table. Julia settled in for a story. She listened to tales of great evil. Kids are so cute at that age.

Ten years passed. Kai no longer had to sneak. All boys his age eat a lot at night. Kai sat in front of his X-Box. He passed a bag of Doritos to his left. He passed a bottle of Mountain Dew too.

He gave the snacks to Blergh. Blergh grunted in gratitude. He swallowed everything whole. The dude still had not learned to chew. Blergh grunted again. He used his many tentacles. He pointed at the television. He pointed at the three controllers in his tentacles. He pointed at the fourth one at Kai's feet. They were ready to play Call of Duty. It was going to be another great night.
syntax_simple.writingprompts::52: The ship reached the beacon. The pilot nervously activated his directional scanning. He had used his last jump fuel. He reached this sector. The pilot felt an inexplicable chill. He glanced out his viewing port. He figured it was jump jitters. He routed power to his security drone anyways. Sensors did not find anything. He should have known it was a waste of time. He had more important things to focus on. He needed to find fuel. The directional scanner pinged. It drew his attention to a large hull. The hull floated some distance from his vessel. A thick cloud of gas partially obscured it. The ship was powered-down. The initial system scan had not detected it. He brought the impulse engines online. He moved towards the derelict vessel. He hailed the ship simultaneously. No response came back. That was curious. Abandoned vessels were not unheard of. The pristine condition of the ship was more unusual. It did not have a single dent. He had found abandoned hulls before. They were pocketed with scorch marks from a laser blast. They showed signs of a short range teleporter. Some sign of battle was always evident. He briefly considered donning his EVA suit. He headed to the drone bay instead. He took remote control of the security drone. It was meant for boarding defense. It could be used as an exploration unit in a pinch. Moments later the drone slid through the airlock. It was a sleek machine. It was armed to the teeth with an assortment of lasers and close combat weapons. These weapons had saved the pilot's life more than once. He had schematics for this hull. The drone made a beeline for engineering. Any remaining fuel would be found there. The problem with remotely controlling the drone was the demand on the pilot. It demanded the full attention of the pilot. The airlock had not sealed. If the pilot was paying attention, he would have noticed his door system had malfunctioned. His dying screams echoed. He was torn to pieces. The pilot should have known that giant alien spiders are no joke. He made a fatal error. He died alone.
syntax_simple.writingprompts::53: My day starts like any other day. I do not need an alarm clock. Human time means nothing here. The cultists scream with rapturous glee. Mister Cthulhu does not mind my sleep schedule. I must do my job well. I fear for my soul. My soul gets devoured like an eclair. My body goes into the spawning pool. I have worked here three years. I have not had one major fuck up. I check the back wall of my ice cold obsidian house. Mister Cthulhu leaves my to-do list there. I find a young woman. She is pinned to my wall with a trident. Her body is writhing in pleasure. Her body is squirming in pleasure. My list is etched into her face. It is a short day. Mister Cthulhu killed Death a few years ago. No one dies anymore. I free the young woman. I take the harpoon with me. I have a few things to do today. I must clean the inside of the temple of Yog-Sothoth. I must get the salt balance sorted out in the Deep One's spawning pool. I must give the Hydra some antacids. The poor girl has been thrashing about for a few hours. She is ravaging the Earth's coasts with tidal waves. I set that as the first priority. Mister Cthulhu does not like it when other people kill his food. I work hard for my boss. I stay alive every day. I keep the ancient gods happy. I do my tasks.
syntax_simple.writingprompts::54: Elwood and Shara leaned against a concrete pillar. They stood in a high school courtyard. They watched a young man. His name was Dale. He was Elwood's newest charge. He looked very unassuming. Shara examined her claws. She spoke to Elwood. She asked about his assignment. She questioned the source of this job. Elwood crossed his arms. He stood against his chest. He answered her question. He called this job a softball pitch. He mentioned the management downstairs. A group of girls walked over. They leaned against the pillar. They occupied the same space as the demons. A strong gust of wind blew. Papers flew from the girls. Binders flew from the girls. The girls shrieked in surprise. They ran after their items. Shara felt annoyed. She spoke to Elwood. She disliked occupying the same space. She turned to the girls. She held her arm out. She held her claws behind her thumb. She flicked her claws outwards. She used a snap. The books flew out of the hands of the girls again. The papers flew again. She called them little wretches. Dale chewed on his burrito. It was a bean and cheese burrito. He looked at the scene. He looked across the courtyard. He had a specific expression. He looked like a placid cow. He chewed on grass like a cow. Shara asked about the kid. She wondered about his behavior. Elwood did not know. He suggested the boy was stupid. Elwood chewed on his thumb. He thought about a strategy. He suggested a time jump. He wanted to go to 6th period. Shara gave Elwood a glance. She raised an eyebrow. She agreed with him. A sound happened. It sounded like tearing canvas. They transported to a new location. They rested on a ledge. It was under a window. It was in the back of the classroom. Shara asked about the plan. Elwood pressed a finger to his lips. He used a long-clawed finger. He told her to hush. Dale hit his desk with his head. He was out cold. Elwood flung his arms wide. He brought them in together. He made a grand gesture. Every student turned to face Dale. They did not say a word. Shara called it cute. Elwood smiled. He told Dale to wake up. Every student spoke in a flat tone. They spoke in unison with Elwood. Dale sat up. His face was slick with drool. He rubbed his eyes. He looked at the class. The class looked back at him. Elwood and the students spoke again. They told Dale to wake up. No one blinked. Dale glanced from side to side. He said he was awake. Elwood flung his arms apart. The class resumed as normal. No one remembered the event. Only Dale was aware of the past. Shara asked about the plan. She felt unimpressed. Dale noticed his notes. He was behind. He began writing in a hurry. Shara talked about the time. She called it a daytime creep. It was not 3 am. She called it creepy stuff. Elwood did not mind. Shara looked at Dale. She saw no clue on his face. She thought the event was unusual. She told Elwood to go. She flexed a claw. She walked away. She begged Elwood to follow. They left through the wall. Elwood spun around. He made a slapping motion. He made a bitch-slapping motion. Dale grunted. His head jerked forward. Loose hair flew up at the back. His pencil shot out. It hit the muscular kid. The muscular kid sat in front of him. A girl looked at Dale. She showed plain disgust. She called him a weirdo. She shifted in her desk. She moved away from him. Shara laughed. The demons waited outside. They waited for the end of the period. They waited for Dale. Shara felt bored. She mentioned the nighttime. She said it was easier. Elwood disagreed. He liked his style. He wanted genuine results. He wanted results during the day. He thought night was too easy. People forget things quickly. He hated the morning light. He loved daytime haunting. Shara did not speak. She yawned. The bell sounded. The period ended. Dale was the last one out. He walked slowly. He looked at his phone. Elwood flapped his wings. He dove into the phone. An alert popped up. Dale clicked on the read button. Elwood jumped into view. He yelled at the phone. He shouted the name Dale. He used the phone speaker. Dale hit the power button. He put the phone in his pocket. He thought about his friends. He thought his friends messed with alerts. He continued walking. He went to his next class. Elwood stretched out of the phone. He made a pop sound. He took his place. He stood next to Shara. They leaned against the wall. Elwood watched Dale walk away. He still did not get the kid. Shara asked about the daytime. Elwood let out a sigh. He agreed to her way. They vanished. They made a pop and a sizzle. They burst into the room. They stayed above the bed. They stared down at Dale. They flapped their wings. Elwood asked about the plan. Shara gave a half smile. She extended her index claw. She curled it into her palm. The sheet was pulled off. It moved with her finger. Dale scratched his stomach. He rolled over. Elwood felt lost for words. He called the act scary. Shara narrowed her eyes. She shot her hand out. She grabbed the air. Dale screamed in pain. Shara yanked her arm back. Dale flew off the bed. He crashed against the wall. Books fell off the shelf. They hit his head. Elwood dropped his jaw. He looked at Shara. He looked at Dale. He called her lack of subtlety. Shara told him to watch. Dale stood up. He picked up the books. He put them on the shelf. The door opened. His mom asked about him. Dale said he was fine. He claimed a leg cramp. He said he fell down. Shara threw her arms up. She expressed her frustration. Elwood agreed with her. He hated the kid. They popped out of the air. They left the room. They disappeared completely.

syntax_simple.writingprompts::57:
Dr. Kevin Bruin. Log Entry E72. The Moment. To you. You are investigating my disappearance. I may not return. No one knows their time. We predict its movement. We avoid it. We cannot stop it. The worst attempts occurred under Marshall Law. The isolation periods were terrible. They were short. They were still terrible. One iso-man asked me a question. He asked about the survival of everyone. We had to interact with people. We isolated them selfishly. He asked about death. He asked if the moment should cause death. His eyes locked into mine. My eyes were full of panic. My eyes were full of guilt. His eyes were peaceful. His eyes were peaceful for a reason. The moment had passed him. The moment had not passed me.

There are rules for the moment. The first rule exists. It only affects men. It affects every man. Age does not matter. The second rule exists. Its intent is not to kill. Deaths have occurred. These deaths involve the very young. These deaths involve the very old. Medical intervention prevents them. Third, it affects men on a singular basis. One man experiences the moment at a time. There are no reported cases of simultaneous experiences. Four, its movement is proximity based. You are near someone. That someone experiences the moment. You are likely to be next. Five, physical barriers cannot contain it. The isolation of an infected area failed. The moment went through the male population. It moved outwards. Sixth, you can outrun it. It moves at the speed of an average human. Finally, the experience itself is incredibly painful.

I went somewhere. People asked me about the moment. I started my research. I claimed the phenomenon was explainable. I made observations. I formed a hypothesis. I conducted experiments. I tested things month after month. I looked for a virus. I looked for a bacterium. I looked for a parasite. I looked for mass hysteria. None of it fit. There was no explanation. People talked about aliens. People talked about God’s punishment. I laughed. I exclaimed that science would find the answer. Eventually no answer came. I doubted for a while. I started to believe the extremists. Few people know this about me. There is one more rule. I accept this rule. Others do not accept it. It is sentient. Extinction is its end game. I am a man of science. I cannot be scared anymore. I must test my hypothesis. You now understand my absence. Men my age are less likely to survive. We can find the answer. Science will prevail. I performed an orchidectomy on myself. You will read this soon. I will be within the current spread of the moment. I wonder about the thoughts of people. They will see a naked old man. I will walk into the fire. Is he mad? Is he a religious nut? No pun is intended. I will succeed. I believe this. You will hear stories. You will hear them before I return. This is the log. The stories will describe a crazy old man. His faith made him immune to the moment. That will be true. Know that faith triumphed. It was faith in science. 

If I do not return. Dan. Love always.
syntax_simple.writingprompts::59: A small lamp burned on the desk. The light was steady. The human wore thin spectacles. They sat on his nose. Stacks of parchment occupied a corner. The man read through pages. He scribbled notes on a sheet. Empty ink bottles sat on the floor. The man was very busy. Ronn stood at the entrance. He readied his heavy flail. The chains dangled. Their echoes filled the room. The man did not look up. He ignored the intruders. He held up a finger. He continued his reading. Ronn looked at his group. They exchanged glances. They shrugged their shoulders. The group stood still for a moment. The man smacked his tongue. He felt disappointment. He replaced the parchment. He pushed his glasses closer to his eyes. He called for his guests. He wanted them to approach. They moved forward. Apologies my friends he said. His voice cracked. It was unpracticed. He spoke again. Come. Come. The adventurers stepped forward slowly. Wilm looked around. He scouted for suspicious stones. He looked for a tripwire. The cobbles turned to green. The tasseled edge of the rug stood before them. The group stopped. Come the man muttered. He showed no impatience. Firrel tested his weight. His boot hit the rug. Solid ground lay beneath it. The rest of the group followed. Wait the man screamed. The group assumed a defensive stance. They drew their weapons. They held their shields. I meant the carpet he said. The adventurers looked at their feet. The jade fibers turned purple. Blood dripped from their bodies. Querth felt shame. His face flushed. Sorry the wizard whispered. The man rolled his eyes. It is already ruined he said. Nothing can be done now. Let us get this over with. The adventurers reached the desk. They stood a pace away. The man raised an open palm. He begged their halt. Hordes of creatures led them to the chamber. The throne room was a study. A librarian sat there. Well then congratulations are in order. The man clapped his hands. Smashing job he said. I am Pollock. I will handle your processing. Processing Edmund echoed. Yes replied Pollock. You finished in this dreadful castle. You are on your way home. You will enjoy the spoils. I must handle the last odds and ends. The adventurers nodded. They felt content. They kept their weapons handy. They had cut through many legions. The battle felt concluded. Excellent let us get started. You slaughtered one hundred and fifty three goblins. You killed twenty nine orcs. You destroyed eighteen kobolds. You finished two dragons. It is impressive. Edmund smirked. He rolled the handle of his axe. It caught the light. Ronn and Dismal groaned. They hated the chaos. It stopped the warrior from gloating. You broke down forty one doors. You set off two fire traps. You triggered six spike snares. You hit three boulders. You caused one acid spill. You freed ten prisoners from the dungeons. All in a day's work Wilm interjected. Quite responded Pollock. He felt no impression. Your adventure has a cost. The total is eight million eight hundred thirty seven thousand two hundred and fifty one gold pieces. Querth could not grasp the figure. They were used to generous spoils. A few hundred gold was the most they had ever seen. We could not carry that much coin Dismal remarked. We could not spend it. That is expected Pollock laughed. You can pay in installments. Pay shouted Firrel. What do you mean pay. Your fines he said. Your damages. You cannot go around killing things. You cannot damage property. You cannot set off traps. These things require professional calibration. We were on a quest Ronn pleaded. We tried to save the village. I see sneered Pollock. Does that mean the village will pay the fines. Will they rebuild the castle. Will they reset the protections. Will they mop the floors. Will they rehire the guards. Will they retrain dragons. Will they inform the families of those lost. The group stood in silence. Their eyes were wide. I did not think so. But it was a quest Ronn repeated. Do you have a license. Do you have a Writ of Pacification for this quest. Ronn shook his head. No need to answer. I know you do not. You should have applied for one. This castle would have been better protected. I would not have been needed. A little WP at the start would have saved us the mess. You caused an unauthorized rampage. Who was supposed to file our WP Querth asked. They considered the question. They looked at Dismal. You have ruined us. I am sorry Dismal cried. I did not know. I did not know this would happen. The circle closed around him. The group looked to dispatch their foe. They saw the enemy within. The moral is tag your posts or else your friends will murder you.
